solution: 편향된 정보를 인공지능에 입력하는 것은 부정확하거나 심지어 해로운 결과를 초래한다는 점을 사례와 함께 설명한 뒤, 쓰레기가 들어가면 쓰레기가 나온다는 것을 기억하라는 비유적인 표현을 사용해 마무리하고 있으므로, 입력되는 정보의 질이 나쁘면 결과물 또한 나쁘다는 의미로 이해할 수 있다. 따라서 밑줄 친 ⓐ ‘쓰레기가 들어가면 쓰레기가 나온다’가 의미하는 바로 ❹ ‘인공지능이 부정확하거나 편향적인 데이터로부터 학습할 때, 그것의 결과는 그러한 결함을 반영할 가능성이 높다.’가 알맞다.

body:
One of the key characteristics of Strong AI is that ______. It can generalize from its training data and apply its knowledge to new situations. For example, a Strong AI system designed to recognize objects in images can learn to recognize objects it hasn’t seen before based on its previous training. Another key attribute of Strong AI is that it is designed to be self-aware and conscious. This means that it can think, reason, and make decisions like a human being. While current AI systems are far from achieving this level of intelligence, some researchers believe that it is possible to create Strong AI in the future.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: it must receive separate instructions for every new situation
it is specialized in performing a limited range of predefined tasks
it is built for learning and adjusting to unfamiliar situations
it can tailor its responses exclusively to situations covered by its earlier training
it can process vast amounts of information to perform calculations with exceptional accuracy
solution: 강한 인공지능은 훈련 데이터로부터 일반화하여 자신의 지식을 새로운 상황에 적용할 수 있으며, 그 예로 이미지 속 객체를 인식하도록 설계된 강한 인공지능 시스템은 이전 훈련을 바탕으로 전에 본 적이 없는 객체를 인식하는 법을 배울 수 있다고 설명하므로, 강한 인공지능이 새로운 상황을 학습하고 그 상황에 적응하도록 설계되어 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❸ ‘그것은 익숙하지 않은 상황을 학습하고 그것에 적응하도록 만들어져 있다'가 알맞다.

body:
A: Ms. Lee, I have already read your article. What is an AI domestic assistant exactly?
B: It’s an AI-powered device ⓐ[designing / designed] to help with household tasks.
A: (A)I’m pretty sure that it will help people with laundry, washing dishes, and organizing their closets.
B: Yes, exactly. I can’t wait for this AI machine ⓑ[to come / coming] out. It is expected ⓒ[to be / being] released on June 1.

위 대화의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: designed coming being
designing coming to be
designed to come being
designing to come to be
designed to come to be
solution:
ⓐ 수식을 받는 앞의 명사구 an AI-powered device가 타동사 design(~을 고안하다)의 대상이며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘be designed+to부정사(~하도록 고안되다)’의 수동 표현을 이루는 to부정사구가 이어져 있으므로 과거분사 designed가 알맞다.
ⓑ 동사구 can’t wait와 to부정사의 의미상주어인 ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 for this AI machine에 이어져 있으므로 ’~가 …하기를 기다릴 수 없을 지경이다, ~가 …하기를 몹시 기다리다’라는 뜻의 ’can’t wait+for+목적격+to부정사‘를 이루는 to부정사 to come이 알맞다.
ⓒ 동사 expect는 ’expect+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …할 것으로 예상하다)‘의 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하며 수동 표현은 ’be expected+to부정사(…할 것으로 예상되다)‘로 나타내므로, 수동태 is expected 뒤에 to부정사구를 이루는 to be가 알맞다. 참고로, 주어 It이 가리키는 this AI machine이 ’출시되는‘ 대상이므로 수동형 to부정사(to+be+p.p.)가 쓰인다.

body:
Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies described in films are now a reality. One of them is self-driving cars. In Total Recall, for example, the taxi driver is the vehicle’s computer system. The taxi is capable of driving itself without any human intervention. (A)그 영화를 본 후, 많은 사람들이 자율주행 자동차를 원했습니다. Luckily, self-driving cars are being developed and certain versions are already on the road. Additionally, many other AI technologies from movies are either in use or under development.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 완료형 분사구문을 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓸 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 9단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
want, see, many people, that movie
→ ______
answer: Having seen that movie, many people wanted self-driving cars.
solution:
• 사람들이 영화를 ‘본’ 것이 자율주행 자동차를 ‘원했던’ 과거 시점의 이전에 발생한 일이므로, <조건>에 따라 주절의 시점보다 앞서 일어난 일을 표현하는 완료형 분사구문(Having+p.p~)을 사용해 Having 뒤에 동사 see를 과거분사(p.p.)인 seen으로 변형하고, 목적어로 명사구 that movie를 쓴다.
• 콤마(,) 뒤에 주절의 주어 many people을 쓰고, want를 과거형인 wanted로 변형한 후, 목적어로 self-driving cars를 쓴다.

This movie, set in 2001, ⓐrealistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that (A)______. In the movie, the ship has a computer system, called “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance to ⓑunderstand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts conduct experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft. Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw ⓒlogical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. The AI helper for a spaceship, which was only seen in the film at the time, has become a ⓓdream. In 2008, the International Space Station, a large spacecraft orbiting Earth, started to use an AI robot named CIMON. It is a floating spherical robot that can move around inside the spacecraft. CIMON, weighing only 5 kg, serves as a ⓔcompetent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when asked.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓓ dream(꿈) → reality(현실)

body:
Minority Report
Minority Report, a film ⓐset in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements ⓑwhat can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes. There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After scanning him and identifying ⓒwho he is, the advertising system offers products that may be appealing to him. Nowadays, we frequently encounter personalized advertisements provided by AI. For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems provide us with advertisements based on our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology ⓓidentifying people through scanning eyes, some devices have already been developed. However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. (A)They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. On the other hand, devices employing AI ⓔhas overcome this limitation. (B)They can scan people’s eyes when (C)they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now.

(A) ______
(B) ______
(C) ______
answer:
(A) those that do not use AI technology
(B) devices employing AI
(C) people
solution:
(A) They는 앞 문장의 those that do not use AI technology(AI 기술을 사용하지 않는 것들(=기기들))를 가리킨다.

body:
The film production industry extensively utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also enables them to make what they intended to express ⓐ[come / to come] alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, through ⓑ[which / that] actors’ faces on the screen are aged or made younger. For example, when ⓒ[providing / provided] with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program (A)[accelerates / prolongs] the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained to (B)[learn / teach] how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly (C)[realistic / unrealistic]. These results are maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to the convenience and the naturalness of the results, it is expected that this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: to come which provided
come which providing
to come that providing
come which provided
to come that provided
solution:
ⓐ 사역동사 make와 목적어인 명사절 what they intended to express에 이어져 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)(~을 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이므로, 동사원형 come이 알맞다.
ⓑ 전치사 through의 목적어 자리에 쓰였으며, 뒤에 완전한 절(actors‘ ~ younger)이 이어지므로, ’전치사+관계대명사+완전한 절‘ 형태로 앞 절의 an AI-based program을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루는 목적격 관계대명사가 올 자리이며, 전치사 뒤에 관계대명사 that은 쓰이지 않으므로, 목적격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.
ⓒ 접속사 when 뒤에 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태인 ’접속사+분사~‘ 구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 생략된 주어 it(=the AI program)이 ’제공받는‘ 대상이고 뒤에 ’provide ~ with …(~에게 …을 제공하다)‘의 목적어 없이 전치사 with가 바로 이어져 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ’~ be provided with …(~가 …을 제공받다)‘의 과거분사 provided가 알맞다.

solution:
(A) 다양한 연령대의 다양한 얼굴 이미지를 생성하는 기존의 기술들은 방대한 과정을 요구했다고 한 뒤에 However(그러나)로 이어지므로, 새로 개발된 자동화 프로그램은 그 과정을 빠르게 한다는 대조적인 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 accelerates(~을 가속화한다)가 알맞다.
prolongs ~을 연장한다

body:
When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!”
“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”
“Zambezi?”
“It’s the name we gave the little elephant.”
So the elephant was alive! Aaron beamed, his heart beating faster. Samuel motioned for him to follow. Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, ⓐwas covered by blankets. He seemed to be having trouble breathing. The image of his father, lying under blankets at home just before he died, flashed through Aaron’s mind, and he felt a lump in his throat.
Samuel nudged him forward. Aaron knelt and, with shaking hands, ⓑreached out to touch Zambezi’s thick skin. It felt surprisingly warm. Zambezi opened one eye. Slowly, his trunk curled upward and brushed Aaron’s arm.
“How are you?” Aaron whispered.
He sat down on the straw, and the elephant rested his trunk on Aaron’s leg. They stayed like that for some time, while Samuel watched them ⓒcuriously.
“Here,” Samuel whispered, handing a milk bottle to Aaron. “Maybe you will have better luck than we’ve had.”
Aaron had seen enough babies nurse ⓓto know what to do. He tilted the bottle, spilling some drops onto the elephant’s lip. Zambezi licked the milk off his lip and then began to suck from the bottle, looking Aaron in the eyes as he ⓔdid. Samuel shook his head in amazement. Aaron’s mind rushed back to the day he first met the elephant.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓐ was covered → covered 또는 which was covered
(완전한 절(He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones)에 접속사 없이 다른 동사구(was covered ~)가 이어질 수 없으므로, 흐름상 앞의 명사구 a wrinkled bag of bones를 수식하는 분사구나 관계사절이 이어져야 한다. 수식을 받는 명사구 a wrinkled bag of bones가 ‘덮여 있는’ 대상이고 목적어 없이 전치사구가 이어지므로, was covered를 과거분사 covered로 고치거나, 앞에 적절한 주격 관계대명사를 넣어 which was covered로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 등위접속사 and 뒤에 이중 콤마(,)로 전치사구가 삽입된 형태로, 주어 Aaron에 이어지는 두 번째 동사이므로 과거동사 knelt와 병렬을 이루는 reached는 알맞다.
ⓔ 부사절 접속사 as가 이끄는 절의 주어 he가 단수이므로 단수 동사로 수일치한 것은 알맞으나, 일반동사인 look을 대신하는 대동사 자리로 흐름상 과거동사 did는 알맞다.

The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, ⓐby which he has been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. ⓑWith the cook and the gardener pull from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them waving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ에서 어법상 어색한 부분을 두 군데씩 찾아서 고친 후, 전체를 다시 쓰시오.
ⓐ ______
ⓑ ______
answer:
ⓐ where[in which] he had been working for a few months
ⓑ With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck.
solution:
ⓐ • 완전한 절을 이끌고, 선행사인 장소 명사구 Lion’s Inn을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 장소의 관계부사 where로 고치거나 흐름상 ‘work in ~(~에서 일하다)’의 전치사 in을 사용한 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 in which로 고친다.
*본문에는 where가 쓰였음
• 뒤의 부사구(for a few months)가 나타내는 Aaron은 Lion 여관으로 향했던 과거 사실보다 그가 몇 개월 동안 일해 오고 있었다는 것이 더 앞선 사실을 나타내므로 과거완료 진행(had been+-ing)이 되도록 has been working을 had been working으로 고친다.
ⓑ • ’~가 …한 상태로, ~가 …한 채로‘라는 뜻의 ’with+명사(구)+분사‘ 구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 명사구 the cook and the gardener가 ’당기는‘ 주체이므로, pull을 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 pulling으로 고친다.
• 주어와 부사에 이어 동사 자리로 동사 manage는 목적어로 to부정사를 취하므로 drag, pull, and push를 to drag, pull, and push로 고친다.

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I ⓐdo. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart ⓑhammering in his chest. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw.
Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi ⓒswallowed pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours.
Aaron recorded the amounts that Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. (A) He felt ⓓproud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel. (B) Each time he saw the veterinarian ⓔfrown, Aaron’s stomach got tense. (C) When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared that he’d never get better. (D) One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow ⓕcomparing to his own. (E) Samuel reassured him that all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But that didn’t stop Aaron from worrying. Bezi still had a fever. Aaron knew only too well ⓖwhat medicine couldn’t cure everything.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ 동사(sat)가 있는 완전한 절(Aaron sat straight up)에 접속사 없이 다른 절이나, 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으며, 흐름상 주절의 주어와 다른 의미상의 주어 heart가 남아있으며 부대상황(~하면서)을 나타내는 독립분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 의미상 주어 heart가 그의 가슴에서 심장이 ‘쿵쾅거리는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 hammering은 알맞다.
ⓓ 2형식 동사 felt의 보어 자리로 형용사 proud는 알맞다.
ⓔ 과거동사 saw와 목적어 the veterinarian에 이어져 ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 보다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형, 능동·진행일 때는 현재분사, 수동일 때는 과거분사가 쓰인다. 목적어 the veterinarian이 ‘얼굴을 찌푸리는’ 주체이므로, 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 frown은 알맞다.
오답
ⓐ do → am (‘~도 (마찬가지로) 그러하다’의 뜻으로 쓰인 부사절 접속사 as가 이끄는 절에서 주어에 이어지는 동사 자리로, 흐름상 앞의 be동사가 쓰인 be proud를 대신해야 하므로, do를 주어에 일치시킨 현재시제 am으로 고친다.)
ⓒ swallowed → to swallow (to부정사 to get과 Bezi에 이어져 ‘get+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하도록 하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 to부정사를 쓰므로 swallowed를 to swallow로 고친다.
ⓕ comparing → compared (완전한 절(Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow)에 이어지는 분사 자리로 앞 문장 Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow을 부연 설명하고, 앞 문장이 ‘비교되는’ 대상이므로 comparing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 compared로 고친다.)
ⓖ what → that (완전한 절(medicine couldn’t cure everything)을 이끌어 동사 knew의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)

(B)Aaron은 여전히 자신을 필요로 하는 아기 코끼리 가까이에서 잠을 자며, 밤낮으로 지켜보고 그 또는 그녀에게 먹이를 준다. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.
윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: getting better each day
losing interest in his daily activities
showing little interest in his surroundings
remaining dependent on human attention
becoming increasingly restless inside his stall
solution:
Bezi의 움푹 들어간 피부가 둥근 배로 바뀌고 볼에도 살이 차올랐으며, 움직임이 활발해지고 다른 코끼리들과 어울리며 바깥으로 나가 진흙에서 즐겁게 첨벙거릴 때 그의 눈은 빛이 났다고 설명하고 있으므로, Bezi가 활기를 찾고 건강을 회복하고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ① ‘날마다 더 좋아지고 있는’이 알맞다.

② 그의 일상 활동에 흥미를 잃어 가고 있는
③ 그의 주변 환경에 거의 관심을 보이지 않는
④ 인간의 관심에 계속 의존한 채 남아있는

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart hammering in his chest. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw.
Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours.
Aaron recorded the amounts that Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The head keeper was aware that Aaron had saved Bezi from the pool.
Aaron’s mother said that his father would be proud of him for working at the orphanage.
Aaron barely slept, jolting upright whenever Bezi let out a snort.
Aaron missed his sister’s breathing but gradually found comfort in Bezi and the scent of straw.
Bezi took his medication on his own and gradually recovered, spending less and less time in the stable.
solution:
Samuel과 사육사들은 Aaron에게 Bezi이 약을 먹도록 하는 속임수를 보여주었고, Bezi는 여전히 아파 대부분의 시간을 마구간에서 잠으로 보냈다고 언급하고 있으므로, ⑤ ‘Bezi는 스스로 약을 먹었고 점차 회복하여 마구간에서 보내는 시간이 점점 줄어들었다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 수석 사육사는 Aaron이 수영장에서 Bezi를 구했다는 것을 알고 있었다.
② Aaron의 어머니는 그가 고아원에서 일하는 것에 대해 그의 아버지가 그를 자랑스러워하실 것이라고 말했다.
③ Aaron은 Bezi가 코를 힝힝거릴 때마다 놀라 벌떡 일어나면서 거의 잠을 자지 못했다.
④ Aaron은 그의 여동생의 숨소리를 그리워했지만, 점차 Bezi와 짚 냄새에서 위안을 찾았다.

body:
The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, where he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage (A)[by which / in which] the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, ⓐ______. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, (B)[shook / shaking]. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them (C)[waving / to wave] their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: by which shook waving
in which shaking to wave
in which shook waving
by which shaking to wave
in which shaking waving
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(he had been working for a few months)을 이끌고, 선행사인 장소 명사구 Lion’s Inn을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 흐름상 ‘work in ~(~에서 일하다)’의 전치사 in을 사용한 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 in which가 적절하다.
본문변형 where → in which
(B) (동사(watched)가 있는 완전한 절(He watched the elephant)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 the elephant를 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상의 주어인 the elephant가 ‘몸을 떠는’ 주체이고 동사 shake는 ‘떨다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰였으므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 shaking이 적절하다.
(C) ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하는 것을 보다)’의 5형식 구문에서 지각동사 see의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형이나 현재분사를 사용하며, 목적어 them(some men in uniform)이 ‘흔드는’ 주체이고 목적어 their arms가 이어지므로 능동이자 진행 중인 동작을 나타내기 위해 쓰인 현재분사 waving이 적절하다.

body:
Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why ⓐsinging in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier ⓑenjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of ⓒbeing played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed privately on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music ⓓthat is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have more entertainment options today than in the past ⓔwhich people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: People today spend less time with others, which partly explains the decline in group singing.
Personal music devices have made listening to music more dependent on social interaction.
People from different backgrounds may not know the same songs, making group singing less common.
Those who worry about their social image may feel awkward singing in front of others.
People often gathered around the piano or the guitar simply for enjoyment in the past.
solution:
기술의 발전으로 음악은 우리의 개인용 재생 장치로 혼자 즐기는 것이 되었다고 했으므로 ② ‘개인용 음악 기기들은 음악 감상을 사회적 상호작용에 더 의존하게 만들었다.‘는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 오늘날 사람들은 다른 사람들과 보내는 시간이 더 적으며, 이는 집단으로 노래하는 일이 감소한 이유를 부분적으로 설명해 준다.
③ 서로 다른 배경을 가진 사람들은 같은 노래를 모를 수도 있으며, 이로 인해 함께 노래하는 일이 더 드물어진다.
④ 자신의 사회적 이미지에 대해 걱정하는 사람들은 다른 사람들 앞에서 노래하는 것을 어색하게 느낄 수 있다.
⑤ 과거에는 사람들이 단지 즐거움을 위해 피아노나 기타 주변에 모이곤 했다.

body:
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel connected to others and to something greater. Thus, (A)함께 노래하는 사람들이 더 건강한 정신을 가지고 있으며, 자신의 지역사회에 더 적극적으로 참여한다는 것은 놀라운 일이 아니다. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.

<조건>
• 가주어를 사용할 것
• 적절한 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 축약형을 사용하여 18단어로 영작할 것

<보기>
communities, surprise, readily participate in, healthy minds, sing together, have, no

→ ______
answer: it's no surprise that people who[that] sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities
solution:
• 가주어 it과 be동사 is를 축약한 it’s 뒤에 ‘놀라운 것이 아니다’를 뜻하도록 부정어 no, 명사 surprise를 차례대로 쓰고, 진주어를 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• 진주어절의 주어 people을 쓰고, people을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작한다. 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 who를 쓰고, ‘함께 노래하다’를 뜻하도록 sing together를 쓴다.
*본문에서는 who가 쓰였음
• 주어 people에 이어지는 동사 have를 쓰고, 형용사 healthy의 비교급 healthier를 사용한 목적어 healthier minds를 이어 쓴다.
• 등위접속사 부사 readily의 비교급 more readily를 쓰고 ‘~에 참여하다’를 뜻하는 구동사 participate in과 목적어 their communities를 차례대로 쓴다.

body:
The communal nature of music remains and is vividly demonstrated at live concerts. Whether you’re in the crowd at the Mercury Lounge or Madison Square Garden, the point is to gather with people who (A)[love / loves] what you love. If the point wasn’t to gather or to share in the mass performance, you’d just stay home and listen to music by yourself. When you sing along to songs at a concert, you don’t just listen to the music; you participate in it, “completing” the musical experience. This creates a sense of belonging and a strong bond with the musician. Many musicians remember the first time (B)[which / when] their audience sang along with them. Maybe it means (C)[that / what] they have reached the point in their career where they have become popular. Even singers with long, successful careers feel energized by the power of the crowd and get inspired for their next music project.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: love / when / that

loves / which / that

body:
Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed privately on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have more entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.

The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel (C)[connected to / detached from] others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. solution:
(A) 오늘날에는 사람들이 집단으로 보내는 시간이 줄고 사회적으로 고립되는 경향이 있으며, 개인용 기기로 음악을 즐기는 일이 쉬워졌다고 했으므로 음악을 ‘혼자’ 즐긴다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 privately(혼자)가 적절하다.
collectively 집단으로
(B) 과거에는 사람들이 단순히 즐거움을 위해 피아노나 기타 주변에 모였지만, 오늘날에는 집단으로 노래하는 것이 덜 흔해졌다고 했으므로, 사람들이 여가를 즐길 수 있는 다른 선택지가 ‘늘어났다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 more(더 많은)가 적절하다.
less 더 적은
(C) 함께 노래하는 활동은 사람들을 더 가까워지게 하고 유대감과 소속감을 형성한다고 했고, 뒤에서 함께 노래하는 사람은 자신의 지역사회에 더 적극적으로 참여한다고 했으므로, 함께 노래하는 활동을 통해 형성된 소속감과 목적의식이 우리가 다른 사람들과 또 더 큰 무언가와 연결되어 있다고 느끼게 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 connected to(~에 연결된)가 적절하다.
detached from ~와 동떨어진

body:
Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed (A)[privately / collectively] on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have (B)[less / more] entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel (C)[connected to / detached from] others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re ⓐ______. Being together is the key.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: watching musical performances through digital devices
competing against each other in musical contests
sharing recorded music with online communities
listening to music individually at home
singing collectively in virtual spaces
solution:
앞에서 함께 노래하는 것이 스트레스를 줄이고 유대감과 소속감을 형성하는 등 여러 긍정적인 효과를 가져온다고 설명하고, 마지막 문장에서 함께하는 것이 핵심이라고 강조하므로, 물리적으로 같은 장소에 있지 않더라도 함께 노래함으로써 이러한 이점을 얻을 수 있다는 내용이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘가상 공간에서 다른 사람들과 함께 노래하고 있는’이 적절하다.
본문변형 singing with others online → singing collectively in virtual spaces
오답
① 디지털 기기를 통해 음악 공연을 관람하고 있는
② 음악 경연 대회에서 서로 경쟁하고 있는
③ 온라인 공동체와 녹음된 음악을 공유하고 있는
④ 집에서 개별적으로 음악을 듣고 있는

body:
In a highly connected world where technology doesn’t necessarily connect people in a human way, individuals ______. The invention of portable music players and earphones has made music more personal, too. However, the communal elements persist, manifesting their power in singing events, large and small. Singing with others can be a way to heal and help us feel connected, happy, and healthy. Maybe it is in our genes as a social species. Just open your mouth, start making a sound, and let your voice go. You’ll know how good it is almost instantly.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: find fewer opportunities to enjoy music privately
become socially isolated and feel intense loneliness
enjoy music through shared listening experiences
consume music more frequently through digital devices
prioritize digital communication over face-to-face meetings
solution:
앞에서 기술이 사람들을 반드시 인간적인 방식으로 연결하는 것은 아니라고 했고, 뒤에서 휴대용 음악 재생 기기와 이어폰의 발명이 음악을 더욱 개인적으로 만들었다고 했으므로, 기술의 발달로 사람들 사이의 유대감이 약해지고 개인의 외로움이 커진다는 내용이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ② ‘사회적으로 고립되고 극심한 외로움을 느끼다’가 적절하다.
오답
① 음악을 혼자 즐길 기회가 더 적어지다
③ 함께 음악을 듣는 경험을 통해 음악을 즐기다
④ 디지털 기기를 통해 음악을 더 자주 소비하다
⑤ 대면 만남보다 디지털 소통을 우선시하다

body:
B: Could you help me choose a book to borrow, Ms. Han?
W: Okay. What kind of book are you looking for?
B: I usually read fantasy novels, like the Harry Potter series, but I want to try something different.
W: I see. There are many different genres, including science fiction, mystery, and adventure.
B: Science fiction sounds interesting. Can you tell me more about it?
W: It combines science and imagination with exciting futuristic adventures.
B: ______
W: Yes, that’s a great example. That movie was based on science fiction stories written by Isaac Asimov.
B: I get it. Can you recommend a science fiction novel?
W: Sure! Ender’s Game by Orson Scott Card is a popular choice. It’s about a young boy who is trained to fight an alien invasion in the future.
B: Okay, I’ll give it a try. Thank you.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Could you explain why the movie I, Robot is so popular?
Are you satisfied with the movie I, Robot?
Why don't we watch the movie I, Robot?
That reminds me of the movie I, Robot!
I’m interested in the movie I, Robot.
solution:
빈칸 앞에서 여자가 공상 과학 장르는 과학과 상상력을 결합하여 흥미진진한 미래의 모험을 보여준다고 했고, 빈칸이 포함된 남자의 말에 대한 답변으로 여자가 ‘맞아, 그건 아주 좋은 예시야.’라고 대답하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 남학생이 공상 과학 장르의 적절한 영화 예시를 언급하는 내용이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ④ ‘영화 ‘아이, 로봇’을 생각나게 해요!‘가 적절하다.
오답
① 영화 ‘아이, 로봇’이 왜 그렇게 인기 있는지 설명해 주시겠어요?
② 영화 ‘아이, 로봇’에 만족하나요?
③ 영화 ‘아이, 로봇’을 보는 게 어때요?
⑤ 저는 영화 ‘아이, 로봇’에 관심이 있어요.

choices: The boy usually reads fantasy books but is now looking for a book from a different genre.

solution:
Isaac Asimov가 쓴 공상 과학 이야기를 바탕으로 한 영화는 ‘아이, 로봇’이며, ‘엔더스 게임’은 Orson Scott Card가 쓴 소설이므로 ④ ‘한 선생님은 인기가 많기 때문에 Isaac Asimov가 쓴 ’엔더스 게임‘을 추천한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

① 소년은 보통 판타지 책을 읽지만, 이제는 다른 장르의 책을 찾고 있다.
② 한 선생님은 공상 과학이 과학적 아이디어와 상상력, 미래의 모험을 결합한다고 설명한다.

body:
On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy named Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. Feeling ⓐthat his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, ⓑnoticed his mother’s concern, smiled at her and continued following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, imagining ⓒwhat it might hold.
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him ⓓwhat he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he ⓔhad made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided it would be fine ⓕto let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and ⓖenjoyed the beach as they had always done, but he did not.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ noticed → noticing (완전한 절(The boy ~ along)을 이루는 주어 The boy와 동사 smiled 사이에 이중 콤마로 삽입된 분사구문으로, 의미상 주어인 The boy가 어머니의 걱정을 ‘알아차린‘ 주체이므로 noticed를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 noticing으로 고친다.)
ⓓ what → if 또는 whether (뒤에 완전한 절(he ~ beach)을 이끌어 ask의 직접목적어인 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 what은 쓸 수 없으며, 흐름상 ’~인지 아닌지 그에게 물었다‘의 의미가 되어야 자연스러우므로, ’~인지 아닌지‘의 의미를 갖는 명사절 접속사 if 또는 whether로 고친다.)
ⓖ enjoyed → enjoying (흐름상 ’뒤따라가서 해변을 즐기고 싶었다‘라는 뜻으로 felt like의 목적어 running과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 enjoyed를 enjoying으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(his attention was elsewhere)을 이끌어 분사 Feeling의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓒ 분사 imagining의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로, ’의문사+주어+동사 ~‘의 어순을 갖는 간접의문문을 이끄는 의문사 what이 쓰인 것은 적절하며, what은 의문사이자 hold의 목적어 역할을 함께 하고 있다.
ⓔ 평소 가던 곳에 싫증이 났다고 어머니가 생각하게 만든 것이 후회를 하는 과거 시점보다 먼저 발생한 것이므로 과거 시제보다 앞설 때 사용하는 과거완료 had made는 적절하다.
ⓕ decided의 목적어 역할을 하는, 접속사 that이 생략된 명사절의 주어 자리 it은 가주어이므로, 이에 상응하는 진주어로 to부정사 to let이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the sudden fear and loneliness experienced in an unfamiliar environment
Jerry’s growing fear of leaving his familiar surroundings
Jerry’s curiosity about the unknown beyond his usual beach
a mother’s efforts to protect her son from coastal dangers
the importance of spending summer vacations with family
solution:
Jerry는 평소 가던 해변보다 조금 더 멀리 있는 바위투성이의 만에 시선을 두고, 그곳에 무엇이 있을지 상상해보며 계속 흘낏 바라보았고 다음 날 결국 바위를 보러 가고 싶다고 말하였으므로 이 글의 주제로 ③ ‘평소 다니던 해변 너머에 있는 미지의 것에 대한 Jerry의 호기심’이 적절하다.

body:
Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried ⓐdiving with them, but he was too afraid.
(A) At fifty, he started to worry. At one hundred, he wondered whether he should yell for help. But around one hundred and fifty, he realized that they were in fact swimming through some rocks in the water and coming out the other side.
(B) Feeling ⓑrejected, Jerry watched the boys from a distance and noticed that they were underwater for a long time. He started counting the seconds.
(C) ⓒNoticed his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.
After they left, he tried to do what they ⓓhad done, but when he tried to open his eyes to see underwater, his eyes stung from the salty water. With his eyes closed, however, he was unable to see the tunnel that the boys had swum through. His only option was to give up and ⓔgo home.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: Jerry가 소년들과 함께 다이빙을 시도했으나 너무 두려워했다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 두려워서 하지 못한 다이빙을 his hesitation(그의 망설임)으로 이어받아 소년들이 흥미를 잃고 Jerry의 외침을 무시한 채 헤엄쳐 떠나는 상황을 설명하는 (C), 이 상황을 Feeling rejected(거절당했다고 느끼며)로 이어받아 소년들이 물속에 오랫동안 있는 것을 보고 초를 세기 시작했다는 내용의 (B), 초를 세는 행동을 50초, 100초, 150초 등의 구체적인 수치와 함께 설명하며 소년들이 물속의 바위 사이로 헤엄쳐 반대편으로 나오고 있음을 깨닫는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

solution:
ⓒNoticed → Noticing (완전한 절(the boys ~ Merci!)과 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 the boys가 그의 망설임을 ‘알아차린’ 주체이므로 Noticed를 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 Noticing으로 고친다.)

ⓑ 의미상 주어인 Jerry가 ‘거절당했다’고 느낀 것이므로 Feeling의 보어로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 rejected가 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
ⓓ 소년들이 떠난 뒤, Jerry가 소년들이 했던 것을 시도해봤다는 내용으로, Jerry가 시도한 과거 시점(tried)보다 소년들이 한 것이 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로 과거보다 앞서는 과거완료 had done이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
ⓔ 동사 was에 이어져 주격보어 역할을 하는 to부정사구 to give up과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되며, to부정사구가 병렬 연결될 때 두 번째 to는 생략 가능하므로 동사원형 go는 적절하다.

body:
Back home that evening, Jerry asked his mother for swimming goggles. After receiving them the next day, he ran off back to the bay. Underwater, he was now able to see the tunnel clearly. He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin frightened him. He gave up and decided to ______.
From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks to practice his breathing and diving. Some days, he pushed himself too hard, and his nose would bleed from too much practice. His mother told him that she was worried about him and had him join her at their usual beach. But the beach looked different to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: ask the local boys to guide him
find another route to get inside the tunnel
practice holding his breath underwater instead
focus on making some lasting memories with his mother
wait until he was older and stronger before trying again
solution:
Jerry는 물속에서 굴을 보았지만 어둠과 피부에 닿는 해초의 느낌 때문에 두려움을 느껴 포기했으나 이후 매일 아침 어머니와 떨어져 바위로 가서 호흡과 다이빙을 연습했다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 굴에 다시 도전하기 위해 수중 호흡 능력을 향상하는 데 집중했다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ③ ‘대신 물속에서 숨 참는 연습을 하다’가 적절하다.
오답
① 현지 소년들에게 자신을 안내해줄 것을 요청하다
② 굴 안으로 들어가기 위해 다른 경로를 찾다
④ 어머니와 오래 남을 추억을 만드는 데 집중하다
⑤ 다시 시도하기 전에 나이가 더 들고 힘이 더 세질 때까지 기다리다

body:
[1]
Jerry soon began to feel restless being back at the beach with his mother, and he worried that all the practice he had put in would go to waste. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and practicing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. (A)그는 준비가 되어 있는 것이 자신을 좌절하게 했던 굴을 자신이 정복하는 데 도움이 되리라는 것을 알았다.
[2]
After a few days, his mother told him that they would soon need to return home. This news urged him to go back to the bay. He felt that he absolutely needed to go through the tunnel before they went home. His fear, however, made him think that just practicing some more and trying again next year might be wiser.
But even after reaching that conclusion, he found himself sitting on the rock with a longing to overcome his fear and conquer the tunnel. It would be now or never. He decided to try once more. His hands were shaking, but he placed them firmly at his sides. He looked up at the sky, filled his lungs with air, and then sank fast into the ocean.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• that을 두 번 사용할 것
• 동명사를 사용할 것
• 과거완료시제를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 15단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
help, prepare, will, defeat, know, the tunnel, conquer
→ ______
answer: He knew that being prepared would help him conquer the tunnel that had defeated him.
solution:
• 주어 He, 동사 knew를 쓰고, 목적어로 명사절이 쓰이므로 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• 의미상 주어인 He가 ‘준비된’ 대상이며, 동명사를 주어로 써야 하므로 that절의 주어 자리에 수동형 동명사 being prepared를 쓰고 주절의 동사 knew와 시제가 일치하도록 조동사 will을 과거형 would로 변형한다. 동사 help는 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적어 him에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리에 동사원형 conquer 또는 to부정사 to conquer를 쓸 수 있지만, 단어 수 제한에 따라 동사원형 conquer를 쓴다.
• conquer의 목적어인 명사구 the tunnel을 쓰고 the tunnel을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계대명사 that을 쓰고, 굴이 자신을 좌절하게 한 것이 알고 있는(knew) 과거 시점보다 더 먼저 발생한 것이므로, 동사 defeat를 과거완료 had defeated로 변형하고 목적어 him을 이어준다.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) The day after staying at the beach with his mother, Jerry returned to the rocky bay because he did not want his practice to be wasted. (T/F)
(B) Whenever he was with his mother, Jerry explored the underwater tunnel and practiced holding his breath. (T/F)
(C) When his mother announced that they would soon return home, Jerry felt he had to pass through the tunnel before they left. (T/F)
(D) Although Jerry wanted to conquer the tunnel, he decided to postpone his next attempt until the following year. (T/F)
(E) Despite his trembling hands, Jerry took a deep breath and quickly sank into the ocean. (T/F)
choices: T-F-T-F-F
T-F-T-F-T
F-T-T-F-T
T-F-F-T-T
F-F-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-F-T이다.
(A) 어머니와 함께 해변에서 머문 다음 날, Jerry는 자신의 연습이 헛수고가 되는 것을 원하지 않았기 때문에 바위투성이의 만으로 돌아갔다. (일치)
(B) Jerry는 어머니와 함께 있을 때마다 수중 굴을 탐험하고 숨을 참는 연습을 했다(→만에서는 굴을 탐험하고, 어머니와 다시 함께 있을 때마다 호흡 연습을 했다). (불일치)
(C) 어머니가 곧 집으로 돌아갈 것이라고 알렸을 때, Jerry는 그들이 떠나기 전에 반드시 굴을 통과해야 한다고 느꼈다. (일치)
(D) Jerry는 굴을 정복하고 싶었지만, 다음 시도를 내년까지 미루기로 결정했다(→미루는 것이 현명할지도 모른다고 생각했지만, 지금이 아니면 절대 할 수 없을 것 같아서 다시 시도했다). (불일치)
(E) 떨리는 손에도 불구하고, Jerry는 깊이 숨을 마시고 바닷속으로 빠르게 가라앉았다. (일치)

body:
He soon found the entrance to the tunnel. He took the edges of the hole in his hands and drew himself into it. It was pitch black, but he kept counting, just as he (A)[had / has] practiced. Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two… Soon he reached a hundred, a hundred and one… He kept moving through the tunnel, and when he thought he couldn’t ⓐlast any longer, he spotted a crack of light at the end. The feeling of victory filled him as he realized (B)[what / that] with a few more strokes, he would be coming out the other side. He felt like he was ⓑrunning out of air, but he kept kicking and thinking just a little bit more!
Finally, his hands found the exit of the tunnel, and he swam out into the open sea. At first, he started to gasp like a fish out of water, but after some time, his heart quieted and his eyes cleared. He had ⓒmade it. After resting a short while on the warm rock, he got on his feet and walked back home. His mother’s eyes lit up, as she was happy to see him back. “Did you have a nice morning?” she asked. Jerry replied with ⓓpride, “Mom, I can stay underwater for two minutes, three minutes, at least!” His mom thought about telling him to rest for the remainder of the day, but she didn’t have to. He was now ⓔreluctant to stay home and rest. (C)[Go / Going] to the bay was no longer important to him.

solution: ⓔ reluctant(마지못한) → happy(행복한)

body:
On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy named Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. (A) But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. (B) The boy, noticing his mother’s concern, smiled at her and continued following along. (C) He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, ⓐ[imagining / imagined] what it might hold. (D)
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. (E) He first answered no, regretting that he ⓑ[had / has] made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided ⓒ[that / it] would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they had always done, but he did not.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
Feeling that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘어머니는 Jerry의 관심이 다른 곳에 있다고 느끼고, 그가 무슨 생각을 하고 있을지 걱정했다.’라는 뜻으로, 그의 관심이 다른 곳에 있었다고 했으므로 이 문장 앞에는 Jerry가 시선 또는 관심을 다른 곳으로 돌리는 행동이 제시되어야 한다. (B) 앞에서 Jerry의 시선이 평소 가던 해변이 아닌 조금 더 멀리 있는 바위투성이의 만을 향했다고 했으므로, 이를 본 어머니가 Jerry의 관심이 다른 곳에 있다고 느껴 걱정했다는 내용이 자연스럽게 이어진다. 또한 (B) 뒤에 이어지는 his mother’s concern(어머니의 걱정)이 주어진 문장에서 언급한 어머니의 걱정을 가리키므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (B)이다.

solution:

body:
He soon found the entrance to the tunnel. He took the edges of the hole in his hands and drew himself into it. It was pitch black, but he kept counting, just as he had practiced. Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two… Soon he reached a hundred, a hundred and one… He kept moving through the tunnel, and when he thought he couldn’t last any longer, he spotted a crack of light at the end. The feeling of victory filled him as he realized that with a few more strokes, he would be coming out the other side. He felt like he was running out of air, but he kept kicking and thinking just a little bit more!
Finally, his hands found the exit of the tunnel, and he swam out into the open sea. At first, he started to gasp like a fish out of water, but after some time, his heart quieted and his eyes cleared. He had made it. After resting a short while on the warm rock, he got on his feet and walked back home. His mother’s eyes lit up, as she was happy to see him back. “Did you have a nice morning?” she asked. Jerry replied with pride, “Mom, I can stay underwater for two minutes, three minutes, at least!” His mom thought about telling him to rest for the remainder of the day, but she didn’t have to. He was now happy to stay home and rest. Going to the bay was no longer important to him.

By continuing to count and kick until he swam out of the dark tunnel despite (A) ______, Jerry finally (B) ______ and felt (C) ______ of himself, which made him feel happy enough to (D) ______ without needing to (E) ______.
<조건>
• (A), (B), (D)는 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓸 것
• (C), (E)는 본문에서 찾아 변형하여 쓸 것
• (A), (D), (E)은 4단어, (B)는 2단어, (C)는 1단어로 쓸 것
answer:
(A) running out of air (B) made it (C) proud
(D) stay home and rest (E) go to the bay
solution: 요약문 그가 어두운 굴에서 헤엄쳐 나올 때까지 (A)공기가 부족해짐에도 불구하고 계속 숫자를 세고 발차기를 함으로써, Jerry는 마침내 (B)해냈고 자신을 (C)자랑스럽게 느꼈으며, 이는 그가 (D)만으로 갈 필요 없이 (E)집에 머물며 쉴 수 있을 만큼 행복하게 느끼게 했다.

The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he had made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but (A)그녀는 그를 혼자 가게 해도 괜찮을 것이라고 판단했다. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they had always done, but he did not.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 생략할 것
• ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 13단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
fine, let, on one's own, will, decide, go
→ ______
answer: she decided it would be fine to let him go on his own
solution:
• 주어 she, 동사 decided를 쓰고 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절이 이어져야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that을 써야 하지만 <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사 that을 생략한다.
• 가주어 it을 쓰고 주절의 동사 decided와 시제가 일치하도록 조동사 will을 과거형 would로 변형하고 be동사 be와 보어 fine을 이어 쓴다.
• 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 to let을 쓰고 동사 let이 ‘~하게 (허락)하다’라는 뜻의 사역동사로 쓰일 때 ‘let+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 let의 목적어 him에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리에 동사원형 go를 쓴다. ‘혼자서’를 뜻하는 on his own을 이어 쓴다.

body:
M: Black holes are the strangest objects in the universe. They are regions in space with strong gravity that (A)[is / are] so powerful that even light cannot escape it. Black holes are formed when stars collapse. One interesting fact about them is (B)[what / that] black holes are invisible. So how do we know that they exist? We can detect black holes by their gravitational influence. For example, if a star comes close to a black hole, its enormous gravity will begin to pull in the star instantly. When black holes swallow up stars, powerful energy is created. The light from this energy can (C)[detect / be detected] from great distances with telescopes. The first photograph of a black hole was taken by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019. This was a major breakthrough and has had a huge impact on the scientific community.
위 담화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: is / that / be detected
are / that / be detected
is / what / be detected
is / that / detect
are / what / detect
solution:
(A) 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에 이어진 관계사절의 동사 자리이며, 선행사가 단수명사구 detect이므로 be동사 단수형인 is는 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(black holes are invisible)을 이끌어 be동사 is 뒤의 주격 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 주어 The light가 ‘감지되는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사구(from ~ telescopes)가 이어지고 있으므로 조동사 can 뒤에서 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 be detected가 적절하다.

body:
Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, curious about what lies beyond our world. This inherent desire ⓐto explore the universe has encouraged technological innovations that can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements ⓑare space telescopes and space robots, which have paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere ⓒinvisible. Consequently, the space ⓓwhere we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies ⓔlocated billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them ⓕstudying the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓓ where → that 또는 which (동사 see의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we ~ surface)을 이끌어 선행사 the space를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 where는 목적격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.)
*ⓓ는 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
ⓕ studying → to study (현재분사 enabling, 목적어 them에 이어져 ‘enable+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이므로, studying을 to부정사 to study로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ’탐험하려는 (이 타고난 욕망)‘이란 뜻으로 명사구 This inherent desire를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to explore는 적절하다.
ⓑ 강조를 위해 부사구 Among these advancements가 문장의 맨 앞에 위치하면서 동사와 주어가 도치되어 ’부사구+be동사+주어’의 어순으로 써야 한다. 뒤에 이어지는 주어인 명사구 space telescopes and space robots가 복수이므로 이에 수일치한 복수동사 are는 적절하다.
ⓒ 분사구문을 이루는 현재분사 making과 목적어 some objects beyond the atmosphere에 이어져 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’(~를 …하게 만들다)의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, make는 5형식 동사로 쓰일 때 목적격보어로 형용사를 취하므로 형용사 invisible은 적절하다.
ⓔ 명사구 stars, black holes, and galaxies를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, locate는 ‘위치하다, 위치시키다’라는 뜻의 타동사로 수식을 받는 대상인 수식을 받는 stars, black holes, and galaxies가 ‘위치한’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 located는 적절하다.

body:
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. ⓐOrbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in (A)facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and ⓑmade space exploration an even more intriguing journey.
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its (B)predecessor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to ⓒthat of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times (C)wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, ⓓwhich can pass through dusty regions more (D)effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly (E)enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected ⓔto offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ that → those (복수명사인 capabilities를 가리키므로 that은 복수형 대명사인 those로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(Hubble ~ space) 앞에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 Hubble이 ‘궤도를 그리며 도는’ 주체이며, orbit이 ‘궤도를 돌다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰였으므로 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 Orbiting은 적절하다.
ⓑ 현재완료를 이루는 과거분사 sparked와 등위접속사 and로 병렬구조를 이루고 있으므로 과거분사 made는 적절하다.
ⓓ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ Hubble)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 infrared light를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which는 적절하다.
ⓔ Webb을 가리키는 대명사 주어 it이 ‘기대되는’ 대상이며, ‘expect+O+O·C(to부정사)(~가 …할 것으로 기대하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘be expected+to부정사’를 이루는 is expected에 이어지는 to부정사 to offer는 적절하다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 알맞게 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오. (한 단어를 변형할 것)
<보기>
or even / come in / vehicles / humans / a range of / resemble / those of / shapes / spacecraft
→ Robots also ______.
answer: come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans
solution:
• 동사 자리에 ‘다양한 ~로 제공되다’라는 뜻을 나타내는 come in a range of를 쓴 다음, 전치사의 목적어 자리에 shapes를 쓴다.
• 완전한 절에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되어 있으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 Robots가 ‘닮은’ 주체이고 단어를 변형하라는 조건이 있으므로 동사 resemble(~와 닮다)을 능동의 의미인 현재분사 resembling으로 변형하여 쓴다.

body:
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle designed to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. ⓐ다양한 과학 장비를 갖춘 로버는 마치 움직이는 실험실과 같은 기능을 하면서 이동 중에 실험과 조사를 수행한다. An iconic example is Curiosity, which landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. These findings suggest the possibility that some form of life might (A)[have existed / exist] on Mars in the past.

Robonaut 2 was designed to assist astronauts in spacewalks and perform various tasks in dangerous environments. Despite their diversity, these robots share a common mission: to fearlessly venture into the unexplored territories of the universe.

As technology advances, we find ourselves closer to the secrets of the universe than ever before. The future of space exploration promises wonders beyond our imagination, and this fills us with great excitement.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: have existed / which / naming
exist / what / naming
have existed / which / named
exist / which / named
have existed / what / named
solution:
(A) 과거 시점을 나타내는 부사구 in the past가 있으므로 앞의 조동사 might와 함께 과거에 일어난 일에 대한 약한 추측을 나타내는 ‘조동사+have+p.p.’를 이루는 have existed가 적절하다.
(B) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(resemble ~ movement)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 humanoid robots를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
(C) 주어 A humanoid robot을 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리로, 수식을 받는 A humanoid robot은 ‘이름 지어진’ 대상이며 뒤에 ’name A B(A를 B라고 이름 짓다)‘의 5형식 구조에서 name의 목적어 없이 목적격보어에 해당하는 Robonaut 2가 이어지므로 수동 표현인 ’A be named B(A가 B라고 이름 지어지다)‘를 이루는 과거분사 named 적절하다.

body:
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, (A)[resulting / results] in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light (B)[used / using] by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it (C)[is expected / expects] to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: resulting / used / expects
results / using / expects
results / used / is expected
resulting / used / is expected
resulting / using / is expected
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(It ~ mirror)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용(Webb이 Hubble의 거울보다 지금이 약 3배 더 큰 벌집 무늬 거울을 특징으로 한다는 것)이 ‘초래하는’ 주체이고 result in은 ‘~을 초래하다, 야기하다’라는 뜻의 자동사적 동사구이므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 resulting이 적절하다.
(B) 명사구 the visible light를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리로, 수식을 받는 the visible light가 ‘사용되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 행위의 주체가 by Hubble의 형태로 제시되어 있으므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 used가 적절하다.
(C) Webb을 가리키는 대명사 주어 it이 ‘기대되는’ 대상이며, ‘expect+O+O·C(to부정사)(~가 …할 것으로 기대하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘be expected+to부정사’를 이루는 to부정사 to offer가 이어지고 있으므로 수동태인 is expected가 적절하다.

This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. (B)______, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.
윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: Nevertheless / Furthermore
As a result / That is
For example / In other words
Consequently / Moreover
For instance / Therefore
solution:
(A) 지구 대기는 자외선과 적외선과 같은 특정 유형의 빛을 흡수하여 관측을 왜곡하고 대기권 너머의 일부 천체를 보이지 않게 만든다는 내용 뒤에서 그 결과에 해당하는 내용인 이러한 대기의 영향으로 지구 표면에서 관찰하는 우주의 모습이 실제 모습과 상당히 달라질 수 있다는 내용이 제시되므로, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 인과간계를 연결하는 As a result(그 결과) 또는 Consequently(결과적으로)가 적절하다.
(B) Hubble 우주 망원경이 우주에 대한 인류의 이해를 넓히고 천체의 관계, 은하의 형성, 우주의 팽창에 관한 중요한 발견을 가능하게 했다는 점을 설명한 뒤, Hubble 망원경의 아름다운 이미지가 사람들의 상상력을 자극하고 우주 탐사를 더욱 흥미로운 여정으로 만들었다는 Hubble 망원경의 또 다른 긍정적인 기여를 덧붙이고 있으므로, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 추가적인 정보를 덧붙이는 연결어 Furthermore(게다가) 또는 Moreover(게다가)가 적절하다.
오답
① 그럼에도 불구하고 게다가
② 그 결과 다시 말해서
③ 예를 들어 다시 말해서
⑤ 예를 들어 그러므로

(A)______, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.

These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference.
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. (A) Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. (B) It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. (C) Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. (D) Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. (E) As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 특징들은 Webb이 크게 향상된 선명도와 최소한의 간섭으로 우주의 경관을 제공할 수 있게 한다.’라는 뜻으로, These features(이러한 특징들)가 쓰였으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 Webb이 더 선명하고 방해가 적은 우주 관측을 가능하게 하는 특징들이 언급되어야 한다. (C) 앞에서 언급된 Hubble보다 약 3배 큰 지름의 거울과 6.25배 넓은 이미지 수집 면적, (D) 앞에서 언급된 지구에서 150만 킬로미터 떨어진 곳에서 지구와 함께 태양을 공전하는 위치적 특징, (E) 앞에서 언급된 먼지가 많은 구역을 더 효과적으로 통과할 수 있는 적외선 포착 능력은 모두 우주를 더 선명하게, 관측을 방해하는 요소를 최소화하면서 볼 수 있게 하는 특징들이므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 이 세 가지 특징이 모두 제시된 뒤이자, 이러한 능력으로 인해 기대되는 결과를 설명하는 내용 앞인 (E)이다.

body:
Thorough space exploration goes beyond (A)[direct / remote] observations and includes up-close examinations of celestial bodies, material collection, and on-site experiments. While human astronauts can be sent on these missions, it is often safer and more cost-effective to use robots. Robots can better withstand the harsh conditions of space, including extreme temperatures and high radiation levels that can pose serious risks to human astronauts.
A variety of robots have been developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in (B)[movable / fixed] positions, while others are engineered for mobility. Robots also come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers launched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the presence of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, marking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes (C)[ended / continued] their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: remote / fixed / ended
direct / movable / ended
remote / fixed / continued
remote / movable / continued
direct / fixed / continued
solution:
(A) 우주 탐사는 천체에 직접 접근하여 자세히 조사하고, 물질을 수집하며, 현장에서 실험을 수행하는 활동까지 포함한다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 직접 접근하여 수행하는 탐사와 대비되는 관찰 방식을 나타내는 remote(원격의)가 적절하다.
direct 직접적인
(B) 다른 로봇들은 이동할 수 있도록 설계되었다는 내용과 역접을 나타내는 while(반면에)로 연결되어 있으므로, 이동하는 것과 대비되는 fixed(고정된)가 적절하다.
movable 움직일 수 있는
(C) 성간 우주에 진입하여 지구에서 가장 멀리 떨어진 인간이 만든 물체가 되었다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 여정을 계속 했다는 흐름을 이루는 continued(계속 했다)가 적절하다.
ended 끝냈다

body:
W: Take a look outside your window. Is it hot and sunny? Is it cloudy and rainy? Is there snow on the ground? When you look out the window, you’re seeing what the weather is like today. Weather is only temporary. For example, a heavy snow can turn into a flood after just a few warm spring days. Climate, on the other hand, is more than just a few warm or cool days. Climate describes the typical weather conditions in an entire region for a very long time, 30 years or more. Keeping an eye on changing weather can help us plan ahead. We know if black clouds are forming overhead, it’s probably a good idea to stay inside. But it’s important to keep an eye on changes in the earth’s climate, too.

다음 담화의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Weather tells us about temporary conditions, whereas climate shows the typical patterns of a region over a much longer period.
Since climate varies from region to region, we need to understand the climate characteristics of each region.
Weather patterns in a region can be predicted accurately by observing short-term changes in temperature.
Climate change occurs so slowly that it has very little impact on our daily lives.
We should take action to prevent global warming and extreme weather disasters.
solution: 창밖의 기온, 구름, 비, 눈 등을 통해 확인할 수 있는 날씨는 며칠 사이에도 달라질 수 있는 일시적인 현상인 반면, 기후는 30년 이상의 오랜 기간에 걸쳐 한 지역에서 전형적으로 나타나는 날씨 조건을 의미한다고 설명하므로 이 담화의 요지로 ❶ ‘날씨는 우리에게 일시적인 상태에 대해 알려 주는 반면, 기후는 훨씬 더 긴 기간에 걸친 한 지역의 전형적인 패턴을 보여 준다.’가 적절하다.

body:
Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people (A)[to track / track], adapt to, and even control the weather. Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer (B)[that / what] could measure temperature. The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us. The weather — or more broadly, the climate — (C)[has caused / causing] significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: to track / that / causing
track / what / has caused
to track / that / has caused
track / that / has caused
to track / what / causing
solution:
(A) 현재완료형 동사 have allowed의 목적격보어 자리로, allow는 5형식 구문(allow+목적어+목적격보어)으로 쓰일 때 to부정사를 목적격보어로 취하는 동사이므로, 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to track이 알맞다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(could ~ temperature)을 이끌어 명사구 a thermometer를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
(C) 주어 The weather와 대시(—)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 ‘or more broadly, the climate’에 이어지는 동사 자리이므로 has caused가 알맞으며 과거부터 현재까지 인류 역사 전반에 걸쳐 중대한 사건들을 초래해 왔음을 나타내고 있다.

body:
Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard ⓐto say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that ⓑremain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we ⓒwill be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears ⓓto be as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it ⓔlook like an enormous snowball.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ will be → would be
ⓓ to be → to have been

There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered ⓐthat humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed ⓑto evolve in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally ⓒinterrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period ⓓthat occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it ⓔhad not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not have spread outside of Africa.

body:
There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered ⓐthat humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed ⓑto evolve in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally ⓒinterrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period ⓓthat occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it ⓔhad not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not have spread outside of Africa.

the impact of human activities on the climate of eastern Africa
environmental adaptation during the early stages of human evolution
stable food and water supplies supporting human settlement in Africa
the contribution of climate shifts to the global spread of early humans

body:
Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how desperate things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

(A) At the height of their civilization, the Mayans achieved remarkable milestones in architecture, astronomy, and mathematics. (T/F)
(B) The practice of clearing and burning forests for farming helped reduce severe deforestation across the Yucatán Peninsula. (T/F)
(C) The Yucatán Peninsula mainly relied on rainfall for water, so underground root systems were essential to preserving its water resources. (T/F)
(D) Over a two-century span, researchers discovered that annual rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula was reduced to 70 percent of its previous level. (T/F)
(E) The collapse of the Mayan civilization appears to have been sparked by severe droughts alongside wars and other conflicts. (T/F)

다음 글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
choices: T-F-T-T-F
T-F-T-F-T
F-F-T-F-T
T-F-F-F-T
F-T-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-F-T이다.
(A) 자신들의 문명이 절정에 달했을 때, 마야인들은 건축, 천문학, 수학에서 놀라운 성과를 이루었다. (일치)
at the height of ~ ~이 절정에 있는[달했을 때]
(B) 농사를 짓기 위해 숲을 개간하고 불태우는 관행은 유카탄반도 전역의 심각한 삼림 벌채를 줄이는 데 도움이 되었다(→가져왔다). (불일치)
(C) 유카탄반도는 주로 강수에 수자원을 의존했으며, 지하 근계는 이 지역의 수자원을 보존하는 데 필수적이었다. (일치)
(D) 2세기에 걸친 기간 동안, 연구자들은 유카탄반도의 연간 강수량이 이전 수준의 70퍼센트로(→70%만큼이나) 감소했다는 것을 발견했다. (불일치)

solution:

(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(may ~ time)을 이끌어 명사구 a rare phenomenon을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
(C) 관계사절(under which ~ form)의 수식을 받는 주어 the circumstances에 이어지는 동사 자리이므로 match가 적절하다.

body:
Fog Saves the American Revolution
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally undetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. (A)역사가들은, 그 안개가 없었다면, Washington은 분명히 붙잡혀서 영국 정부에 의해 반역자로 처벌됐을 것이라는 데 대체로 동의한다. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 가정법을 사용하되 접속사를 생략할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
for, that fog, it, punish, widely agree, as, capture, a traitor, will, historians
→ ______ ______ ______ ______ Washington ______ ______ surely ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ by the British government, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog.
solution:
• 주어 Historians를 쓰고 ‘대체로 동의한다’를 뜻하도록 부사 widely와 동사 agree를 쓴다. 동사 agree의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• ‘~가 없었다면 …했을 것이다’의 의미로, 과거 사실을 반대 상황을 가정하고 있으므로 가정법 과거완료 'if it had not been for ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+have+p.p.'의 구조로 쓰되, 주절의 주어 Washington으로 시작하고 있으므로 뒤에 조동사 will의 과거형 would를 쓰고 Washington이 ‘붙잡혀 처벌되는’ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 have (surely) been captured와 접속사 and 뒤에 have been을 생략한 과거분사 punished를 쓴다. ‘반역자로서’를 뜻하도록 ’~로서‘ 뜻하는 전치사 as와 명사구 a traitor를 이어 쓴다.
• ’(만약) ~가 없었다면’을 뜻하는 가정법 과거완료 구문 ’if it had not been for ~’를 사용하되 <조건>에 따라 접속사 if를 생략해야 하며, if가 생략되면 주어와 동사가 도치되므로 주어 it과 조동사 had을 도치한 had it not been for를 쓰고 that fog를 이어 쓴다.

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways to influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
There have been two main approaches aimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth. On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface brighter by painting the roof tops white or even adding highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere more reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it reaches the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would be fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or breaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials. (A)______, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to fertilize ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while taking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ emitted into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and isolate CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. (B)______, some believe that we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: In addition / In fact
For instance / In other words
Moreover / Nevertheless
For example / Still
Therefore / That is
solution:
(A) 앞에서 대기 중 이산화탄소를 포집하여 지하에 저장하거나 안정적인 물질에 탄소를 가두는 접근법을 설명하고, 뒤에서는 철가루를 바다에 뿌려 식물성 플랑크톤의 성장을 촉진함으로써 대기 중 이산화탄소를 줄이는 구체적인 방법을 제시하므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 For instance(예를 들어), For example(예를 들어)가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에서 탄소 포집 기술이 전 세계 배출량을 기껏해야 10%까지 줄이는 데 그칠 수 있다는 한계를 제시한 뒤, 뒤에서 이러한 한계에도 불구하고 기후 변화를 늦추기 위해 여러 해결책을 함께 추진해야 한다는 견해를 언급하므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고), Still(그럼에도 불구하고)이 적절하다.
