A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists ______, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.

Were it not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.

Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. body:
Fog (A)[Saves / Dooms] the American Revolution
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally (B)[detected / undetected] by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in (C)[defeat / victory] for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: Dooms / undetected / defeat
Saves / detected / victory
Dooms / detected / defeat
Saves / undetected / victory
Saves / undetected / defeat
solution:
(A) 안개 덕분에 혁명군이 영국군의 공격에서 벗어나 Washington 장군이 포로로 잡히는 것을 피할 수 있었으며 결국 미국을 독립적인 국가로 만들었으므로, 미국 혁명을 구했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 Saves(구하다)가 적절하다.
(B) 혁명군이 안개 덕분에 몇백 미터 떨어진 곳의 영국군에게 발각되지 않은 채 이스트강을 건넜다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 undetected(발각되지 않은)가 적절하다.
(C) 뒤에서 미국을 독립적인 국가로 만들었다고 했으므로 미국 혁명이 신생 식민지들의 승리로 끝났다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 victory(승리)가 적절하다.

On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy ⓐnamed Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. Feeling that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, noticing his mother’s concern, ⓑsmiling at her and continued following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, ⓒimagining what it might hold.
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he had made his mother ⓓthink that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided it would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they ⓔhave always done, but he did not.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 골라 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
기호 알맞게 고친 표현
(1) ______ : ______
(2) ______ : ______
solution:
ⓑ 주어 The boy에 이어지는 동사 자리로, 뒤의 과거형 동사 continued와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 smiling을 과거형 동사 smiled로 고친다.
ⓔ Jerry가 느꼈던 과거시점(felt)보다 더 이전에 항상 해 오던 일을 나타내므로 have always done을 과거완료 had always done으로 고친다.
오답
ⓐ 명사구 a young English boy를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a young English boy가 Jerry라고 이름 ‘지어진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 named는 적절하다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(He ~ bay)에 콤마로 이어지며, ‘~하면서’의 의미를 갖는 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문의 분사 자리로 의미상주어 He가 ‘상상하는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 imagining이 적절하다.
ⓓ 과거완료 had made의 make는 사역동사로 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/p.p.)’의 구조로 쓰이며, 목적어 his mother가 ‘생각하는’ 주체이므로 목적격보어로 능동 관계를 나타내는 동사원형 think가 쓰인 것은 적절하다.

Back home that evening, Jerry asked his mother for swimming goggles. After receiving them the next day, he ran off back to the bay. Underwater, he was now able to see the tunnel clearly. He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin frightened him. He gave up and decided to practice holding his breath underwater instead.
From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks to practice his breathing and diving. Some days, he pushed himself too hard, and his nose would bleed from too much practice. His mother told him that she was worried about him and had him join her at their usual beach. But the beach looked different to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.
Jerry soon began to feel restless being back at the beach with his mother, and (A)그가 쏟았던 모든 연습이 쓸모없게 될까 걱정했다. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and practicing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. He knew that being prepared would help him conquer the tunnel that had defeated him.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 관계대명사를 생략할 것
• 과거완료를 사용할 것

• 14단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
put in, will, the practice, worry, go to, waste, all
→ ______
answer: he worried that all the practice he had put in would go to waste
solution:
• 주어 he, 동사 worried를 쓰고 worried의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작해야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• that절의 주어 all the practice를 쓰고 all the practice를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계대명사를 써야 하나, <조건>에 따라 생략한다.
• 연습에 노력을 쏟은 일이 걱정한 시점보다 먼저 발생했으므로 과거완료형 had put in을 써서 목적어가 생략된 불완전한 절을 완성한다.
• 주어 all the practice에 이어지는 동사 자리에 주절에 시제를 일치시켜 과거형 조동사 would와 ’쓸모없게 되다’를 뜻하는 ’go to waste‘를 차례대로 쓴다.

He soon found the entrance to the tunnel. He took the edges of the hole in his hands and drew himself into it. It was pitch black, but he kept counting, just as he had practiced. Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two… Soon he reached a hundred, a hundred and one… He kept moving through the tunnel, and when he thought he couldn’t last any longer, he spotted a crack of light at the end. The feeling of victory filled him as he realized that with a few more strokes, he would be coming out the other side. He felt like he was running out of air, but he kept kicking and thinking just a little bit more!

But the beach looked different to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.
Jerry soon began to feel restless being back at the beach with his mother, and he worried that ______. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and practicing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. He knew that being prepared would help him conquer the tunnel that had defeated him.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: his mother would forbid him from swimming
the local boys would forget about him entirely
he might injure himself without proper equipment
his dedicated effort would end up being meaningless
he would miss the opportunity to spend more time with his mother
solution:
Jerry는 굴에 들어가는 데 실패한 뒤 매일 아침 바위투성이의 만에서 숨 참기와 다이빙을 연습했으며, 때로는 코피가 날 정도로 무리하기도 했다. 그러나 어머니와 평소 가던 해변에 머물게 되자 안절부절못하기 시작했고, 결국 다시 바위투성이의 만으로 돌아가 굴 탐험과 숨 참기 연습을 다시 이어서 했으며, 그는 준비가 되어 있어야 자신을 좌절하게 했던 굴을 정복하는 데 도움이 되리라는 것을 알고 있다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 그동안 자신이 쏟아부은 연습과 노력이 무용지물이 될까 봐 걱정했다는 흐름이 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ④ ‘그의 헌신적인 노력이 결국 아무 의미가 없게 될 것이다’가 적절하다.
본문변형 all the practice he had put in would go to waste → his dedicated effort would end up being meaningless

① 어머니가 그가 수영하는 것을 금지할 것이다
② 현지 소년들이 그를 완전히 잊을 것이다
③ 적절한 장비 없이는 그가 다칠 수도 있다
⑤ 어머니와 더 많은 시간을 보낼 기회를 놓칠 것이다

After a few days, his mother told him (A)[what / that] they would soon need to return home. This news urged him (B)[going / to go] back to the bay. He felt that he absolutely needed to go through the tunnel before they went home. ⓐ하지만 그의 두려움은 그저 연습을 좀 더 하고 내년에 다시 시도하는 것이 더 현명할지도 모른다고 생각하게 만들었다.
But even after reaching that conclusion, he found himself (C)[sit / sitting] on the rock with a longing to overcome his fear and conquer the tunnel. It would be now or never. He decided to try once more. His hands were shaking, but he placed them firmly at his sides. He looked up at the sky, filled his lungs with air, and then sank fast into the ocean.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: that / to go / sitting
what / going / sitting
that / to go / sit
what / to go / sit
that / going / sitting
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(they ~ home)을 이끌어 동사 told의 직접목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
(B) urged의 목적격보어 자리이며, 동사 urged는 ‘urge+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 to부정사 to go가 적절하다.
(C) found의 목적격보어 자리로, 동사 found는 ‘find+목적어+목적격보어(분사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰여 ‘~하는 …를 발견하다’의 의미를 가지며, 목적어 himself가 ‘앉는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 sitting이 적절하다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 동명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것

→ His fear, however, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: made him think that just practicing some more and trying again next year might be wiser
solution:
• 주어 His fear에 이어지는 동사 made를 쓰고, 사역동사 made는 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)’로 쓰이므로 목적어 him과 동사원형 think를 차례대로 쓴다.

• ‘~할지도 모른다’를 뜻하는 조동사 might와 be동사의 원형 be를 쓰고, ’더 현명한‘을 뜻하도록 형용사 wise를 비교급 wiser로 변형하여 이어 쓴다.

body:
Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried diving with them, but he was too afraid. Noticing his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.

다음 글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Being far from his mother made Jerry feel a little lonely shortly after he began swimming at the rocky bay. (T/F)
(B) While diving into the deep water from the rocks, Jerry came across a group of local boys around his age. (T/F)
(C) As Jerry swam closer, the boys ignored him and swam away before he could even reach them. (T/F)
(D) The boys lost interest in Jerry when they realized that he was too frightened to dive with them. (T/F)
(E) Jerry attempted to get their attention by shouting a few words in their language, but they paid no attention and swam away. (T/F)
choices: T-F-T-T-F
F-T-T-F-T
T-F-F-T-F
T-F-F-F-T
T-F-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-F-T-T이다.
(A) Jerry가 바위투성이 만에서 수영을 시작한 직후, 어머니에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다는 것은 조금 외롭게 느껴졌다. (일치)
(B) 바위에서 깊은 물속으로 다이빙하는 동안(→바위투성이 만에서 수영하는 동안), Jerry는 자신과 나이가 비슷한 한 무리의 현지 소년들을 우연히 만났다. (불일치)
(C) Jerry가 더 가까이 헤엄쳐 갔을 때, 소년들은 그를 무시하고 그가 그들에게 도착하기도 전에 헤엄쳐 가 버렸다(→그들은 그를 보려고 돌아섰고 한 명이 미소 지으며 그에게 손을 흔들었다). (불일치)
(D) 소년들은 Jerry가 너무 두려워 그들과 함께 다이빙을 할 수 없다는 것을 알아차렸을 때 Jerry에게 관심을 잃었다. (일치)
(E) Jerry는 그들의 언어로 몇 마디 외쳐 그들의 관심을 끌려고 했지만, 그들은 아무런 주의를 기울이지 않고 헤엄쳐 가 버렸다. (일치)

body:
Feeling rejected, Jerry watched the boys from a distance and noticed that they were underwater for a long time. He started counting the seconds. At fifty, he started to worry. At one hundred, he wondered whether he should yell for (A)help. But around one hundred and fifty, he realized that they were in fact swimming through some rocks in the water and ⓐcome out the other side. After they left, he tried to do what they ⓑhave done, but when he tried to open his eyes to see underwater, his eyes stung from the salty water. With his eyes closed, however, he was unable to see the tunnel that the boys had swum through. His only option was ⓒto give up and go home.
Back home that evening, Jerry asked his mother for swimming goggles. After ⓓreceiving them the next day, he ran off back to the bay. Underwater, he was now able to see the tunnel (B)clearly. He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin (C)frightened him. He gave up and decided to practice holding his breath underwater instead.
From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks to practice his breathing and diving. Some days, he pushed himself too hard, and his nose ⓔwould bleed from too much practice. His mother told him that she was (D)worried about him and had him join her at their usual beach. But the beach looked (E)the same to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓐ come → coming (‘헤엄쳐서 통과해 반대편으로 나오고 있다’라는 뜻으로 be동사 were와 함께 과거진행형을 이루는 현재분사 swimming과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 come을 현재분사 coming으로 고친다.)
ⓑ have done → had done (Jerry가 노력한 과거 시점(tried)보다 소년들이 했던 것이 먼저 발생한 일이므로 have done을 과거완료 had done으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ be동사 was에 이어지는 보어 자리이며 등위접속사 and 뒤에 동사원형 go와 병렬로 연결되므로 to부정사구 to give up은 적절하다. 동사원형 go는 앞에 to가 생략되었다.
ⓓ 전치사 After에 이어지는 목적어 자리이며 뒤에 대명사 them이 있으므로 목적어를 취할 수 있는 동명사 receiving은 적절하다.
ⓔ 과거에 종종 있었던 일(코피가 나기도 했다)을 나타내므로 ‘~하곤 했다’를 뜻하는 조동사 would는 적절하다.

body:
On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy named Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. Feeling that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, (A)[noticing / ignoring] his mother’s concern, smiled at her and continued following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, imagining what it might hold.
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he had made his mother think that he was (B)[bored / content] with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat (C)[accessible / dangerous], but she decided it would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they had always done, but he did not.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: ignoring / content / dangerous
noticing / bored / dangerous
noticing / content / accessible
ignoring / bored / dangerous
noticing / bored / accessible
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 Jerry는 어머니를 향해 미소를 지으며 계속 따라갔지만, 어깨 너머로 계속 거친 만을 흘낏 보며 그곳에 무엇이 있을지 상상했다고 했으므로, 자신의 관심이 다른 곳에 쏠려 있다는 것을 어머니가 걱정하고 있음을 알아차렸음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 noticing(알아차리는)이 적절하다.
ignore ~을 무시하다
(B) 첫 번째 단락에서 Jerry의 시선이 평소 가던 해변이 아닌 다른 곳을 향하자 어머니가 이를 걱정했고, 두 번째 단락의 첫 문장에서 어머니가 다른 해변에 가 보고 싶은지 물었으므로, Jerry는 자신이 평소 가던 해변에 싫증을 느낀다고 어머니가 생각하게 만든 것을 후회했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 bored(지루한)가 적절하다.
content 만족한
(C) 접속사 but(그러나)으로 대조되어 연결되는 다음 절에서 그를 혼자 가게 해도 괜찮을 것이라고 판단했다고 했으므로 앞에서는 그가 가리킨 장소가 다소 위험해 보였다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 dangerous(위험한)가 적절하다.
accessible 접근할 수 있는

choices: Balancing Personal Ambition with Caution and Safety
How Changing Environments Influence Children’s Choices and Activities
Why Postponing Difficult Decisions Can Lead to Better Long-Term Outcomes
From Persistent Effort and Practice to a Decisive Act of Courage against Fear

body:
He soon found the entrance to the tunnel. He took the edges of the hole in his hands and drew himself into it. It was pitch black, but he kept counting, just as he had practiced. Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two… Soon he reached a hundred, a hundred and one… He kept moving through the tunnel, and when he thought he couldn’t last any longer, he spotted a crack of light at the end. The feeling of victory filled him as he realized that with a few more strokes, he would be coming out the other side. He felt like he was running out of air, but he kept kicking and thinking just a little bit more!
Finally, his hands found the exit of the tunnel, and he swam out into the open sea. At first, he started to gasp like a fish out of water, but after some time, his heart quieted and his eyes cleared. He had made it. After resting a short while on the warm rock, he got on his feet and walked back home. His mother’s eyes lit up, as she was happy to see him back. “Did you have a nice morning?” she asked. Jerry replied with pride, “Mom, I can stay underwater for two minutes, three minutes, at least!” His mom thought about telling him to rest for the remainder of the day, but she didn’t have to. He was now happy to stay home and rest. Going to the bay was no longer important to him.

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What did Jerry see when he thought he could not continue any longer?
How did Jerry feel when he found the end of the tunnel?
What did Jerry do after he swam out into the open sea?
What did Jerry tell his mother when he returned home?
Why did Jerry’s mother consider telling him to rest for the remainder of the day?
solution:

body:
B: Cathy, what are you looking at?
G: I’m looking at the painting, Space Opera Theatre.
B: Can I see?
G: Sure. Here you go. It won first place in an art competition.
B: Wow, it looks so aesthetically ⓐ[pleasing / pleased]! Who is the painter with such talent?
G: Actually, it was painted by using an AI art generator.
B: What is an AI art generator exactly?
G: It’s an artificial intelligence program ⓑ[that / what] produces digital images.
B: Unbelievable! How can it do that?
G: When a person provides a written text, the AI software converts it into images. Then they are printed on canvas.
B: This is so fascinating! I’ve never imagined AI ⓒ[using / being used] in the field of art!

위 대화의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: pleasing / what / using
pleased / that / being used
pleasing / that / using
pleased / what / being used
pleasing / that / being used
solution:
ⓐ 2형식 동사로 쓰인 looks의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 올 자리이며, the painting, Space Opera Theatre를 가리키는 주어 it이 ‘즐거움을 주는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 형태의 형용사 pleasing이 알맞다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(produces digital images)을 이끌고 있으며 앞에 선행사인 명사구 an artificial intelligence program이 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
ⓒ imagined의 목적어인 동명사(구)를 이루는 자리로, 앞에 목적격 형태로 쓰인 동명사의 의미상 주어 AI가 ‘사용되는’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동형 동명사(being+p.p.)인 being used가 알맞다.

body:
Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies ⓐdescribing in films are now a reality. One of them ⓑis self-driving cars. In Total Recall, for example, the taxi driver is the vehicle’s computer system. The taxi is capable of driving ⓒitself without any human intervention. ⓓHaving seen that movie, many people wanted self-driving cars. Luckily, self-driving cars are being developed and certain versions are already on the road. Additionally, many other AI technologies from movies are ⓔeither in use or under development.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: 수식받는 앞의 명사구와 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 described로 고쳐야 한다.
ⓑ: One of 뒤의 복수대명사 them에 수일치 시킨 복수동사 are로 고쳐야 한다.
ⓒ: 동명사 driving의 의미상 주어인 the taxi와 목적어가 같은 대상이므로 재귀 용법의 재귀대명사 itself는 알맞다.
ⓓ: 주절 동사(wanted)가 나타내는 과거시점 이전에 일어난 일이므로 완료형 분사구문(Having+p.p.~)을 이루는 Having seen은 알맞다.
ⓔ: 상관접속사 ‘either A or B(A이거나 B인)’에 의해 두 개의 전치사구(in use, under development)가 병렬연결을 이룬 것은 알맞다.
solution: ‘One of+복수명사(구)’ 형태가 주어인 경우 이어지는 동사는 핵심주어인 One에 수일치 시킨 단수동사를 쓰므로, 주어 One of them 뒤에 One에 수일치한 단수동사 is가 쓰인 것은 알맞다.

body:
2001: A Space Odyssey
This movie, set in 2001, realistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that (A)human imagination goes far beyond reality. In the movie, the ship has a computer system, called “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance to understand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts conduct experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft. Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw logical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. (B)그 당시에 영화에서만 보였던 우주선의 AI 도우미가 현실이 되었습니다. In 2008, the International Space Station, a large spacecraft orbiting Earth, started to use an AI robot named CIMON. It is a floating spherical robot that can move around inside the spacecraft. CIMON, weighing only 5 kg, serves as a competent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when asked.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)human imagination goes far beyond reality가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Human technology always develops faster than scientific imagination.
Artificial intelligence was already fully operational in space long before 1968.
Space exploration relies heavily on historical events rather than futuristic visions.
Realistic movies prevent scientists from introducing innovative ideas into space programs.
Creative ideas and fiction can anticipate real-world developments long before they occur.
solution:
다른 행성으로 향하는 우주선 속 과학자들의 집단을 사실적으로 묘사한 영화 <2001: A Space Odyssey>는 최초의 달 착륙보다 1년 앞선 1968년에 개봉되었으며, 당시 영화에서만 볼 수 있었던 우주선의 AI 도우미가 이후 국제우주정거장의 AI 로봇 CIMON으로 현실이 되었다고 했으므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘인간의 상상력이 현실을 훨씬 넘어선다’는 인간의 창의적 아이디어와 상상력이 미래의 세계를 예견할 수 있음을 뜻한다고 볼 수 있다. 따라서 (A)가 의미하는 바로 ⑤ ‘창의적인 아이디어와 허구는 현실 세계의 발전이 일어나기 훨씬 전에 그것을 예견할 수 있다.’가 알맞다.
오답
① 인간의 기술은 항상 과학적 상상력보다 더 빠르게 발전한다.
② 인공지능은 1968년 훨씬 이전에 이미 우주에서 완전히 작동하고 있었다.
③ 우주 탐사는 미래지향적 비전보다 역사적 사건에 크게 의존한다.
④ 사실적인 영화는 과학자들이 우주 프로그램에 혁신적인 아이디어를 도입하는 것을 방지한다.

This movie, set in 2001, realistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft. Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when asked.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 계속적 용법의 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• 현재완료를 한 번 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
the film, become, a reality, only see
→ The AI helper for a spaceship, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ at the time, ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: which was only seen in the film, has become a reality
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 계속적 용법의 관계대명사를 사용하여 주어 The AI helper for a spaceship을 부연 설명하는 관계사절이 주어와 동사 사이에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입된 형태가 되도록 한다. 먼저 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which를 쓴 후, 선행사인 주어가 부사구 at the time(그 당시에)이 나타내는 과거 시점에 ‘보였던’ 대상이므로 과거시제 수동태(was/were+p.p.)를 사용해 선행사의 핵심인 단수명사구 The AI helper에 수일치한 과거형 be동사 was를 쓴 후, only see를 only seen으로 변형한다. 이어서 부사구 in the film을 쓴다.
• 콤마(,) 뒤 문장의 동사 자리에 <조건>에 따라 현재완료(have/has+p.p.)를 사용하여 주어의 핵심인 단수명사구 The AI helper에 수일치한 단수형 조동사 has를 쓴 뒤, become의 과거분사형인 become을 쓰고, 보어인 명사구 a reality를 써서 완성한다.

body:
Minority Report
Minority Report, ⓐa film setting in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes.
(A) However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. On the other hand, ⓑdevices employ AI have overcome this limitation. They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now.
(B) For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems ⓒprovide us with advertisements based on our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices ⓓhave already been developed.
(C) There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After ⓔscanning him and identifying who is he, the advertising system offers products that may be appealing to him. Nowadays, we frequently encounter ⓕpersonalized advertisements provided by AI.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ setting → set (주어 Minority Report와 동사구 was released 사이에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 주어와 동격을 이루는 명사구가 ‘명사구+분사구’ 형태로 올 수 있으나, 명사구 a film이 ‘설정된’ 대상이므로 수동 표현인 ‘be set in ~ ((특정 장소·시대 등)을 배경으로 하다)’의 과거분사 set 뒤에 전치사구(in ~ 2050)가 이어져 분사구를 이루도록 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 setting을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 set으로 고친다.)
ⓑ employ → employing 또는 which[that] employ (주어 devices 뒤에 접속사 없이 두 개의 동사구가 연달아 쓰일 수 없으므로, 주어 devices와 동사구 have overcome 사이에 주어를 수식하는 분사구나 관계사절이 온 구조가 되어야 한다. 수식받는 devices가 ‘활용하는’ 주체이므로 employ를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 employing으로 고치거나, 적절한 주격 관계대명사 which[that]를 추가하고 선행사가 되는 복수명사 devices에 수일치한 복수동사 employ를 사용해 which[that] employ로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 employing이 쓰였음
ⓔ is he → he is (전치사 After의 목적어로 동명사 scanning과 identifying이 이끄는 두 개의 동명사구가 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 것은 알맞으나, identifying의 목적어 자리에 의문사 who가 이끄는 명사절이 의문사 뒤 평서문의 간접의문문 어순으로 와야 하므로, ‘be동사+주어’가 아닌 ‘주어+be동사’의 순서가 되도록 is he를 he is로 고친다.)
오답
ⓕ 타동사 encounter의 목적어로 명사구 personalized advertisements가 쓰인 것과, 앞의 명사구가 AI에 의해 ‘제공되는’ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 provided 뒤에 ’by+명사‘ 형태의 by AI가 이어져 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 과거분사구를 이룬 것은 모두 알맞다.

body:
Minority Report
Minority Report, ⓐa film setting in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes.
(A) However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. On the other hand, ⓑdevices employ AI have overcome this limitation. They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now.
(B) For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems ⓒprovide us with advertisements based on our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices ⓓhave already been developed.
(C) There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After ⓔscanning him and identifying who is he, the advertising system offers products that may be appealing to him. Nowadays, we frequently encounter ⓕpersonalized advertisements provided by AI.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 영화 <Minority Report>에 사람의 눈을 스캔해 개인을 식별하는 AI 기반 광고가 등장한다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 주인공이 쇼핑몰에 들어가는 장면을 구체적으로 묘사한 뒤 오늘날 우리가 AI가 제공하는 개인 맞춤형 광고를 자주 접한다고 하는 (C), For instance(예를 들어)를 사용해 온라인 쇼핑몰, 영상 공유 플랫폼, 소셜 미디어의 AI 시스템이 이전 검색이나 온라인 활동을 바탕으로 광고를 제공하는 예를 들고 눈을 스캔해 사람을 식별하는 장치가 이미 개발되었다고 설명하는 (B), However(그러나) 뒤에 앞서 언급한 devices를 those로 가리켜 AI 기술을 사용하지 않는 장치들의 치명적인 한계를 제시한 뒤 AI를 사용하는 장치들은 그 한계를 극복했다고 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
These days, AI-based programs or robots are widely used in the medical industry. Some AI programs have been refined to the point that they can not only identify cancer quickly and accurately, but also predict the chance of getting cancer. AI robots are also used in operating rooms. Based on the collected data, AI surgical robots can conduct cognitive activities such as voice recognition, decision-making, problem-solving, and more. Under the guidance and control of doctors, they can conduct elementary operations such as cutting and stitching patients undergoing surgery. Another example is the development of an AI system to ______. It analyzes the patient’s profile and data and assigns scores indicating the need for transfer to an intensive care unit. The medical team intervenes when a patient’s scores reach a certain level.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: reduce the overall cost of surgical procedures in hospitals
replace human doctors completely in intensive care units
anticipate when a hospitalized patient’s health may decline
schedule routine checkups for patients who have been discharged
automatically prescribe medication without a doctor’s approval
solution:
AI 시스템이 환자의 프로필과 데이터를 분석하여 집중 치료실로의 이송 필요성을 나타내는 점수를 부여하고, 점수가 일정 수준에 도달하면 의료진이 개입한다고 했으므로, 입원 환자의 상태가 악화될 시점을 예측하는 AI 시스템을 소개하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ③ ‘입원 환자의 건강이 언제 악화될 수 있는지를 예상하다’가 알맞다.
본문변형
forecast when a hospitalized patient’s condition is likely to get worse → anticipate a potential decline in a hospitalized patient’s health

② 중환자실에서 인간 의사를 완전히 대체하다
④ 퇴원한 환자에 대한 정기 검진 일정을 잡다
⑤ 의사의 승인 없이 약을 자동으로 처방하다

body:
The film production industry extensively utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also ⓐ[enables / enabling] them to make what they intended to express come alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, through which actors’ faces on the screen are aged or made younger. For example, when provided with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program accelerates the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained ⓑ[to learn / learning] how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly realistic. These results are maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to (A)______, it is expected ⓒ[that / what] this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: enables / to learn / what
enabling / to learn / what
enables / to learn / that
enabling / learning / that
enables / learning / that
solution:
ⓐ 상관접속사 ‘not only A, but also B(A뿐만 아니라, B도)’에 의해 주어 it에 대한 현재형 단수동사 assists와 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, 현재형 단수동사 enables가 알맞다.
ⓑ 동사 train은 ‘train+목적어+to부정사(~을 …하도록 훈련하다)’의 형태로 쓰이며 수동 표현은 ‘~ be trained+to부정사(~가 …하도록 훈련받다)’로 나타내므로, 수동태가 쓰인 동사구 was then trained 뒤에 to부정사인 to learn이 알맞다.
ⓒ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리에서 완전한 절(this ~ filmmaking)을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.

This is a science fiction animation that was released in 2014. There is a scene in the movie ⓐwhich a boy meets Baymax, a personal medical aid AI robot. The robot scans the boy’s body to detect (A)potential health problems using its sensors and cameras. ⓑThat it discovers within seconds is a wound in his arm. It administers medicine on the wound. Some AI programs have been (C)refined to the point ⓒthat they can not only identify cancer quickly and accurately, but also predict the chance of getting cancer. Under the guidance and control of doctors, they can conduct elementary operations ⓔsuch as cutting and stitching patients undergone surgery. Another example is the development of an AI system ⓕto forecast when a hospitalized patient’s condition is likely to get worse. What AI technology from a movie do you think will be used in our lives in the future?

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ which → where 또는 in which (관계대명사 which가 완전한 절(a boy ~ robot)을 이끌 수 없으므로, 관계사절이 수식하는 선행사 a scene에 어울리는 관계부사 where 또는 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태의 in which로 고친다. 그 외, Baymax와 동격 관계를 이루는 명사구 a personal medical aid AI robot이 동격의 콤마(,)로 연결된 것은 알맞다.)
*원래 지문에는 where가 쓰였음
ⓑ That → What (완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 That 뒤에 타동사 discovers의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(it discovers within seconds)이 이어질 수 없으며, 흐름상 보어인 a wound in his arm을 강조하는 ‘What+주어+동사~+be동사 … (~한 것은 바로 …이다)’ 형태의 강조 구문을 이루어야 하므로, That을 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 명사절을 이끌 수 있는 관계대명사 What으로 고친다. 그 외, 앞 문장의 단수명사구 The robot을 가리키는 단수 지시대명사 it이 관계사절의 주어로 쓰인 것과, 관계대명사 what이 의미상 목적어 역할을 하므로 단수동사로 수일치한 능동태 discovers가 뒤에 목적어 없이 쓰인 것은 모두 알맞다.)
ⓔ undergone → undergoing (such as(~와 같은)의 목적어 자리에 두 개의 동명사 cutting과 stitching이 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되고 뒤에 공통의 목적어 patients가 이어진 것은 알맞으며, 명사 patients를 수식하는 분사구가 뒤에 이어질 수 있으나, 수식받는 명사 patients가 타동사 undergo(~을 받다)의 주체이고 명사 surgery가 목적어에 해당하므로, 과거분사 undergone을 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 undergoing으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 선행사에 point가 있을 때 관계부사 where 대신 관계부사 대용의 that이 흔히 쓰이므로, 관계부사 대용의 that이 완전한 절(they ~ accurately)을 이끌어 선행사 the point를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 것은 알맞다. 복수명사구 Some AI programs를 가리키는 복수 대명사 they가 관계사절의 주어로 쓰이고, 조동사 can 뒤에 ’not only A, but also B(A뿐만 아니라, B도)‘ 형태의 상관접속사를 이루는 not only와 동사원형 identify가 쓰인 것과, 목적어 cancer 뒤에 동사를 수식하는 두 개의 부사 quickly와 accurately가 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 있는 것 또한 모두 알맞다.

choices: frequently / based on / development
hardly / based on / development
frequently / based on / criticism
hardly / regardless of / development
frequently / regardless of / criticism

It is certain that AI will continue to play a significant role in more and more aspects of our lives. Accordingly, these days, a lot of movies feature various kinds of AI. body:
When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!”
“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”
“Zambezi?”
“It’s the name we gave the little elephant.”
So the elephant was ⓐalive! Aaron beamed, his heart beating faster. Samuel motioned for him to follow. Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, covered by blankets. He seemed to be having trouble ⓑto breathe. The image of his father, lying under blankets at home just before he died, flashed through Aaron’s mind, and (A)______.
Samuel nudged him forward. Aaron knelt and, with shaking hands, ⓒreached out to touch Zambezi’s thick skin. It felt surprisingly warm. Zambezi opened one eye. Slowly, his trunk curled upward and brushed Aaron’s arm.
“How are you?” Aaron whispered.
He sat down on the straw, and the elephant rested his trunk on Aaron’s leg. They stayed like that for some time, while Samuel watched them curiously.
“Here,” Samuel whispered, ⓓhanding a milk bottle to Aaron. “Maybe you will have better luck than we’ve had.”
Aaron had seen enough babies ⓔto nurse to know what to do. He tilted the bottle, spilling some drops onto the elephant’s lip. Zambezi licked the milk off his lip and then began to suck from the bottle, ⓕlooked Aaron in the eyes as he did. Samuel shook his head in amazement. Aaron’s mind rushed back to the day he first met the elephant.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓑ to breathe → breathing (have trouble+-ing(~하는데 어려움을 겪다)의 표현으로 to breathe를 breathing으로 고친다.)
ⓔ to nurse → nurse 또는 nursing (과거완료 had seen과 목적어 enough babies에 이어져 ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 보다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 지각동사의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형, 능동·진행일 때는 현재분사, 수동일 때는 과거분사가 쓰인다. 목적어 enough babies가 ‘젖을 먹는’ 주체이고, 동사 nurse가 ‘젖을 먹다’는 자동사로 쓰였으므로 to nurse를 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 nurse 또는 능동·진행의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 nursing으로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 nurse가 쓰였음
ⓕ looked → looking (완전한 절(Zambezi licked the milk off his lip and then began to suck from the bottle)에 접속사 없이 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 부대상황(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상의 주어 Zambezi가 ‘쳐다보는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사 Aaron이 이어지므로, looked를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 looking으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 2형식 동사 was의 보어로 형용사가 올 자리이므로, ‘살아있는’의 의미를 나타내는 형용사 alive는 알맞다.
ⓒ 등위접속사 and에 의해, 과거동사 knelt와 병렬 구조를 이루고 있으므로, 과거동사 reached는 알맞다.
ⓓ 완전한 절에 이어지는 분사구문으로 주절의 주어 Samuel이 ‘건네는’ 주체이므로, 능동 관계를 나타내는 현재분사 handing은 알맞다.

ⓕ lain → lying (동사(watched)가 있는 완전한 절(He watched the elephant)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 the elephant를 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상의 주어인 the elephant가 ‘누워있는’ 주체이고 동사 lie는 ‘눕다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰였으므로, lain을 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 lying으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓖ ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하는 것을 보다)’의 5형식 구문에서 지각동사 see의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형이나 현재분사를 사용하며, 목적어 them(some men in uniform)이 ‘흔드는’ 주체이고 목적어 their arms가 이어지므로, 능동이자 진행 중인 동작을 나타내기 위해 쓰인 현재분사 waving은 알맞다.

body:
The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. (A)Aaron은 Lion 여관으로 향했고, 그곳에서 그는 몇 개월 동안 일해 오고 있었다. As Aaron approached the gate, he was ⓐstartling by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around ⓑnervously for the mother elephant. But there ⓒwere no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers ⓓhad gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys ⓔwho worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, ⓕlain on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them ⓖwaving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Poachers Who Hunted Elephants Near Lion's Inn
A Baby Elephant’s Struggle to Survive Without Its Mother’s Protection
The Rescue of a Young Elephant Through Aaron's Courage and Teamwork
The Difficulties of Caring for a Baby Elephant Separated from Its Family
A Young Elephant’s Journey from the Wild to an Unfamiliar Human Environment
solution:
Aaron은 수영장에서 마구 움직이며 격렬하게 발길질을 하는 작은 코끼리를 발견하고, 빨리 도움이 필요하다고 판단하여 정원사에게 도움을 요청한 뒤 밧줄과 갈퀴를 가져와 물로 곧장 뛰어들었으며, 부엌에서 일했던 소년 한 명과 함께 코끼리의 배 아래로 밧줄을 넣고 요리사와 정원사의 도움을 받아 기진맥진한 코끼리를 끌고 당기고 밀어 간신히 덱 위로 올려놓았다고 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 ③ ‘Aaron의 용기와 협력을 통한 어린 코끼리의 구조’가 알맞다.
오답
① Lion's Inn 근처에서 코끼리를 사냥한 밀렵꾼들
② 어미의 보호 없이 살아남기 위한 아기 코끼리의 투쟁
④ 가족과 떨어진 아기 코끼리를 돌보는 데 따르는 어려움
⑤ 야생에서 낯선 인간의 환경으로 향하는 어린 코끼리의 여정

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re (A)short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision ⓐwas made.
The first few nights at the orphanage ⓑwere not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart ⓒhammered in his chest. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find (B)discomfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw.
Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi ⓓto swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles ⓔthat the keepers offered him every few hours.
Aaron recorded the amounts that Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. He felt (C)proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
But mothers worry, and so ⓕwas Aaron. Each time he saw the veterinarian frown, Aaron’s stomach got (D)tense. When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared ⓖwhat he’d never get better. One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow compared to his own. Samuel (E)reassured him that all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But that didn’t stop Aaron from ⓗworrying. Bezi still had a fever. Aaron knew only too well that medicine couldn’t cure everything.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: (B) discomfort(불편함) → comfort(편안함)

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호>    <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓒ 동사(sat)가 있는 완전한 절(Aaron sat straight up)에 접속사 없이 절이나 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 부대상황(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 특히 여기서는 주절의 주어와 다른 의미상의 주어 heart가 앞에 위치한 독립분사구문을 이루어야 한다. 따라서 의미상 주어 heart가 그의 가슴에서 심장이 ‘쿵쾅거리는’ 주체이므로 hammered를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 hammering으로 고친다.
ⓕ ‘~도 (마찬가지로) 그러하다’의 뜻으로 쓰인 부사 so가 문두에 와서 주어와 대동사가 도치되어 so 뒤에 대동사가 이어진 구조로, 흐름상 앞의 일반 동사 worry를 대신해야 하므로, was를 흐름상 과거 동사로 대동사 did로 고친다.
ⓖ 완전한 절(he’d never get better)을 이끌어 동사 feared의 목적어 역할의 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.
오답
ⓑ 주절의 주어 The first few nights at the orphanage의 핵심 단어인 복수명사구 The first few nights에 수일치한 흐름상 과거형 복수동사 were는 알맞다.
ⓓ ‘…가 ~하도록 하다[만들다]‘ ’의 의미를 갖는 ‘get+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사/과거분사)‘ 구문으로 목적어 Bezi가 ’삼키는‘ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 to부정사 to swallow는 알맞다.
ⓔ 4형식 동사 offered의 직접목적어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the bottles를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 that은 알맞다.
ⓗ '…가 ~하는 것을 막다‘의 의미를 갖는 ’stop+목적어+from+(동)명사(구)’의 구조로 전치사 from 뒤에 쓰인 worrying은 알맞다.

solution:

body:
One morning, Aaron watched sadly as the other elephants played, kicking a large can and rolling joyfully in the mud. He was wishing Bezi could have the company of other elephants, when suddenly he heard Samuel shout, “Come quick!” Aaron dropped the rake he was holding and ran to where Samuel and the other keepers crowded. On a dusty truck lay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap.
After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets to cover the injured elephant. (A) He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine. (B) He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so careless! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable. (C) He had been preparing himself for the worst, but ⓐhe got a shock of a different kind. (D) The little elephant was standing up with his trunk hanging over the half wall of his stall. (E) He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with relief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm.

It wasn’t until the new elephant was settled in her stall that Aaron realized with a start that he’d forgotten all about Zambezi.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘새 코끼리가 자신의 우리에 적응하고 나서야 Aaron은 깜짝 놀라며 자신이 Zambezi에 대한 모든 것을 잊고 있었다는 것을 깨달았다.’라는 뜻으로, 어린 코끼리가 덫에 걸려 발 중 하나에 심한 상처를 입었고, 수의사의 치료를 도왔다는 설명 뒤에, Aaron이 Zambezi에 대한 모든 것을 잊고 그를 오랫동안 혼자 둔 적이 없어 무슨 일이 생겼을까 봐 걱정하며 마구간으로 급히 달려갔다는 설명 앞인 (B)에 들어가야 한다.

solution:

The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, where he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant (A)______. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together ⓐthey were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw ⓑthem waving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.

waved its trunk at the workers

One morning, Aaron watched ⓐsadly as the other elephants played, kicking a large can and rolling joyfully in the mud. He was wishing Bezi could have the company of other elephants, when suddenly he heard Samuel shout, “Come quick!” Aaron dropped the rake he was holding and ran to where Samuel and the other keepers crowded. On a dusty truck lay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly ⓑwound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap.
After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets to cover the injured elephant. He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and ⓒadministered medicine.
It wasn’t until the new elephant was settled in her stall that Aaron realized with a start that he’d forgotten all about Zambezi. He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so ⓓcareful! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable.
He had been preparing himself for the worst, but he got a shock of a different kind. The little elephant was standing up with his trunk hanging over the half wall of his stall. He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with ⓔrelief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓓ careful(주의 깊은) → careless(부주의한)

body:
Bezi was getting better each day. His sunken skin slowly gave way to a round belly, and his cheeks filled out, too. Before long, he was moving around more, even trying to leave his stall. The other orphans approached curiously, (A)[prodded / prodding] him all over with their trunks.
Eventually, Bezi was allowed to venture outside. He seemed to love the older orphans, following them around the pen and imitating their behavior. Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over (B)[to search / searched] for a bottle with his trunk.
Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs him, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — (C)[when / which] there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A)    (B)    (C)
choices: prodded    to search    when
prodding    to search    which
prodded    searched    which
prodding    to search    when
prodding    searched    which
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(The other orphans approached curiously)에 접속사 없이 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 부대상황(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상의 주어 The other orphans가 ‘쿡 찌르는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사 him이 이어지므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 prodding이 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절 뒤에 이어지는 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 앞의 동사 came running over에 ‘찾기 위해’라는 뜻으로 이어져야 하므로, 목적(~하기 위해)를 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사인 to search가 적절하다.
(C) ‘대시(—)’에 이어져, 앞의 when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals을 부연 설명하는 완전한 절(there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages)을 이끌고 있으므로, 관계부사 when이 적절하다.

body:
In 2015, Matthew McConaughey, an American actor and producer, gave the commencement speech at the University of Houston. Speaking to some 4,000 graduates, he shared personal stories and lessons, hoping to help young people ⓐto find their paths in life.
Today, I’m going to talk to you about some things I’ve learned in life. I hope you think of ㉠them as signposts or approaches that can guide your paths in life. You can apply them in your own lives, in your own ways if you choose to. So here we go.
Number One. ⓑSeek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, ㉡it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. (A) This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. (B) Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. (C) It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. (D) Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome. (E)
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, ⓒthought, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance ⓓto acknowledge.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role ⓔto become its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever ⓕhave before. However, what I realized was ⓖthat aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making ㉢it.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 4개이다.
ⓒ thought → thinking (앞의 완전한 절(I used to have ~ the outcome)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이끄는 분사 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 I가 ‘생각한’ 주체이므로, thought를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 thinking으로 고친다.)
ⓓ to acknowledge → to be acknowledged (‘need+목적어+to부정사(~가 …할 필요가 있다)’를 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, 목적어 my performance가 ‘인정받는’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, to acknowledge를 수동형 to부정사(to+be+p.p.)인 to be acknowledged로 고친다.)
ⓔ to become → became (구접속사 As soon as(~하자마자)가 이끄는 부사절의 주어 the daily act of making a movie or performing a role에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 흐름상 과거의 일이므로, to become을 과거동사 became으로 고친다.)
ⓕ have → had (유사관계대명사의 역할을 하는 than(~보다)이 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이며, 주절 동사(received)가 나타내는 과거시점 이전(before)의 경험을 나타내야 하므로, 과거완료(had+p.p.)인 had received에서 반복되는 과거분사 received가 생략된 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 have를 had로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 준사역동사는 목적격보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 취해 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)(~가 …하는 것을 돕다)’의 형태로 쓰이므로, help와 목적어 young people 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to find는 알맞다.
본문변형 find →to find

choices: ⓐ: thrilling → thrilled
ⓑ: Wooderson should → should Wooderson
ⓒ: Define → Defining
ⓓ: what → where
ⓔ: leave → left
solution:
ⓓ what → that[which] (주어가 없는 불완전한 절(are healthier for you)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 more places를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이나 완전한 절을 이끄는 관계부사 where가 쓰일 수 없다. 따라서 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 that이 쓰였음
ⓔ leave → are left (주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 관계사절의 동사 자리이며, 흐름상 현재시제로 선행사인 복수명사구 important things에 수일치한 복수동사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수와 태를 일치시켜야 하며, 선행사가 ‘남겨진’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로 현재시제 수동태를 써야 한다. 따라서 leave를 are left로 고친다.)
본문변형 left → that are left
오답

ⓑ 부정어 neither가 문장이나 절의 맨 앞에 쓰일 때 도치가 적용되어 조동사가 있는 경우 ‘neither+조동사+주어’의 어순으로 쓰이므로, Wooderson should를 should Wooderson으로 고친 것은 알맞다. 참고로, 주어 뒤에 have been there가 반복을 피하기 위해 생략되었다.
ⓒ 동사 helps에 대한 주어 자리에 동명사(구)나 to부정사(구)가 와야 하므로, 동사원형 Define을 동명사 Defining으로 고친 것은 알맞다.

Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to (A)[scare / comfort] myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here ⓐto speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ⓑus to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed ⓒadmit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t (B)[accept / deny] that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, (C)[confront / ignore] your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage ⓓto overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing ⓔthat you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, ⓕovercoming your fears. You are the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: scare accept confront
scare accept ignore
scare deny confront
comfort deny ignore
comfort deny confront
solution:
(A) 앞서 두려움을 인정하라고 했으며, 자신은 매일 아침 출근 전에 긴장하고, 오늘 연설 전에도 긴장했다고 설명하므로, 하루에 적어도 한 번은 스스로를 겁주어 두려움을 마주한다는 흐름이 되는 scare(~을 놀라게 하다, ~을 무섭게 하다)가 알맞다.
comfort ~을 안심시키다, ~을 위로하다
(B) 두려움을 인정하라고 조언하는 흐름이므로, 그것이 별것 아닌 것처럼 굴지 말고 그것의 존재를 부정하지 말라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 don’t 뒤에 deny(~을 부정하다)가 알맞다.
accept ~을 받아들이다
(C) 뒤에 그것을 극복할 용기를 발견하게 된다는 결과를 제시하므로, 두려움에 맞서라는 흐름이 되는 confront(~에 맞서다)가 알맞다.
ignore ~을 무시하다

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. (A)[Which / Whichever] way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking (B)[what / that] you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means ⓐ______. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors (C)[that / which] needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: Which what which
Whichever that that
Whichever that which
Which that which
Whichever what that
solution:
(A) 주절(I know ~ journey) 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 부사절이 와야 하며, 뒤에 수식받는 명사 way가 이어져 있으므로, ‘~하는 어느 …든지 상관없이’를 뜻하는 ‘whichever+명사+주어+동사~’ 형태의 양보 부사절을 이끌 수 있는 복합관계형용사 Whichever가 알맞다.
(B) 타동사로 쓰인 know의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you already know)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 the places and ways of thinking을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
본문변형 (B)는 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 원래 지문에서는 생략되어 있었음
(C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(needed them)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사 neighbors를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 사람 선행사와 쓰일 수 있는 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
본문변형 who → that

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. (A)[Which / Whichever] way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking (B)[what / that] you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means ⓐ______. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors (C)[that / which] needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
• No Latin-American had served as a US Supreme Court justice before Sotomayor.
• Studying various subjects will help people find their way through life differently.
• Earning a living is excluded from what counts as good use of education.
• Making sure no one nearby went without food, Sotomayor's grandmother improved the lives of those in her community.
• Sotomayor's mother, a doctor by profession, provided medical care to her neighbors.
• Sotomayor considers her family's lesson less important than what she learned at school.
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은 총 3개이다.
교육의 바람직한 활용은 생계를 꾸리고 가족을 부양하는 것을 포함한다고 했으므로, ‘생계를 꾸리는 것은 교육의 바람직한 활용에 해당하는 것에서 제외된다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
자신의 어머니는 간호조무사로서 주사가 필요한 이웃들에게 주사를 놓거나 혈압을 재거나 붕대를 교체하는 일로 사람들을 도왔다고 했으므로, ‘직업이 의사였던 Sotomayor의 어머니는 이웃들에게 의료 서비스를 제공했다.’ 또한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
Sotomayor의 가족은 그녀가 직업으로서 무슨 일을 하는가가 아니라 다른 사람에게 무엇을 베푸는가로 행복을 측정하라고 가르쳤으며, 그것은 자신이 인생에서 발견한 가장 중요한 교훈이자 가장 깊은 의미의 원천이라고 했으므로, ‘Sotomayor는 가족의 교훈을 학교에서 배운 것보다 덜 중요하게 여긴다.’도 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
제시문
• 라틴계 미국인 중 누구도 Sotomayor 이전에 미국 대법관을 지낸 적이 없었다.
• 다양한 과목을 공부하는 것은 사람들이 삶에서 각기 다르게 자신의 길을 찾도록 도울 것이다.
• 생계를 꾸리는 것은 교육의 바람직한 활용에 해당하는 것에서 제외(→포함)된다.
• 주변의 누구도 먹을 것 없이 지내지 않도록 확실히 함으로써, Sotomayor의 할머니는 지역사회 사람들의 삶을 개선했다.
• 직업이 의사(→간호조무사)였던 Sotomayor의 어머니는 이웃들에게 의료 서비스를 제공했다.
• Sotomayor는 가족의 교훈을 학교에서 배운 것보다 덜 중요하게(→인생에서 발견한 가장 중요한 교훈이자 가장 깊은 의미의 원천으로) 여긴다.

Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.

I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. body:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the biggest catch phrases these days. While cutting-edge technology might have benefits for many people, it is also a cause of concern for those trying to start a career. With so many jobs disappearing, what kind of career should you pursue, and what skills should you have to survive in the AI age? Whether you like it or hate it, AI technology is probably here to stay. Here are the core competencies you need to foster for a great career in the age of AI.
Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle built by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact that the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding factual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he would probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and no matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context in which you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how accurate the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. (A)우리는 인공지능이 가장 잘하는 것에 집중하기보다는 인공지능이 잘하지 못하는 것을 할 수 있어야 한다.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 관계대명사 what을 두 번 사용할 것
• 동명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
good, able, best, focus on, do
→ We must ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ AI ______ ______ ______ ______ rather than ______ ______ ______ AI ______ ______.
answer: We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.
solution:
• <보기>에 주어진 able을 사용하여 ‘~할 수 있다’라는 뜻의 ‘be able+to부정사’ 구문을 이루도록 제시된 must 뒤에 be able to do를 가장 먼저 쓴다.
• <조건>에 따라 관계대명사 what을 사용해 do의 목적어 역할을 하는 관계사절을 ‘what+불완전한 절’의 형태로 쓴다. do 뒤에 what을 가장 먼저 쓰고 관계사절의 주어인 AI가 제시되어 있으므로 ‘~을 잘하다’를 뜻하는 ‘be good at‘을 사용하여 단수주어에 수일치한 동사 is를 쓰고, 부정 부사 not과 good at을 이어서 쓴다.
• 구전치사 rather than 뒤에는 동명사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 동사 focus를 동명사 focusing으로 변형하여 쓰고, 전치사 on의 목적어 자리에는 <조건>에 따라 관계대명사 what을 사용한 관계사절을 쓴다. 관계사절의 주어 AI 다음에 단수주어에 수일치한 does로 변형하여 쓰고 부사의 최상급인 best를 이어서 쓴다.

body:
Strong AI and Weak AI are two fascinating branches of artificial intelligence that capture our imagination. Strong AI, like something from a sci-fi movie, can think, learn, and perform various tasks and cope with various situations just like humans. The current level of AI systems cannot do such things yet. Weak AI, on the other hand, the kind we now encounter daily, (A)[focus / focuses] on conducting one job well. It can do things such as recommending movies, giving us directions, or even helping us pick the perfect songs. However, it outperforms humans only in the specific tasks it is designed for, and it operates under far more constraints than even the most basic human intelligence. There are several differences between Weak AI and Strong AI.
What Is Weak AI?
Did you know that the computer playing chess and the helpful voice assistant on your phone are both examples of Weak AI? They may be impressive, but they’re designed for specific tasks and can’t handle anything outside their programming. Weak AI is a category of artificial intelligence confined to a finite domain. By performing operations that require considerable time and utilizing methods that are not always accessible to people, this technology can be advantageous to society.
It concentrates on tasks such as responding to user input searches or playing games. While it is only as good as its programming and training, Weak AI still helps convert enormous amounts of data into useful information by identifying patterns and (B)[generate / generating] predictions.
What Is Strong AI?
Strong AI is designed to mimic the cognitive abilities of a human being. It is called “strong” because it has the potential (C)[perform / to perform] a wide range of tasks, rather than being limited to a specific set of tasks. The more an AI system approaches the abilities of a human being, with all our intelligence, emotion, and broad knowledge, the “stronger” the AI system is considered.
One of the key characteristics of Strong AI is that it is designed to learn and adapt to new situations. It can generalize from its training data and apply its knowledge to new situations. For example, a Strong AI system designed to recognize objects in images can learn to recognize objects it hasn’t seen before based on its previous training. Another key attribute of Strong AI is that it is designed to be self-aware and conscious. This means that it can think, reason, and make decisions like a human being. While current AI systems are far from achieving this level of intelligence, some researchers believe that it is possible to create Strong AI in the future.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: focuses generating perform
focus generate perform
focuses generating to perform
focuses generate to perform

body:
Strong AI and Weak AI are two fascinating branches of artificial intelligence that capture our imagination. Strong AI, like something from a sci-fi movie, can think, learn, and perform various tasks and cope with various situations just like humans. The current level of AI systems cannot do such things yet. Weak AI, on the other hand, the kind we now encounter daily, (A)[focus / focuses] on conducting one job well. It can do things such as recommending movies, giving us directions, or even helping us pick the perfect songs. However, it outperforms humans only in the specific tasks it is designed for, and it operates under far more constraints than even the most basic human intelligence. There are several differences between Weak AI and Strong AI.
What Is Weak AI?
Did you know that the computer playing chess and the helpful voice assistant on your phone are both examples of Weak AI? They may be impressive, but they’re designed for specific tasks and can’t handle anything outside their programming. Weak AI is a category of artificial intelligence confined to a finite domain. By performing operations that require considerable time and utilizing methods that are not always accessible to people, this technology can be advantageous to society.
It concentrates on tasks such as responding to user input searches or playing games. While it is only as good as its programming and training, Weak AI still helps convert enormous amounts of data into useful information by identifying patterns and (B)[generate / generating] predictions.
What Is Strong AI?
Strong AI is designed to mimic the cognitive abilities of a human being. It is called “strong” because it has the potential (C)[perform / to perform] a wide range of tasks, rather than being limited to a specific set of tasks. The more an AI system approaches the abilities of a human being, with all our intelligence, emotion, and broad knowledge, the “stronger” the AI system is considered.
One of the key characteristics of Strong AI is that it is designed to learn and adapt to new situations. It can generalize from its training data and apply its knowledge to new situations. For example, a Strong AI system designed to recognize objects in images can learn to recognize objects it hasn’t seen before based on its previous training. Another key attribute of Strong AI is that it is designed to be self-aware and conscious. This means that it can think, reason, and make decisions like a human being. While current AI systems are far from achieving this level of intelligence, some researchers believe that it is possible to create Strong AI in the future.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the biggest catch phrases these days. While cutting-edge technology might have benefits for many people, it is also a cause of concern for those ⓐtry to start a career. With so many jobs disappearing, what kind of career should you pursue, and what skills should you have to survive in the AI age? Whether you like it or hate it, AI technology is probably here to stay. Here are the core competencies you need to foster for a great career in the age of AI.
Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle ⓑbuilt by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact that the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding factual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he ⓒwill probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and ⓓhowever hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context ⓔwhere you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell ⓕhow accurately the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.

It is AI that is good at collecting and classifying information. Meanwhile, it is humans that are best at dealing with people. The ability to understand, empathize, and communicate with people emotionally is potentially the most important human ability that artificial intelligence cannot replace. For example, AI disease diagnostic programs, which are already used in many hospitals, may accurately diagnose a patient’s illness such as cancer, but they don’t have the human touch that can make eye contact, empathize with pain, share worries, hold hands, or give encouragement to patients in despair. It is human doctors who can cure the patient’s emotional distress. Actually knowing and caring about what others think and feel is a unique competitive advantage we still possess.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>

<보기>
assess, analyze, provide, necessary, the quality, the information
→ When ______ ______ ______ ______ by AI, ______ ______ always ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ of information
answer: When analyzing the information provided by AI, it is always necessary to assess the quality of information
solution:
• 접속사를 남겨둔 분사구문을 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 주어진 접속사 When 다음에 분사를 쓴다. 문맥상 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 일반적인 사람들(we 또는 you)이 ’분석하는‘ 주체이므로 analyze는 능동의 의미인 현재분사 analyzing으로 변형하고 쓰고, 목적어 the information을 쓴다. 이를 분사를 뒤에 연결하되, the information은 ‘제공되는’ 대상이므로 provide를 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 provided로 변형하여 쓴다.
• ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문을 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 ‘it(가주어) ~ to부정사(진주어)’를 이용하여 영작한다. 주절의 자리에 가장 먼저 it is를 쓰고, 빈도부사 always 다음에 형용사 necessary가 쓴 다음, 진주어 자리에는 to부정사 to assess를 쓰고 목적어 the quality를 이어서 쓴다.

Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle built by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact that the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding factual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he would probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and no matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context in which you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how accurate the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.
In the age of AI, using information matters more than (A)______ it, so we need to understand the context and have some prior knowledge of the topic to ask the right questions, and then check the (B)______ of AI’s answers.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: retaining    clarity
collecting    completeness
organizing    correctness
summarizing    relevance
memorizing    accuracy
solution:
[요약문] AI 시대에는 정보를 (A)암기하는 것보다 활용하는 것이 더 중요하므로, 우리는 적절한 질문을 하기 위해 질문의 맥락을 이해하고 그 주제에 관한 배경지식을 어느 정도 갖추어야 하며, 다음으로 AI 답변의 (B)정확성을 확인해야 한다.
오답
① 기억하는 것 명확성
② 모으는 것 완전함
③ 정리하는 것 정확함
④ 요약하는 것 관련성

body:
Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed privately on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people (A)[is / are] becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us (B)[to feel / feel] awkward. Lastly, we have more entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun (C)[do / to do] so.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: are / to feel / do
are / to feel / to do
is / feel / do
are / feel / to do
is / feel / to do
solution:
(A) 주격 관계사절의 수식을 받는 주어 The list of music에 상응하는 동사 자리이며, 주어의 핵은 단수명사 list이므로 이에 수일치한 단수동사 is가 알맞다.
(B) 동사원형 make, 목적어 us에 이어지는 목적격 보어 자리로, 사역동사 make는 ’make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/p.p.)(~가 ~…하도록[되도록] 하다)‘의 구조를 취하며, 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계이므로 동사원형 feel이 알맞다.
(C) 가주어 it, be동사 was, 주격보어 fun에 이어지는 진주어 자리로, to부정사 to do가 알맞다.

body:
Although group singing has become ⓐless common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown ⓑwhat singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and ⓒincreasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds ⓓthat can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel connected to others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together ⓔhave healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely ⓕto contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news ⓖare that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓑ what → that (완전한 절(singing ~ serotonin)을 이끌어 동사 have shown의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓖ are → is (주어의 핵 news는 불가산명사이므로 동사 are을 is로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ has become의 보어 자리이므로, 열등 비교급 형용사 less common은 적절하다.
ⓒ 전치사 by의 목적어인 동명사구 reducing stress와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 구조를 이루고 있으므로 뒤의 명사구(the releas ~ serotonin)을 이끄는 동명사 increasing은 알맞다.
ⓓ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ way)을 이끌어 명사 bonds를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ 관계사절 who sing together의 수식을 받는 복수주어 people에 이어지는 동사 자리이므로 복수동사 have는 적절하다.
ⓕ 형용사 likely(가능성이 있는)는 to부정사와 함께 쓰여 ’be more likely+to부정사(~할 가능성이 더 높다)‘을 뜻하므로 to부정사 to contribute는 적절하다.
