body:
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Differences in Observational Capabilities Between Hubble and Other Space Telescopes
The Importance of Space Telescopes in Monitoring Changes in Earth's Climate
How Hubble Advanced Astronomy and Sparked Curiosity About Space
The Development of Space Telescopes for Exploring Distant Planets
How Hubble Was Launched and Placed in Orbit
solution: Hubble이 상세한 우주 이미지를 전송하여 천체 간의 관계, 은하의 형성, 우주의 팽창 등에 관한 선구적인 발견을 이끌고 천문학적 이해를 넓혔을 뿐만 아니라, 사람들의 상상력을 자극하고 우주 탐사에 대한 흥미를 높이는 데에도 기여했다는 점을 설명하는 글이므로 이 글의 제목으로 ❸ ‘Hubble이 천문학을 발전시키고 우주에 대한 호기심을 불러일으킨 방식’이 적절하다.

body:
Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, curious about what lies beyond our world. This inherent desire to (A)______ has encouraged technological innovations that can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements are space telescopes and space robots, which have paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. Consequently, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is (B)______. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.

다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: (A) explore the universe (B) visible to the human eye
(A) develop scientific instruments (B) not visible on Earth
(A) develop scientific instruments (B) produced by distant stars
(A) explore the universe (B) not visible on Earth
(A) discover the origins of life (B) visible to the human eye
solution:
(A) 앞에서 우리는 우리가 사는 세계 너머에 무엇이 있는지 궁금해하며 하늘을 바라보았다고 했으며 우주 망원경과 우주 로봇을 언급하고 있으므로 우주를 탐험하려는 타고난 욕망이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 explore the universe(우주를 탐험하다)가 적절하다.
(B) 지구의 대기가 자외선과 적외선을 흡수하여 관측에 왜곡을 일으키고 대기권 너머를 관측하기 어렵게 만든다고 했으며, 이런 한계를 극복하기 위해 망원경을 대시 너머인 우주로 보냈고, 우주 망원경의 능력이 먼 천체를 선명하게 관측할 수 있도록 한다고 했으므로, 우주 망원경이 지구에서는 볼 수 없는 빛을 포착한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 not visible on Earth(지구에서 볼 수 없는)가 적절하다.

body:
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to ______. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: determine the exact age of individual stars
provide clearer views with minimal interference
collect visible light from distant celestial objects
capture images of larger areas of Earth’s surface
detect changes in the orbits of distant celestial objects
solution: Webb의 거울은 Hubble보다 지름이 약 세 배 크고 이미지 수집 면적도 6.25배 넓으며, Hubble이 사용하는 가시광선보다 먼지가 많은 영역을 더 효과적으로 통과하는 적외선을 포착하는 데 특화되었다고 했으므로, 이러한 특징을 통해 천체를 더 뚜렷하게 관측할 수 있다는 내용이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ❷ ‘방해를 최소화하면서 더 선명한 시야를 제공하다‘가 적절하다.

body:
A variety of robots have been developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in fixed positions, while others are engineered for (A)[mobility / immobility]. Robots also come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers launched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the (B)[presence / absence] of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, marking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes continued their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
As we journey through the vast universe, telescopes and robots have been our eyes and hands. Their lenses and sensors (C)[obscure / reveal] the beauty and mysteries of galaxies, planets, and celestial wonders. As technology advances, we find ourselves closer to the secrets of the universe than ever before. The future of space exploration promises wonders beyond our imagination, and this fills us with great excitement.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: mobility presence obscure
immobility absence obscure
immobility presence reveal
mobility presence reveal
mobility absence reveal
solution:
(A) 다양한 로봇들의 특징을 설명하는 부분으로 일부 로봇들은 고정된 위치에 머무른다는 내용과 역접의 접속사인 while로 연결되어 있으므로 다른 로봇들은 이동할 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 mobility(이동성)가 적절하다.
immobility 부동성
(B) 뒤에서 Io의 활발한 화산이 다른 행성에서 관찰된 지질학적 과정의 최초 증거가 되었다고 설명하므로 활화산들이 ‘존재’한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 presence(존재)가 적절하다.
absence 부재
(C) 앞에서 망원경과 로봇의 렌즈와 센서가 우주 탐사에서 인간의 눈과 손 역할을 하며, 뒤에서 우주의 비밀에 더욱 가까워졌다고 설명하므로 우주의 아름다움과 신비를 ‘드러내다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reveal(~을 드러내다)이 적절하다.
obscure ~을 덮어 가리다

body:
The Old Man and the Sea is about an old man called Santiago. Santiago hadn’t ⓐ[caught / been caught] a fish in 84 days, so people thought he was unlucky, maybe cursed. In order to change his terrible luck, Santiago decided to go out into the deep ocean, ⓑ[which / where] was far beyond the other fishermen. (A) At first, he only caught a small tuna, but at the end of the 85th day, a powerful, magnificent marlin bit Santiago’s fishing hook. (B) The fish was so strong it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days. (C) Santiago learned to respect the fish, to admire its courage, and to appreciate its beauty. (D) Instead, he tied it to the side of his boat and tried to return home. (E) Unfortunately, a shark smelled the marlin’s blood and ⓒ[threatening / threatened] to eat Santiago’s prized fish.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ / ⓑ / ⓒ
choices: caught / which / threatening
caught / which / threatened
been caught / which / threatened
caught / where / threatened
been caught / where / threatening
solution:
ⓐ 주어 Santiago가 타동사 catch(잡다)의 주체이며 뒤에 목적어 a fish가 이어지므로, had에 이어져 과거완료 능동태(had+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 caught가 알맞다.
ⓑ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was ~ fishermen)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 the deep ocean을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.
*ⓑ which was는 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
ⓒ 과거형 동사 smelled와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 있으므로, 과거형 동사 threatened가 알맞다.

body:
The Old Man and the Sea is about an old man called Santiago. Santiago hadn’t ⓐ[caught / been caught] a fish in 84 days, so people thought he was unlucky, maybe cursed. In order to change his terrible luck, Santiago decided to go out into the deep ocean, ⓑ[which / where] was far beyond the other fishermen. (A) At first, he only caught a small tuna, but at the end of the 85th day, a powerful, magnificent marlin bit Santiago’s fishing hook. (B) The fish was so strong it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days. (C) Santiago learned to respect the fish, to admire its courage, and to appreciate its beauty. (D) Instead, he tied it to the side of his boat and tried to return home. (E) Unfortunately, a shark smelled the marlin’s blood and ⓒ[threatening / threatened] to eat Santiago’s prized fish.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
When it finally died, he saw it was too big to put inside the boat.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘마침내 그것이 죽었을 때 그는 그것이 너무 커서 배 안에 넣을 수 없다는 것을 알았다.’라는 뜻으로, finally(마침내)로 3일간의 사투가 끝났음을 나타내는 흐름이므로, 청새치가 3일 동안 Santiago의 배를 끌고 다녔고, 이에 그는 그것의 용기를 존경하고 아름다움을 높이 평가했다는 내용의 뒤이자, Instead(대신에)로 주어진 문장에서 언급된 청새치를 it으로 가리켜 그것을 배 안에 넣는 대신 배 옆에 묶은 채로 집으로 돌아가려고 했다는 문장 앞인 (D)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

body:
Santiago saw the shark’s jaws opening and ⓐclosing in anticipation. He knew this shark no longer cared about the dangers of a boat or of a fisherman. The smell of blood took away the shark’s fear, making it ⓑbravely and recklessly. Santiago didn’t have much rope left over from tying up the marlin, but he tightened the short remaining piece of rope into a knot on his spear. The shark got closer and closer, mouth ⓒopen and teeth shining in the sunlight.
(A)______. The spear wasn’t very long, too short ⓓto hit the shark before it arrived at the marlin. Still, Santiago refused to give up. The shark’s eyes ⓔflashing and he bit the beautiful fish just above the tail. It ripped and bit and took a huge piece of meat — at least 40 pounds — out of the giant marlin.
윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Santiago began to regret catching such an enormous fish.
Santiago’s mind felt strong and clear, his willpower restored.
The sight of the shark left Santiago too frightened to take any action.
Santiago’s confidence dwindled as he realized how dangerous the shark was.
Santiago felt confident that his spear would easily defeat the approaching shark.
solution:
첫 번째 문단에서 상어가 피 냄새로 두려움 없이 점점 가까이 다가오는 위협적인 상황에서도 Santiago가 남은 짧은 밧줄 조각을 창에 단단히 조여 매듭을 지으며 상어에 맞설 준비를 하고 있었고, 창이 너무 짧아 상어가 청새치에 도달하기 전에 맞추기는 어렵지만 Santiago는 포기하길 거부했다는 내용이 이어지므로, Santiago가 상어에 맞서기로 했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❷ ‘Santiago의 정신은 강해지고 맑아졌으며, 의지력이 회복되었다.’가 알맞다.
오답
① Santiago는 그렇게 거대한 물고기를 잡은 것을 후회하기 시작했다
③ 상어의 모습은 Santiago를 너무 두렵게 만들어 아무런 행동도 하지 못하게 했다
④ Santiago가 상어가 얼마나 위험한지를 깨닫자 그의 자신감이 점차 줄어들었다
⑤ Santiago는 자신이 창이 다가오는 상어를 쉽게 물리칠 것이라고 확신했다

body:
The old man could hear the marlin’s skin tearing and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, where the brain was. It turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its struggling.
Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He had cast the spear too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too short. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. After a moment, it lay still on the surface before sinking slowly into the water, taking the spear with it.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 지문에서 찾아 알맞게 쓰시오. (필요시 변형하고, 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것)
Although Santiago succeeded in killing the shark by ______ his spear into its head, he failed to retrieve the weapon, which ______ into the ocean with the ______ shark.
solution: [요약문] Santiago는 창을 상어의 머리에 꽂아 넣음[던짐]으로써 상어를 죽이는 데 성공했지만, 그 무기를 회수하는 데 실패했고, 그 무기는 죽은 상어와 함께 바다 속으로 가라앉았다.

body:
So much of the marlin’s blood flowed into the water from where it had (A)bitten. Santiago knew ⓐ______. He had no spear, and his boat was still many miles from the land. The fisherman knew he would fail, (B)understood that he had no hope of protecting the beautiful marlin. Santiago didn’t care. He would struggle (C)as long as he could, even if he could not succeed.
“A man can be destroyed,” he said. “But not defeated.”
Santiago turned back to his boat and looked at the great fish. The shark had ruined the marlin’s powerful tail and made it (D)so ugly it hurt Santiago’s spirit (E)whenever he looked at its torn flesh. Santiago felt sorry for catching the marlin and wanted to apologize to the beautiful animal.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): 주어 it은 ‘물렸던’ 대상이므로, 과거완료 수동태가 되도록 been bitten으로 고쳐야 한다.
(B): 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 The fisherman이 ‘이해하는’ 주체이므로 현재분사 understanding으로 고쳐야 한다.
(C): ‘가능한 오래’라는 뜻으로 as long as possible로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
(D): 과거형 동사 made의 목적격보어 자리에서 ‘so+형용사+that절(너무 ~해서 …한)’ 구문을 이루고 있다.
(E): 부사절을 이끄는 접속사로 no matter when으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
solution:
(E) whenever가 부사절을 이끄는 접속사라는 설명은 알맞으나, whenever는 ‘~할 때마다’라는 뜻의 시간의 접속사로 쓰였으므로 every time 등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 참고로, whenever가 ‘언제 ~하더라도’라는 뜻의 양보의 의미로 쓰일 때는 no matter when으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
오답
(A) 관계부사 where가 이끄는 절의 주어 it(= the marlin)이 타동사 bite(~을 물다)의 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, had에 이어져 과거완료 수동태(had+been+p.p.)를 이루는 been bitten으로 고쳐야 한다는 설명은 적절하다.

Santiago’s successful defense of the marlin against repeated vicious shark attacks
Santiago’s serious dilemma over whether to defend the beautiful marlin

Are you keen on exploring the world of literature? Is reading your hobby? Here’s an exciting type of event — literary festivals! These events are ⓐhosted in cities with rich literary histories, connecting authors and readers. Take a glance at these festivals across different regions!
Edinburgh International Book Festival
Where: Edinburgh, Scotland
The Edinburgh International Book Festival happens every year in Edinburgh, ⓑwhich was designated the first UNESCO City of Literature. The festival is one of the largest literary ⓒevent globally and is typically held in August. It takes place at the University of Edinburgh’s College of Art, ⓓcreating a village atmosphere. There are outdoor screens for live events, making it an engaging experience for all.
Frankfurter Buchmesse
Where: Frankfurt, Germany
The Frankfurter Buchmesse is the world’s largest book fair, drawing together publishers, authors, and book fans from across the globe. It is held for five days in October, with the initial two days usually ⓔreserving for trade visitors and professionals, while the following days are open to the general public. This fair is a must for anybody, speaking any language, ⓕwhich has ambitions in the publishing world or simply loves to read.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓒ event → events (’가장 ~한 것들 중의 하나‘라는 뜻의 ’one of the+최상급+복수명사(구)’ 구문을 이루어야 하므로, 단수명사 event를 복수명사 events로 고친다.)
ⓔ reserving → reserved (전치사 with, 목적어 the initial two days와 함께 ‘~가 …한 상태로[채로]’를 뜻하는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사’ 구문을 이루어야 하며, 명사구인 the initial two days는 ‘지정된’ 대상이므로 reserving은 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 reserved로 고친다.)
ⓕ which → who 또는 that (주어가 없는 불완전한 절(has ~ read)을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사 자리로, 선행사가 이중콤마(,)로 삽입된 분사구 speaking any language 앞의 anybody이므로, which를 사람이 선행사일 때 사용하는 who 또는 선행사에 관계없이 사용할 수 있는 that으로 고친다.)
*ⓕ는 원래 지문에서 who였음
오답
ⓓ 완전한 절(It takes place at the University of Edinburgh’s College of Art)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되어 있으며 문맥상 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 it(=The Edinburgh International Book Festival)이 분위기를 ‘만들어내는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 creating은 적절하다.

“Don’t think, old man,” he said. “Sail on this course and take it when it comes.”
But he couldn’t stop thinking. Alone on the ocean, with the poor marlin’s blood spilling into the water, all he could do was think. He thought of the great baseball player Joe DiMaggio. He wondered if Joe DiMaggio could have killed the shark without losing the spear. Santiago thought of his own ⓐwounded hands and wondered how Joe DiMaggio could play baseball so well in spite of his own injuries. He wondered if he, like Joe DiMaggio, could ignore the ⓑunbearable pain and fatigue in his body long enough to meet his goals.
“Think about something ⓒdistressing, old man,” he said. “Every minute now you are closer to home. You sail lighter for the loss of 40 pounds.”
However, Santiago knew this was false hope. Too much blood in the water. Too many sharks. Too far from land with these ⓓfierce ocean currents. Still, the fisherman promised he would continue to fight. (A)두려움도 자신의 창을 잃은 것도 그의 결심을 빼앗아갈 수 없었다. He had to come up with a new weapon, removing the rowing oars and attaching his knife to one.
“Now,” he said. “I am still an old man. But I am not unarmed.”
The breeze got stronger and his boat ⓔgained speed. He felt fresh, and his determination returned. The sharks would almost certainly take his beautiful marlin, but Santiago would never cease fighting them. A man can be destroyed, but never defeated.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• Neither로 시작할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것
• 총 13단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
take away, fear, the loss, determination, of, could
→ ______
answer: Neither fear nor the loss of his spear could take away his determination. 또는 Neither fear nor the loss of his spear could take his determination away.
solution:
Neither로 시작하라는 <조건>에 따라 ‘A도 B도 아닌’이라는 뜻의 상관접속사 ’neither A nor B’를 사용하여 주어 자리에 Neither fear nor the loss of his spear를 쓴다. 과거형 조동사 could와 구동사 take away를 이어서 쓴다. 구동사 ‘take ~ away(~을 빼앗다)’는 명사(구)를 목적어로 취한 경우 take와 away 사이에 또는 away 다음에 목적어가 올 수 있으므로 take his determination away 또는 take away his determination으로 쓴다.
*원래 지문에는 take away his determination이 쓰였음

body:
Santiago saw the shark’s jaws opening and closing in anticipation. He knew this shark no longer cared about the dangers of a boat or of a fisherman. The smell of blood took away the shark’s fear, making it brave and reckless. Santiago didn’t have much rope left over from tying up the marlin, but he tightened the short remaining piece of rope into a knot on his spear. The shark got closer and closer, mouth open and teeth shining in the sunlight.
Santiago’s mind felt strong and clear, his willpower restored. The spear wasn’t very long, too short to hit the shark before it arrived at the marlin. Still, Santiago refused to give up. The shark’s eyes flashed and he bit the beautiful fish just above the tail. It ripped and bit and took a huge piece of meat — at least 40 pounds — out of the giant marlin.
The old man could hear the marlin’s skin tearing and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, where the brain was. It turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its struggling.
Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He had cast the spear too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too short. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. After a moment, it lay still on the surface before sinking slowly into the water, taking the spear with it.

choices: Santiago‘s Tough Decision to Give up His Precious Catch
Santiago’s Triumph over the Shark at a Heavy Price
The Shark’s Lucky Escape from Santiago’s Deadly Attack
Santiago‘s Intense Confrontation with a Pack of Merciless Sharks
Santiago: A Fearless Fisherman Who Killed a Shark with His Bare Hands

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’으로 시작할 것
• 목적격 관계대명사 that을 생략할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• (1)과 (2)는 각각 6단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
think, spill, could do, the poor marlin’s, all
→ (1) ______ into the water (2) ______
answer:
(1) with the poor marlin’s blood spilling
(2) all he could do was think
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’ 구문을 사용한다. 먼저 전치사 with와 명사구 the poor marlin’s blood를 쓴 후, 명사구인 the poor marlin’s blood가 ‘쏟아지고 있는’ 주체이므로 주어진 동사 spill을 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 spill로 변형하여 쓴다.
• ‘그가 할 수 있는 모든 것’을 영작하기 위해 가장 먼저 all을 쓰고, 그 뒤에 all을 수식하는 관계사절 he could do를 쓴다. 목적격 관계대명사 that은 <조건>에 따라 생략한다. 주어인 all he could do는 여기서 ‘그가 할 수 있는 유일한 일’을 뜻하므로 be동사 단수형 was를 쓴다. ‘All (that)+주어+do의 형태+be동사’ 구문에서는 보어로 오는 to부정사의 to를 생략할 수 있으며, 6단어로 쓰라는 <조건>이 있으므로 원형부정사 think를 쓴다.

However, Santiago knew this was false hope. Too much blood in the water. Too many sharks. Too far from land with these strong ocean currents. Still, the fisherman promised he would continue to fight. Neither fear nor the loss of his spear could take away his determination. He had to come up with a new weapon, removing the rowing oars and attaching his knife to one.
“Now,” he said. “I am still an old man. But I am not unarmed.”

When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!”
“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”
“Zambezi?”
“It’s the name we gave the little elephant.”
So the elephant was alive! Aaron beamed, his heart ⓐbeaten faster. Samuel motioned for him to follow. Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, covered by blankets. He seemed to be having trouble breathing. The image of his father, lying under blankets at home just before he died, ⓑflashing through Aaron’s mind, and he felt a lump in his throat.
Samuel nudged him forward. Aaron knelt and, with shaking hands, reached out to touch Zambezi’s thick skin. It felt surprisingly ⓒwarmly. Zambezi opened one eye. Slowly, his trunk curled upward and brushed Aaron’s arm.
“How are you?” Aaron whispered.
He sat down on the straw, and the elephant rested his trunk on Aaron’s leg. They stayed like that for some time, while Samuel watched them curiously.
“Here,” Samuel whispered, handing a milk bottle to Aaron. “Maybe you will have better luck than we’ve had.”
Aaron had seen enough babies nurse to know what to do. He tilted the bottle, spilling some drops onto the elephant’s lip. Zambezi licked the milk off his lip and then began to suck from the bottle, looking Aaron in the eyes as he ⓓwas. Samuel shook his head in amazement. Aaron’s mind rushed back to the day ⓔwhich he first met the elephant.

Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs ⓔhim, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
(A) But mothers worry, and so did Aaron. Each time he saw the veterinarian frown, Aaron’s stomach got tense. When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared that he’d never get better. One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow compared to his own. Samuel reassured him that all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But ⓐ______. Bezi still had a fever. Aaron knew only too well that medicine couldn’t cure everything
(B) Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours. Aaron recorded the amounts that Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
(C) The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart hammering smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw. Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 수석 사육사가 동물들과 잘 지내는 Aaron에게 직원이 부족한 고아원에서 일할 것을 제안하고, 어머니도 그의 결정을 지지하며 쉬는 날에는 집에 올 수 있다고 격려하자, Aaron은 고아원에서 일하기로 결정했다는 주어진 글 다음에, Aaron은 처음 며칠 밤 거의 잠을 자지 못하고 집의 익숙한 소리와 냄새를 그리워했지만, 머지않아 Bezi와의 친밀감에서 위안을 찾고 Bezi에게 약을 먹이고 혈액을 채취하는 방법을 배워, 고아원에서 생활하기 시작한 Aaron의 모습을 구체적으로 설명한 (C), Aaron이 실제로 Bezi에게 우유를 먹이고, 마신 양을 기록하며, 수의사의 진료를 돕는 등 자신이 코끼리의 엄마가 된 것 같다며 자부심을 느끼며 구체적인 돌봄 활동을 수행하는 모습을 설명한 (B), ‘엄마’가 된 것 같다는 내용에 이어 But(그러나)으로 시작하여 엄마들이 걱정하듯 Aaron도 마찬가지로 Bezi의 건강 상태를 걱정하며, Bezi가 더 나아지지 않을까 봐 계속 걱정하는 모습을 설명한 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

④ Aaron은 Bezi의 상태를 기록하고 수의사를 도우면서 Bezi를 세심하게 돌보는 데 자부심을 느꼈다.

One morning, Aaron watched sadly as the other elephants played, kicking a large can and rolling joyfully in the mud. He was wishing Bezi could have the company of other elephants, when suddenly he heard Samuel shout, “Come quick!” Aaron dropped the rake he was holding and ran to ⓐwhich Samuel and the other keepers crowded. On a dusty truck ⓑlay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap.
After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets ⓒto cover the injured elephant. He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine.
(A)새 코끼리가 자신의 우리에 적응하고 나서야 Aaron은 깜짝 놀라며 자신이 Zambezi에 대한 모든 것을 잊고 있었다는 것을 깨달았다. He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so careless! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable.
He had been preparing ⓓhimself for the worst, but he got a shock of a different kind. The little elephant was standing up with his trunk ⓔto hang over the half wall of his stall. He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with relief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• ‘It ~ that … ’ 강조 구문을 사용할 것
• 명사절 접속사 that을 사용할 것
• 축약형을 사용할 것
• 완료 시제를 쓸 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형 및 추가할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
realize, in her stall, with a start, forget, until, settle, all, the new elephant
______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ with a start ______ ______ ______ ______ about Zambezi.
answer: It wasn’t until the new elephant was settled in her stall that Aaron realized with a start that he’d forgotten all about Zambezi.
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 ‘it ~ that … (…한 것은 바로 ~이다)’ 강조 구문을 사용하되, ‘~하고 나서야 비로소 ~하다’의 not until 구문과 함께 쓰일 때는 ‘It+be동사+not+until+완전한 절+that+주절’의 형태로 쓰인다.
• 여기서는 흐름상 과거 사실을 나타내야 하므로 과거시제와 was not의 축약형을 사용하여 it wasn’t를 쓰고, 강조되는 부분으로 until 부사구를 이어주되, 주어 the new elephant가 ‘적응하게 되다’는 수동의 의미를 나타내도록 settle을 수동태(be동사+p.p.)를 활용하여 흐름상 과거시제로 was settled를 써서 until the new elephant was settled in her stall을 쓴다.
• that 뒤는 주절이 이어지므로, 주어와 동사로 흐름상 과거시제를 사용하여 Aaron realized를 쓴다.
• 동사 realized의 목적어로 완전한 절을 이끌도록 <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사 that을 쓰고, 주어와 동사를 쓰되, 새 코끼리가 자신의 우리에 적응하게 된 과거 사실보다 그가 모든 것을 잊었던 사실이 먼저 일어났기 때문에 과거 완료시제(had+p.p.)를 활용하고 축약형을 사용하여 he’d forgotten을 쓰고 목적어 all을 쓴다.

Aaron cared for a new baby elephant injured by a ______, remembered that he had left Zambezi ______ and rushed to ______ ______, where he felt a sense of ______ to find Bezi moving and showing signs of recovery.
solution: [요약문] Aaron은 덫에 걸려 부상을 입은 새로운 아기 코끼리를 돌보았고, 자신이 Zambezi를 혼자 두었다는 것을 기억하여 마구간으로 서둘러 갔으며, 그곳에서 Bezi가 움직이고 회복의 징후를 보이는 것을 발견하고 안도감을 느꼈다.

The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, where he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. (A)요리사와 정원사가 가장자리에서 잡아당기고, Aaron과 다른 소년은 그 기진맥진한 동물을 끌고, 당기고, 밀어서 간신히 덱 위로 올려놓았다. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them waving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old ... found the mother ... killed ... poachers ....” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• ‘with+명사+분사’ 구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형 및 추가할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
from, the cook, the gardener, manage, pull, onto the deck, the edge, exhausted, drag, push
______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, Aaron and the other boy finally ______ ______ ______, ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck
solution:
• ‘~가 …한 상태로, ~가 …한 채로’라는 뜻의 ‘with+명사(구)+분사’ 구문을 활용하여 with, 명사구 the cook and the gardener를 쓴 후 명사구가 ‘잡아당기는’ 주체이므로 제시어 pull을 현재분사 pulling으로 변형하여 쓰고, 전치사구 from the edge를 쓴다.
• 주어진 주어와 부사에 이어 동사 자리에 ‘그럭저럭[간신히] ~하다’의 의미를 나타내는 ‘manage+to부정사’를 활용하여 흐름상 과거 시제로 managed to drag, pull, and push를 쓰고, 목적어로 the exhausted animal을 쓰고, 부사구 onto the deck을 쓴다.

Bezi was getting better each day. His sunken skin slowly gave way to a round belly, and his cheeks filled out, too. Before long, he was moving around more, even trying to leave his stall. The other orphans approached curiously, prodding him all over with their trunks.
Eventually, Bezi ______. He seemed to love the older orphans, following them around the pen and imitating their behavior. Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over to search for a bottle with his trunk.
Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs him, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: was allowed to venture outside
was given special medical attention
was moved to a larger enclosure nearby
was forced to remain under constant care
was separated from the other orphan elephants
solution:
Bezi는 날마다 상태가 좋아져 움푹 들어간 피부가 둥근 배로 바뀌고 볼에도 살이 차올랐으며, 얼마 지나지 않아 더 많이 움직이고 심지어 우리를 나가려 하기까지 했고, 결국 나이가 더 많은 코끼리들을 따라다니며 그들의 행동을 흉내 내고 진흙에서 첨벙거리며 놀았다고 설명하고 있으므로, 건강이 회복되어 우리 밖으로 나가는 것이 허락되었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❶ ‘바깥으로 과감히 나가도록 허락되었다’가 알맞다.

② 특별한 의료적 관심을 받았다
③ 근처의 더 큰 우리로 옮겨졌다
④ 지속적인 보살핌을 받도록 강요받았다
⑤ 다른 고아 코끼리들로부터 분리되었다

With controversy, plenty of ⓔcurious people are waiting for the result.
위 담화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?

body:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the biggest catch phrases these days. While cutting-edge technology might have ⓐbenefits for many people, it is also a cause of concern for those trying to start a career. With so many jobs disappearing, what kind of career should you pursue, and what skills should you have to survive in the AI age? Whether you like it or hate it, AI technology is probably here to stay. Here are the core ⓑcompetencies you need to foster for a great career in the age of AI.
Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle built by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to be very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the ⓒpresence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact that the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding ⓓfactual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he would probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and no matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. (A)올바른 질문들을 하기 위해, 여러분이 질문을 하고 있는 맥락을 이해해야한다, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how ⓔlengthy the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details memorized. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on what AI does best.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ lengthy(긴, 장황한) → accurate(정확한)

• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (중복 사용 가능하며, 필요시 변형할 것)

<보기>
you’re, the question, the context, ask, the right questions, understand
(1) ______, you must (2) ______
answer:
(1) To ask the right questions
(2) understand the context in which you’re asking the question
solution:
(1) <조건>에 따라 부사적 용법 중 목적(~하기 위해)을 나타내는 to부정사를 사용하여 ask를 to부정사인 To ask로 변형한 후, 목적어로 명사구 the right questions를 쓴다.
(2) 조동사 must 뒤에 동사원형 understand와 목적어인 명사구 the context를 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용해 the context를 수식하는 관계사절을 쓴다. 먼저 선행사에 어울리는 전치사 in을 사용해 in which를 쓴 뒤, 현재진행형(be동사+-ing)을 사용해 you’re 뒤에 ask를 현재분사 asking으로 변형하고 목적어로 명사구 the question을 쓴다.

body:
According to a future job report published by a top global investment bank, up to 300 million jobs around the world could be affected by artificial intelligence. The report also noted that technological innovation has historically created employment growth in the long run. In the age of AI, the ability to adapt to new technologies and work environments is crucial. You must embrace change and be open to learning and mastering new skills. It is very likely that many of those without AI skills will be left behind. That is why we must become life-long learners.
Continuous upskilling and reskilling will enable you to stay valuable in the changing job market. AI will replace some jobs but substantially alter many more. Furthermore, you probably won’t be replaced by AI. More likely a person with AI skills will replace you.
In conclusion, ______. Instead of fearing AI, we must embrace it as a companion in this new era and find ways to collaborate with it and complement it. We must also focus on developing interpersonal skills that machines cannot replace. By doing so, we can not only survive in this era of AI but also thrive and prosper.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: surviving and competing with AI requires a shift in mindset
human intelligence will eventually be dispensable as AI continues to advance
the primary goal of education should be to discourage cooperation with AI
interpersonal skills are no longer the key to success in an AI-dominated society
thriving alongside artificial intelligence relies on maintaining conventional ways of thinking

body:
It is AI that is good at collecting and classifying information. Meanwhile, it is humans that are (A)[most / least] skilled at dealing with people. The ability to understand, empathize, and communicate with people emotionally is potentially the most important human ability that artificial intelligence cannot replace. For example, AI disease diagnostic programs, which are already used in many hospitals, may (B)[accurately / inaccurately] diagnose a patient’s illness such as cancer, but they don’t have the human touch that can make eye contact, empathize with pain, share worries, hold hands, or give encouragement to patients in despair. It is human doctors who can cure the patient’s emotional distress. Actually knowing and caring about what others think and feel is a unique competitive advantage we still (C)[possess / lack].
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: most / accurately / possess
least / inaccurately / lack
most / inaccurately / possess
least / accurately / possess
most / accurately / lack
solution:
(A) 사람들을 이해하고, 공감하고, 감정적으로 소통하는 능력은 인공지능이 대체할 수 없는 어쩌면 인간의 가장 중요한 능력이라는 내용이 이어지므로, 사람을 상대하는 것에 가장 능숙한 것은 인간이라는 흐름이 되는 most(가장)가 알맞다.
(B) but(하지만) 뒤에 인공지능 질병 진단 프로그램에는 인간적인 손길이 없다는 내용이 이어지므로, 인공지능 질병 진단 프로그램은 환자의 질병을 정확하게 진단할 수는 있다는 장점을 언급하는 흐름이 되는 accurately(정확하게)가 알맞다.
(C) 정서적 공감과 소통 능력은 인공지능이 대체할 수 없는 인간의 중요한 능력이라고 했으며, 그 예로 환자의 정서적 고통을 치료할 수 있는 것은 인간 의사라고 설명하므로, 다른 사람이 생각하고 느끼는 것을 실제로 알고 마음을 쓰는 것은 우리가 여전히 보유하고 있는 고유한 경쟁 우위라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 possess(~을 소유하다)가 알맞다.

body:
Strong AI and Weak AI are two fascinating branches of artificial intelligence that capture our imagination. Strong AI, like something from a sci-fi movie, can think, learn, and perform various tasks and cope with various situations just like humans. The current level of AI systems cannot do such things yet. Weak AI, on the other hand, the kind we now encounter daily, focuses on conducting one job well. It can do things such as recommending movies, giving us directions, or even ⓐhelping us pick the perfect songs. However, it outperforms humans only in the specific tasks it is designed for, and it operates under far more constraints than even the most basic human intelligence ⓑis. There are several differences between Weak AI and Strong AI.
What Is Weak AI?
Did you know that the computer playing chess and the helpful voice assistant on your phone are both examples of Weak AI? They may be impressive, but they’re designed for specific tasks and can’t handle anything outside their programming. Weak AI is a category of artificial intelligence ⓒconfined to a finite domain. By performing operations that require considerable time and utilizing methods that are not always accessible to people, this technology can be advantageous to society.
It concentrates on tasks such as responding to user input searches or playing games. While it is only as good as its programming and training, Weak AI still helps ⓓconvert enormous amounts of data into useful information by identifying patterns and generating predictions.
What Is Strong AI?
Strong AI is designed to mimic the cognitive abilities of a human being. It is called “strong” because it has the potential to perform a wide range of tasks, rather than being limited to a specific set of tasks. ⓔThe most an AI system approaches the abilities of a human being, with all our intelligence, emotion, and broad knowledge, the “stronger” the AI system is considered.
One of the key characteristics of Strong AI is that it is designed to learn and ⓕadapt to new situations. It can generalize from its training data and apply its knowledge to new situations. For example, a Strong AI system designed to recognize objects in images can learn to recognize objects it hasn’t seen before based on its previous training. Another key attribute of Strong AI is ⓖthat it is designed to be self-aware and conscious. This means that it can think, reason, and make decisions like a human being. While current AI systems are far from achieving this level of intelligence, some researchers believe that it is possible to create Strong AI in the future.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
ⓑ is → does 또는 is 삭제
(‘비교급+than ~’ 구문에서 접속사로 쓰인 than이 이끄는 비교절의 동사 자리로, 주어(even the ~ intelligence)의 핵심단어 intelligence가 단수이므로 단수동사로 수일치하는 것은 알맞으나, 앞 절의 일반동사를 포함한 동사구 operates under constraints를 대신하는 대동사(do/does/did)가 와야 하므로, is를 does로 고치거나, 비교 구문에서 as나 than 뒤에 반복되는 어구는 생략할 수 있으므로 is를 삭제한다.)
ⓔ The most → The more
(‘the+비교급+주어+동사~’ 형태인 주절(the “stronger” ~ considered)에 상응하여 그 앞에 ‘The+비교급+주어+동사~’ 형태의 비교절이 와서 ‘~할수록 더 …하다’라는 뜻의 ‘the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 …’ 구문을 이루어야 하므로, The most를 ’The+비교급‘인 The more로 고친다.)

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘더욱이, 인공지능이 가짜 정보를 제공한다는 기사가 자주 보도된다.’라는 뜻으로, Moreover(더욱이)를 사용해 앞서 제시된 인공지능의 문제점에 새로운 내용을 추가하는 흐름이므로, 인공지능이 틀리거나 편향된 정보를 많이 만들어 내며, 정보를 만든 사람의 의도를 이해하지 못하고 진위를 판단할 능력도 없다는 문제점들을 설명한 내용의 뒤이자, For example(예를 들어)을 사용해 주어진 문장에 언급된 기사의 구체적인 한 예로 인공지능이 만든 존재하지 않는 판례를 실제 법정에 제출한 변호사의 사례를 제시하는 내용 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Before the Internet, people with vast knowledge were considered to be the most talented. Quiz shows with difficult questions, such as the name of the famous stone castle built by Cormac MacCarthy in 1446, used to ⓐ[be / being] very popular. However, things have changed, and now with the presence of AI, many people question why one would memorize such information. Unlike in the past, this is because you can quickly find answers on the Internet, and if you want, an AI assistant will even find an answer for you.
In 2011, the 74-time winner of a popular American quiz show competed against a supercomputer. The fact ⓑ[that / which] the computer won a resounding victory shows that humans cannot keep up with computers in finding factual information. If that person were to compete with current AI, he would probably lose by a larger margin.
We don’t need to memorize all the answers, and no matter how hard we try, we cannot rival AI in memorizing vast quantities of information. What we need to focus on is obtaining the “right” answers from AI, and the key is to ask the right questions to elicit the answer you want from AI. That is not to say you don’t need to study. To ask the right questions, you must understand the context in which you’re asking the question, and you also need background knowledge on the topic. When AI provides an answer, you must also be able to tell how accurate the answer is. We are currently in an era where the ability to use information is more important than having all the details ⓒ[memorize / memorized]. We must be able to do what AI is not good at rather than focusing on (A)what AI does best.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: be / that / memorize
be / that / memorized
being / which / memorize
being / that / memorized
be / which / memorized
solution:
ⓐ used to 뒤에 쓰였으므로 ‘(예전에) ~였다 (지금은 아니다)’라는 뜻으로 과거의 상태를 나타내는 표현인 ’used to+동사원형‘을 이루는 동사원형 be가 알맞다.
ⓑ 앞의 추상명사구 The fact의 구체적 내용에 해당하는 완전한 절(the computer ~ victory)이 뒤에 이어지므로, 동격 접속사 that이 알맞다.
ⓒ than 뒤에 동명사 형태로 쓰인 having과 목적어 all the details 뒤에 이어져 ‘have+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, 목적어 all the details가 ‘암기되는’ 대상으로 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동의 관계이므로, 과거분사 memorized가 알맞다. 참고로, 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동의 관계일 때는 목적격보어로 동사원형을 쓴다.

AI can often find the information we want quickly, but there are problems with this. AI creates a lot of false or biased information. Further, AI cannot understand the intentions of the person who created the information, nor (A)does it have the ability to judge whether the information is right or wrong. Moreover, stories of AI (B)providing fake information are often reported. For example, there was a case of a lawyer (C)who submitted non-existent cases made by AI to a real court. There has also been an example of AI recommending restaurants that didn’t exist.
Just as much as misleading information, ⓐ______ causes incorrect or even harmful output. A world-famous Internet company had AI (D)study ten years of employee records to create a new employee selection algorithm. However, the company decided not to use the algorithm when it favored men over women. The proportion of male employees was very high and thus the AI’s machine learning had an underlying bias towards male data. (E)When analyzing the information provided by AI, it is always necessary to assess the quality of information — remember: garbage in, garbage out.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): 부정어 nor가 절 앞에 쓰였으므로 ‘조동사+주어+동사원형’의 어순으로 도치되었다.
(B): 전치사 of의 목적어 자리에 쓰인 동명사로, 의미상 주어 AI가 목적격 형태로 앞에 위치해 있다.
(C): a lawyer를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사이며, that으로 바꿀 수 있다.
(D): 사역동사 had의 목적격보어 자리이며 목적어 AI가 ‘학습하는’ 주체이므로 능동 관계를 나타내는 동사원형이 쓰였다.
(E): 접속사를 생략하지 않은 분사구문을 이루고 있으며, When it analyzes로 바꿀 수 있다.
solution: (E) 접속사를 생략하지 않은 분사구문이며 ‘접속사+주어+동사’로 바꿀 수 있으나, 주절의 it은 가주어이고, 진주어인 to부정사구(to assess ~ information)의 의미상 주어, 즉 ‘평가하는’ 주체와 부사절의 주어인 ‘분석하는’ 주체가 일반인이므로, it이 아닌 일반 주어(we, you 등)를 사용하여 When we[you] analyze와 같은 형태로 바꿀 수 있다.

날씨와 계절이 음악 선호에 영향을 미칠 수 있으므로, 가수가 신곡을 차트 상위권에 올리고 싶다면 노래가 날씨나 계절에 어떻게 어울릴지를 고려하는 것이 좋다고 했을 뿐, 따뜻하고 화창한 날씨에 신곡을 발표하는 것이 성공을 보장한다고 한 것은 아니므로 ④ ‘해당 연구는 음악가들이 성공 가능성을 보장하기 위해 따뜻하고 화창한 날씨에 신곡을 발표해야 한다고 권고했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 최근 연구는 사람들의 음악 선호도가 날씨와 계절의 변화에 영향을 받을 수 있음을 시사한다.

body:
Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people to track, adapt to, and even ⓐcontrol the weather. Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer that could measure temperature. The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us. The weather — or more broadly, the climate — has caused significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks.
Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! ⓑIt is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues ⓒthat remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we ⓓwould have been in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears to have been as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, ⓔmaking it look like an enormous snowball.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ would have been → would be (‘~가 없다면’이란 뜻으로 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거 구문에서 if가 생략되어 도치된 부사절 ‘Were it not for ~‘가 쓰였으므로, 주절의 시제를 가정법 과거(주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 ~)로 일치시켜야 한다. 따라서 would have been을 would be로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ have allowed의 목적격보어로 쓰인 to부정사에서, to에 이어지는 동사원형 track, adapt와 ’A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬 연결되고 있으므로 동사원형 control은 적절하다.
ⓑ 진주어 to say에 상응하는 가주어 자리이므로 It은 적절하다.
ⓒ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(remain ~ fossils)을 이끌어 선행사 clues를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(ice ~ earth)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어 it이 있으며 의미상 주어인 앞 절 전체가 거대한 눈덩이처럼 보이게 ‘만드는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 making은 적절하다.

There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively ⓐwet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally ⓑinterrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. ㉠이 기후 변화가 아니었다면, 그 당시 인류는 아프리카 밖으로 퍼져 나가지 않았을지도 모른다.
[2]
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then (A)[moves / moving] onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its ⓒchief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula ⓓdropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to (B)[have triggered / trigger] the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how ⓔfavorable things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year (C)[is / are] many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

body:
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental changes, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.
윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) A recent study examined roughly 100 paintings by William Turner and Claude Monet. (T/F)
(B) The skies depicted in the paintings became increasingly hazy, although industrial air pollution remained relatively stable. (T/F)
(C) The Industrial Revolution brought unprecedented transformations to the skies of London and Paris. (T/F)
(D) Turner and Monet must have been particularly sensitive to changes in atmospheric conditions during their lifetimes. (T/F)
(E) The research concluded that the hazy skies in Turner’s and Monet’s paintings were mainly the result of changes in their artistic techniques. (T/F)
choices: F-T-F-T-T
T-F-T-F-F
F-T-T-F-T
T-F-F-T-F
T-F-T-T-F
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-T-F이다.

(B) 산업 대기 오염이 비교적 일정하게 유지되었음에도 불구하고(→증가하면서), 그림에 묘사된 하늘은 점점 더 흐릿해졌다. (불일치)
(C) 산업 혁명은 London과 Paris의 하늘에 전례 없는 변화를 가져왔다. (일치)
(D) Turner와 Monet은 생전에 대기 상태의 변화에 특히 민감했을 것이다. (일치)
(E) 그 연구는 Turner와 Monet의 그림 속 흐릿한 하늘이 주로 그들의 예술적 기법의 변화로 인한(→환경의 변화를 반영한) 것이라고 결론 내렸다. (불일치)

Historians widely (A)[agree / disagree] that Washington would ⓑbe surely captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.

body:
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. (A)과거의 이러한 자연적 기록들이 없다면, 우리는 오래전의 기후에 대해 전혀 알지 못할 것이다.
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears to have been as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it look like an enormous snowball.

• 접속사가 생략된 부사절로 시작할 것
• 가정법을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 24단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
it, the climate, for, this, be in the dark, record, will, as to, the long past, natural
→ ______
answer: Were it not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 ‘~이 없다면, …일 것이다’의 의미를 갖는 가정법은 현재 사실의 반대 상황을 나타내는 가정법 과거로 ‘if it were not for ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …’의 구조를 취하나, <조건>에 따라 접속사가 생략된 부사절로 시작해야 하므로 if를 생략해야 한다. 가정법에서 if가 생략되면 주어와 동사가 도치되므로 ‘Were it not for ~’로 시작해야 하므로 뒤에 ‘과거의 이러한 자연적 기록들’을 뜻하도록 these natural records와 수식어 of the past를 이어 쓴다.
• 주절은 동일하게 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …’의 구조를 취하므로 조동사 will의 과거형 would와 be in the dark(아는 바가 전혀 없다)를 함께 쓴다.
• ’~에 관해서‘를 뜻하는 구전치사 as to와 ’오래전의 기후‘를 뜻하는 목적어 the climate of the long past를 쓴다.

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways ⓐto influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
There have been two main approaches aimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth. On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface brighter by painting the roof tops white or even ⓑadd highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere more reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it reaches the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would ⓒbe fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or breaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials. For example, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to fertilize ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while taking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ ⓓemitting into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and isolate CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. Still, some believe ⓔthat we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 골라 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
기호 알맞게 고친 표현
(1) ______ : ______
(2) ______ : ______
solution:
ⓑ 흐름상 ‘지붕을 칠하거나 반사율이 높은 덮개를 추가함으로써’라는 뜻으로 전치사 by의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 painting과 등위접속사 or로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 add를 동명사 adding으로 고친다.
ⓓ CO₂를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, CO₂가 ‘방출되는’ 대상이므로 emitting을 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 emitted로 고친다.
오답
ⓐ ‘영향을 미칠 (방법)’이라는 뜻으로 명사 ways를 수식하므로 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to influence는 적절하다.
ⓒ 주어 reflective particles가 ‘발사된’ 대상이므로 조동사 would에 이어지는 수동태(be+p.p.) be fired는 적절하다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(we ~ change)을 이끌어 동사 believe의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Climate engineering includes methods for reflecting sunlight and removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
Making the earth’s surface more reflective can reduce the amount of sunlight that contributes to global warming.
Reflective particles are released into clouds to absorb sunlight and increase the heat reaching the earth’s surface.
Ocean planktons take in carbon dioxide as they grow and carry some of the carbon to the ocean floor.
Considering the energy consumed in carbon capture, the process could reduce total global emissions by no more than one-tenth.
solution:
바람직하지 않은 온난화를 막기 위한 첫 번째 접근법으로, 대기 중의 태양 빛을 반사하여 지표면에 도달하기 전에 산란시키기 위해 비행기나 열기구를 이용해 구름에 밝고 반사율이 높은 입자를 살포한다고 했으므로 ③ ‘반사 입자들은 햇빛을 흡수하고 지구 표면에 도달하는 열을 증가시키기 위해 구름 속으로 방출된다.‘는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 기후 공학은 햇빛을 반사하고 대기에서 이산화탄소를 제거하는 방법을 포함한다.
② 지구 표면을 더 반사적으로 만드는 것은 지구 온난화에 기여하는 햇빛의 양을 줄일 수 있다.
④ 해양 플랑크톤은 성장하면서 이산화탄소를 흡수하고 탄소의 일부를 해저로 운반한다.
⑤ 탄소 포집에 소모되는 에너지를 고려하면, 이 과정은 전 세계 총배출량을 최대 10분의 1만큼 줄일 수 있다.

body:
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
다음 글의 주제를 <보기>의 단어 및 표현들을 알맞게 배열하여 완성하시오.
<보기>
in / of / natural / past climate / the importance / understanding Earth's / records
→ ______
answer: the importance of natural records in understanding Earth's past climate
solution: 제시문 지구의 과거 기후를 이해하는 데 있어 자연 기록의 중요성

body:
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally undetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, ______. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: if the revolutionaries had chosen a different route
but for the dense fog concealing their movement
had the British soldiers crossed the river earlier
if Washington had received additional troops
without moving to Brooklyn and Queens
solution:
미국인들이 몇 백 미터 떨어진 곳에 있던 영국군에게 발각되지 않고 이스트강을 건너 탈출할 수 있었던 이유가 자욱한 안개 덕분이라는 내용이 앞에 언급되었으므로, 그 안개가 없었다면, Washington은 붙잡혀서 영국 정부에 의해 처벌됐을 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ② ‘그들의 이동을 숨겨 준 짙은 안개가 없었더라면‘이 적절하다.
본문변형 had it not been for that fog → but for the dense fog concealing their movement
오답
① 혁명군이 다른 경로를 선택했더라면
③ 영국군 병사들이 더 일찍 강을 건넜더라면
④ Washington이 추가 병력을 지원받았더라면
⑤ 브루클린과 퀸스로 이동하지 않았다면

body:
B: Hey, Haeun, how was your weekend?
G: Oh, hey! I watched the movie Les Misérables on television. My mom is a huge fan of the novel and wanted me to experience the story.
B: No way! I’m a huge fan, too. I’ve read the book twice and the movie once. So, ______?
G: Absolutely. The background music really showed me the characters’ emotions.
B: I couldn’t agree more. The music is so important that I actually looked for a musical version of the story last year.
G: Wow, you’re a real fan of the story! Which version did you like the most?
B: I’m not sure I can choose. However, if you want the most detailed version, you should read the book.
G: Nice! I’d love to read the book and compare it with the film.
B: Definitely do that. You might pick up on some new points if you watch the movie again after reading the book.
G: Thanks for the tip!

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: did you enjoy the movie
did you find the movie intriguing
did you find the movie interesting
did you find the movie predictable
did the movie capture your interest
solution:
자신이 열혈 팬이라면서 책을 두 번 읽었고 영화를 한 번 봤다는 소년이 묻는 질문으로, 이에 대한 답변으로 혜은이 ‘물론이야’라고 답한 후 배경음악이 등장인물들의 감정을 정말 잘 보여줬다는 이유를 설명하고 있으므로, 그것이 재미있었는지 묻는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ④ ‘영화가 뻔하다고 생각했니’는 빈칸에 알맞지 않다.
오답
① 영화를 즐겼니
② 영화가 흥미진진했니
③ 영화가 재미있었니
⑤ 영화가 너의 흥미를 사로잡았니

body:
The Old Man and the Sea is about an old man called Santiago. Santiago hadn’t caught a fish in 84 days, so people thought he was unlucky, maybe cursed. In order to change his terrible luck, Santiago decided to go out into the deep ocean, far beyond the other fishermen. At first, he only caught a small tuna, but at the end of the 85th day, a powerful, magnificent marlin bit Santiago’s fishing hook. The fish was so strong it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days. Santiago learned to ______, to admire its courage, and to appreciate its beauty. When it finally died, he saw it was too big to put inside the boat. Instead, he tied it to the side of his boat and tried to return home. Unfortunately, a shark smelled the marlin’s blood and threatened to eat Santiago’s prized fish.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: think highly of the fish
consider the fish inferior
feel ashamed of his failure
despise his powerful opponent
regard the fish as an unworthy opponent
solution:
85일째 날이 끝날 무렵 Santiago의 낚싯바늘을 문 힘세고 거대한 청새치는 너무 강해서 그의 배를 3일 동안 끌고 다녔다고 했으며, Santiago는 그 용기에 감탄하고, 그 아름다움을 높이 평가하게 되었다는 내용이 이어지므로, Santiago는 청새치의 강인함을 인정하여 존경하게 되었다는 흐름으로 빈칸에는 ① ‘그 물고기를 높이 평가하다[존중하다]’가 알맞다.
본문변형 respect → think highly of
오답
② 그 물고기를 열등하다고 여기다
③ 자신의 실패를 부끄러워하다
④ 자신의 강력한 상대를 경멸하다
⑤ 그 물고기를 상대할 가치가 없는 적수로 여기다

solution:

② Santiago가 장엄한 청새치와 점차 발전시킨 정서적 유대감
③ 상어를 찾아 나섬으로써 자신의 불운을 뒤바꾸려는 Santiago의 필사적인 노력
④ Santiago가 거대한 청새치를 잡기 위해 사용했던 낚시 기술

body:
Santiago saw the shark’s jaws opening and closing in anticipation. He knew this shark no longer cared about the dangers of a boat or of a fisherman. The smell of blood took away the shark’s fear, making ⓐit brave and reckless. Santiago didn’t have much rope left over from tying up the marlin, but he tightened the short remaining piece of rope into a knot on his spear. The shark got closer and closer, mouth open and teeth shining in the sunlight.
(A) The old man could hear the marlin’s skin tearing and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, where the brain was. ⓑIt turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its struggling.
(B) Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He had cast ⓒit too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too short. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. After a moment, ⓓit lay still on the surface before sinking slowly into the water, taking the spear with it.
(C) Santiago’s mind felt strong and clear, his willpower restored. The spear wasn’t very long, too short to hit the shark before it arrived at the marlin. Still, Santiago refused to give up. The shark’s eyes flashed and ⓔhe bit the beautiful fish just above the tail. It ripped and bit and took a huge piece of meat — at least 40 pounds — out of the giant marlin.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: Santiago는 상어의 턱이 기대에 차서 열리고 닫히는 모습을 보고 남은 짧은 밧줄을 창에 단단히 조여 매듭을 지었으며, 상어가 점점 더 가까워졌다는 주어진 글 다음에, 창이 너무 짧아 상어가 청새치에 도달하기 전에 맞출 수는 없었지만 Santiago는 포기하길 거부했고, 상어는 청새치의 꼬리 바로 위를 물어 적어도 40파운드에 달하는 커다란 고기 조각을 가져갔다는 내용의 (C)가 가장 먼저 온다. 다음으로 Santiago가 창을 상어의 머리에 꽂아 넣으며 청새치의 껍질이 찢어지고 뼈가 부러지는 소리를 들을 수 있었고 상어는 몸을 뒤집고 꼬리로 물을 내리쳤다는 내용의 (A), Santiago는 상어의 몸에 너무 깊숙이 박힌 창을 빼내지 못했고, 이미 죽은 상어는 잠시 후 창과 함께 물속으로 천천히 가라앉았다는 내용의 (B)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

<조건>

<보기>
look at, make, ruin, hurt, whenever, so, spirit, the marlin’s, its torn flesh, ugly, powerful
→ The shark ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ it ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: had ruined the marlin’s powerful tail, made it so ugly, hurt Santiago’s spirit whenever he looked at its torn flesh
solution:
• 문맥상 상어가 청새치의 꼬리를 망가뜨리고 흉하게 만들었던 것이 Santiago의 마음을 아프게 했던 것보다 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로 <조건>에 따라 주어진 동사 ruin을 과거완료 형태 had ruined로 변형하고 쓰고 목적어로 the marlin’s powerful tail을 이어서 쓴다. 등위접속사 and 뒤에 과거완료를 이루는 ruined와 병렬 구조를 이루도록 make를 과거분사 made로 변형하고 쓰고 목적어로 앞에 있는 명사구 the marlin’s powerful tail을 대신하는 단수대명사 it을 쓴다.
• made의 목적격보어 자리에는 형용사가 올 수 있으며, ‘너무 ~해서 …하다’는 뜻의 ‘so+형용사+that’ 구문을 이루어야 하므로 so ugly을 이어서 쓴다. <조건>에 따라 접속사 that을 생략해야 하므로, 결과를 나타내는 부사절의 주어 it 뒤에 과거형 동사 hurt를 쓰고 목적어로 Santiago’s spirit을 쓴 후에 ’~할 때마다‘를 뜻하는 부사절 접속사 whenever를 쓰고 주어 he와 주어진 동사 look을 과거동사 looked로 변형하여 쓰고, 전치사 at과 목적어 its torn flesh를 이어서 쓴다.

body:
“Don’t think, old man,” he said. “Sail on this course and take it when it comes.”
But he couldn’t stop thinking. Alone on the ocean, with the poor marlin’s blood ⓐspill into the water, all he could do was ⓑthink. He thought of the great baseball player Joe DiMaggio. He wondered if Joe DiMaggio could have killed the shark without losing the spear. Santiago thought of his own injured hands and wondered how ⓒJoe DiMaggio could play baseball so well in spite of his own injuries. He wondered if he, like Joe DiMaggio, could ignore the unbearable pain and fatigue in his body ⓓenough long to meet his goals.
“Think about something cheerful, old man,” he said. “Every minute now you are closer to home. You sail lighter for the loss of 40 pounds.”
However, Santiago knew this was false hope. Too much blood in the water. Too many sharks. Too far from land with these strong ocean currents. Still, the fisherman promised he would continue to fight. Neither fear ⓔor the loss of his spear could take away his determination. He had to come up with a new weapon, removing the rowing oars and attaching his knife to one.
“Now,” he said. “I am still an old man. But (A)______.”
The breeze got stronger and his boat sped up. He felt fresh, and his determination returned. The sharks would almost certainly take his beautiful marlin, but Santiago would never cease fighting ⓕthem. A man can be destroyed, but never defeated.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ spill → spilling (전치사 with, 목적어 the poor marlin’s blood와 함께 ‘~가 …하면서’를 뜻하는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사’ 구문을 이루어야 하며, 명사구인 the poor marlin’s blood가 ‘바다로 쏟아지는’ 주체이며, spill이 ‘쏟아지다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰여 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사구 into the water가 이어지고 있으며 문맥상 ‘피가 쏟아지고 있는’ 진행의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 spill은 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 spilling으로 고친다.)
ⓓ enough long → long enough (enough가 부사로 쓰여 형용사나 부사를 수식할 때 형용사/부사의 뒤에서 수식하며, 이어지는 to부정사 to meet과 함께 ‘~하기에 충분히 …한‘ 형용사/부사+enough+to부정사’ 구문을 이루어야 하므로 enough long을 부사 long 뒤에 enough가 위치한 어순의 long enough로 고친다.)
ⓔ or → nor (앞에 Neither가 함께 쓰여 ’A도 B도 아닌’을 뜻하는 상관접속사 ’neither A nor B’ 구조를 이루어야 하므로, or를 nor로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 주어가 What, All, The only thing 등이 이끄는 명사절로 일반동사 do와 함께 사용될 때, 주격보어로 오는 to부정사의 to는 생략 가능하므로 all이 이끄는 주어 all he could do에 이어지는 보어 자리에 to를 생략한 원형부정사 think는 적절하다.

Are you keen on exploring the world of literature? Is reading your hobby? Here’s an exciting type of event — literary festivals! These events are hosted in cities with rich literary histories, ⓐseparating authors and readers. Take a glance at these festivals across different regions!
Edinburgh International Book Festival
Where: Edinburgh, Scotland
The Edinburgh International Book Festival happens every year in Edinburgh, which was ⓑdesignated the first UNESCO City of Literature. The festival is one of the largest literary events globally and is typically held in August. It takes place at the University of Edinburgh’s College of Art, creating a village atmosphere. There are outdoor screens for live events, making it an ⓒengaging experience for all.
Frankfurter Buchmesse
Where: Frankfurt, Germany
The Frankfurter Buchmesse is the world’s largest book fair, drawing together publishers, authors, and book fans from across the globe. It is held for five days in October, with the initial two days usually ⓓreserved for trade visitors and professionals, while the following days are open to the general public. This fair is a ⓔmust for anybody, speaking any language, who has ambitions in the publishing world or simply loves to read.

Toronto International Festival of Authors
Where: Toronto, Canada
If you’re in Toronto in September, don’t miss Canada’s oldest literary festival! It’s all about books, authors, and readers coming together. You’ll find Canadian and international writers sharing new stories and talking about writing as an art. Also, if you love mysteries, there’s the Motive Crime & Mystery Festival waiting for you in Toronto as well!
Louisiana Literature Festival
Where: Humlebaek, Denmark
The Louisiana Literature Festival is an annual literary event held in Humlebaek, which is 30 minutes north of Copenhagen, Denmark. It is held around the third weekend of August at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. The festival includes engaging conversations among writers as well as between writers and critics. It also features readings and diverse performances.

• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
shine, get, close, open, teeth, in the sunlight
→ The shark ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: got closer and closer, mouth open, teeth shining in the sunlight
solution:
• 주어진 동사 get은 과거형 동사 got으로 변형하여 쓰고, ‘비교급 and 비교급’ 구문을 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 형용사 close를 비교급 closer로 변형하여 closer and closer를 이어서 쓴다.
• 주절에 콤마(,)로만 연결되어 있으며 의미상 주어가 주절의 주어인 the shark와 다른 mouth와 teeth이며 독립분사구문을 사용하라는 <조건>이 있으므로, mouth로 시작하는 독립분사구문을 영작한다. mouth를 쓰고 being open을 이어서 써야 하지만 빈칸이 두 개 제시되어 있으므로 being을 생략하여 mouth open으로 쓴다.
• and 뒤에는 teeth를 먼저 쓰고, teeth는 ‘빛나는’ 주체이며 shine은 ‘반짝이다’라는 뜻의 자동사이므로 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 shining으로 변형하여 쓰고 부사구 in the sunlight를 이어서 쓴다.

body:
The old man could hear the marlin’s skin tearing and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, where the brain was. It turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its struggling.
Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He had cast the spear too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too short. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. After a moment, it lay still on the surface before sinking slowly into the water, taking the spear with it.

body:
So much of the marlin’s blood flowed into the water from where it had (A)[bitten / been bitten]. Santiago knew more sharks would come before long. He had no spear, and his boat was still many miles from the land. The fisherman knew he would fail, understanding that he had no hope of protecting the beautiful marlin. Santiago didn’t care. He would struggle as long as he could, even if he could not succeed.
“A man can be destroyed,” he said. “But not (B)[defeating / defeated].”
Santiago turned back to his boat and looked at the great fish. The shark had ruined the marlin’s powerful tail and (C)[made / making] it so ugly it hurt Santiago’s spirit whenever he looked at its torn flesh. Santiago felt sorry for catching the marlin and wanted to apologize to the beautiful animal.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: been bitten defeated making
bitten defeated made
been bitten defeated made
bitten defeating making
been bitten defeating made
solution:
(A) 관계부사 where가 이끄는 절의 주어 it(= the marlin)이 타동사 bite(~을 물다)의 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, had에 이어져 과거완료 수동태(had+been+p.p.)를 이루는 been bitten이 알맞다.
(B) 주어인 A man은 defeat(패배시키다, 물리치다)의 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 defeated가 알맞다. 참고로, ‘a man cannot be defeated’에서 앞의 절과 중복되는 부분이 생략된 표현이다.
(C) 과거완료(had p.p.) 시제를 이루는 과거분사 ruined와 등위접속사 and로 병렬구조를 이루고 있으므로 과거분사 made가 적절하다.

body:
G: Mr. Roberts, you don’t look so well. Are you okay?
M: Hi, Sumi. Well, I’m feeling a bit under the weather today.
ⓐ Oh, “feeling under the weather” means feeling slightly ill or being in low spirits. I’m afraid I might have caught a cold or something.
ⓑ What do you mean? The forecast says the weather will be fine today.
ⓒ I’m sorry to hear that.
ⓓ Oh, don’t worry. I’m just feeling a bit down. That’s all.
G: I’m curious where the expression “feel under the weather” came from. Maybe from the fact that bad weather can make you sick?
M: Possibly. Or some suggest that it came from the old sailing ships. They say if a sailor was feeling ill, he would be sent below deck to protect him from the weather.
G: That’s very interesting. Come to think of it, there are many idioms about weather in Korean, too.
M: There must be. Those expressions show how closely the weather and our lives are connected.
G: You said it. By the way, I hope you get well soon, or may I say, lightning fast.
M: There you go. Thanks!

solution: 정답은 ① 이다. (해설 없음)

There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet ⓐwas most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is ⓑbelieved to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, ⓒmeant conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts ⓓthat lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not ⓔspread outside of Africa.

body:
[1]
One of the most famous pieces of art in the world may have been inspired by an unusual weather event. A study suggests that the sky depicted in Edvard Munch’s The Scream may actually be an accurate representation of a weather phenomenon known as “Mother of Pearl Clouds,” a rare phenomenon that may have a big impact on anyone who sees it for the first time. The typical colors in this rare weather event are the same as the colors in Munch’s painting, and the circumstances under which these rare clouds form match Munch’s environment at the time (A)[which / when] he conceived The Scream.
[2]
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found (B)[what / that] over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental changes, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must (C)[have been / be] more keenly aware of the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: (A) when (B) what (C) have been
(A) which (B) that (C) have been
(A) which (B) what (C) be
(A) when (B) that (C) be
(A) when (B) that (C) have been
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(he conceived The Scream)을 이끌어 시간을 나타내는 선행사 the time을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 when이 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(over ~ too)을 이끌어 동사 found의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 조동사 must와 함께 쓰여 ’~했음에 틀림없다‘라는 의미로 과거 사실에 대한 강한 추측을 나타내는 must have p.p.가 와야 하므로 have been이 적절하다.

body:
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics ⓐwhat were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which ⓑinvolve cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found ⓒthat, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, ⓓseems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how desperate things ⓔhad become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many ⓕcarved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ what → that (주어가 없는 불완전한 절(were ~ time)을 이끌어 선행사 advances in mathematics를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 주격 관계대명사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓑ involve → involves (콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 slash-and-burn agriculture를 부연 설명하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 선행사 slash-and-burn agriculture가 단수명사구이므로 이에 수일치하도록 involve를 단수동사 involves로 고친다.)

One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth. On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface brighter by painting the roof tops white or even adding highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert.
