Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people to track, adapt to, and even control the weather. (A) Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer that could measure temperature. (B) The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. (C) However, modern technological solutions to environmental issues often fail to address the fundamental causes of global climate change. (D) But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us. (E) The weather — or more broadly, the climate — has caused significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 인류가 역사적으로 날씨를 추적하고 적응하며 제어하기 위해 다양한 기술을 발전시켜 왔지만, 실제로는 날씨와 기후가 인류의 삶과 역사에 더 큰 영향을 미쳐 왔다는 내용의 글이다. (A)와 (B)에서는 인류가 날씨를 제어하기 위해 사용한 기술의 사례를 제시하고, (D)에서는 인류가 날씨를 제어하는 경우보다 날씨가 인류에게 영향을 미치는 경우가 훨씬 더 많다고 하며 글의 흐름을 전환하고, (E)에서는 날씨와 기후가 강제 이주, 전쟁, 예술 작품 창작 등 인류 역사의 중대한 사건에 영향을 미쳤음을 구체적으로 설명한다. 반면 (C) ‘그러나 현대의 환경 문제에 대한 기술적 해결책은 종종 지구 기후 변화의 근본적인 원인을 다루는 데 실패한다.’는 날씨를 제어하려는 인류의 시도와 그보다 더 큰 날씨가 인류에게 미치는 영향을 다루는 글의 중심 흐름에서 벗어나므로 (C)는 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally undetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: How Dense Fog Delayed the Independence of the New American Nation
The Surprising Impact of Climate Conditions on the American Revolution
Military Strategies That Led Washington to Victory over British Forces
Why British Forces Struggled to Maintain Control over the Colonies
The Long, Tough Journey to American Independence

body:
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental changes, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more (A)______ the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often (B)______ realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.

다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: (A) acutely conscious of (B) associated with
(A) largely indifferent to (B) distinguished from
(A) largely indifferent to (B) contrasted with
(A) highly sensitive to (B) associated with
(A) acutely conscious of (B) distinguished from
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways to influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
There have been two main approaches aimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth. On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface (A)[darker / brighter] by painting the roof tops white or even adding highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere more reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it (B)[reaches / leaves] the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would be fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or breaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials. For example, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to (C)[deplete / fertilize] ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while taking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ emitted into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and isolate CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. Still, some believe that we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: (A) brighter (B) reaches (C) fertilize
(A) darker (B) leaves (C) fertilize
(A) brighter (B) reaches (C) deplete
(A) darker (B) reaches (C) deplete
(A) brighter (B) leaves (C) deplete
solution:
(A) 지표면에서 햇빛을 반사하기 위해 지붕을 흰색으로 칠하거나 사막에 반사율이 높은 덮개를 설치한다고 했으므로 지구 표면의 밝기가 증가시킨다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 brighter(더 밝은)가 적절하다.
(B) 지구 온난화를 막기 위한 접근법을 설명하는 것이므로 태양의 빛이 지표면에 도달하기 전에 산란한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reaches(~에 도달하다)가 적절하다.
(C) 뒤에서 플랑크톤이 성장하면서 대기 중 이산화탄소를 흡수하고, 일부 탄소를 포함한 상태로 바다 바닥에 가라앉는다고 했으므로 해양 플랑크톤의 성장을 촉진한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 fertilize(~의 성장을 촉진하다)가 적절하다.

body:
Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because ______. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how desperate things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: local farmers had developed effective methods of preventing soil erosion
the soil naturally retained moisture throughout the year
seasonal floods serves as a reliable source of water
rivers provided sufficient water for farming
rain was its chief water source
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears to have been as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it look like an enormous snowball.
Climate Change Drives Humans out of Africa
There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. (A)호모 사피엔스는 20만 년 전보다 이전의 어느 시점에 동아프리카에서 진화한 것으로 여겨진다. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not have spread outside of Africa.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• to부정사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 차례대로 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 15단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
Homo sapiens, believe, evolve, in, sometime over
→ ______
answer: Homo sapiens is believed to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago.

body:
Fog Saves the American Revolution
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally ⓐundetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a ⓑtraitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.
A Weather Phenomenon Inspires a Famous Painting
One of the most famous pieces of art in the world may have been inspired by an unusual weather event. A study suggests that the sky depicted in Edvard Munch’s The Scream may actually be an accurate ⓒrepresentation of a weather phenomenon known as “Mother of Pearl Clouds,” a rare phenomenon that may have a big impact on anyone who sees it for the first time. The typical colors in this rare weather event are the same as the colors in Munch’s painting, and the ⓓcircumstances under which these rare clouds form match Munch’s environment at the time he ⓔconceived The Scream.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
<보기>
ⓐ undetected: not noticed by anyone
ⓑ traitor: a person who is betrayed by their friends, their country, etc.
ⓒ representation: a person who is typical of a particular group
ⓓ circumstance: the conditions that affect a situation, action, event etc.
ⓔ conceive: to think of a new idea, plan etc and develop it in your mind
solution:
ⓐ 아무에게도 발견되지 않은: 누구에게도 발견되지 않은
ⓓ 환경: 상황, 행동, 사건 등에 영향을 미치는 조건들
ⓔ 구상하다: 새로운 생각이나 계획 등을 떠올리고 마음속으로 발전시키다

body:
But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us.

Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people to track, adapt to, and even control the weather. (A) Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer that could measure temperature. (B) The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. (C) In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. (D) The weather — or more broadly, the climate — has caused significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks. (E)

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘하지만 우리가 날씨를 제어하기보다는 날씨가 우리를 훨씬 더 많이 제어한다.’라는 뜻으로, 주어진 문장에 But이 쓰였으므로 이 문장 앞에는 인류가 날씨를 제어해 온 내용이, 이 문장 뒤에는 날씨가 인류를 제어하는 내용이 와야 한다. (B) 앞에서 갈릴레오가 최초의 온도계를 구상하고, (C) 앞에서 1902년에 최초의 에어컨이 등장하며, (D) 앞에서 과학자들이 매사추세츠 상공에 비구름을 만든 사례를 통해 인류가 날씨를 제어해 온 과정을 보여 주고 있다. 반면 (D) 뒤에서는 강제 이주, 전쟁, 예술 작품 창작 등 인류 역사 전반에 걸쳐 날씨가 영향을 미친 사례를 제시하고 있으므로, 인류의 날씨 제어에서 날씨의 인류 제어로 글의 흐름이 전환되는 (D)에 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

body:
After some time, a servant came in and told Trevor that the frame maker wanted to speak to him.
“Don’t run away, Hughie,” he said as he went out. “I will be back in a moment.”
The old beggar took advantage of Trevor’s absence to rest for a moment on a bench that was behind him. (A)그는 너무 지치고 비참해 보여서 Hughie는 그를 불쌍히 여기지 않을 수 없었다. Hughie reached into his pocket to see how much money he had. All he could find ⓐ[was / were] a few coins. “Poor old fellow,” he thought to himself. “(B)______.” He walked across the studio and slipped a gold coin into the beggar’s hand.
The old man was ⓑ[startled / startling], and a faint smile came across his dry lips. “Thank you, sir,” he said. “Thank you.”
When Trevor returned, Hughie said goodbye and left the studio, blushing a little at ⓒ[what / that] he had done, and he walked home.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
⦁‘so ~ that …’ 구문을 활용할 것
⦁look, exhaust, miserable, help, pity를 모두 사용하되 필요시 변형하여 쓸 것
⦁13단어로 쓸 것
→ ______
answer: He looked so exhausted and miserable that Hughie could not help pitying him.
solution:
• '너무 ~해서 …하다'는 ‘so ~ that …’ 구문으로 나타내고, '지치고 비참해 보였다'는 주격보어로 형용사를 취하는 look 뒤에 두 형용사를 and로 병렬 연결해 쓴다.
• '지친'은 주어 he가 '지치게 된' 대상이므로 exhaust를 과거분사형 형용사 exhausted로 변형하여 쓴다.
• '불쌍히 여기지 않을 수 없었다'는 '~하지 않을 수 없다'라는 뜻의 ‘cannot help+동명사’를 과거형으로 바꿔 could not help pitying으로 쓴다.

“(B)What an amazing model!” said Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. “ⓒHow a miserable man he looks! How much does the model get for posing?”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ에서 어색한 부분을 찾아서 고친 후, 전체를 다시 쓰시오.
ⓐ eagerly sought after → ______
ⓑ holding out his hat for donations with the others → ______
ⓒ How a miserable man he looks → ______
answer:
ⓐ eagerly sought after → were eagerly sought after
ⓑ holding out his hat for donations with the others → holding out his hat for donations with the other
ⓒ How a miserable man he looks → How miserable he looks
solution:
ⓐ and가 앞의 완전한 절과 연결하고 있으므로, 절의 형태가 되어야 하는데, 주어 his pictures가 '찾아지는' 대상이므로 문장의 동사로 수동태가 필요하다. 복수 주어와 과거 시제에 맞게 were를 추가하여 were eagerly sought after로 고친다. 부사 eagerly가 그 과거분사를 수식하고 있으며, seek after는 '~을 찾다, 구하다'라는 뜻의 구동사이다.
ⓑ 두 손 가운데 나머지 하나를 가리키므로 the others를 the other로 고친다. with one hand와 with the other가 짝을 이루는 구조이고, while이 이끄는 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 he와 같아 생략되었다.
ⓒ ‘~하게 보이다’라는 뜻의 look 뒤에서 형용사 miserable이 주격보어로 쓰이며, 이를 강조하는 감탄문은 ‘How+형용사+주어+동사!’ 구조이므로 a와 man을 삭제한다.

“Well, Alan, did you get the picture ⓑto finish all right?” he asked.

“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I will probably find him ⓓwaiting for me when I get home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I think it is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”
“But he looks ⓔmarvelously in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”

“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”

어법상 알맞은 것은 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ이다.

ⓒ 의문형용사 what이 명사 prospects를 수식하여 의문사구 what prospects를 이루고, ‘의문사구+주어+동사’의 어순인 what prospects you have로 쓰였으므로 알맞다.
ⓓ find의 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어 him이 '기다리고 있는' 주체이므로 현재분사는 알맞게 쓰였다.

“What on earth do you mean?” shouted Hughie.
“The old man you saw today in the studio,” said Trevor, “was Baron* Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, and he buys all my pictures. He gave me a commission to paint him as a beggar. And I must say he looked magnificent in his rags. (A)______; they are an old suit I got in Spain.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie. “Good heavens! I gave him a gold coin!” Hughie sank into the chair in shock.
“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and burst out laughing.
“You should have told me, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name mentioned. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”
“What a fool he must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in the highest spirits after you left. He kept smiling to himself and rubbing his old, wrinkled hands together. I couldn’t understand why he was so interested to know all about you, but I see it all now.”
Hughie sighed. “The best thing I can do is go to bed,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very unhappy.

On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar.” Inside was a check for ten thousand pounds.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: '~했어야 했는데 (하지 않았다)'는 뜻으로, 과거에 하지 않은 일에 대한 유감이나 후회를 나타낸다.
ⓑ: even은 비교급 rarer를 강조하는 부사로, far나 much로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
ⓒ: 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사구로 in order to bring you this letter로 나타낼 수도 있다.
ⓓ: 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문으로, 주어 Hughie가 감정을 느끼는 주체임을 나타낸다.
ⓔ: 명사구 a fool 대신 형용사 foolish를 써서 How foolish he must think I am!으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
solution: to bring you this letter는 ‘commission+목적어+to부정사’(~에게 …하도록 의뢰하다) 구문에서 목적어 me가 수행하도록 의뢰받은 일을 나타내는 목적격보어이므로, 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법으로 설명한 ③은 알맞지 않다.

body:
A: What kind of AI technology do you think will be developed in the future?
B: I think there will be emotional AI technology.
A: (A)What is emotional AI technology exactly?
B: It can read and understand human emotions. (B)______.
위 대화의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말이 되도록 <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 알맞게 배열하시오.
<보기>
emotionally interact / that / I’m / with AI / will / we / pretty sure / be able to
→ ______
answer: I’m pretty sure that we will be able to emotionally interact with AI.
solution:
• 미래에 개발될 AI 기술로서 감정 AI 기술에 대해 언급했으며, 그 기술은 인간의 감정을 읽고 이해할 수 있다고 설명하고 있으므로, 감정 AI 기술을 이용해 미래에 우리가 할 수 있게 될 일에 대해 말하는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 <보기>의 단어와 표현을 사용해 ‘난 우리가 감정적으로 AI와 소통할 수 있다고 꽤 확신해.’라는 뜻이 되도록 한다.
• 확실성의 정도를 나타내는 표현인 ‘I’m pretty sure +that+완전한 절(나는 ~라고 꽤 확신해)‘과 미래의 능력이나 가능성을 나타내는 표현인 ’will be able+to부정사(~할 수 있을 것이다)‘를 활용한다.

AI has been progressing rapidly over the years, and its potential is only beginning to be fully recognized. (A)It is certain that AI will continue to play a significant role in more and more aspects of our lives. Accordingly, these days, a lot of movies feature various kinds of AI. (B)Some AI robots have personalities and emotionally engage with people in the same way that humans do. Furthermore, some AI characters are physically indistinguishable from humans. (C)These movies are not only fun to watch, but also inspiring. (D)Movie studios are spending vast amounts of money using AI to generate realistic digital backgrounds and special effects. (E)They show us what AI might be like in the future and how it could affect us. What AI technology from a movie do you think will be used in our lives in the future?
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: AI가 우리 삶의 점점 더 많은 측면에서 중요한 역할을 할 것이라는 이유로 요즘 많은 영화에 다양한 종류의 AI가 등장하고 있으며, 이러한 영화들이 미래의 AI의 모습과 그것이 우리에게 미칠 영향을 보여 준다는 내용이므로, 영화 제작 과정에 사용되는 AI 기술에 관한 문장인 (D) ‘영화 스튜디오들은 사실적인 디지털 배경과 특수 효과를 생성하기 위해 AI를 사용하는 데 막대한 돈을 쓰고 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 무관하다.

body:
Minority Report, a film set in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify ⓐindividuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes. There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After scanning him and identifying who he is, the advertising system ⓑoffers products that may be appealing to him. Nowadays, we frequently encounter ⓒpersonalized advertisements provided by AI. For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems provide us with advertisements based on our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices have already been developed. However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing ⓓstill. On the other hand, devices ⓔlacking AI have overcome this limitation. They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ lacking(~이 없는) → employing(~을 사용하는)

solution:

This is a science fiction animation that was released in 2014. There is a scene in the movie where a boy meets Baymax, a personal medical aid AI robot. The robot scans the boy’s body to detect potential health problems using its sensors and cameras. (A)그것이 몇 초 이내에 발견하는 것은 그의 팔에 있는 상처입니다. It administers medicine on the wound. In another scene where he has a mood swing, Baymax checks his hormone levels to determine the cause of his mood swing.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• What으로 시작하여 쓸 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 11단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
a wound, within seconds, it, in his arm, discover
→ ______
answer: What it discovers within seconds is a wound in his arm.
solution:
• What으로 시작하라는 <조건>에 따라 ‘What+주어+동사~+be동사 … (~한 것은 바로 …이다)’ 형태의 강조 구문을 활용한다. 먼저 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’을 의미하는 관계대명사 What을 쓰고 관계사절의 주어로 대명사 it을 쓴 뒤, 현재시제를 사용하되 주어가 단수이므로 discover를 단수동사로 수일치한 discovers로 변형한다. 관계대명사 What이 관계사절 내에서 의미상 목적어 역할을 하므로 discovers 뒤에 목적어를 다시 쓰지 않고 부사구 within seconds를 바로 이어서 쓴다.
• What절 주어를 단수 취급하며 단수동사로 수일치한 is를 추가한 후, 보어 자리에 강조 대상인 명사구 a wound in his arm을 써서 문장을 완성한다.

Some AI programs ⓐhave been refined to the point that they can not only identify cancer quickly and accurately, but also ⓑpredicting the chance of getting cancer. AI robots are also used in operating rooms. ⓒBased on the collected data, AI surgical robots can conduct (B)[cognitive / physical] activities such as voice recognition, decision-making, problem-solving, and more. Under the guidance and control of doctors, they can conduct (C)[elementary / autonomous] operations such as cutting and stitching patients undergoing surgery. ⓓAnother example is the development of an AI system to forecast when a hospitalized patient’s condition is likely to get worse. It analyzes the patient’s profile and data and ⓔassigns scores indicating the need for transfer to an intensive care unit. The medical team intervenes when a patient’s scores reach a certain level.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓑ predicting → predict (‘not only A, but also B(A뿐만 아니라, B도)’ 형태의 상관접속사에 의해 조동사 can에 연결되는 동사원형 identify와 병렬연결을 이루어야 하므로 predicting을 동사원형 predict로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주어 Some AI programs가 타동사 refine(~을 개선하다)의 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으며, 흐름상 과거부터 현재까지 ‘개선되어 왔다’라는 의미를 나타내야 하므로, 복수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 복수형 조동사를 사용한 현재완료 수동태(have+been+p.p.)인 have been refined는 알맞다.
ⓔ 단수주어 It에 수일치한 현재형 단수동사 analyzes와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 있으며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사 scores가 있으므로, 능동태이자 현재형 단수동사인 assigns는 알맞다.

body:
The film production industry extensively utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also enables them to make what they intended to express come alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, through which actors’ faces on the screen are aged or made younger. For example, when provided with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program accelerates the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained to learn how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly realistic. These results are maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to the convenience and the naturalness of the results, it is expected that this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the history of makeup techniques in the film industry
the limitations of using AI programs in movie production
the process of casting actors for different age groups in films
the ethical concerns over altering actors’ appearances with AI
how AI makes filmmaking more convenient and its results more realistic
solution:

body:
The film production industry extensively utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also enables them to make what they intended to express come alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, through which actors’ faces on the screen are aged or made younger. For example, when provided with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program accelerates the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained to learn how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly realistic. These results are maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to the convenience and the naturalness of the results, it is expected that this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: AI allows filmmakers to bring their creative intentions to life with greater realism.
A newly developed AI program helps filmmakers digitally age or de-age actors’ faces on screen.
Unlike older techniques, the new automatic program speeds up the workflow.
To train the AI program, a few hundred photos of young adults’ faces were gathered as input.
The AI program successfully maintains realistic results even when the actors display a variety of facial expressions.

body:
Hughie Erskine was a ⓐwonderfully good-looking man, with crisp brown hair, a sculpture-like profile, and grey eyes. He had every accomplishment except ⓑthat of making money. He lived on two hundred pounds a year ⓒwhen an old aunt gave him. He had tried everything. He had gone to the stock exchange for six months. He ⓓhad been a tea merchant for a little longer. Ultimately, he became nothing. He was a delightful, incompetent young man with a perfect profile and no profession.
ⓔTo make matters worse, he was in love. The girl he loved was Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loved Hughie, too, and the colonel was very fond of him. However, he would not hear of any engagement. He would say “Come to me, my boy, when you have got ten thousand pounds of your own, and we will talk about it.”
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ when → which 또는 that (선행사 two hundred pounds a year를 수식하는 관계사절에서 타동사 gave의 직접목적어가 빠져 있으므로, 관계부사 when을 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 고친다. 관계사절의 him은 간접목적어이다.)
오답
ⓐ 형용사 good-looking을 꾸미는 부사 wonderfully는 적절하다.
ⓑ that은 앞의 단수명사 accomplishment를 대신하며, of making money가 뒤에서 수식한다.
ⓓ 과거의 경험을 서술하는 흐름에서 그보다 앞선 일을 나타내고 있으므로 과거완료 had been은 적절하다.
ⓔ '설상가상으로'라는 뜻의 독립부정사를 이루므로, To make는 알맞게 쓰였다.

body:
One morning, Hughie dropped in ⓐto see a great friend of him, Alan Trevor. Trevor was a painter. He was a strange, rough fellow with a bushy red beard. However, when he took up the brush, he was a real master, and his pictures were eagerly sought after.
When Hughie came into the studio, he found Trevor ⓑputting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar. The beggar was standing on a raised platform in a corner of the studio. He was a wrinkly old man with a pitiful expression. He wore a ragged brown cape, and he leaned on a rough stick with one hand while ⓒheld out his hat for donations with the other.
“What an amazing model!” said Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. “ⓓWhat miserable he looks! How much does the model get for posing?”
“A penny an hour.”
“And how much do you get for your painting, Alan?”
“Oh, I get two thousand pounds for this!”
“Well, I think the model should have a share,” cried Hughie, ⓔlaughed. “He is working ⓕjust as hardly as you!”
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 5개이다.
ⓐ of him → of his (a friend와 소유격의 의미를 함께 나타내는 이중소유격이므로 of 뒤에 소유대명사를 쓴다.)
ⓒ held → holding (while이 이끄는 분사구문에서 주어 he가 모자를 '내밀고 있는' 주체이므로 현재분사로 고친다.)
ⓓ What → How (뒤에 형용사 miserable이 이어지므로 「How+형용사+주어+동사」 어순의 감탄문을 이끄는 How로 고친다.)
ⓔ laughed → laughing (주어 Hughie가 '웃는' 주체이므로 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사로 고친다.)
ⓕ hardly → hard ('열심히'라는 뜻의 부사는 hard이며, hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 뜻이므로 원급 비교 구문의 문맥에 맞지 않는다.)
오답
ⓑ find의 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어 Trevor가 마무리 작업을 '하고 있는' 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 putting은 알맞게 쓰였다.

“Don’t run away, Hughie,” he said as he went out. “I will be back in a moment.”

Hughie reached into his pocket to see how much money he had. (A)그가 찾을 수 있었던 것은 몇 개의 동전뿐이었다. “Poor old fellow,” he thought to himself. “He needs money ⓒmore than I do.” He walked across the studio and slipped a gold coin into the beggar’s hand.
The old man was ⓓstartled, and a faint smile came across his dry lips. “Thank you, sir,” he said. “Thank you.”

body:
That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor ⓐ[sat / sitting] by himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture ⓑ[finishing / finished] all right?” he asked.
“Finished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor. “And, by the way, the old model you saw ⓒ[is / are] quite curious about you. I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I will probably find him waiting for me when I get home. Poor old man! (A)내가 그를 위해 무언가를 해 줄 수 있다면 좋을 텐데. I think it is (B)[dreadful / fortunate] that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”
“But he looks (C)[marvelous / unattractive] in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
“You told that old beggar about my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and (D)[irritated / delighted].
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is (E)______. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: sat finished is
sitting finishing are
sat finishing are
sitting finished are
sitting finished is
solution:
ⓐ ‘find+목적어+목적격보어’(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다) 구조에서 목적어 Trevor가 혼자 ‘앉아 있는’ 주체이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 sitting이 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘get+목적어+목적격보어’(~을 …되게 하다) 구조에서 목적어 the picture가 ‘완성되는’ 대상이므로 과거분사 finished가 알맞다.
ⓒ 주어는 명사구 the old model이며, 중심 명사 model이 단수이므로 단수동사 is가 알맞다. you saw는 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 관계사절로, the old model을 수식한다.

① Trevor는 그 그림을 이미 완성하고 액자까지 끼웠다.

body:
“What ⓐon earth do you mean?” shouted Hughie.
“The old man you saw today in the studio,” said Trevor, “was Baron* Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, and he buys all my pictures. He gave me a commission to paint him as a beggar. And I must say he looked magnificent in his rags. Or perhaps I should say in my rags; they are an old suit I got in Spain.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie. “Good heavens! I gave him a gold coin!” Hughie sank into the chair in shock.
“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and ⓑburst out laughing.
“You should have told me, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve ⓒmade a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name mentioned. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”
“ⓓWhat a fool he must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in ⓔthe highest spirits after you left. He kept smiling to himself and rubbing his old, wrinkled hands together. I couldn’t understand why he was so interested to know all about you, but ㉠I see it all now.”
Hughie sighed. “The best thing I can do is go to bed,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very unhappy.
*baron 남작
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 바꾸어 쓸 때 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: in the world
ⓑ: suddenly began to laugh
ⓒ: been fooled by someone
ⓓ: How foolish he must think I am!
ⓔ: a very cheerful mood
solution:
make a fool of oneself는 '스스로 어리석은 행동을 해 창피를 당하다'라는 뜻이므로, 누군가에게 속았다는 뜻의 be fooled by someone으로는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.
오답
ⓐ on earth는 의문문에서 의문사를 강조하는 표현이므로 in the world로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
ⓑ burst out laughing은 '갑자기 웃음을 터뜨리다'라는 뜻이므로 suddenly began to laugh로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
ⓓ ‘What+a(n)+명사+주어+동사’ 감탄문을 ‘How+형용사+주어+동사’로 바꾼 것으로, think의 목적절에서 보어가 명사 a fool에서 형용사 foolish로 바뀌었을 뿐 의미는 같다.
ⓔ the highest spirits는 '매우 좋은 기분'이라는 뜻이므로 a very cheerful mood로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.

• <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용할 것 (필요시 단어를 추가하거나 변형할 것)
• (A), (B) 모두 도치 구문으로 작성할 것
• (A)는 10단어, (B)는 7단어로 빈칸을 완성할 것
<보기>
(A): servant, bring, card, write, on
(B): check, thousand, for
(A) ______ “Monsieur Gustave Naudin, messenger from Baron Hausberg.”
(B) Inside ______.
answer:
(A) a servant brought him a card on which was written
(B) was a check for ten thousand pounds
solution:
(A) ‘bring+간접목적어+직접목적어’(~에게 …을 가져다주다) 구조로 brought him a card를 쓴다. a card를 수식하는 관계절에서 위치를 나타내는 on which가 앞에 놓이고, 적힌 내용을 나타내는 인용구가 주어로 뒤에 오는 도치 구조를 사용하여 on which was written을 쓴다.
(B) 장소를 나타내는 부사 Inside를 문장 앞에 두고, 조건에 따라 동사와 주어를 도치하여 was a check로 쓴다. ‘만 파운드짜리’는 for ten thousand pounds로 나타낸다.

body:
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie. “Good heavens! I gave him a gold coin!” Hughie sank into the chair in shock.
“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and burst out laughing.
“You should have told me, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name mentioned. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”
“What a fool he must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in the highest spirits after you left. He kept smiling to himself and rubbing his old, wrinkled hands together. I couldn’t understand why he was so interested to know all about you, but I see it all now.”
Hughie sighed. “The best thing I can do is go to bed,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very unhappy.
The next morning, as Hughie was at breakfast, (A)한 하인이 그에게 ‘Hausberg 남작의 전령 Gustave Naudin 씨’라고 적힌 카드를 가져다주었다.
“I suppose he has come for an apology,” said Hughie to himself, and he told the servant to let the visitor in.
An old gentleman with gold spectacles and grey hair came into the room and said, “Do I have the honor of addressing Monsieur Erskine?”
Hughie bowed.
“I have come from Baron Hausberg,” continued the messenger. “The Baron — ”
“I beg, sir, that you will offer him my deepest apologies,” stammered Hughie.
“The Baron,” said the old gentleman, with a smile, “has commissioned me to bring you this letter,” and he handed a sealed envelope to Hughie.
On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar.” (B)안에는 만 파운드짜리 수표가 있었다.
When Hughie and Laura got married, Alan Trevor was the best man and the Baron made a speech at the wedding breakfast.
“Millionaire models,” remarked Alan, “are quite rare. But (C)______.”
*baron 남작 / *monsieur ~씨, 님 (영어의 Mr. 또는 Sir에 해당하는 프랑스의 경칭)
윗글의 빈칸 (C)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: rich painters are rarer still
generous beggars are even rarer
poor models are much more common
model millionaires are even rarer
millionaire painters are hard to find
solution:
남작은 '늙은 거지가 보내는 결혼 선물'이라며 Hughie에게 만 파운드짜리 수표를 보내 그와 Laura의 결혼을 축하했고, 앞의 model은 '그림 모델'을, 뒤의 model은 '모범이 되는'을 뜻하므로, 모델이 된 백만장자보다 남에게 선행을 베푸는 모범적인 백만장자가 더 드물다는 의미이다. 따라서 ④ '귀감이 되는 백만장자는 더욱 보기가 힘들다'가 적절하다.
오답
① 부유한 화가는 그보다 더 드물다
② 너그러운 거지는 더욱 드물다
③ 가난한 모델은 훨씬 더 흔하다
⑤ 백만장자 화가는 찾기 어렵다

Hughie Erskine was a wonderfully good-looking man, with crisp brown hair, a sculpture-like profile, and grey eyes. He had every ⓐ______ except that of making money. He lived on two hundred pounds a year that an old aunt gave him. He had tried everything. He had gone to the stock exchange for six months. He had been a tea merchant for a little longer. Ultimately, he became nothing. He was a delightful, ⓑ______ young man with a perfect profile and no profession.
To make matters worse, he was in love. The girl he loved was Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loved Hughie, too, and the colonel was very fond of him. However, he would not hear of any engagement. He would say “Come to me, my boy, when you have got ten thousand pounds of your own, and we will talk about it.”
윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
ⓐ　　　　　　　 ⓑ
choices: inheritance　ambitious
profession　impractical
opportunity　hardworking
qualification　successful
accomplishment　incompetent
solution:
ⓐ 돈 버는 재주만 없었다는 서술에 이어 완벽한 외모와 매력을 묘사하므로, 빈칸 ⓐ에는 '재능, 성취'를 뜻하는 accomplishment가 알맞다.
ⓑ 증권거래소에서 일하고 차 상인으로도 일했지만 결국 직업을 갖지 못했다고 했으므로, 빈칸 ⓑ에는 ‘무능한’을 뜻하는 incompetent가 알맞다.

① 유산　야심 있는
② 직업　비현실적인
③ 기회　근면한
④ 자격　성공한

body:
That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor sitting ⓐby himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right?” he asked.
“ⓑFinished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor. “And, by the way, the old model you saw is quite curious about you. I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I will probably find him waiting for me when I get home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I think ⓒthat is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”
“But he looks marvelous in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me ⓓhow is Laura. The old model was quite interested in her.”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
“You told that old beggar about my private affairs?” cried Hughie, ⓔlooked very red and irritated.
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ that → it (뒤에 이어지는 that절이 진주어이므로 가주어 자리에는 it을 쓴다.)
ⓓ how is Laura → how Laura is (tell의 직접목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이므로 ‘의문사+주어+동사’ 어순으로 고친다.)
ⓔ looked → looking (주어 Hughie가 얼굴이 붉어지고 짜증이 난 상태로 '보이는' 주체이므로 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 전치사 by와 재귀대명사가 결합한 by oneself가 '혼자서'라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로 알맞게 쓰였다.
ⓑ ‘주어+be동사’가 생략된 형태로, 그림이 '완성되고 액자에 끼워진' 대상이므로 과거분사는 알맞게 쓰였다.

One morning, Hughie dropped in to see a great friend of his, Alan Trevor. Trevor was a painter. He was a strange, rough fellow with a bushy red beard. However, when he took up the brush, ⓐ______, and his pictures were (A)[eager / eagerly] sought after.
When Hughie came into the studio, he found Trevor putting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar. The beggar was standing on a (B)[raised / risen] platform in a corner of the studio. He was a wrinkly old man with a pitiful expression. He wore a ragged brown cape, and he leaned on a rough stick with one hand while holding out his hat for donations with the other.
“What an amazing model!” said Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. “How (C)[miserable / miserably] he looks! How much does the model get for posing?”
“A penny an hour.”
“And how much do you get for your painting, Alan?”
“Oh, I get two thousand pounds for this!”
“Well, I think the model should have a share,” cried Hughie, laughing. “He is working just as hard as you!”
윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: he was a real master
he was a terrible painter
he preferred painting beggars
he hardly ever finished a work
he was just an ordinary craftsman
solution:
앞에서 그가 거칠고 투박한 사람이었다고 한 뒤 However로 대조하고 있고, 빈칸 뒤에서 사람들이 그의 그림을 열렬히 찾았다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 ① '그는 진정한 대가였다'가 알맞다.
오답
② 그는 형편없는 화가였다
③ 그는 거지를 그리는 것을 더 좋아했다
④ 그는 작품을 거의 완성하지 않았다
⑤ 그는 그저 평범한 장인이었다

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A)　　　　 (B)　　　(C)
choices: eager　risen　miserable
eager　raised　miserably
eagerly　raised　miserably
eagerly　risen　miserable
eagerly　raised　miserable
solution:
(A) ‘사람들이 그의 그림을 열렬히 찾았다’라는 의미로, 동사구 were sought after를 수식하는 부사 eagerly가 알맞다.
(B) 수식 대상인 platform이 ‘높이 올려진’ 대상이므로, 타동사 raise(~을 올리다)의 과거분사 raised가 알맞다. risen은 자동사 rise(오르다)의 과거분사이다.
(C) look이 ‘~하게 보이다’라는 뜻으로 쓰여 주어 he의 상태를 설명하는 보어가 필요하므로 형용사 miserable이 알맞다. ‘How+형용사+주어+동사!’ 구조의 감탄문이다.

윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: The old model stood on a platform with a cheerful expression.
Hughie visited Trevor's studio to have his own portrait painted.
Trevor had just begun the beggar's portrait when Hughie arrived.
The old model leaned on a stick and held out his hat for donations.
Hughie believed that the painter worked harder than the old model.
solution:
늙은 모델이 한 손으로는 거친 지팡이에 기대고 다른 손으로는 기부를 받으려고 모자를 내밀고 있었다고 했으므로, ④ '그 늙은 모델은 지팡이에 기댄 채 기부를 받으려고 모자를 내밀었다.'는 일치하는 내용이다.

body:
After some time, a servant came in and told Trevor that the frame maker wanted to speak to him.
“Don’t run away, Hughie,” he said as he went out. “I will be back in a moment.”
The old beggar took advantage of Trevor’s absence to rest for a moment on a bench that was behind him. (A)He looked so exhausting and miserable that Hughie could not help pity him. Hughie reached into his pocket to see how much money he had. All he could find was a few coins. “Poor old fellow,” he thought to himself. “(B)He needs money much than I are.” He walked across the studio and slipped a gold coin into the beggar’s hand.
The old man was startled, and a faint smile came across his dry lips. “Thank you, sir,” he said. “Thank you.”
When Trevor returned, Hughie said goodbye and left the studio, (C)blushed a little at what he has done, and he walked home.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(C)에서 어법상 어색한 부분을 각각 두 군데씩 찾아서 고친 후, 전체를 다시 쓰시오. (단, 단어를 추가하거나 삭제하지 말 것)
(A) ______
(B) ______
(C) ______
answer:
(A) He looked so exhausted and miserable that Hughie could not help pitying him.
(B) He needs money more than I do.
(C) blushing a little at what he had done
solution:
(A) 주어 He가 '지치게 된' 대상이므로 exhausting을 과거분사형 형용사 exhausted로 고치고, '~하지 않을 수 없다'라는 뜻의 cannot help는 목적어로 동명사를 취하므로 pity를 pitying으로 고친다. 감각동사 look은 주격보어로 형용사를 취하므로 exhausted와 miserable이 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 보어 자리에 쓰였고, ‘so+형용사+that절’은 '너무 ~해서 …하다'라는 뜻으로 정도와 그 결과를 나타낸다.
(B) than과 짝을 이루는 비교급이 와야 하므로 much를 more로 고치고, 앞의 일반동사 needs를 대신하는 대동사 자리이므로 are를 주어 I에 수일치한 do로 고친다.
(C) 주절의 주어 Hughie가 '얼굴을 붉히는' 주체이므로 blushed를 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사 blushing으로 고치고, 화실을 떠난 시점(left)보다 앞서 일어난 일이므로 has done을 과거완료 had done으로 고친다. 전치사 at의 목적어 자리에 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 이끄는 명사절이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.

That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor sitting by himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right? (A)” he asked.
“Finished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor. “(B) I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have. (C)”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I will probably find him waiting for me when I get home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I think it is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits. (D)”
“But he looks marvelous in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her. (E)”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
“ⓐ______” cried Hughie, looking very red and irritated.
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
And, by the way, the old model you saw is quite curious about you.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그런데 말이야, 네가 본 그 늙은 모델이 너에 대해 몹시 궁금해하더라.’라는 뜻으로, Trevor가 그 모델에게 Hughie에 대한 모든 것을 말해야 했던 이유를 제시하며, 뒤 문장 I had to tell him all about you의 him이 가리키는 the old model을 소개하므로 (B)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

“What on earth do you mean?” shouted Hughie.
“The old man ㉠whom you saw today in the studio,” said Trevor, “was Baron* Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, and he buys all my pictures. He gave me a ⓐcommission to paint him as a beggar. And I must say he looked ⓑmagnificent in his rags. Or perhaps I should say in my ⓒrags; they are an old suit I got in Spain.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie. “Good heavens! I gave him a gold coin!” Hughie sank into the chair in shock.
“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and ㉡bursting out laughing.
“(A)너는 나에게 말해 주었어야 한다, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name ㉢mentioning. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”
“What a fool he must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in the highest ⓓspirits after you left. He kept smiling to ㉣himself and rubbing his old, ⓔwrinkled hands together. I couldn’t understand why he was so ㉤interesting to know all about you, but I see it all now.”
Hughie sighed. “(B)내가 할 수 있는 가장 최선의 일은 잠자리에 드는 것이다,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home ㉥feeling very unhappy.
*baron 남작
윗글의 밑줄 친 ㉠~㉥ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 ㉠, ㉣, ㉥이다.
㉠ 선행사 The old man 뒤에서 saw의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로, 목적격 관계대명사 whom은 알맞게 쓰였다.
본문변형 ㉠은 목적격 관계대명사로 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
㉣ smiling의 의미상 주어인 He와 같은 대상을 가리키므로, 재귀대명사 himself는 알맞게 쓰였다.
㉥ 완전한 절에 이어지는 분사구문을 이끄는 준동사 자리이다. 주어 Hughie가 '느끼는' 주체이므로, 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사 feeling은 알맞게 쓰였다.
오답
㉡ bursting → burst (등위접속사 and로 앞의 과거형 동사 shouted와 병렬을 이루므로 과거형으로 고친다.)
㉢ mentioning → mentioned (‘would like+목적어+목적격보어’(~가 …하는 것을 원하다) 구조에서 목적어 his name이 ‘언급되는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 mentioned로 고친다.)
㉤ interesting → interested (주어 he가 '관심을 갖게 된' 대상이므로 과거분사형 형용사로 고친다.)

<조건>
• <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용할 것 (필요시 변형하거나 단어를 추가할 것)

(A): should, tell
(B): the, thing, go

(B) ______
answer:

solution:
(A) • ‘말해 주었어야 한다’는 과거에 하지 않은 일에 대한 후회이므로 ‘should have+과거분사’를 써서 should have told로 쓴다.
• tell의 간접목적어로 뒤에 me를 두어 You should have told me로 쓴다.
(B) • ‘가장 좋은 일’은 good의 최상급 best를 써서 the best thing으로 쓴다.
• ‘내가 할 수 있는’은 the best thing을 수식하는 관계사절로 쓰는데, do의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 목적격 관계대명사 that을 생략한 I can do로 쓴다.
• ‘잠자리에 드는 것이다’는 is의 보어 자리이므로 to부정사로 나타내지만, 주어부에 do가 포함된 경우 보어로 쓰인 to부정사의 to를 생략할 수 있으므로 원형부정사 go to bed로 쓴다.

Hughie sighed. “The best thing I can do is go to bed,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very ⓓhappy.
The next morning, as Hughie was at breakfast, a servant brought him a card on which was written “Monsieur* Gustave Naudin, messenger from Baron Hausberg.”
“I suppose he has come for an apology,” said Hughie to himself, and he told the servant to let the visitor in.
An old gentleman with gold spectacles and grey hair came into the room and said, “Do I have the honor of addressing Monsieur Erskine?”
Hughie bowed.
“I have come from Baron Hausberg,” continued the messenger. “The Baron — ”
“I beg, sir, that you will offer him my deepest ⓔgratitude,” stammered Hughie.
“The Baron,” said the old gentleman, with a smile, “has ⓕcommissioned me to bring you this letter,” and he handed a sealed envelope to Hughie.
On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar.” Inside was a check for ten thousand pounds.
When Hughie and Laura got married, Alan Trevor was the best man and the Baron made a speech at the wedding breakfast.
“Millionaire models,” remarked Alan, “are quite rare. But model millionaires are even ⓖmore uncommon.”
*baron 남작 / *monsieur ~씨, 님 (영어의 Mr. 또는 Sir에 해당하는 프랑스의 경칭)
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
흐름상 어색한 것은 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ로 총 4개이다.
ⓐ a success(성공한 사람) → a fool(바보)
ⓒ reluctant(꺼리는) → interested(관심 있는)
ⓓ happy(행복한) → unhappy(불행한)
ⓔ gratitude(감사) → apologies(사과)
본문변형 ⓖ rarer → more uncommon

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A), (B)의 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 알맞게 배열하시오. (단, 필요한 것만 골라 쓰고, 필요시 변형할 것)
<보기>
(A) know / would / whether / his name / I / mention / didn't / like / Hausberg / was

solution:

(B) 명사구 a fool을 강조하는 감탄문이므로 what을 사용한다. 조동사 must가 ‘틀림없이 ~하다’라는 강한 추측을 나타내므로 he must think로 배열하고, think의 목적어 역할의 명사절에서 보어 a fool이 문장 앞으로 이동한 형태인 What a fool he must think I am!으로 쓴다. how는 사용하지 않는다.

B: Mom, I’m home. (A)I can’t stand this hot weather!
W: You’ve had a tough time outside, huh? It really seems the earth is getting hotter and hotter every year.
B: I’m going to turn on the air conditioner right away. I’ll close all the windows first.
W: Wait! Why don’t we leave the windows open just for a short while? I read that it’s better to keep them open for some time after you turn on the air conditioner.
B: Why is that?
W: The hot air in the house needs to be pushed out first, especially on a very hot day like this.
B: I see what you mean.
W: Let’s set the temperature at around 26 degrees.
B: At 26? Why so high? Why don’t we choose a very low temperature to cool the air quickly and then turn the air conditioner off?
W: Well, we can actually save more energy by keeping the air conditioner on at a moderate temperature and not turning it on and off frequently.
B: Okay. Then, if it doesn’t feel cool enough, I’ll use the fan, too.
W: Sounds good! You know, saving energy is saving the earth.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: I’m not happy about this hot weather.
This hot weather is very annoying.
I’m annoyed by this hot weather.
I don't mind this hot weather.
I'm used to this hot weather.
solution:
‘I can’t stand ~‘는 ‘~을 정말 못 참겠다’라는 의미로, 어떤 상황, 행동 등에 대해 더 이상 참을 수 없을 만큼 화나거나 싫어하는 감정을 표현할 때 사용하며, ‘I’m not happy about ~‘ ’I’m annoyed by ~‘ ’~ is very annoying.‘과 같은 표현으로도 화나거나 싫어하는 감정을 나타낼 수 있다. ‘I don't mind ~’는 ‘~을 신경 쓰지 않는다’라는 뜻이고, I'm used to+명사(구)’는 ‘~에 익숙하다’를 뜻하므로 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은 ④ ‘이 더운 날씨를 신경 쓰지 않아요.’, ⑤ ‘이 더운 날씨에 익숙해요’이다.
오답
① 이 더운 날씨가 마음에 들지 않아요.
② 이 더운 날씨는 너무 짜증나게 해요.
③ 이 더운 날씨 때문에 짜증나요.

body:
Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people to track, adapt to, and even control the weather. Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer that could measure temperature. The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us. The weather — or more broadly, the climate — has caused significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Technological progress made it possible for humans to monitor, adjust to, and regulate the weather.
Galileo developed the concept of a thermometer about three centuries before air conditioner was introduced.
Scientists succeeded in generating rain clouds over Massachusetts before the 20th century.
Weather exerts a much greater influence on human life than humans exert on it.
Climatic factors have influenced human history in various ways, affecting forced migration, military conflicts, and artistic creations.
solution:
1946년에(=20세기 중반) 연구자들이 매사추세츠주 상공에서 비구름을 만들어 내는 데 성공했다고 설명하므로, ③ ‘과학자들은 20세기 이전에 매사추세츠주 상공에서 비구름을 만들어 내는 데 성공했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 기술의 발전은 인간이 날씨를 관찰하고, 날씨에 적응하고, 날씨를 통제하는 것을 가능하게 했다.
② Galileo는 에어컨이 도입되기 약 3세기 전에 온도계의 개념을 고안했다.
④ 날씨는, 인간이 날씨에 미치는 영향보다 인간의 삶에 훨씬 더 큰 영향을 미친다.
⑤ 기후 요인은 강제 이주, 군사적 충돌, 예술 작품의 창작에 영향을 미치면서, 다양한 방식으로 인류 역사에 영향을 미쳐 왔다.

body:
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. ⓐIt were not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
About 55-56 million years ago, ⓑthe global mean temperature appears to be as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it look like an enormous snowball.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ에서 어법상 어색한 부분을 한 군데씩 찾아 각각 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
어색한 표현         알맞게 고친 표현
ⓐ ______ → ______
ⓑ ______ → ______
answer:
ⓐ It were not → Were it not 또는 If it were not
ⓑ to be → to have been
solution:
ⓐ ‘~이 없다면’이라는 뜻의 현재 사실을 반대로 가정하는 가정법 과거구문의 if절은 ‘if it were not for ~’로 쓰이며, if가 생략되면 주어와 동사가 도치된 ‘were it not for ~’의 형태로 쓰이므로, It were not에 if가 없으므로 이를 도치된 Were it not으로 고치거나 또는 if를 넣어 If it were not으로 고친다.
*본문에는 Were it not for ~가 쓰였음
ⓑ 지구의 평균 온도가 23도나 되었던 것은 약 5천 5백만 년에서 5천 6백만 년으로 과거의 일이므로, 주절의 현재 시제(appears)보다 더 앞선 시간을 나타내기 위해 완료부정사(to have+p.p.)를 써야 한다. 따라서 to be를 to have been으로 고친다.

body:
There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time ______.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: might have experienced more favorable living conditions in Africa
would have accelerated their migration into the Arabian peninsula
might have developed different migration routes across Africa
would not have maintained a stable population
might not have spread outside of Africa
solution:

There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time ______.

choices: Why is climate change considered an important factor in human history?
Where is Homo sapiens believed to have evolved?
How did the climate of eastern Africa change from 125,000 years ago?
What were the specific environmental changes in eastern Africa caused by the drier climate?
What made the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas suitable migration routes during the wet period?

body:
Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that ⓐwere far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region ⓑthat depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, ⓒcombined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans ⓓthemselves left behind a clue of how desperate things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year ⓔis many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ is → are (장소를 나타내는 부사구 ‘Among ~ year‘가 강조를 위해 문장의 맨 앞으로 이동하면 1형식 동사와 주어는 도치된다. 따라서 문장의 주어는 뒤에 이어지는 복수명사구 many carved stones이므로 이에 수일치하여 단수동사 is를 복수동사 are로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치하며, 선행사 advances in mathematics가 복수명사구이므로 이에 수일치한 복수동사 were는 적절하다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(depended ~ systems)을 이끌어 명사구 a region을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
ⓒ 뒤에 동사 seems가 있으므로, 이중 콤마(,)로 주어인 The drought을 부연 설명하는 분사구가 삽입된 형태로, 명사구 The drought가 전쟁 및 다른 갈등과 ’결합된‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 combined는 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어 The Mayans를 강조하여 ’마야인들 자신이‘라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로, 복수형 재귀대명사 themselves는 적절하다.

body:
Fog Saves the American Revolution
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, (A)[which / where] British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally undetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, (B)[had it / it had] not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, (C)[what / which] made the United States an independent nation.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) / (B) / (C)
choices: where / it had / which
which / had it / which
where / had it / what
where / had it / which
which / it had / what
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(British ~ attack)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 장소를 나타내는 선행사 Brooklyn and Queens를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다.
(B) ‘~이 없었다면’이라는 뜻의 과거 사실과 반대되는 상황(그 안개가 없었다면)을 가정하는 가정법 과거완료구문은 ‘if it had not been for ~’ 또는 if를 생략한 도치구문 ‘had it not been for ~’의 형태로 쓰이며, that 뒤에서 두 완전한 절이 접속사 없이 연결될 수 없으므로 if가 생략된 형태임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 도치된 had it이 적절하다.
(C) 불완전한 절(made ~ nation)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 절 전체를 선행사로 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways to influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
(A) On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface brighter by painting the roof tops white or even adding highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere ⓐmore reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it reaches the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would be fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
(B) There have been two main approaches ⓑaimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth.
(C) The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or ⓒbreaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials.
For example, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to fertilize ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while ⓓtaking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ emitted into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and ⓔisolating CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. Still, some believe that we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 최근 과학자들이 기후 시스템 자체에 영향을 미치는 ‘기후 공학’ 연구를 본격화하고 있다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 기후 공학의 두 가지 주요 접근법이 있으며 그 첫 번째 접근법인 태양 광선을 반사하여 지구 온난화를 늦추는 방법을 설명하는 (B), 첫 번째 접근법인 태양 광선을 반사하는 구체적인 방법 중 지상에서(On the ground level) 실행하는 방안과 대기 수준에서(On the atmospheric level) 실행하는 방안을 구체적으로 설명하는 (A), 다른 접근법인 이산화탄소를 포집하여 지하에 저장하거나 분해하는 것을 설명하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ isolating → isolate 또는 to isolate (흐름상 ‘이산화탄소를 포집하고 분리하는 데 사용되는’을 뜻하므로 to부정사 to capture와 등위접속사 and로 병렬로 연결되어야 한다. 따라서 isolating을 to부정사 to isolate 또는 to를 생략한 동사원형 isolate로 고친다.)

body:
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental changes, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
A recent study of paintings by Turner and Monet revealed that the increasingly hazy ______ depicted in their works reflected rising industrial ______ ______ during the Industrial Revolution demonstrating that ______ ______ accurately captured environmental changes although ______ is generally viewed as distinct from realism.
answer: skies, air pollution, impressionist artists, impressionism
solution: 요약문 Turner와 Monet의 그림들에 대한 최근 연구는 그들의 작품에 묘사된 점점 더 흐릿해지는 하늘이 산업혁명 동안 증가하는 산업 대기 오염을 반영했다는 것을 밝혀냈으며, 이는 인상주의가 일반적으로 사실주의와 구별되는 것으로 여겨지지만 인상주의 화가들이 환경 변화를 정확하게 포착했음을 보여준다.

body:
Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
(A)약 5천 5백만 년에서 5천 6백만 년 전쯤 지구의 평균 온도는 23도만큼 높았던 것으로 보인다, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it look like an enormous snowball.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• to부정사를 사용할 것
• 원급비교를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 빈칸에 11단어로 쓸 것
<보기>
mean temperature, be, global, appear
→ About 55-56 million years ago, ______ 23°C.
answer: the global mean temperature appears to have been as high as
solution:
• ’지구의 평균 온도‘를 뜻하는 주어 the global mean temperature를 쓰고 ’appear+to부정사(~인 것처럼 보인다)‘를 사용하여 주어에 수일치한 단수동사 appears와 보어 to부정사를 써야하는데, 과거에 지구의 평균 온도가 23도나 되었던 것을 나타내야 하므로 주절의 현재 시제(appears)보다 더 앞선 시간을 나타내기 위해 완료부정사(to have+p.p.)를 써야 한다. 따라서 to have been으로 변형하여 이어 쓴다.
• 원급비교 ’as ~ as …(~만큼 …한)‘를 사용하여야 하며, been에는 형용사가 이어져야 하므로 as high as를 쓴다.

body:
There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not have spread outside of Africa.

Effects of Long-Term Drought on African Food and Water Supplies
Changing Climate Patterns That Paved the Way for Early Human Migration
How Ancient Climate Changes Influenced the Evolution of Homo sapiens
The Fundamental Factors Revealed by Early Human Settlement Patterns

One of the most famous pieces of art in the world may have been inspired by an unusual weather event. A study suggests that the sky depicted in Edvard Munch’s The Scream may actually be an accurate representation of a weather phenomenon known as “Mother of Pearl Clouds,” a rare phenomenon that may have a big impact on anyone who sees it for the first time. The typical colors in this rare weather event are the same as the colors in Munch’s painting, and (A)이 드문 구름들이 형성되는 환경이 Munch가 ‘절규’를 구상했던 당시의 환경과 잘 들어맞는다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용할 것
• 관계부사는 생략할 것
• form을 자동사로 사용할 것
• 대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
this, the circumstances, cloud, match, conceive, under, rare, Munch’s environment
→ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ at the time ______ ______ The Scream
answer: the circumstances under which these rare clouds form match Munch’s environment, he conceived
solution:
• ‘이 드문 구름들이 형성되는’의 수식을 받는 주어 the circumstances를 쓴 뒤, 뒤에 수식하는 절의 주어 these rare clouds와 자동사 form가 이어지므로 완전한 절을 이끄는 ‘전치사+관계대명사’가 수식 절 앞에 쓰여야 한다. 일반적으로 선행사 the circumstances는 전치사 under와 함께 쓰이므로, 목적격 관계대명사 which와 함께 under which로 완전한 절(these rare clouds form)을 이어준다.
• 주어 the circumstances에 대한 동사로, 복수동사 match를 쓰고 목적어 Munch’s environment를 쓴다.
• the time을 선행사로 하는 ‘Munch가 ‘절규’를 구상했던‘의 수식절을 영작해야 하며, <조건>에 따라 관계부사는 생략해야 하므로 뒤에 완전한 절을 이어주되, 대명사를 사용해야하므로 남은 빈칸에 he conceived를 넣어 완성한다.

body:
Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of ______. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how ineffective their scientific achievements were in preventing the civilization’s decline
how greatly declining rainfall affected their agricultural practices
how significantly their conflicts contributed to the civilization’s decline
how seriously deforestation threatened their water resources
how desperately they longed for rain to save them

본문변형 how desperate things had become → how desperately they longed for rain to save them

body:
Air Pollution Brings the Hazy, Dreamy Impressionist Skies
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution ⓐincreased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution ⓑtransformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental ⓒstability, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the ⓓatmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather ⓔaccurately, a reality of environmental changes.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓒ stability(안정성) → changes(변화들)

body:
In 2015, Matthew McConaughey, an American actor and producer, gave the (A)commencement speech at the University of Houston. Speaking to some 4,000 graduates, he shared personal stories and lessons, ⓐhoping to help young people find their paths in life.
Today, I’m going to talk to you about some things I’ve learned in life. I hope you think of them as (B)signposts or approaches that can guide your paths in life. You can apply them in your own lives, in your own ways if you ⓑchoose to. So here we go.
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. ㉠______, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of (C)standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. ㉡______, if happiness is ⓒthat you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. ㉢______, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do ⓓwhat we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a (D)means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally ⓔbecame happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own (E)reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ that → what (전치사 after의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you’re after)을 이끌어, is의 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that을 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 명사절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ choose는 to부정사를 목적어로 취할 수 있으며, 동사(구)의 반복을 피하기 위해 to부정사에서 to만 남기고 나머지를 생략한 형태인 대부정사를 쓸 수 있으므로, choose와 to부정사의 to 뒤에 동사원형 apply를 포함한 동사구 ‘apply them in your own lives, in your own ways’가 생략된 choose to는 알맞다.
ⓔ 흐름상 주어 I에 대한 첫 번째 과거동사 began과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬연결을 이루어야 하며, 뒤에 보어인 비교급 형태의 형용사 happier가 있으므로, 2형식 동사 become의 과거형인 became은 알맞다.

Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to ⓐfinding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. (A)저는 거기에 없었어야 했고, Wooderson도 그러지 말아야 했습니다. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we ⓑdo.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually (B)[realizing / ignoring] who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not ⓒhelp us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or ⓓengaging in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and (C)[keep / stop] giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are (D)[healthier / unhealthier] for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things ⓔleaving in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓐ 명사 step 뒤에 전치사 to가 와서 ‘step to+명사(구)/동명사(구)(~로의 단계)’의 형태로 쓰일 수 있으며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 our identity가 있으므로, 목적어를 취할 수 있는 동명사 finding은 알맞다.
ⓑ 일반동사(구)의 반복을 피하기 위해 대동사 do/does/did를 쓸 수 있으므로, 흐름상 현재형 복수동사 belong을 대신하는 대동사 do는 알맞다.
오답
ⓒ help → helps (동명사구 주어인 ‘Defining ourselves by who we are not’에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 동명사(구)는 단수 취급하므로, 수일치를 위해 복수동사 help를 단수동사 helps로 고친다.)
ⓓ engaging → engage (조동사 may 뒤에 두 개의 동사원형이 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결된 형태의 동사구 bully and gossip과 등위접속사 or에 의해 병렬연결을 이루어야 하므로, engaging을 동사원형 engage로 고친다.)
ⓔ leaving → left (동사 have와 목적어인 명사구 important things 뒤에 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사가 올 수 있으나, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘남겨진’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 leaving을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 left로 고친다.)

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• ‘조동사+have+p.p.’를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어를 사용할 것 (중복 사용 가능)
• 9~10단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
there, should, neither
→ ______
answer: I shouldn’t[should not] have been there, and neither should Wooderson.
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 ‘조동사+have+p.p.’를 사용하되, <보기> 제시어로 조동사 should가 있으므로 과거의 일에 대한 후회를 나타내는 표현인 ‘shouldn’t[should not]+have+p.p.(~하지 말았어야 했다)‘를 사용해 주어 I 뒤에 shouldn’t 또는 should not과 have를 쓰고, ‘있다’를 뜻하는 동사 be의 과거분사인 been을 추가한 후, 장소부사 there를 쓴다.

body:
Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves ⓐ[overcoming / to overcome] that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and (A)______. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, ⓑ[abandoning / abandoned] your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined ⓒ[having / to have] to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing what you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, overcoming your fears. You are (B)the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: overcoming abandoned having
overcoming abandoning to have
to overcome abandoned to have
to overcome abandoning to have
to overcome abandoning having
solution:
ⓐ ‘~을 부추겨서 …하게 하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘dare+목적어+to부정사(구)’를 사용하므로, 동사 dare와 목적어인 ourselves 뒤에 to부정사인 to overcome이 알맞다.
