body:
Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. Whichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Education keeps people within the boundaries they are already familiar with.
As a child, Sotomayor had clearly pictured herself working at the Supreme Court.
According to Sotomayor, education becomes less valuable when it is not used well.
Sotomayor believes that improving one's community requires a highly visible role like a Supreme Court justice.
Sotomayor's family taught her to judge happiness by her career achievements.

⑤ Sotomayor의 가족은 그녀에게 자신의 직업적 성취로 행복을 판단하라고 가르쳤다. (→그녀의 가족은 자신이 직업으로서 무슨 일을 하는가가 아니라 다른 사람들에게 무엇을 베푸는가로 행복을 측정하라고 가르쳤다.)

body:
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Career success is the most dependable source of lasting happiness.
Happiness and joy are similar in that both rely on achieving specific goals.
Enjoying our daily work is the surest way to achieve greater external success.
We should pursue joy in the process rather than happiness dependent on results.
We should keep raising our standards after reaching each goal to stay motivated.

body:
Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Discovering our true self usually begins with (A)______ things that do not truly represent us, and (B)______ such things leaves us with only what really matters.
(A) (B)
choices: recognizing embracing
recognizing removing
ignoring embracing
hiding removing
ignoring analyzing

Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.

G: Daehun, did you know that sunsets on Mars are different from those on Earth?
B: Really? You mean they’re not red and orange?
G: That’s right, they aren’t. Sunsets are somewhat blue on Mars.
B: Wow! Why is that?
G: It’s because of the Martian atmosphere. Unlike Earth’s atmosphere, it’s full of large dust particles.
B: How does that affect the sunset colors?
G: When the sun sets on Mars, these particles filter out the red light from the sun and allow only the blue light to reach our eyes.
B: Oh, that’s really surprising!
G: Plus, the sky on Mercury would look black during the day because the planet has virtually no atmosphere.
B: Interesting! ______ learn that each planet has such unique features.

how different atmospheric conditions affect the color of planets’ skies
the influence of solar distance on the temperatures of different planets
the way planetary rotation affects the length of day and night
the reasons behind the formation of dust storms on Mars

body:
Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, curious about (A)[that / what] lies beyond our world. This inherent desire to explore the universe has encouraged technological innovations (B)[what / that] can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements are space telescopes and space robots, (C)[that / which] have paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: what / that / which
that / what / which

that / that / that
what / what / which
solution:
(A) ‘자동사+전치사구’ 구조의 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(lies beyond our world)을 이끌어 전치사 about의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하며, 문맥상 우리의 세계 너머에 ‘무엇이’ 있는지를 궁금해 하는 것이므로 의문사와 주어의 역할을 동시에 하여 명사절인 간접의문문을 이루는 의문대명사 what이 적절하다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ pursuit)을 이끌어 명사구 technological innovations를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(have ~ space)을 이끌어, 앞의 명사구 space telescopes and space robots(우주 망원경들과 우주 로봇들)를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.

When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and ⓐmade some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. (A) To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere. (B)
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that ⓑis not visible on Earth. (C) This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, ⓒallowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. (D) The data and images ⓓare gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics. (E)
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, ⓔstands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?

solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘결과적으로, 우리가 지구 표면에서 보는 우주는 실제 모습과 상당히 다를 수 있다.’라는 뜻으로, 앞의 내용으로 인한 결과를 나타내는 연결어 Consequently가 쓰였으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 지구 표면에서 관측한 우주의 모습이 실제 모습과 달라질 수 있는 원인이 제시되어야 한다. 따라서 지구의 대기가 우리 시야에 장애물을 만들어 관측에 왜곡을 일으키고 대기권 너머의 일부 물체들을 보이지 않게 한다는 내용 다음이자 한계를 극복하기 위해 망원경을 대기 너머의 우주로 발사한다는 내용 앞인 (A)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the contrasting observational abilities of two space telescopes
the discovery of new planets through astronomical observations
the challenges of maintaining space telescopes over extended missions
the engineering challenges of designing a honeycomb-patterned mirror
the enhancement of astronomical observations through Webb's advanced technology

Thorough space exploration goes beyond remote observations and includes up-close examinations of celestial bodies, material collection, and on-site experiments. While human astronauts can be sent on these missions, it is often safer and more cost-effective to use robots. Robots can better withstand the harsh conditions of space, including extreme temperatures and high radiation levels that can pose serious risks to human astronauts.

body:
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers ⓐlaunched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the presence of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, ⓑmarking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes continued their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle designed to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. ⓒEquipped with various scientific instruments, rovers conduct experiments and investigations while in motion, functioning like roaming laboratories. An iconic example is Curiosity, ⓓwhich landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. These findings suggest the possibility ⓔwhich some form of life might have existed on Mars in the past.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 관계대명사 that을 두 번 사용할 것
• 배수사를 사용한 비교 표현을 두 번 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것 (숫자도 한 단어로 봄)
<보기>
6.25 times, large, result in, wide, feature, an image collection area, three times, a honeycomb-patterned mirror, about
→ It ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider
solution:
• 단수주어 It에 수일치한 단수동사 features와 목적어 a honeycomb-patterned mirror를 쓰고, 목적어인 a honeycomb-patterned mirror를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하되 <조건>에 따라 관계대명사 that를 쓰고, 선행사에 수일치한 단수동사 is를 쓴 다음, 숫자 앞에서 ‘약, 대략’이라는 뜻을 나타내는 부사 about 뒤에 <조건>에서 언급한 배수사를 사용한 비교 표현인 three times larger를 이어서 쓴다.
• 완전한 절(It ~ mirror)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지고 있으므로 <조건>에 따라 분사구문으로 영작한다. 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용(It ~ mirror)이 ‘초래하는’ 주체이므로 ’~을 초래하다‘를 뜻하는 구동사 result in을 능동의 의미인 현재분사구 resulting in으로 변형하여 쓰고 전치사 in 뒤에 목적어인 an image collection area를 쓴다.
• 명사구 an image collection area를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작한다. 관계대명사 that과 선행사에 수일치한 단수동사 is를 쓰고, 배수사 6.25 times(6.25배)와 형용사 wide의 비교급 wider를 이어 쓴다.

All the philosophical dilemmas about whether translation “reflects” or instead “transforms” what’s in the original ⓐ[needs / need] to be swept aside. This is exactly the dichotomy ⓑ[that / what] Merleau-Ponty’s account of perception is trying to free us from: are we “seeing” objects or “constituting” them? Neither, because we perceive things in a world we live in and have the power ⓒ[to transform / transforms]: a chair is something we can go sit in; a mug is something we can pick up. (A) One of Merleau-Ponty’s many great metaphors is that perception neither finds the world nor creates it: it reveals it, which he expresses using the term révélateur, the developing fluid for photographs in a darkroom. (B) Photographic development involves a series of chemical reactions that require precise temperature and timing. (C) The act of seeing develops what’s in the world, like developing a photograph. (D) Likewise, a translation “develops the photograph” of the original text. (E) Translators don’t simply “recognize” what’s there, but nor are we “changing” it into anything it isn’t already, though we can be more or less aggressively interventionist in our darkroom. As a translator I take up the affordances of the original, moving through its world and ㉠______.

choices: what realizing go
what realized to go
that realized go

that realized to go
solution:

You want to ask somebody out, but you fear ⓑthat he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they ⓒare deserved. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity ⓓto overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and ⓔgive them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ are deserved → deserve (앞의 주어 they가 가리키는 fears가 타동사 deserve(~을 받을 만하다)의 주체이며, 명사구 the credit이 의미상 목적어에 해당하므로, they 이하는 앞에 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that이 생략된 채로 선행사인 the credit을 수식하는 관계사절이며, 능동태 타동사 deserve의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절의 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 수동태 are deserved를 능동태 deserve로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 scare의 목적어 자리이며, to부정사의 의미상 주어인 I와 동일한 대상이므로, 재귀 용법의 재귀대명사 myself는 알맞다.
ⓔ 동사원형으로 시작하는 앞의 명령문(confront your fears)과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 명령문을 이끌어야 하므로, 동사원형 give는 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사는 생략할 것
• 형용사적 용법의 to부정사를 한 번 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• (1)은 4단어, (2)는 8단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
dare, increase, overcome, an asset, our need
I think (1) ______ because it (2) ______ that fear.
answer:
(1) fear is an asset
(2) increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome
solution:
(1) think의 목적어 자리에 <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사 that은 생략하고 완전한 절이 이어지도록 ‘주어+be동사+보어’ 형태로 fear is an asset을 쓴다.
(2) because가 이끄는 절의 주어 it에 수일치하도록 increase를 단수동사 increases로 변형하고, 목적어로 명사구 our need를 쓴다. <조건>에 따라 형용사적 용법의 to부정사를 사용해 명사구 our need를 수식하는 to부정사구가 이어지도록 dare를 to부정사인 to dare로 변형한다. 이어서 ‘~을 부추겨서 …하게 하다’라는 뜻의 ‘dare+목적어+to부정사(구)’를 사용하되, to부정사인 to dare의 의미상 주어(우리)와 dare의 목적어가 동일한 대상이므로 재귀 용법의 재귀대명사 ourselves를 목적어 자리에 쓴 후, overcome을 to부정사인 to overcome으로 변형한다.

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. ⓐWhichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you ⓑto grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and ⓒexpose you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless (A)______. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something ⓓmuch more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring ⓔthat no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me ⓕmeasure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓒ expose → exposes (노출시키는 주체가 주어 it이므로, 단수동사 takes가 이끄는 동사구 ‘takes ~ know’와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 동사구를 이끌도록 expose를 단수동사 exposes로 고친다.)
ⓕ measure → to measure (동사 teach는 ‘teach+목적어+목적격보어(~에게 …하도록 가르치다)’의 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, taught와 목적어 me에 이어진 목적격보어 자리의 동사원형 measure를 to부정사인 to measure로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ ‘~에게 …할 권한을 부여하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘empower+목적어+to부정사(구)’를 사용하므로, empowers와 목적어 you 뒤에 이어진 to부정사 to grow는 알맞다.
ⓓ -thing으로 끝나는 부정대명사는 형용사가 뒤에서 수식하며, much는 ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 비교급을 강조할 수 있으므로, something 뒤에 비교급 강조 부사 much와 비교급 형태의 형용사 more significant가 이어진 형태의 much more significant는 알맞다.

body:
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 두 번째 단락에 드러난 ‘I’의 태도 변화로 알맞은 것은?
choices: indifferent to success → hungry for fame
eager for recognition → obsessed with awards
confident in his talent → doubtful of his ability
fixated on results → absorbed in the work itself
engrossed in the task itself → focused on results

body:
Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: The director's offer of additional scenes was turned down.
Problems in some scenes were noticed as soon as the film was released.
Recognizing the places we don't fit in is regarded as less valuable than recognizing where we belong.
Letting go of friends who have a bad influence on us will lead us to healthier environments.
We are advised to find our real selves before removing what does not suit us.
solution:
여러분의 가장 좋은 면을 끌어내지 못하고, 너무 많이 괴롭히거나 험담을 할 수도 있는 친구들에게 시간과 에너지를 그만 쏟으라고 하며, 그들을 놓아줄 때 자신에게 더 건강한 곳에서 더 많은 시간을 보내게 될 것이라고 했으므로, ④ '우리에게 나쁜 영향을 미치는 친구들을 놓아주는 것은 우리를 더 건강한 환경으로 이끌 것이다.'는 일치하는 내용이다.
오답
① 추가 장면에 대한 감독의 제안은 거절되었다. (→‘I’는 신이 나서 그 제안을 수락했다.)
② 영화가 개봉되자마자 일부 장면의 문제점이 발견되었다. (→몇 년 전에 그 영화를 다시 보았을 때 자신의 캐릭터가 어울리지 않는 두 개의 장면이 있다는 것을 깨달았다.)
③ 우리가 어울리지 않는 곳을 인식하는 것은 우리가 속한 곳을 인식하는 것보다 덜 가치 있는 것으로 여겨진다. (→우리가 속하지 않는 곳을 아는 것은 우리가 속한 곳을 아는 것만큼 중요하다.)
⑤ 우리는 우리에게 맞지 않는 것을 제거하기 전에 우리의 진정한 자아를 찾으라는 조언을 받는다. (→먼저 자신이 아닌 존재를 제거할 때, 자신이 있어야 할 곳과 진정한 자신을 찾게 될 것이라는 조언을 받는다.)

body:
Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing what you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, overcoming your fears. You are the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Fear is something valuable that pushes us to challenge ourselves.
Denying our fears helps protect the chance to get over them.
Everyone is bound to face their greatest fear sooner or later.
Overcoming our fears allows us to become stronger and to value ourselves more.
Making mistakes is no reason to stop moving forward with our lives.

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. Whichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.

Hughie Erskine was a (A)[wonderful / wonderfully] good-looking man, with crisp brown hair, a sculpture-like profile, and grey eyes. He had every accomplishment except (B)[that / those] of making money. He lived on two hundred pounds a year (C)[what / that] an old aunt gave him. He had tried everything. He had gone to the stock exchange for six months. He had been a tea merchant for a little longer. Ultimately, he became nothing. He was a delightful, incompetent young man with a perfect profile and no profession.
To make matters worse, he was in love. The girl he loved was Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loved Hughie, too, and the colonel was very fond of him. However, he would not hear of any engagement. He would say “Come to me, my boy, ⓐ______, and we will talk about it.”

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) / (B) / (C)
choices: wonderful / that / what
wonderful / those / that
wonderfully / those / what
wonderfully / that / what
wonderfully / that / that
solution:
(A) 뒤의 형용사 good-looking을 수식하는 자리이므로 부사 wonderfully가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에 나온 단수명사 accomplishment를 대신하는 대명사 자리이므로 단수형 that이 적절하다.
(C) 선행사 two hundred pounds a year가 있고, 뒤에 gave의 직접목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 앞에 별도의 선행사를 두지 않는다.

After some time, a servant came in and told Trevor that the frame maker wanted to speak to him.
“Don’t run away, Hughie,” he said as he went out. “I will be back in a moment.”
The old beggar took advantage of Trevor’s absence to rest for a moment on a bench that was behind him. He looked so exhausted and miserable that Hughie ______. Hughie reached into his pocket to see how much money he had. All he could find was a few coins. “Poor old fellow,” he thought to himself. “He needs money more than I do.” He walked across the studio and slipped a gold coin into the beggar’s hand.
The old man was startled, and a faint smile came across his dry lips. “Thank you, sir,” he said. “Thank you.”
When Trevor returned, Hughie said goodbye and left the studio, blushing a little at what he had done, and he walked home.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: wanted Trevor to finish the painting quickly
could not help feeling sorry for him
wondered whether the model was truly poor
felt uncomfortable staying alone with him
hoped to find a better model for Trevor
solution:
노인이 매우 지치고 비참해 보였고, 이어서 Hughie가 자신보다 노인에게 돈이 더 필요하다고 생각하며 금화를 건네므로, 빈칸에는 ② ‘Hughie는 그를 불쌍히 여기지 않을 수 없었다’가 가장 적절하다.
본문변형 could not help pitying him → could not help feeling sorry for him

① Hughie는 Trevor가 그림을 빨리 완성하기를 원했다
③ Hughie는 그 모델이 정말 가난한지 궁금해했다
④ Hughie는 그와 단둘이 있는 것이 불편했다
⑤ Hughie는 Trevor에게 더 나은 모델을 찾아 주기를 바랐다

body:
That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor sitting by himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right?” he asked.
“Finished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor.
(A)
“You told that old beggar about my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and irritated.
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
(B)
“But he looks marvelous in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
(C)
“And, by the way, the old model you saw is quite curious about you. I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have.”
(D)
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “ⓐ나는 아마 집에 도착하면 그가 나를 기다리고 있는 것을 발견할 것이다. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I think it is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 그림을 완성했다고 답한 주어진 글에 이어, 같은 발화에서 늙은 모델이 Hughie를 궁금해해 그에 대해 다 말해야 했다고 덧붙이는 (C), 그 모델을 동정하며 헌 옷을 주고 싶어 하는 Hughie의 반응인 (D), (D)의 his rags를 them으로 받아 그 차림이 멋지다고 답하며 Laura 이야기까지 했다고 밝히는 (B), 사생활 누설에 분노하는 Hughie에게 그 거지가 유럽에서 가장 부유한 사람 중 한 명임을 알려 주는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• <보기>에 주어진 단어를 차례대로 사용할 것
• 12단어로 쓸 것
<보기>
probably, find, get
→ ______
answer: I will probably find him waiting for me when I get home.
solution:
• ‘나는 아마 ~을 발견할 것이다’는 미래시제 will과 부사 probably를 결합해 will probably find로 쓰고, probably는 조동사와 동사원형 사이에 둔다.
• ‘find+목적어+현재분사’(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다) 구조에서 목적어 him이 ‘기다리는’ 주체이므로 목적격보어로 능동 의미의 현재분사 waiting을 써서 나타낸다.
• '집에 도착하면'은 시간을 나타내는 부사절이므로 미래의 일이라도 현재시제를 써서 when I get home으로 쓴다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (D)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• understand, why, interest, know, all, so, be를 사용할 것(필요시 변형할 것)
• 간접의문문을 사용할 것
• 13단어로 쓸 것 (축약형은 한 단어로 셀 것)
→ ______
answer: I couldn't understand why he was so interested to know all about you
solution:
• '이해할 수 없었다'는 could의 부정형 couldn't 뒤에 understand를 써서 나타내고, understand의 목적어로 '왜 ~했는지'를 나타내는 간접의문문을 쓰므로 '의문사+주어+동사' 어순인 why he was so interested로 쓴다.
• 주어 he가 ‘관심을 가지게 된’ 대상이므로 과거분사형 형용사 interested로 변형하여 쓰고, 부사 so가 앞에서 수식하도록 배열한다.
• ‘~하는 데 관심이 있는’이라는 뜻이 되도록 형용사 interested를 뒤에서 수식하는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to know를 쓰고, ‘당신에 대한 모든 것’은 all about you로 쓴다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓘ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓔ were written → was written (‘전치사+관계대명사’인 on which 뒤에서 주어와 동사가 도치된 구조이며, 뒤에 이어지는 주어가 카드에 적힌 문구 하나이므로 단수동사 was로 고친다.)
ⓕ let → to let (‘tell+목적어+to부정사’(~에게 …하라고 말하다) 구조이므로, 목적어 the servant 뒤에 목적격보어로 to let을 쓴다.)
ⓗ sealing → sealed (수식 대상인 envelope가 ‘봉해진’ 대상이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 sealing을 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 sealed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주어 he가 옷을 ‘입은 상태’를 나타내므로 dressed는 적절하다.
ⓑ keep의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 smiling과 등위접속사 and로 병렬을 이루므로 rubbing은 적절하다.
ⓒ는 형용사 interested 뒤에서 '~하고 싶어 하는'의 의미를 완성하는 to부정사이므로 to know가 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어 The best thing I can do에 동사 do가 포함되어 있어 주격보어 자리의 to부정사에서 to를 생략할 수 있으므로 원형부정사 go가 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓖ 전치사 of의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사 addressing이 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓘ 장소를 나타내는 Inside가 앞에 놓이면서 주어와 동사가 도치되었으며, 주어 a check가 단수이므로 was는 적절하다.

solution:
남작이 '늙은 거지가 보내는 결혼 선물'이라며 Hughie에게 만 파운드짜리 수표를 보내고 결혼 피로연에서 축사까지 한 내용의 글이다. 앞의 Millionaire models는 거지 모델 노릇을 한 남작처럼 '모델이 된 백만장자'를, 어순을 뒤집은 model millionaires는 '모범이 되는 백만장자'를 뜻하므로, 남을 위해 기꺼이 큰돈을 베푸는 부자는 모델이 된 부자보다 훨씬 더 드물다는 의미이다. 따라서 ④ '자신의 재산을 남에게 선의를 베푸는 데 쓰는 부자들은 찾기가 더 어렵다.'가 적절하다.

③ 부유한 사람들은 가난한 남자들의 결혼식에 좀처럼 참석하지 않는다.
⑤ 부유한 사람들은 거지들에게 좀처럼 돈을 주지 않는다.

One morning, Hughie dropped in to see a great friend of his, Alan Trevor. Trevor was a painter. He was a strange, rough fellow with a bushy red beard. However, when he took up the brush, he was a real master, and ⓐhis pictures were eagerly sought after.
When Hughie came into the studio, ⓑhe found Trevor putting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar. ⓒThe beggar was standing on a raised platform in a corner of the studio. He was a wrinkly old man with a pitiful expression. He wore a ragged brown cape, and he leaned on a rough stick with one hand ⓓwhile holding out his hat for donations with the other.
“What an amazing model!” said Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. “ⓔHow miserable he looks! How much does the model get for posing?”
“A penny an hour.”
“And how much do you get for your painting, Alan?”
“Oh, I get two thousand pounds for this!”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: people eagerly sought after his pictures
ⓑ: he found that Trevor was putting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar
ⓒ: On a raised platform in a corner of the studio was standing the beggar.
ⓓ: while he was holding out his hat for donations with the other

solution:
현재의 모습을 나타내는 현재시제 looks를 사용했지만, 전환한 문장은 과거시제 had를 사용하여 과거의 모습을 나타내므로 원문과 같은 뜻이 되지 않는다. What a miserable look he had! 자체는 문법적으로 가능한 감탄문이다.
오답
ⓐ 구동사 seek after가 쓰인 수동태 문장 his pictures were eagerly sought after를 행위자인 일반 사람들(people)을 주어로 한 능동태로 바꾼 것이므로 전환이 적절하다.
ⓑ 'find+목적어+목적격보어' 구문에서 목적격보어로 쓰인 현재분사 putting을 that절로 바꾼 것으로, 주절의 동사 found가 과거시제이고 Hughie가 작업실에 들어갔을 때 Trevor가 그림을 마무리하고 있던 중이므로 과거진행형 was putting을 쓴 것은 적절하다.
ⓒ 장소를 나타내는 부사구 On a raised platform in a corner of the studio를 문장 앞에 두면서 동사 was standing을 주어인 명사구 the beggar 앞에 둔 도치 문장이므로 전환이 적절하다.

choices: have been / what / was

solution:
ⓐ ‘~인 것 같다, ~인 것으로 보이다’라는 뜻의 ‘seem+to부정사’에서 주절과 같은 시점의 동작이나 상태를 나타낼 경우 단순부정사(to+동사원형)를 사용하고 주절보다 이전일 경우는 완료부정사(to+have+p.p.)를 사용하며, ‘채취되었던 것’이 seems가 나타내는 현재보다 이전 과거의 일이므로, to 뒤에 수동형 완료부정사(to+have+been+p.p.)를 이루는 have been이 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘so+형용사구’인 so precious and scarce 뒤에서 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절(only ~ afford it)을 이끌고 있으므로, ‘매우 ~해서 …하다’라는 뜻의 ‘so+형용사(구)/부사(구)+that+완전한 절’ 구문을 이루는 접속사 that이 알맞다.
ⓒ 주어(ten sheets of gim)의 핵이 가산명사 복수형인 sheets이므로 복수동사로 수일치한 were가 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사 that을 사용할 것
• 현재완료를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어를 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)

show, CO₂, store, capture, seaweed
→ In fact, research shows ______ as it grows.

solution:
• <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사 that을 사용해 shows의 목적어인 명사절을 ‘that+완전한 절’ 형태로 쓴다.
• 명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 절의 주어로 seaweed를 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 현재완료를 사용하되 주어가 ‘입증되는’ 대상이므로, 현재완료 수동태(have[has]+been+p.p.)로 단수명사인 주어에 수일치한 단수조동사 has와 been을 쓴 뒤 show를 과거분사 shown으로 변형한다.
• ‘~한다는 것이 입증되다’라는 뜻의 ‘be shown+to부정사’를 사용해 먼저 capture를 to부정사인 to capture로 변형한 뒤, 등위접속사 and 뒤에 단어 수를 고려해 to를 생략한 동사원형으로 store를 쓴다. 타동사 capture(~을 붙잡다)와 store(~을 저장하다)의 공통의 목적어로 CO₂를 쓴다.

body:
It is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man named Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with some seaweed ⓐattached to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and found it to be delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea ⓑwhere he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people to enjoy gim, but it was not productive enough to cultivate as much gim as we consume today.
ⓒTo our surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. While researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, which ⓓfunction like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and ⓔattach them to cultivating frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ attach → attaching (‘by+동명사(구)(~함으로써)’를 이루는 첫 번째 동명사구 artificially collecting spores와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 동명사구를 이끌어야 하며, 뒤에 목적어로 대명사 them이 있으므로, 동사 attach를 능동형 동명사인 attaching으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)(~가 …한 상태로)’를 이루는 분사 또는 ‘~가 있는’이라는 뜻으로 쓰인 전치사 with의 목적어인 명사구 some seaweed를 수식하는 분사가 올 수 있으며, 앞의 명사구가 ‘부착된’ 대상이고, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘attach ~ to …(~을 …에 부착하다)’의 전치사 to가 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘~ be attached to …(~가 …에 부착되다)’의 과거분사 attached는 알맞다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(he had ~ seaweed)을 이끌어 장소 명사구인 the sea를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, 관계부사 where는 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘~에게 …하게도’라는 뜻을 ‘to+소유격+추상명사’로 나타낼 수 있으므로, ‘우리에게 놀랍게도’라는 뜻으로 전치사 To와 소유격 our, 추상명사 surprise를 사용해 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓴 To our surprise는 알맞다.
ⓓ 콤마(,) 뒤에 쓰인 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절의 동사가 올 자리이며, 관계사절의 내용이 과학적 사실에 해당하고, 관계사절이 부연 설명하는 선행사가 복수명사 spores이므로, 현재시제이자 복수동사로 수일치한 function은 알맞다.

body:
Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. So (A)[desired / devalued] was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.” There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was (B)[medical / environmental]. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it (C)[elaborated / restricted] one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

choices: desired / medical / elaborated
desired / medical / restricted
devalued / medical / elaborated
devalued / environmental / restricted

(A) ‘블랙 골드’나 ‘향신료의 제왕’이라는 화려한 별명을 얻었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 흑후추가 매우 인기를 끌었다는 흐름이 되는 desired(열망된)가 알맞다.
devalued 평가절하된
(B) 흑후추는 사람들이 잘 자고, 음식을 소화하고 일광 화상과 통증으로부터의 피부 자극을 완화하는 데 도움이 되는 치료제라고 여겨졌다는 구체적 설명이 뒤에 이어지므로, 흑후추가 과거 높이 평가된 두 번째 이유는 의학적인 것이라는 흐름이 되는 medical(의학적인)이 알맞다.
environmental 환경적인
(C) 책상 위에 흑후추를 두는 것은 부와 품위의 상징이었다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 흑후추가 사회적 지위와 부를 명시적으로 나타냈다는 흐름이 되는 elaborated(~을 상세히 말했다)가 알맞다.

body:
This is a NASA satellite image of the area near Wando, taken from space. NASA initially wondered what the black lines were and later discovered they are farms that grow gim. From this picture, you can guess that Korea is currently producing a lot of gim. It is relatively cheap and is frequently used in various Korean dishes, such as gimbap (a type of seaweed rice roll), gimjaban (roasted seaweed), and gimbugak (a type of crispy seaweed and rice chip). (A)그러나, 그것은 과거에는 매우 비쌌고, 오늘날 사람들이 즐길 수 있는 만큼 모든 사람들이 즐길 수는 없었습니다.
Gim in the Past
Gim seems to have been harvested in the past by women who walked into the sea during low tide to collect it from rocks. It was so precious and scarce that only royalty, like kings and queens, and the very wealthy had the privilege to afford it. During the Joseon period, ten sheets of gim were said to cost twenty cotton rolls, which cost a lot at the time. So you can imagine how expensive gim was. You might be wondering how gim became more affordable and readily available in recent years. Two figures are behind the striking popularity of gim today.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The satellite image captured by NASA indicates that a substantial amount of gim is currently cultivated in Korea.
Gim serves as an accessible ingredient used in a wide array of traditional Korean culinary items.
In earlier times, gim was mostly collected from coastal rocks at low tide by female gatherers.
Due to its extreme rarity, gim was once difficult to obtain even for the wealthy, except for royalty.
During the Joseon Dynasty, ten sheets of gim were worth the equivalent of twenty cotton rolls.

Did you know that gim is also eaten in South Africa? In the first half of 2017, Korean gim accounted for approximately 43% of the South African market. Not surprisingly, Korea is the world’s largest gim producer and exporter, dominating roughly 70% of the global gim market. According to Graph 1, gim exports overseas were only $100 million in 2010, but have steadily increased year after year, and reached $600 million in 2020. To where is gim exported? In 2019, the top three export destinations for Korean gim were the United States, Japan, and China. Furthermore, the number of export destinations is continuously increasing. According to Graph 2, gim was only exported to 64 countries in 2010, but by September 2021, gim exports had expanded to 112 countries worldwide.

choices: Korean gim held a market share of around 43% in South Africa during the first six months of 2017.
Korea leads the international gim market as its top manufacturer and exporter, making up about 70% of global supply.
Foreign sales of gim surged from $100 million in 2010 to $600 million a decade later through continuous annual growth.
As of 2019, the United States, Japan, and China were the three smallest importers of Korean gim.
The global reach of Korean gim expanded from 64 nations in 2010 to 112 countries by September 2021.

W: Logan, how was your weekend? Did you do anything special?
M: It was good. I went to the city homeless shelter as usual.
W: (A)Are you saying that you visit there regularly?
M: Yeah. I volunteer there every Saturday, serving meals to people at the shelter.
W: That’s amazing. It must be rewarding.
M: It really is. Every week, I feel like I’ve made a difference in people’s lives.
W: That’s awesome. Did you know that volunteering can have a positive impact on your health, too?
M: What do you mean? Like an impact on physical health?
W: Yes. It can actually decrease your blood pressure and cholesterol level. It’s called the “Mother Teresa effect.”
M: Interesting… So rather than just helping others when I volunteer, it sounds like I’m benefiting a lot, too.
W: Kindness makes a world of difference!

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Do you mind visiting there regularly?
Do you expect to visit there regularly?
Do you mean that you visit there regularly?
In other words, do you visit there regularly?
Are you interested in visiting there regularly?
solution:

오답
① 정기적으로 그곳을 가도 괜찮니?
② 정기적으로 그곳을 가는 것을 예상하니?
⑤ 정기적으로 그곳을 방문하는 데 관심이 있니?

body:
Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to ⓐskip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters ⓑworse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny?
A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes ⓒdiscomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously ⓓchange your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so ⓔunusual that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?

body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.

<보기>
of / and self-control / on / the / negative / effects / attention / hunger
→ ______
answer: the negative effects of hunger on attention and self-control

body:
Hunger and Hormones
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But ⓐ우리가 배가 고프면 포도당 수치는 떨어지며, 세포들이 해야 하는 것을 수행하지 못하게 막고, 이는 신체의 적절한 기능 작동에 뚜렷한 위협이 된다. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• 알맞은 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어를 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
from, prevent, perform, suppose
glucose levels fall when we are hungry, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body
answer: preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do
solution:
• 완전한 절(glucose ~ hungry)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문으로 영작해야 하며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절 전체가 세포를 ‘막는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 preventing과 목적어 cells를 쓴다.
• ‘…가 ~을 하는 것을 막다’의 의미로 ‘prevent+O+from+동명사 ~’의 구조로 쓰이므로 preventing cells 뒤에 from과 동명사 performing을 차례대로 쓴다.
• 동명사 performing의 목적어를 영작하기 위해 ‘~하는 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what을 쓰고 주어 they와 ‘~해야 한다’를 뜻하는 ‘be supposed+to부정사‘를 주어 they와 수일치하여 are supposed to로 변형하여 쓴 뒤, 동사원형 do를 이어 쓴다.

body:
ⓐWhat is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter ⓑthat helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is ⓒdisrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings ⓓare related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show ⓔthat, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas ⓕresponsibly for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓓ are related → related (앞에 문장의 동사 have also come이 있으므로 명사구 interesting findings를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, interesting findings가 ‘관련된’ 대상이므로 are related를 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 related로 고친다.)
ⓕ responsibly → responsible (접속사 while이 이끄는 절의 주어부(the activity patters ~ decision-making)를 이루는 요소로, 앞의 명사 areas를 수식하는 어구를 이끌어야 한다. 따라서 부사 responsibly를 형용사 responsible로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ stomach)을 이끌어 선행사 없이 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 ‘~하는 것’이라는 뜻으로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 What은 적절하다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(helps ~ brain)을 이끌어 선행사 a neurotransmitter를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
ⓒ 주어 normal functioning of mood regulation이 ‘방해받는’ 대상이므로 be동사 is와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 disrupted는 적절하다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(when ~ altered)을 이끌어 동사 show의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.

body:
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry ⓐgets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals ⓑare closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when ⓒdepriving of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. body:
Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. ⓐ______, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, creating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. ⓑ______, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact that we are all different and share a plate of understanding.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ    ⓑ
choices: Moreover    For example
Furthermore    However
As a result    Nevertheless
Therefore    For instance
However    Besides
solution:
ⓐ 앞에서 쓴맛에 민감하게 반응하게 만드는 특정 유전자가 있어서 오이를 싫어하게 될 수 있다고 했고, 뒤에서 수박, 참외, 고수 같은 다른 음식들 역시 이 유전자에 민감한 사람들에게 거부감을 받을 수 있다고 추가로 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로, 앞서 언급된 내용에 새로운 내용을 추가할 때 쓰는 연결어 'Moreover(게다가)', 'Furthermore(게다가)'가 적절하다.
ⓑ 앞 문장에서 특정 유전자가 고수(cilantro)에 포함된 화학 화합물과 같은 냄새 성분에 특정 개인들을 더 민감하게 만들 수 있다고 설명하고, 뒤에서 그에 대한 구체적인 사례로, 어떤 사람들은 고수에서 비누나 로션 같은 냄새를 감지할 수 있다고 했으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로, 일반적 설명에 대한 구체적인 예시를 제시할 때 쓰는 연결어 ‘For example(예를 들어)', ‘For instance(예를 들어)'가 적절하다.
오답
② 게다가    그러나
③ 그 결과    그럼에도 불구하고
④ 그러므로    예를 들어
⑤ 그러나    게다가

body:
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger ⓐcaused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment.
(A) Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown ⓑthat the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings.
(B) That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often ⓒlook for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
(C) Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, ⓓindicating a lack that needs to be addressed.
Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit ⓔwhat needs to be addressed.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 배고픔이 감정적 분노를 유발하는 현상(hangry)과 반대로, 외로움이 신체적 영양 섭취에 대한 욕구로 이어지는 ‘외로움에서 오는 허기(lonely hunger)’라는 현상을 소개하는 주어진 글 뒤에, That is(다시 말해)로 시작하여 ‘외로움에서 오는 허기’를 구체적으로 설명하는 (B), (B)에서 외로움에서 오는 허기로 인해 발생하는 ‘감정적 섭식’이라는 현상을 설명한 뒤, 뇌 영상 연구를 근거로 외로움과 배고픔을 느낄 때 뇌의 동일한 영역이 활성화된다는 점을 언급하는 (A), Studies also support(연구들은 또한 지지한다)로 시작하여 앞선 (A)에서 언급된 연구와 더불어 외로움이 배고픔과 유사한 신호로 작용한다는 또 다른 연구 결과를 제시하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. (A)이 문구가 의미하는 것은 배고픔이 여러분의 기분과 수행 능력을 실제로 바꿀 수 있다는 것이다. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

• 주어 What절은 일반적으로 단수 취급하므로 단수동사 is로 수일치 한다.
• 동사 is에 이어지는 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하되, <조건>에 따라 접속사 that을 생략하고, 명사절의 주어 hunger, 조동사 can 뒤에 seriously change를 쓰고 등위접속사 and로 병렬로 연결되는 목적어 your mood and performance를 이어 쓴다.

The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in ⓐ[that / which] the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know ⓑ[what / that] hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed ⓒ[to do / to be done], an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in (A)[line / conflict] with psychological studies.
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that (B)[low / high] levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in ㉠______. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly (C)[altered / stabilized]. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

which    that    to do
which    what    to be done
that    that    to be done
which    that    to be done
solution:
ⓐ 뒤에 완전한 절(the participants ~ ink)을 이끌어, 앞의 전치사 in과 함께 콤마 앞의 the Stroop task를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이뤄야 하므로, which가 알맞다. 참고로 전치사 뒤에 관계대명사 that은 올 수 없다.
ⓑ 동사 know의 목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 절(hunger ~ reaction, too)을 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘~하는 것’의 의미로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 이끄는 절은 불완전한 절이어야 하므로, 목적어가 없는 to do가 알맞다.

in conflict with ~ ~와 충돌하여, ~와 상충하여
(B) 앞 문단에서 포도당 수치가 떨어지면 코르티솔이 분비되어 코르티솔 수치가 높아진다고 했으므로, 공복에 대한 영향으로 ‘높은’ 코르티솔의 수치가 세로토닌을 떨어뜨린다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 high(높은)가 적절하다.
low 낮은
(C) 첫 문장에서 공복이 뇌에 영향을 미친다고 했고, 마지막에는 배고플 때 평소와 달라진다는 점을 강조하므로, 고차원적 인지 기능을 담당하는 영역의 활동 양식이 크게 ‘달라진다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 altered(바뀌게 된)가 적절하다.
stabilize 안정화시키다

body:
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in ⓐ[that / which] the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know ⓑ[what / that] hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed ⓒ[to do / to be done], an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in (A)[line / conflict] with psychological studies.
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that (B)[low / high] levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in ㉠______. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly (C)[altered / stabilized]. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

윗글의 빈칸 ㉠에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: regulating the digestive process during hunger
transmitting nutrients to different areas of the brain
storing long-term memories related to food intake
increasing cortisol production during stressful situations
maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being
solution:
세로토닌은 뇌의 여러 부위에 있는 뉴런 간의 소통을 돕는 신경 전달 물질이라는 설명에 이어, 뒤에 세로토닌 수치가 불균형해지면 감정 조절의 정상적인 기능이 방해받고, 이는 우울감, 짜증 증가, 높은 불안감으로 이어질 수 있다고 언급되고 있으므로, 뉴런 간의 소통을 돕는 신경 전달 물질인 세로토닌이 정서적인 안정감을 유지하는데 있어 중요한 역할을 하는 것을 알 수 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ⑤ '정서적 균형과 전반적인 행복감을 유지하는 것'이 들어가야 한다.

② 영양소를 뇌의 여러 영역으로 전달하는 것

body:
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 각각 쓰시오.
“______ ______" is a phenomenon in which feelings of loneliness, associated with activity in the ______ brain area as physical hunger, drive people toward ______ ______ because of a lack of ______ ______, even though this coping method carries long-term health risks.
answer: Lonely hunger, same, emotional eating, social nourishment

body:
Hughie is a charming young man who (A)[have / has] achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won’t let them marry until Hughie (B)[has / will have] 10,000 pounds.
One day, Hughie dropped by (C)[seeing / to see] his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: has / has / seeing
have / has / to see
has / will have / to see
have / will have / seeing
has / has / to see
solution:
(A) 선행사 a charming young man을 수식하는 관계사절에서 현재완료로 쓰인 동사구의 조동사 자리로, 주격 관계대명사 뒤의 동사는 선행사에 수일치 시키므로 선행사인 단수명사구 a charming young man에 수일치시킨 단수 조동사 has가 알맞다..
(B) 주절의 시점이 미래를 나타내더라도 시간 부사절에서는 미래의 일을 현재시제로 나타내므로, 시간을 나타내는 접속사 until이 이끄는 부사절의 동사로 현재시제 동사 has가 알맞다.
(C) 완전한 절(Hughie dropped by)에 흐름상 ‘만나기 위해’라는 의미로 이어져야 하므로 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to see가 알맞다. 참고로, drop by(잠깐 들르다)는 ‘자동사+부사’ 구조의 구동사로 뒤에 by의 목적어가 이어지지 않는다.

body:
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a debate over the proper evaluation and pricing of artists’ paintings
the model’s dissatisfaction with the small amount he receives for posing
Alan’s dissatisfaction with the compensation received by his model
different views on appropriate compensation for an artist and his model
Hughie’s criticism of Alan for demanding excessive payment for his paintings
solution:
늙은 모델이 불행해 보인다고 생각한 Hughie는 모델이 시간당 1실링을 받는 데 비해 화가는 그림 한 점에 2천 기니를 받는다는 사실을 알고 모델도 화가만큼 열심히 일하므로 그에 상응하는 몫을 받아야 한다고 주장하는 반면, Alan은 그림을 그리고 칠하고 캔버스 앞에 서 있다는 것을 강조하며 Hughie에게 말도 하지 말라고 하면서 반박하는 내용이므로, 글의 주제로 ④ ‘화가와 그의 모델에 대한 적절한 보수에 대한 다른 견해’가 알맞다.
오답
① 화가들의 그림에 대한 적절한 평가와 가격 책정에 대한 논쟁
② 자세를 취한 대가로 받는 적은 금액에 대한 모델의 불만
③ 모델이 받는 보수에 대한 Alan의 불만
⑤ 자신의 그림에 지나친 보수를 요구하는 Alan에 대한 Hughie의 비판

After a while, the servant came in and told Alan ⓐthat the frame-maker wanted to see him. Alan said, “I will be back in a moment,” as he went out. The old beggar took advantage of Alan’s absence to rest for a moment on a chair. He looked so sad and lonely. Hughie (A)______ and felt his own pockets to see what money ⓑhe had. All he could find, however, was a few coins. “Poor old fellow, he wants them more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks,” he thought to ⓒhim. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar’s hand. The old man was surprised and smiled faintly. “Thank you, sir,” he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, ⓓblushed a little at what he had done.
Hughie spent the day with Laura, received a gentle scolding for his actions, and ⓔhad to walk home.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ him → himself (흐름상 주어 he가 혼자 생각하는 상황으로 주어 he와 전치사 to의 목적어가 동일한 대상을 가리키므로 목적격 대명사 him을 재귀대명사 himself로 고친다. 참고로 ‘think to oneself’가 ‘마음속으로 생각하다’라는 뜻의 관용적 표현으로 쓰인다.)
ⓓ blushed → blushing (완전한 절(Hughie said goodbye) 다음에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로 이어지므로 동사가 올 수 없고, 흐름상 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 의미상 주어 Hughie가 ‘얼굴을 붉히는’ 주체이며 blush가 ‘얼굴을 붉히다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰이므로 blushed를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 blushing으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ told의 간접목적어 Alan에 이어진 직접목적어 자리로, 완전한 절(the frame-maker ~ him)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루는 접속사 that은 알맞다.
ⓑ see의 목적어인 간접의문문으로 의문사구(what money) 뒤에서 평서문의 어순이 되도록 ’주어+동사‘의 어순으로 쓰인 he had는 알맞다.
ⓔ 주어 Hughie에 연결된 과거형 동사 spent, received와 A, B, and C의 병렬 구조를 이루는 과거형 동사 had는 알맞다.

could hardly bring himself to pity him

solution:

can hardly bring oneself to ~ 좀처럼 ~할 마음이 나지 않다

① 그에 대한 측은한 마음을 참을 수 없었다
③ 불가피하게 그에게 동정적인 마음을 갖게 되었다

body:
That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And (A)by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. ⓐ그는 네가 누구인지, 어디에 사는지, 그리고 네 (미래) 전망은 무엇인지 알고 싶어했어.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were (B)worn, falling to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and (C)appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are (D)heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to (E)reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)를 아래와 같이 바꾸어 쓸 때 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): incidentally
(B): intact
(C): attractive
(D): unfeeling
(E): improve
solution:
(B) worn은 ‘해진, 닳은’을 뜻하므로, shabby(다 해진) 등으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으며, ‘온전한, 손상되지 않은’을 뜻하는 intact와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.
오답
(A) by the way 그런데 = incidentally 그런데
(C) appealing ‘매력적인’ = attractive 매력적인
(D) heartless 무정한 = unfeeling 무정한
(E): reform ~을 개혁하다 = improve ~을 개선하다

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 간접의문문을 사용하고 그 안에는 현재시제를 사용할 것

→ ______
answer: He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.
solution:

• 동사 know의 목적어 자리에 <조건>에 따라 간접의문문을 쓰되, 세 개의 간접의문문이 나열되므로 ‘A, B, and C’의 병렬 구조를 사용한다. 첫 번째 간접의문문으로 ‘누구’를 뜻하는 의문사 who 뒤에 ‘주어+동사 ~’의 평서문의 어순이 되도록 you 뒤에 are를 쓰고, 두 번째 간접의문문으로 ‘어디에’를 뜻하는 의문사 where 뒤에 평서문의 어순이 되도록 you live를 쓰고 접속사 and를 쓴다. 마지막으로 ‘무엇’을 뜻하는 의문사 what 뒤에 평서문의 어순이 되도록 주어 your prospects와 동사 are를 써서 완성한다.

“Sure I did. He knows all about the Colonel, Laura, and the 10,000 pounds,” replied Alan.
“You told that old beggar all my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and angry.
“My dear boy,” said Alan, ⓐsmiling, “that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and ⓑasks me a month ago to paint him as a beggar.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie, feeling embarrassed. “Good heavens! I gave him some coins,” he said, ⓒsinking into an armchair.
“What? You gave him coins?” cried Alan, bursting into laughter. He went on, “Well, ⓓit never occurred to me that you would distribute money in that way. Besides, when you came in, I didn’t know if Hausberg would like his name ⓔmentioned. You know he wasn’t in full dress.”
“Oh no, what did I do? The best thing I can do is ⓕto go to bed, and, my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone,” said Hughie, and he went home, feeling very unhappy.

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 1개이다.
ⓑ asks → asked (주어인 He에 수일치한 단수 동사 is, buys와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬 구조를 이루고 있는 것은 알맞으나, 과거를 나타내는 부사구 a month ago(한 달 전에)로 보아 과거에 이루어진 일이므로 asks를 과거시제 동사 asked로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주절(said Alan)에 접속사 없이 콤마로 연결된 분사구문의 분사 자리로, 의미상 주어 Alan이 웃는 주체이자 smile은 자동사이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 smiling은 알맞다.
ⓓ 흐름상 that 이하의 명사절이 나에게 떠오르지 않은 진주어가 되므로, 이에 상응하는 주어 자리의 가주어 it은 알맞다.
ⓔ like와 목적어 his name에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, like는 ’like+목적어+목적격 보어(~가 …하는 것을 좋아하다)‘의 5형식에서 목적어와 목적격 보어가 수동 관계일 경우 목적격 보어로 과거분사를 취할 수 있으므로, 과거분사 mentioned는 알맞다.

solution:
ⓑ 선행사 the pourquoi tales를 부연 설명하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 주격 관계대명사 뒤의 동사는 선행사에 수일치 하므로 복수 명사구인 선행사에 수일치하도록 단수동사 aims를 복수동사 aim으로 고친다.
ⓓ reveal의 목적어 자리로, 의미상 주어인 leopards와 목적어가 동일한 대상이므로 대명사 them을 재귀대명사 themselves로 고친다.
ⓕ 주어인 복수대명사 They에 수일치한 복수 동사 engage, teach와 함께 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬 연결되어 있으므로, 단수 동사 serves를 복수 동사 serve로 고친다.

ⓔ 동사 explains의 목적어 자리이며 완전한 절(leopards developed ~ survival)이 이어지므로 명사절 접속사 that은 알맞다.

<조건>
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사를 사용하고 관계사절에는 과거완료 시제를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
at, do, arrive, say goodbye, blush a little
______ ______, and ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______
answer: Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at what he had done
solution:
• 흐름상 과거의 일이므로 주어 Alan 뒤에 제시된 동사 arrive를 과거형인 arrived로 변형해 쓴다.
• 제시된 등위접속사 and 다음에 절이 연결되도록 주어 Hughie를 쓰고 주어진 표현인 say goodbye를 과거형인 said goodbye로 변형해 쓴다.
• 콤마(,) 뒤에 <조건>에 따라 ‘얼굴을 붉히며’에 해당하는 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문을 영작한다. 의미상 주어 Hughie가 ‘얼굴을 붉히는’ 주체이며 blush는 자동사이므로 주어진 동사 blush를 현재분사 blushing으로 변형해 쓰고 이어서 부사 a little을 쓴다.
• a little 다음에 전치사 at을 쓰고, 전치사 at의 목적어로 <조건>에 따라 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사를 사용하여 명사절 영작한다. 따라서 관계대명사 what을 쓰고, 주어로 he를, 그리고 <조건>에 따라 주어진 동사 do를 과거완료형 had done으로 변형해 쓴다.

Throughout history, people have always tried to understand themselves and the world they live in, and these efforts are reflected in the stories they tell. An interesting example of such stories is the pourquoi tales, which aim to ______. As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. These imaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, provide creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots. According to this story, leopards were originally plain brown like the desert. However, in order not to reveal themselves while hunting animals in the forest, leopards decided to paint spots on their skins. This story explains that leopards developed spots as a means of survival.
Pourquoi tales serve several purposes. They engage readers with imaginative stories, teach lessons, and serve as a means of passing on knowledge to future generations. These stories explore the complexity of the world around us.

choices: account for how or why certain things came to be
predict how unfamiliar natural phenomena will develop over time
offer factual explanations for the consequences of various phenomena
preserve accurate historical records of unusual events for later generations
challenge traditional beliefs by revealing the facts behind ancient stories

“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his (A)[fortune / liability]?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get an (B)[equitable / inequitable] share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very (C)[idle / busy]. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: fortune / equitable / idle
fortune / equitable / busy
liability / inequitable / idle
liability / equitable / busy
fortune / inequitable / busy
solution:
(A) Alan이 당연하다고 대답하며 거지가 행복해 보이는 게 이상한 상황이라는 의미로 ‘거지가 행복해 보이길 바라는 건 아니겠지, 그렇지?’라고 질문하고 있으므로 이에 앞서 Hughie의 질문으로 노인의 참 불행해 보이는 얼굴이 모델로서 유리한 점이 맞냐는 질문이 되는 흐름이 되는 fortune(자산)이 알맞다.
liability 불리한 요소
(B) 모델들도 화가들만큼 열심히 일하기 때문이라는 이유를 덧붙이고 있으므로, 그 모델도 그 돈에서 공정한 몫을 받아야 한다는 흐름이 되는 equitable(공정한)이 알맞다.

본문변형 a fair → an equitable
(C) Alan은 Hughie의 말을 부정하며 하루 종일 캔버스 앞에서 그리고 서있는 데 드는 노력을 보라고 하면서 자신의 노고를 강조했고 Hughie에게 조용히 하라고 말하고 있으므로 자신이 지금 매우 할 일이 많다는 흐름이 되는 busy(바쁜)가 알맞다.

This is a NASA satellite image of the area near Wando, ⓐtaken from space. NASA initially wondered what ⓑwere the black lines and later discovered they are farms that grow gim. From this picture, you can guess that Korea is currently producing a lot of gim. It is relatively cheap and is (A)frequently used in various Korean dishes, such as gimbap (a type of seaweed rice roll), gimjaban (roasted seaweed), and gimbugak (a type of crispy seaweed and rice chip). However, it ⓒused to be very (B)affordable in the past, so not everyone could enjoy it as much as people can today.

Gim in the Past
Gim seems ⓓto have been harvested in the past by women who walked into the sea during low tide to (C)collect it from rocks. It was so precious and scarce that only royalty, like kings and queens, and the very wealthy had the (D)privilege to afford it. During the Joseon period, ten sheets of gim were said to cost twenty cotton rolls, ⓔwhich cost a lot at the time. So you can imagine how expensive gim was. You might be wondering how gim became more affordable and (E)readily available in recent years. Two figures are behind the striking popularity of gim today.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓑ were the black lines → the black lines were (타동사 wondered의 목적어 자리에 what이 이끄는 간접의문문이 쓰인 것이므로, ‘의문사+평서문(주어+동사~)’의 간접의문문 어순을 이루어야 한다. 따라서 ‘be동사+주어’ 어순의 were the black lines를 ‘주어+be동사’ 어순인 the black lines were로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 콤마(,) 뒤에 앞의 명사구 a NASA satellite image of the area near Wando를 부연 설명하는 분사구가 올 수 있으며, 부연 설명의 대상인 앞의 명사구가 ‘촬영된’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 taken은 알맞다.
ⓓ ‘~인 것 같다, ~인 것으로 보이다’라는 뜻의 ‘seem+to부정사’에서 주절과 같은 시점의 동작이나 상태를 나타낼 경우 단순부정사(to+동사원형)를 사용하고 주절보다 이전일 경우는 완료부정사(to+have+p.p.)를 사용하며, 주어 Gim이 ‘채취되었던’ 대상이고 seems가 나타내는 현재보다 이전 과거의 일이므로, 수동형 완료부정사(to+have+been+p.p.)를 이루는 to have been은 알맞다.
