body:
It is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man named Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with some seaweed attached to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and found it ⓐ[to be / being] delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea where he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people to enjoy gim, but (A)그것은 오늘날 우리가 소비하는 만큼의 많은 김을 재배하기에 충분히 생산적이지 않았습니다.

ⓑ[For / To] our surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. While researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, which function like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching them to ⓒ[cultivate / cultivating] frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ / ⓑ / ⓒ
choices: to be / For / cultivating
to be / To / cultivate
being / For / cultivating
to be / To / cultivating
being / For / cultivate
solution:
ⓐ ‘~가 …인 것을 알게 되다[알아차리다]’라는 뜻으로 ‘find+목적어+(to be+)보어’를 사용하므로, 과거형으로 쓰인 found와 목적어인 대명사 it 뒤에 to부정사인 to be가 알맞다.
ⓑ 뒤에 이어진 소유격 our와 추상명사 surprise와 함께 ‘우리에게 놀랍게도’라는 뜻의 표현을 이루어야 하며, ‘~에게 …하게도’라는 뜻은 ‘to+소유격+추상명사’로 나타내므로, 전치사 To가 알맞다.
ⓒ 흐름상 전치사 to 뒤에 명사(구)가 목적어로 이어져 ‘~을 …에 붙이다’를 뜻하는 ‘attach ~ to …’ 표현을 이루어야 하므로, ‘경작’을 뜻하는 동사파생명사로 뒤의 명사 frames와 함께 ‘경작용 틀들’을 뜻하는 명사구를 이루는 cultivating이 알맞다.

solution:
⦁주어로 단수명사구 this method를 가리키는 대명사 it을 쓰고, 뒤에 흐름상 과거시제를 사용해 단수형 be동사로 수일치한 was와 부정어 not을 쓴 뒤, 보어로 형용사 productive를 연결한다.

As more countries begin to eat gim, it is being consumed in new ways depending on the country. For example, in the United States, as Americans are paying more attention to gim as a healthy food, they enjoy roasted gim snacks with almonds and coconut added. Also, Thailand is producing its own gim snacks by importing gim from Korea and processing it with popular Thai flavors, such as tom yam kung (a sweet and sour flavor) and grilled squid. What is more, gim can be easily added to a variety of dishes. For example, the Culinary Institute of America, an internationally famous culinary university, published a recipe book titled Fabulous and Flavorful Gim. It includes gim recipes, such as gim flavored popcorn, gim fried chicken, and even gim ice cream. It is quite clear that gim is being used to create new and delicious types of food and to give new flavors to old favorites.

body:
Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was ______. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. So desired was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.” There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it elaborated one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

a commonly found plant cultivated exclusively for medical use
a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford
a cheap flavoring agent that lost its popularity due to its strong scent
an overrated agricultural product that caused severe economic crises

To our surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. While researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, which function like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching them to cultivating frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

solution:

Also, Thailand is producing its own gim snacks by importing gim from Korea and (E)processing it with popular Thai flavors, such as tom yam kung (a sweet and sour flavor) and grilled squid. What is more, gim can be easily added to a variety of dishes. For example, the Culinary Institute of America, an internationally famous culinary university, published a recipe book titled Fabulous and Flavorful Gim. It includes gim recipes, such as gim flavored popcorn, gim fried chicken, and even gim ice cream. It is quite clear that gim is being used to create new and delicious types of food and to give new flavors to old favorites.

(B) First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. (C) The third reason is that it elaborated one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk ⓔwas a symbol of wealth and dignity. (D) ⓕConsider all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, both in and outside the kitchen, has ⓖa lot more to offer than meets the eye. (E)

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓑ what → that[which] 또는 what 삭제 (타동사 afford뒤에 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절 ‘peasants could not afford’를 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 a rare and expensive luxury item을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what을 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 고치거나, 목적격 관계대명사는 생략 가능하므로 what을 삭제한다.)
*원래 지문에는 that이 쓰였음
ⓒ pepper was → was pepper (보어인 형용사구 So desired가 강조되어 문두에 쓰였으므로 ‘동사’ 도치를 적용한 ‘so+형용사+be동사+주어~’의 어순이 되도록 pepper was를 was pepper로 고친다.)
ⓕ Consider → Considering (완전한 절(it ~ commodity) 앞에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문 형태의 절이 올 수 없으므로, ‘~을 고려하면’이라는 뜻으로 전치사 역할을 하며 비인칭독립분사구를 이끌도록 동사원형 Consider를 Considering으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓓ 동사원형 sleep, digest와 ‘A, B, and C‘의 병렬구조로 연결되어 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)(~가 …하도록 돕다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루고 있으므로, 동사원형 relieve는 알맞다.
ⓖ ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 쓰여 비교급 more를 강조하는 a lot은 알맞다. 참고로, 비교급을 강조하는 부사(구)로 a lot, much, far, even, still 등이 쓰인다.

Have you ever wondered, “What if I could run so fast that nobody could see me?” If you have asked this kind of question, you may be ready to become the next Galileo. The Italian scientist Galileo Galilei is famous for a thought experiment, which is an imaginary experiment designed to explore a mathematical or scientific hypothesis. Scientific theories can only be proven through physical experiments rather than imaginary ones.
Scientific progress depends more on advanced experimental techniques than on individual creativity.
Creative imagination and curiosity can lead to meaningful scientific discoveries through thought experiments.
Thought experiments are less reliable than physical experiments because they lack direct observation.

The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
다음 글의 요지를 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 알맞게 쓰시오. (단, 주어진 철자로 시작할 것)
If the human body became e______, surface area and v______ would increase at d______ rates, potentially creating numerous life-threatening p______.
solution: 정답은 enormous, volume, different, problems 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height ⓐincreased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. However, the area of the feet ⓑsupporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass ⓒwould have increased far more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body. If a person’s height ⓓwere to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. This shows that while we may wish to grow as ⓔtall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: 현재 사실과 반대되거나 현재에 일어난 가능성이 희박한 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거가 쓰였다.
ⓑ: 수식받는 the area of the feet이 ‘지탱하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 supporting이 쓰였다.
ⓒ: 앞 절의 would be보다 먼저 일어난 일(무게 증가)을 나타내기 위해 가정법 과거완료 would have increased가 쓰였다.
ⓓ: 조건절에 쓰이는 be to용법으로, ‘~하고자 한다면’의 의미로 의도를 나타내는 were to increase가 쓰였다.
ⓔ: ‘as+형용사/부사+as’ 형태의 원급 비교이며, 동사 grow의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사 tall이 쓰였다.
solution: ⓓ if절의 ‘were+to부정사‘는 현재 또는 미래에 실현 가능성이 희박한 일을 가정할 때 사용하는 가정법 과거이며, 이때 주어의 인칭과 수에 관계없이 were을 사용하므로 were to increase가 쓰였다.

body:
[1]
“O, swear not by the moon, the inconstant moon.” This is a famous line from Romeo and Juliet. Juliet warns Romeo not ⓐ[swearing / to swear] his love by the Moon as it may change just as the Moon changes its shape. Although its appearance changes, the Moon is always present in the night sky and plays a crucial role in ⓑ[regulation / regulating] the length of the day on Earth as well as the Earth’s seasons and weather patterns. Then, what would happen if there were no Moon?
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
[2]
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, making up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as ⓒ[efficient / efficiently] as lungs at taking in air.
Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain. Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ / ⓑ / ⓒ
choices: swearing / regulation / efficient
to swear / regulating / efficiently
swearing / regulating / efficient
to swear / regulation / efficiently
to swear / regulating / efficient
solution:
ⓐ 동사 warn은 ‘warn+목적어+목적격보어((not+)to부정사)(~에게 …하(지 말)라고 경고를 주다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어로 to부정사 to swear가 알맞다.
ⓑ 전치사 in의 목적어 자리이며 뒤에 명사구 the length를 목적어로 취할 수 있어야 하므로 동명사 regulating이 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘as+형용사/부사+as’ 형태의 원급 비교 구문이 쓰였으며, 동사 are에 이어지는 주격 보어가 as 사이에 쓰여야 하므로 형용사 efficient가 알맞다.

어색한 표현 → 알맞게 고친 표현

solution:
ⓐ 달이 없는 상황을 가정하고 있으므로 현재 사실에 반대되는 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거 ‘If+주어+동사의 과거시제(be동사 were) ~, 주어+과거 조동사+동사원형’의 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 과거완료형 had not been을 과거형 were not으로 고친다.

According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. ⓑSupposing the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially making summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Ocean movements generated by the Moon’s gravity cause friction that gradually reduces the rate of Earth's rotation.
But for the Moon, the Earth would not slow its spin, leading to a day length significantly below 24 hours.
It is primarily through the Moon's gravitational pull that the tilt of Earth's axis of rotation remains stable.
Without the Moon, the Earth’s overall temperature would simply become much hotter throughout the year.

Undoubtedly, it is an ⓑindispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through ⓒexternal openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as efficient as lungs at taking in air.

If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially ⓓdisrupting the food chain. (A)예를 들면, 잠자리들은 독수리들만큼 커질 수 있으며, 이것은 생태계에서 포식자와 먹이의 균형을 변화시킨다.
Fortunately, you wouldn’t need to worry about giant insects chasing after you if this were to occur. Considering that oxygen is used to ⓔbreak down energy so that muscles can use it, the increase in oxygen would help to use energy more efficiently and improve our capability for physical exercise. body:
1. What if the size of a human body became enormous?
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. However, the area of the feet supporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased far more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body. If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. This shows that while we may wish to grow as tall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.
choices: The scale effect shows that an increase in length can lead to proportionally greater increases in area and volume.
A person ten times taller would have a thousand times the weight of their original body.
Even though the giant’s feet would become larger, they would not provide enough support for the increased body weight.
A giant-sized person could effectively remove body heat because the skin would expand enough to emit the increased heat.
The problems caused by excessive body size would make it impossible for humans to survive in a giant-sized form.

body:
Cloth That Connected the Worlds
It is said ⓐthat silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea ⓑhad dissolved the coating of the cocoon. ⓒThat she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.
For a long time, silk was a material ⓓreserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk ⓔwas eased, and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, prompting the development of the civilizations.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Who is said to have discovered silk production?
What happened to the cocoon when it fell into a cup?
Why were the restrictions on who could wear and use silk relaxed?
What is considered the earliest evidence of the silk trade?
What else was exchanged along the Silk Road besides silk?

body:
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest challenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, (A)달에서 입었던 각각의 우주복은 약 4,000개의 직물 조각과 21겹의 다른 재료로 이루어졌고, 당시 무게가 72 kg에 달했다. It remains the most complex space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: More than 500 million people watched the moment when humans first stepped onto the moon.
The Apollo suits had to withstand extremely high and low temperatures.
NASA chose the company that had earned its reputation by producing women’s underwear.
Using their hands and sewing machines, skilled seamstresses produced the suits mainly from fabric.
NASA’s advanced technology greatly helped the seamstresses create the simplest space suits ever used.
solution:

It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit.
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits ______. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.

Various styles and types of textiles can be used in art. In textile art, blue jeans, not water paints, can be used ⓐto draw pictures. Beautiful threads replace photos of scenic views. These types of textiles can be brilliant tools for expanding artistic creativity.
Ian Berry, Denim Art
Have you ever imagined painting with clothes, not on clothes? Surprisingly, Ian Berry succeeded in this and makes art out of blue jeans. His art looks like a painting, but people suddenly notice the beauty in blue jeans when they look at his art. He collects denim of every shade and uses it to create the shading and the sense of perspective in his portraits, landscapes, and other unique works of art. With just his hands, scissors, and glue, he creates almost three-dimensional pieces. He ⓑhas been making realistic installations of denim for many years. He uses discarded jeans, cuts them up into pieces, and, like a painter, ⓒsorting them according to color. At first glance, the work seems flat, but a closer look reveals different layers of denim ⓓplaced on top of and over each other. They are in fact denim collages. They are almost impossible ⓔto distinguish from paintings.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ sorting → sorts (단수동사 uses, cuts와 함께 ‘A, B, and C’의 형태로 병렬을 이루어야 하므로 sorting을 단수동사 sorts로 고친다.)

ⓐ ‘be used+to부정사(~하는 데 사용되다)’의 의미로, 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to draw는 적절하다.

It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
According to one of many stories, ______ ______ is believed to have been started when Leizu discovered ______ ______ from a ______ in her tea and turned them into a soft, shiny, cool ______.
answer: silk production, soft fibers, cocoon, fabric
solution: 요약문 많은 이야기 중 하나에 따르면, 비단 생산은 Leizu가 자신의 차의 고치로부터 나온 부드러운 섬유를 발견하고 그것들을 부드럽고 반짝이며 시원한 직물로 만들었을 때 시작되었다고 여겨진다.

body:
Technology Doping
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers.
(A) In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits.
(B) It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air.
(C) In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit.
They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 25개의 수영 세계 신기록이 수립된 2008년 베이징 올림픽에서 많은 수영 선수들이 새로운 유형의 수영복을 입었다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 앞서 언급된 새로운 유형의 수영복을 대명사 it으로 이어받아 상어 피부를 모방한 소재로 만들어진 전신 수영복의 특징을 구체적으로 설명하는 (B), (B)의 마지막 부분에서 이 수영복이 부력을 높여준다는 내용이 제시된 뒤, In fact(실제로)를 통해 부력을 높이기 위해 이 수영복(these suits)을 여러 벌 착용한 실제 사례와 해당 수영복을 입은 선수들이 베이징 올림픽에서 세운 세계 기록의 결과를 제시하는 (C), (C)에서 베이징 올림픽 당시의 기록을 설명한 뒤, 베이징 올림픽 이후 대회들에서(In later competitions) 혁신적인 수영복을 착용한 선수들이 계속해서 세계 신기록을 경신했다는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
Various styles and types of textiles can be used in art. In textile art, blue jeans, not water paints, can be used to draw pictures. Beautiful threads replace photos of scenic views. These types of textiles can be brilliant tools for expanding artistic creativity.
People usually take pictures of scenic views, but Teresa Lim paints pictures of tourist spots with a needle and thread when she travels the world. She embroiders places she visits in surprising detail. This method of preserving memories lets her truly take in her surroundings. She spends time sitting in one place, observing details and stitching as the scene reveals itself. She says on her website that her designs “seek to erase the lines and boundaries between being an illustrator and a textile designer.” Her art is a delightful fusion of a canvas and a camera that projects travel scenes onto fabric. She recreates what she sees on cloth and eliminates the need for a vacation photo album.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the creative use of textiles to create unique works of art
the practical advantages of taking photographs while traveling
the growing popularity of traditional embroidery among modern artists
the importance of accurately copying scenic views in textile design
the differences between photography and painting as ways to record travel memories
solution:
다양한 스타일과 종류의 직물이 예술에서 사용될 수 있으며, 그 예시로 Teresa Lim은 여행지의 모습을 사진 대신 바늘과 실로 세밀하게 자수하고, 주변을 관찰하며 여행의 추억을 기록하는 예술 작품을 만든다고 했으므로 이 글의 주제로 ① ‘독특한 예술 작품으로 바뀌는 섬유의 창의적 활용’이 적절하다.
오답
② 여행 중 사진을 찍는 것의 실용적인 장점
③ 현대 예술가들 사이에서 전통적인 자수의 증가하는 인기
④ 직물 디자인에서 풍경을 정확하게 모방하는 것의 중요성
⑤ 여행의 추억을 기록하는 방법으로서 사진과 그림의 차이

body:
We live surrounded by cloth. We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. Wearing clothes is a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. Textiles ─artificial and natural ─have shaped and changed the world we live in. The history of textiles is almost as old as human civilization, and as time has passed, it has been more and more enriched. (A)직물이 세상을 어떻게 바꿔 왔는지를 탐구하는 것은 우리가 인류 문명이 어떻게 진화해 왔는지를 이해하는 데 도움이 된다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 동명사구와 원형부정사를 사용할 것
• 간접의문문을 두 번 사용할 것
• 현재완료를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어를 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 15단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
how, help, explore, textiles, evolve, change, understand
→ ______
answer: Exploring how textiles have changed the world helps us understand how human civilization has evolved.
solution:
• 동사 explore를 동명사 Exploring으로 변형하여 주어 자리에 쓰고, Exploring의 목적어로 ‘어떻게’를 뜻하는 의문부사 how를 사용하여 ‘의문사+주어+동사~’의 어순을 갖는 간접의문문을 영작한다. 따라서 의문부사 how 뒤에 주어 textiles를 쓰고, 과거부터 현재까지 직물이 세상을 바꿔온 것이므로 현재완료 have changed와 목적어 the world를 이어 쓴다.
• 동명사 주어는 단수 취급하므로 단수동사 helps를 쓰고, 동사 help는 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 글자 수 조건에 맞게 helps 뒤에 목적어 us와 동사원형 understand를 차례대로 쓴다.
• 목적격보어 understand의 목적어로, ‘어떻게’를 뜻하는 의문부사 how를 사용하여 ‘의문사+주어+동사’의 어순으로 간접의문문을 영작한다. 의문부사 how 뒤에 주어 human civilization을 쓰고, 과거부터 현재까지 인류 문명이 진화해 온 것이므로 현재완료 have evolved를 쓴다.

body:
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits (A)______ to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.
“Technology doping” in sports means the practice of gaining a competitive edge by using technology to improve performance. This can be against the spirit of fair play. However, since most sports require equipment of some sort, it can be tricky to determine what is technology doping and what is not. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: ceased undermines
ceased elevates
ceased fosters
continued fosters
continued undermines
solution:
(A) 빈칸 뒤에서 FINA가 모든 전신 수영복을 금지하고 수영복의 직물 조건까지 규정했다고 했으므로 혁신적인 수영복으로 인해 선수들이 계속해서 세계 신기록을 경신했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 continued(계속 ~하다)가 적절하다.
(B) 뒤에서 부유한 선수들을 가난한 선수들보다 유리하게 만든다고 했으므로 그것(it)이 인간의 정신력과 노력을 약화시킨다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 undermines(약화시키다)가 적절하다.
오답
① 중단했다 약화시킨다
② 중단했다 높인다
③ 중단했다 촉진한다
④ 계속했다 촉진한다

body:
M: Hello, I’m Professor Noah Williams, and it’s a great honor to be here as a key speaker. With environmental pollution getting worse, sustainable cities are being suggested as a solution to the problem. Today, we will take a look at Copenhagen, one of the greenest cities in the world. Copenhagen, the capital of Denmark, has achieved a remarkable harmony between urban development and environmental conservation. About 62% of its citizens ride bikes to get around the city. Copenhagen has 546 kilometers of bike paths and bridges that allow people to go anywhere in the city by bike. Plus, renewable energy is being generated in a unique power plant called CopenHill. Each year, it converts 440,000 tons of waste into energy that can provide electricity and heating for 150,000 homes. Furthermore, Copenhagen’s buildings are covered with green roofs, where grass and trees are planted. These green roofs improve the air quality of the city and reduce its temperature. Let’s take a closer look at this remarkable city!
다음 담화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Professor Noah Williams introduces Copenhagen as an example of a sustainable city.
Approximately 62% of Copenhagen’s citizens travel by bicycle, using 546 kilometers of bike paths and bridges.
CopenHill, known as a distinctive power plant, generates renewable energy.
Every year, CopenHill transforms 440,000 tons of waste into energy for electricity and heating.
Copenhagen’s buildings with green roofs have little effect on the city’s air quality or temperature.
solution: 코펜하겐의 건물들은 잔디와 나무가 심어져 있는 녹색 옥상으로 덮여 있으며 이러한 녹색 옥상들은 도시의 공기 질을 개선하고 도시의 온도를 낮춘다고 설명하고 있으므로, ❺ ‘녹색 옥상이 있는 코펜하겐의 건물들은 도시의 공기 질이나 온도에 거의 영향을 미치지 않는다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

M: I think it’s ⓐbetter for the environment to buy one with this logo on it!
G: What do you mean by that? What does this logo have to do with the environment?
M: It indicates that the product is guaranteed not to ⓑcontain microplastics.
G: Oh, I read an article about the negative impact of microplastics on the environment. They are especially ⓒbeneficial to marine habitats because they eventually end up in places like rivers, lakes, and oceans.
M: That’s why we should consider purchasing products with this logo. It can ⓓencourage more companies to think about how they develop their products.
G: I never thought about it that way. From now on, I will be ⓔmore conscious about what I buy.
M: Great! Why don’t you check out other products with this logo?
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓒ beneficial(유익한) → harmful(해로운, 유해한)

body:
When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some ⓐhelpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is (A)[why / what] Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer ⓑexperts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success (B)[that / which] the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to ⓒgrow in popularity, with more and more people (C)[signed up / signing up] to volunteer.
By ⓓproviding spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge ⓔnegative impact on our future.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ negative(부정적인) → positive(긍정적인)

choices: why / which / signing up

solution:
(A) be동사인 is의 보어 자리에서 완전한 절(Repair Cafés were started)을 이끌고 있으므로, 선행사 the reason이 앞에 생략된 이유의 관계부사 why가 알맞다.
(B) 명사구 such a success 뒤에 이어져 있으며, 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절(the idea soon spread to neighboring countries)을 이끌고 있으므로, ‘such a(n)+명사+that+완전한 절(대단한 ~여서 …하다)’ 구문을 이루는 접속사 that이 알맞다.
(C) ‘~가 …한 상태로, ~가 …한 채로’라는 뜻의 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’ 구문을 이루어야 하며, 앞의 명사구 more and more people이 ‘신청하는’ 주체이고, ‘신청하다’라는 뜻의 sign up은 자동사와 부사로 이루어진 구동사이므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사를 사용한 signing up이 알맞다. 참고로, 자동사는 수동태나 수동을 나타내는 과거분사로 쓸 수 없다.

body:
On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, ⓐseriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen ⓑis cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it ⓒrepair, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and ⓓpurchase a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing ⓔto do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ repair → repaired (have의 목적어인 대명사 it이 가리키는 her laptop이 ’수리되는‘ 대상이며, ‘have+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문에서 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동의 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 과거분사를 사용하므로, repair를 과거분사 repaired로 고친다. 참고로, 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동이면 목적격보어로 동사원형을 쓰고, 목적어의 행위에 진행이나 지속의 의미가 더해질 경우 현재분사를 쓴다.)
ⓓ purchase → purchasing (문장의 동사 자리에 might seem이 있으므로, 동명사구 getting rid of the old one과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구를 이루도록 purchase를 동명사 purchasing으로 고친다.)

body:
One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices ⓐare that they are too difficult to repair. In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer ⓐinclude a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. (A)색상으로 표시되는 시스템뿐만 아니라 0에서 10 사이의 점수도 사용하여, 그 지수는 소비자들이 제품을 구입하기 전에 그것이 얼마나 쉽게 수리될 수 있는지 알 수 있게 해 준다. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that ⓑrepairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.
The index ⓒdesigned to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when ⓓpurchased new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products ⓔmore easily to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely ⓕto spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world ⓖfollows France’s innovative lead.

body:
On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.
What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. (A) Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. (B) To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. (C) In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. (D) Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. (E) Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
*metric ton 메트릭톤(1,000kg을 1톤으로 하는 중량 단위)
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 이유로 이 문제를 다루기 위해 노력이 이루어지고 있는데, 이 중 대부분은 제품들을 수리하기 더 쉽게 만드는 것에 중점을 두고 있다.’라는 뜻으로, this reason(이러한 이유)이 가리키는 내용에 해당하는 것으로서, 매년 생산되는 전자 쓰레기의 양이 걱정스러운 속도로 증가하고 있다는 문제를 2014년과 2021년의 데이터 및 2030년 예측되는 수치를 통해 구체적으로 설명하는 내용 뒤이자, 주어진 문장에 언급된 문제를 다루기 위한 노력과 관련해, 전 세계의 현실성 있는 접근법을 살펴보자고 언급하는 문장 앞인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. (A)______, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score.
(B)______, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: Alternatively / For instance
As a result / Nevertheless
Therefore / In fact
Conversely / Instead
Alternatively / In fact
solution:
(A) Liz가 필요한 부품을 온라인으로 주문해 직접 교체할 수 있었을 것이라는 내용 뒤에 가까운 수리 카페에 고장 난 장치를 가지고 가서 수리 방법에 대한 조언을 받을 수도 있다는 대안을 설명하고 있으므로 ‘그 대신에, 아니면’을 뜻하는 Alternatively가 알맞다.
(B) Liz의 사례를 들어 손상된 장치와 기기를 개인이 쉽게 고칠 수 있는 세상에 살고 있다면 여러 방식으로 쉽게 자신의 고장 난 기기를 수리할 수 있을 것이라고 가정한 뒤, 이러한 지속 가능한 세상은 우리가 함께 노력하면 누릴 수 있는 미래라고 말하며 앞의 가정적 상황이 실현 가능한 미래임을 강조하고 있으므로, ‘사실은’을 뜻하는 In fact가 알맞다.

body:
When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.
By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés ______. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: allow manufacturers to improve the design and performance of electronic products
encourage people to purchase newer electronic devices instead of repairing old ones
provide professional repair services that require people to pay for technical assistance
help individuals to maintain their devices in good condition and prolong their use
help people dispose of damaged electronic devices before they become a health hazard
solution: 수리 카페는 자신의 고장 난 장치를 수리하고자 하는 사람들이 자유롭게 모여 자원봉사자 전문가에게 고치는 방법을 배우거나, 전자 제품의 수리와 보수 관리에 대한 유용한 지식과 기술을 서로 공유할 수 있는 공간이라고 했으며, 뒤에서는 지속 가능한 관점을 조성한다는 궁극적 효과를 언급하고 있으므로, 수리 카페가 사람들에게 배울 공간을 제공함으로써 사람들이 자신의 전자 기기를 잘 관리하고 더 오래 쓸 수 있게 한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❹ ‘개인들이 자신의 장치를 좋은 상태로 유지하고 그 사용 기간을 연장하도록 돕는다’가 알맞다.

body:
What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
*metric ton 메트릭톤(1,000kg을 1톤으로 하는 중량 단위)
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 각각 쓰시오.
Electronic waste, which harms human ______ and the environment because of its ______ substances, is ______ at a concerning rate every year, and various efforts are being made to tackle this problem, focusing on making electronic products ______ to fix.
solution: 정답은 health, toxic, increasing, easier 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? ⓐImagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new ⓑone. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on ⓒhow to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely ⓓwould have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score.
In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, ⓔmaking our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: 명령문을 이끄는 동사원형으로, 뒤에 명사절 접속사 that이 생략되어 있다.
ⓑ: 단수명사 laptop을 대신해 단수형으로 쓰인 부정대명사이다.
ⓒ: 흐름상 조동사 should를 사용해 how should she fix it으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
ⓓ: 과거에 일어났을 상황에 대한 추측을 나타내는 ‘would have p.p.(~했을 것이다)’가 쓰였다.
ⓔ: 흐름상 접속사 and를 사용해 and it will make로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
solution: ⓒ 문장 내에서 주어, 목적어 등의 역할을 하는 ‘의문사+to부정사’는 간접의문문인 ‘의문사+주어+should/can+동사원형’으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으므로, how to fix it은 how she should fix it으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.

body:
When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.
By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.

Repair Cafés help (A)______ e-waste and foster a more sustainable perspective by enabling individuals to learn and share the knowledge and skills needed to repair and (B)______ their own devices.
(A) (B)
choices: store / upgrade
increase / discard
decrease / maintain
minimize / throw away
maximize / care for

M: Suji, you’ve been working on your homework for so long. Aren’t you hungry? How about a snack?
G: A snack sounds great. I want some hot dogs!
M: Okay. I’ll heat up some frozen hot dogs in the microwave.
G: Thank you! It seems like microwaves can cook almost anything. Dad, have you ever wondered how they work? (A)I’m curious about the science of microwaves.
M: Well, it uses radiation to heat food. The radiation causes the water molecules in the food to vibrate and produce heat.
G: Oh, so it’s the moisture in the food that makes the microwave work?
M: Exactly. Without water molecules, the microwave wouldn’t be able to heat the food.
G: Wow, I didn’t know that. So, if I spray some water on the frozen hot dogs, will they heat up faster?
M: You got it! Yes, they will heat up faster. [beep] Oh, our hot dogs are ready!
G: Yay! Time for a snack!

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것 모두 고르면?
choices: I wonder about
I’d like to know
I’m indifferent to
I’m satisfied with
I’m excited about
solution:
‘I’m curious about ~‘는 ‘나는 ~이 궁금하다’라는 의미로, 어떤 것에 대한 궁금증을 표현할 때 쓰는 표현이다. 따라서 ① ‘I wonder about(나는 ~에 대해 궁금하다)‘와 ② ‘I’d like to know(나는 ~을 알고 싶다)‘로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
오답
③ 나는 ~에 무관심하다
④ 나는 ~에 만족한다
⑤ 나는 ~에 신이 난다

body:
Have you ever wondered, “What if I could run so fast that nobody could see me?” If you have asked this kind of question, you may be ready to become the next Galileo. (A)이탈리아 과학자인 Galileo Galilei는 사고 실험으로 유명한데, 사고 실험이란 수학적 또는 과학적 가설을 탐구하려고 설계된 상상의 실험이다. With only his thoughts, he demonstrated that objects with different masses should fall at the same speed when dropped from the same height in the absence of air resistance. With a hypothesis based on creativity and imagination, anyone can become a great scientist.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 알맞은 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• 명사를 수식하는 분사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
design, famous, hypothesis, experiment
imaginary, explore, a thought experiment
The Italian scientist Galileo Galilei ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ or ______ ______.
answer: is famous for a thought experiment, which is an imaginary experiment designed to explore a mathematical or scientific hypothesis
solution:
• ‘be famous for ~(~으로 유명하다)’를 사용하여 is famous for를 쓰고 ‘사고 실험’을 뜻하는 a thought experiment를 목적어로 쓴다.
• 선행사 a thought experiment를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 콤마(,) 뒤에 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 쓰고 단수 선행사 a thought experiment에 수일치한 단수동사 is, 주격보어 an imaginary experiment를 이어 쓴다.
• 명사구 an imaginary experiment가 과학적 가설을 탐구하려고 ‘설계된’ 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 designed를 쓰고, ‘design+목적어+to부정사(~하려고 …을 설계하다)‘ 구문의 수동형 ’be designed+to부정사’을 사용하여, to부정사 to explore를 쓴 후 제시된 or과 함께 목적어 a mathematical or scientific hypothesis가 되도록 이어 쓴다.

body:
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what ⓐwould happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems ⓑthat would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is ⓒwhat the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. (A) However, the area of the feet ⓓsupports his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). (B) This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased ⓔfar more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body. (C) If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. (D) However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. (E)

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ what → that (완전한 절(the giant ~ feet)을 이끌어 be동사 is에 이어지는 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓓ supports → supporting (뒤에 조동사 would가 있으므로 주어 the area of the feet를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, the area of the feet가 그의 몸을 ‘지탱하는’ 주체이므로 supports를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 supporting으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 'if+주어+과거동사 ~'의 형태로 ‘사람이 거인처럼 엄청난 크기로 자랄 수 있다면’의 현재 사실과 반대되는 일 또는 현재나 미래에 실현 가능성이 희박한 일을 가정하는 가정법 과거가 쓰였으므로, 주절에는 ‘조동사 과거형+동사원형‘이 쓰여야 한다. 따라서 would happen은 적절하다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(would ~ danger)을 이끌어 many problems를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ '훨씬’의 의미로 뒤의 비교급 more을 강조하는 부사 far은 적절하다.

body:
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what ⓐwould happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems ⓑthat would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is ⓒwhat the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. (A) However, the area of the feet ⓓsupports his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). (B) This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased ⓔfar more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body. (C) If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. (D) However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. (E)

This shows that while we may wish to grow as tall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이것은 우리가 거인만큼 크게 자라기를 바라지만 우리는 그 형태로는 생존할 수 없을 거라는 것을 보여준다.’라는 뜻으로, This(이것)가 가리키는 것이 생존이 불가능한 이유라는 것을 알 수 있다. 글의 흐름상 두 번째 문단은 무게 증가(1000배)에 비해 상대적으로 적은 발의 면적 증가(100배)로 인해 거인이 스스로 똑바로 서있을 수 없음을 설명하고 있으며, 세 번째 문단은 우리 몸에서 발생하는 열의 증가량(1000배)에 비해 표면적의 증가(100배)가 상대적으로 적어에 충분한 열이 배출되지 않는다는 설명을 하고 있다. 따라서 우리 생존과 직결된 것은 열 배출 문제를 설명하는 세 번째 문단이며, This가 가리키는 것은 열 배출과 관련된 결과(결과적으로, 충분한 열이 피부를 통하여 신체로부터 배출되지 않을 것)이므로 이 뒤인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what ⓐwould happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems ⓑthat would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is ⓒwhat the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. (A) However, the area of the feet ⓓsupports his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). (B) This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased ⓔfar more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body. (C) If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. (D) However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. (E)

2. What if there were no Moon?
“O, swear not by the moon, the inconstant moon.” This is a famous line from Romeo and Juliet. Juliet warns Romeo not ⓐto swear his love by the Moon as it may change just as the Moon changes its shape. Although its appearance changes, the Moon is always present in the night sky and plays a crucial role in regulating the length of the day on Earth as well as the Earth’s seasons and weather patterns. Then, what would happen if there ⓑwere no Moon?
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean ⓒto rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, ⓓresulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun ⓔto rise every five hours.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ to rise → rise (지각동사 see의 목적격보어 자리로, 지각동사의 목적격보어는 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 때 동사원형 또는 진행을 강조하는 현재분사를 쓰고, 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동 관계일 때는 과거분사를 쓴다. 여기서 목적어 the Sun은 ‘뜨는’ 주체이자 rise가 자동사로 쓰였으므로, 목적격보어로 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 rise가 와야 한다. 따라서 to rise를 동사원형 rise로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 동사 warn은 ‘warn+목적어+목적격보어((not+)to부정사)(~에게 …하(지 말)라고 경고를 주다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격 보어로 쓰인 to부정사 to swear는 적절하다.
ⓑ ‘달이 없다면 무슨 일이 일어날까?‘라는 현재 사실과 반대되는 일(달인 없는 상황)을 가정하고 있으므로 가정법 과거 ‘If+주어+과거 동사 ~, 주어+과거형 조동사+동사원형 …’이 쓰였으며, 이때 If절의 동사로 be동사가 올 때는 주어의 수와 관계없이 과거동사 were을 쓰는 것이 원칙이므로 뒤에 주어 no Moon에 관계없이 were이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
ⓒ 동사 causes는 ‘cause+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어 자리의 to부정사 to rise는 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(the Earth’s ~ down)에 접속사나 주어 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절 전체가 변화를 ‘가져오는[야기하는]’ 주체이자 result는 자동사이므로, 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 resulting은 적절하다.

body:
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, ⓐ[makes / making] up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better ⓑ[have / to have] a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
(A) Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies.
(B) However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain.
(C) While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as ⓒ[efficient / efficiently] as lungs at taking in air.
Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 대기 중에 더 높은 농도의 산소가 있는 것이 더 좋을 것인지, 산소 농도가 두 배가 된다면 무슨 일이 일어나는지 묻는 주어진 글 뒤에, 이 질문에 대한 답변으로 특히 곤충들에게 예상치 못한 결과가 발생할 수 있다고 언급하는 (C)가 이어져야 한다. 곤충은 폐가 없고 외부의 숨구멍을 통해 공기를 받아들이는데, 그 숨구멍이 폐만큼 효율적이지 않다는 (C)에 이어, Therefore(그러므로)로 이어져 현재 산소 농도에서는 곤충이 더 커질 수 없다고 설명한 뒤, 그 이유를 설명하는 (A)가 이어지며, 이후 However(그러나)를 통해 산소 농도가 두 배가 되면 곤충이 산소를 더 쉽게 이용할 수 있어 더 크게 자랄 수 있다는 반대 상황을 제시하는 (B)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
Have you ever heard the expression “I love you to the moon and back”? This expression conveys a deep extent of love, and uses the great distance between the Earth and the Moon as a metaphor. While this expression is easily understood, there are idioms with a scientific background that may not be so obvious. One example is the phrase “once in a blue moon.” Although people may have seen a magnificent full moon brightening the night sky or a tiny crescent resembling a clipped fingernail, it is highly unlikely that they have seen a blue moon. Surprisingly, this extraordinary event does occur. Normally, there is only one full moon in a month. However, every 2.5 years, there can be two full moons in the same month. The second moon is called a “blue moon,” and it occurs because the Moon completes its cycle of phases in only about 29.5 days. From this rare phenomenon of a blue moon emerged the use of the expression “once in a blue moon.” It describes something that happens exceptionally infrequently.

Some common English expressions have (A)______ origins that are not immediately apparent, as illustrated by the expression “once in a blue moon,” which refers to an extremely (B)______ occurrence.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: scientific rare
scientific frequent
cultural rare
cultural frequent
historical often
solution:
[요약문] 극히 (B)드문 일을 가리키는 표현인 ‘once in a blue moon’에서 볼 수 있듯이, 일부 흔히 사용되는 영어 표현들은 쉽게 알아차리기 어려운 (A)과학적 기원을 가지고 있다.
오답
② 과학적 자주
③ 문화적 드문
④ 문화적 자주
⑤ 역사적 종종

body:
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, making up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as efficient as lungs at taking in air.
Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could (A)[shrink / grow] in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain. Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, (B)[altering / maintaining] the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.
Fortunately, you wouldn’t need to worry about giant insects chasing after you if this were to occur. If the oxygen concentration were to double, you would be able to run (C)[slower / faster] than you can right now. Considering that oxygen is used to break down energy so that muscles can use it, the increase in oxygen would help to use energy more efficiently and improve our capability for physical exercise. ㉠이것은 우리에게 운동선수들이 올림픽 경기에서 새로운 세계 기록을 수립하는 것을 기대하게 할 것이다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: grow altering faster
shrink maintaining faster
grow altering slower
shrink altering faster
grow maintaining slower
solution:
(A) 효율적이지 않은 숨구멍을 가진 곤충들은 크기가 현재보다 더 커지면 산소가 몸의 가장 깊은 부위에 도달할 수 없기에 현재 산소 농도에서는 곤충이 현재보다 더 크게 진화할 수 없다고 설명한 뒤, 산소 농도가 두 배가 되면 산소를 더 쉽게 이용할 수 있다고 했으므로 곤충의 크기가 더 커질 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 grow(커지다)가 적절하다.
shrink 줄어들다
(B) 곤충의 크기가 증가하면 생태계에 큰 영향을 미쳐 먹이사슬을 교란할 수 있고, 잠자리와 같은 곤충이 독수리만큼 커질 수 있다고 했으므로 포식자와 피식자의 균형을 변화시킨다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 altering(변화시키는)이 적절하다.
maintain ~을 유지하다
(C) 산소가 두 배가 되면 에너지를 더 효율적으로 사용하여 운동 능력이 향상될 수 있다고 설명하고 있으므로 지금보다 더 빨리 달릴 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 faster(더 빨리)가 적절하다.
slow 느리게

윗글의 밑줄 친 ㉠의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것

<보기>
lead, the Olympics, expect, records, will set, athletes
→ ______
answer: This leads us to expect that athletes would set new world records at the Olympics.
solution:
• 주어 This와 동사 leads를 쓰고, 동사 leads는 ‘lead+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰일 수 있으므로 목적어 us와 목적격보어 to expect를 쓴다.
• to expect의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓰고 뒤에 완전한 절을 연결해야 한다.

body:
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, ⓐfriction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation ⓑrate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s ⓒrotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is ⓓtilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The ⓔhemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially making summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.

<보기>
ⓐ friction: disagreement or unfriendliness caused by people having different opinions
ⓑ rate: a charge or payment that is set according to a standard scale
ⓒ rotation: movement in a circle around a fixed point
ⓓ tilt: to make something move into a position where one side is higher than the other
ⓔ hemisphere: a half of the Earth, especially one of the halves above and below the equator

body:
Colors strengthen the emotions of viewers due to their ability to evoke strong psychological reactions. An excellent example can be found in an animated film where an ordinary citizen becomes a superhero to defeat a villain. At the beginning of the film, the male character, who was once a superhero but had to return to living an ordinary life, is surrounded by dull colors and gray tones. He is working as if he were an ordinary person, hiding his true power. However, when he returns to work as a superhero, the film fills up with bold reds, yellows, and blues. These colors represent power and happiness. This shift reflects his emotional development, and viewers can grasp his mood without words. Through such a process, colors impact the emotional experience of the audience.
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What ability of colors allows them to intensify the emotions of viewers?
Why did the male character in the animated film have to return to living an ordinary life?
What color tones characterize the surroundings of the male character early in the film?
When does the film begin to fill up with vivid colors?
How can viewers figure out the character’s mood without words?

body:
Like the saying “______,” colors get a film’s message across more strongly than words. A good example is the red coat in a movie about the true story of a German businessman who saved thousands of Jews from the Nazis during World War II. While the movie was mostly in black and white, the director chose one particular thing to add color to. It was the red coat of a single lost girl, alone in a crowd of frightened Jews. As such, it was the strong contrast of colors that enabled the director to powerfully symbolize the brutality of the Nazis. The young girl represents innocence while also representing the violence of the Nazis. So, what happened to this young girl? The movie never tells us for sure, but later in the film we see a dead girl in a red coat being loaded into a cart.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: All that glitters is not gold
There are two sides to every story
A picture paints a thousand words
The pen is mightier than the sword
The grass is always greener on the other side
solution:
색상은 영화의 메시지를 말보다 더 강하게 전달한다는 내용이 흑백과 붉은색의 대비를 통해 나치의 잔혹성을 강력하게 나타낸 한 구체적 영화의 예시와 함께 이어지므로, 말보다 시각적 이미지가 의미 전달에 더욱 효과적이라는 내용의 속담을 언급하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ③ ‘그림 하나가 천 마디의 말을 그려낸다’가 알맞다.
본문변형 빈칸은 원래 지문에서 ‘A picture is worth a thousand words’였음

ⓓ had been → were (주절의 동사구(is working)와 같은 현재 시점에서 반대되는 사실을 가정해 ‘마치 ~인 것처럼’이라는 뜻을 나타내야 하므로, ‘as if+가정법 과거(주어+were/과거동사~)’를 사용해 had been을 were로 고친다. 참고로, ‘as if+가정법 과거완료(주어+had+been/p.p.~)’는 ‘마치 ~였던/~했던 것처럼’이라는 뜻으로 주절보다 이전의 시점에서 반대되는 상황을 가정할 때 쓰인다.)
ⓔ reflecting → reflects (콤마(,)와 등위접속사 and 뒤에 완전한 절(viewers can ~ words)이 이어지므로, 콤마(,) 앞도 완전한 절(주어+동사~)의 형태를 이루어야 한다. 따라서 주어 This shift 뒤에 명사구 his emotional development를 목적어로 취하는 능동태 동사가 흐름상 현재시제로 쓰여야 하며, 주어가 단수명사구이므로 단수동사로 수일치 시켜 reflecting을 reflects로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 주어 the male character와 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 관계사절 ‘who ~ life‘ 뒤에 문장의 동사(구)가 와야 하며, 주어가 타동사 surround(~을 둘러싸다)의 대상이고, ’~에 둘러싸여 있다‘라는 뜻으로 ’be surrounded by ~‘를 사용하므로, 단수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 단수형 be동사 is를 쓴 is surrounded by는 알맞다.

Colors strengthen the emotions of viewers due to their ability ⓐto evoke strong psychological reactions. An excellent example can be found in an animated film ⓑwhere an ordinary citizen becomes a superhero to defeat a villain. (A) At the beginning of the film, the male character, who was once a superhero but had to return to living an ordinary life, ⓒis surrounded by dull colors and gray tones. (B) He is working as if he ⓓhad been an ordinary person, hiding his true power. (C) These colors represent power and happiness. (D) This shift ⓔreflecting his emotional development, and viewers can grasp his mood without words. (E) Through such a process, colors impact the emotional experience of the audience.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
However, when he returns to work as a superhero, the film fills up with bold reds, yellows, and blues.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그러나 그가 슈퍼히어로로 되돌아가 활동할 때, 영화는 강렬한 빨강, 노랑, 파랑으로 가득 찬다.’라는 뜻으로, However(그러나)를 사용해 장면의 반전을 도입하는 흐름이므로, 남성 캐릭터가 칙칙한 색상과 회색 톤으로 둘러싸여 있고 마치 보통 사람인 것처럼 일하고 있다는 대조적인 내용의 뒤이자, 주어진 문장에서 언급된 bold reds, yellows, and blues(강렬한 빨강, 노랑, 파랑)를 These colors로 가리켜 이러한 색들이 힘과 행복을 상징한다고 설명하는 문장 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Film directors capture the changes in their characters’ lives through changes in color. Another film from the 1990s follows the dramatic experience of a man with scissor hands who comes down to a town to live with ordinary folks. He always wears black, and the castle where he used to live was a gray and gloomy place. However, in the town where he came to live with his lover, each house is painted (A)[similarly / differently], and the people wear colorful clothes. At first, he is welcomed by the people in town, but as he becomes misunderstood and disliked, the film’s colors gradually become (B)[brighter / darker]. Eventually, he returns to his castle, but he fills his garden with green grass and beautiful, blooming flowers. Moreover, ice powder from his ice sculpture blows in the wind like snow. With such changes, the director shows the audience that his life has become much more (C)[joyful / miserable].
Film directors choose colors to give us the best possible experience. ⓐ영화를 볼 때, 왜 특정 색상들이 한 장면에서 사용되는지 생각하라. You may not know the answer, but your understanding of the film will be deeper.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: similarly brighter joyful
similarly brighter miserable
differently darker miserable
differently brighter miserable
differently darker joyful
solution:
(A) 영화 속의 가위손을 가진 남자가 항상 검은 옷을 입고 있고 그가 예전에 살던 성은 회색빛의 우울한 장소였다는 내용 뒤에 However(그러나)로 대조적인 분위기의 내용이 이어져야 하므로, 마을들은 집집마다 각기 다른 색으로 칠해져 있고 사람들이 다채로운 옷을 입고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 differently(다르게)가 알맞다.
similarly 비슷하게
(B) 영화감독들이 색상의 변화를 통해 캐릭터의 삶의 변화를 포착해낸다는 것을 보여주는 예시로서 영화가 제시되었으므로, 가위손을 가진 남자가 오해받고 미움을 받게 되면서 영화의 색상이 더 어두워진다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 darker(더 어두운)가 알맞다.
brighter 더 밝은
(C) 남자가 성으로 다시 돌아온 후 자신의 정원을 초록빛 풀과 아름답고 활짝 핀 꽃들로 가득 채우며, 그의 얼음 조각상에서 나오는 얼음 가루는 눈처럼 바람에 날린다고 했으므로, 감독이 밝은색과 이미지로의 변화를 통해 남자의 삶이 훨씬 더 즐거워졌음을 보여준다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 much more 뒤에 joyful(즐거운)이 알맞다.
miserable 비참한
본문변형 happier → more joyful

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 접속사를 남겨둔 분사구문을 사용할 것
• 간접의문문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
use, consider, watch, specific, when
→ ______ ______ movies, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ in a scene.
answer: When watching, consider why specific colors are used
solution:
⦁<조건>에 따라 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사 When을 남겨둔 ‘접속사+분사(구)’ 형태의 분사구문을 사용한다. 주절로 이어질 명령문의 생략된 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 ’보는‘ 주체이고, 빈칸 뒤에 제시된 명사 movies가 목적어이므로, 동사 watch를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 watching으로 변형한다.
⦁주절은 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문의 형태가 되어야 하므로, 동사원형 consider를 쓴다. 이어지는 목적어 자리에는 <조건>에 따라 간접의문문을 ’의문사+평서문‘의 어순으로 쓴다. 즉, 의문사 why 뒤에 ’주어+동사~‘의 순서로 주어인 명사구 specific colors를 먼저 쓰고, 주어가 ’사용되는‘ 대상이므로 현재시제 수동태를 사용하여 복수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 복수동사 are와 동사 use를 과거분사로 변형한 used를 쓴다.

Colors are an important aspect of films. They look visually (A)[attractive / attractively] and can be used to convey various emotions and messages to the audience. Film directors carefully select colors like bright yellow to bring a sense of hope, calm blue for peace, and intense red for violence. These color choices are not random; they are intentionally made to impact your experience while you watch the film, even if you don’t consciously notice them. Below are several outstanding examples of how (B)[skillful / skillfully] film directors can use color to add richness to the story and (C)[evoke / evoking] specific emotions from the audience.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

attractive skillfully evoke
solution:
(A) ‘look+보어(~하게 보이다)’의 2형식 감각동사로 쓰인 look의 보어로 형용사(구)가 와야 하며, 보어 자리에 부사(구)는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사 visually의 수식을 받아 형용사구를 이루는 형용사 attractive가 알맞다.
(B) 의문부사 how는 형용사나 부사를 수식해 의문사구를 이룰 수 있으나, 일반동사를 포함한 동사구 can use를 수식해야 하므로, 부사 skillfully가 알맞다.
(C) 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to add와 등위 접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 ‘불러일으키기 위해’라는 의미를 나타내야 하므로, to를 생략한 동사원형 evoke가 알맞다.

body:
The national flags of various European countries are tricolored, with the original being the French flag. The flags of Bolivia, Italy, and Ireland ⓐ[resemble / resembles] the French flag with three colors, while Germany, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, and Russia use three colors with parallel bands. The symbolism of the three colors in each country is different.
Ireland
The Irish tricolor consists of green, white, and orange. It was crafted in celebration of the French Revolution and as a wish for the success of Ireland’s own revolution. Green symbolizes the Irish Catholics, orange represents the Irish Protestants, and white signifies harmony and peace between the two communities.
France
The French tricolor flag, a product of the declaration of the “rights of man” during the French Revolution stating, “All men are born free and equal,” has served as an example for the tricolor flags of numerous countries that followed. The French flag consists of blue, white, and red, ⓑ[symbolizes / symbolizing] liberty, equality, and fellowship.
Germany
The German flag, with its colors of black, red, and gold, has evolved to symbolize unification, liberty, and democracy. These colors came from the reunification of Germany formerly without specific meanings. In modern times, black represents persistence, red represents courage and strength, and gold symbolizes generosity. This flag with three colors, introduced in the late 18th century, became prominent in the 19th century.
Italy
Italy, influenced by the French Revolution in its unification, initially adopted a flag with green, white, and red, along with a shield and cross. However, in 1946, these symbols were removed from the tricolor. The colors symbolize Italy’s landscape and human rights, with red ⓒ[represented / representing] love and the conflict from the Wars of Italian Independence and Unification, and white symbolizing faith and the snowy Alps.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: resemble symbolizing representing
resembles symbolizing representing
resemble symbolizing represented
resembles symbolizes represented
resemble symbolizes representing
solution:
ⓐ 주어 ‘The flags of Bolivia, Italy, and Ireland‘에 대한 동사 자리이며, 주어의 핵심인 The flags가 복수명사구이므로, 복수동사로 수일치한 resemble이 알맞다.
ⓑ 동사가 있는 완전한 절(The French flag consists ~ red)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구(liberty, equality, and fellowship)가 있으므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 symbolizing이 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘~가 …한 채로, ~가 …하면서’를 뜻하는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’ 구문을 이루는 분사 자리로, 명사 red가 ’상징하는‘ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어(love ~ Unification)가 이어지므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 representing이 알맞다.

choices: The tricolor flags of many countries have been modeled after the French flag.

solution:
독일 국기의 검은색, 빨간색, 금색은 통일, 자유, 민주주의를 상징하는 것으로 발전했으며, 이 색깔들은 이전에는 특정한 의미가 없었던 독일 재통일에서 비롯되었고, 현대에는 검은색은 끈기를, 빨간색은 용기와 힘을, 금색은 관용을 상징한다고 했으므로, ④ ‘독일 국기의 색깔들은 처음부터 끈기, 용기와 힘, 그리고 관용을 상징했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
