body:
Colors help audiences grasp the connections between characters, places, and important objects in films, making complex stories ⓐeasier to understand. (A)순식간에 토네이도에 의해 마법의 나라로 휩쓸린 후에 집으로 돌아가려고 시도하는 소녀의 모험을 보여주는 1930년대의 한 영화가 있다. The director uses colors to effectively ⓑconfuse the audience. The girl’s life in a boring village is shown in black and white, and the world of magic is expressed in ⓒvarious colors in the movie. With such color differences, the audience can ⓓdistinguish which world the events take place in. Audiences watching this film are ⓔimmersed in the world of magic as if they were the girl when watching the scenes that turn to color in a flash.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 주격 관계대명사 that을 사용할 것
• 분사구를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
return, sweep away, show, attempt, a girl, a film, in a flash, the adventures
→ ______ ______ ______ ______ from the 1930s ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ after ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ by a tornado to a land of magic.
answer: There is a film, that shows the adventures of a girl attempting to return home, being swept away in a flash
solution:
⦁’~가 있다‘를 뜻하는 ’There+be동사+주어 ~‘ 구문을 활용해 유도부사 There 뒤에 단수동사로 수일치한 is와 단수명사구인 주어 a film을 쓴다.
⦁<조건>에 따라 주격 관계대명사 that을 사용해 a film from the 1930s를 수식하는 관계사절을 ’that+주어가 없는 불완전한 절‘의 형태로 쓴다. 관계사절의 내용은 일반적인 사실을 나타내므로 현재시제를 사용하고, 선행사의 핵심이 단수명사구인 a film이므로 동사 show를 단수동사로 수일치한 shows로 변형한 후, 목적어로 명사구 the adventures of a girl을 쓴다.
⦁명사구 a girl 뒤에 <조건>에 따라 분사구를 사용한다. 수식받는 명사구 a girl이 ’시도하는‘ 주체이므로 동사 attempt를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 attempting으로 변형하고, ’~하려고 시도하다, ~하려고 애쓰다‘라는 뜻으로 ’attempt+to부정사‘를 사용하므로 동사 return을 to부정사인 to return으로 변형한 뒤, 빈칸 수를 고려해 ’집으로‘라는 뜻의 부사로 home을 쓴다.
⦁빈칸 수를 고려해 전치사 after의 목적어로 동명사구가 이어지도록 하되, 동명사의 의미상 주어 a girl이 ’휩쓸린‘ 대상이므로 수동형 동명사(being+p.p.)를 사용해 being 뒤에 ’타동사+부사‘ 구조의 구동사 ’sweep ~ away(~을 휩쓸어 가다)‘의 sweep을 과거분사 swept로 변형하고 부사 away를 쓴다. 이어서 부사구 in a flash를 쓴다.

body:
Like the saying “A picture is worth a thousand words,” colors get a film’s message across more strongly than words (A)do. A good example is the red coat in a movie about the true story of a German businessman who saved thousands of Jews from the Nazis during World War II. (B)While the movie was mostly in black and white, the director chose one particular thing to add color to. It was the red coat of a single lost girl, alone in a crowd of frightened Jews. As such, it was the strong contrast of colors (C)that enabled the director to powerfully symbolize the brutality of the Nazis. The young girl represents innocence (D)while also representing the violence of the Nazis. So, what happened to this young girl? The movie never tells us for sure, but later in the film we see a dead girl in a red coat (E)being loaded into a cart.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): 동사구 ‘get a film’s message across’의 반복을 피하기 위해 쓰였으며, 생략할 수 있다.
(B): ‘~인 반면에’라는 의미로 쓰여 주절과 대조되는 의미의 부사절을 이끌고 있다.
(C): 선행사인 the strong contrast of colors를 수식하는 관계사절을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사이며, which로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
(D): while she also represents 또는 while she is also representing으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
(E): see의 목적어인 a dead girl in a red coat가 ‘실리는’ 대상이며 진행 중인 상황을 나타내므로, 수동태 현재분사구 being loaded가 쓰였다.
solution:
(C) 주어인 the strong contrast of colors를 강조하기 위해 쓰인 ‘it was ~ that …(…한 것은 바로 ~였다)’ 형태의 강조 구문에 쓰인 that이다.
본문변형 (A) do는 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음

body:
Film directors capture the changes in their characters’ lives through changes in color. Another film from the 1990s ⓐfollows the dramatic experience of a man with scissor hands who comes down to a town to live with ordinary folks. He always wears black, and the castle ⓑin which he used to live was a gray and gloomy place. However, in the town where he came to live with his lover, each house ⓒis painted differently, and the people wear colorful clothes. At first, he is welcomed by the people in town, but as he becomes misunderstood and ⓓdisliked, the film’s colors gradually become darker. Eventually, he returns to his castle, but he fills his garden with green grass and beautiful, blooming flowers. Moreover, ice powder from his ice sculpture blows in the wind like snow. With such changes, the director shows the audience ⓔwhat his life has become much happier.
Film directors choose colors ⓕto give us the best possible experience. When watching movies, consider why specific colors are used in a scene. You may not know the answer, but your understanding of the film will be deeper.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 1개이다.
ⓔ what → that (동사 shows와 간접목적어인 the audience 뒤에 이어진 직접목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(his life has become much happier)을 이끌어, ’show+간접목적어+직접목적어(that절)(~에게 …라는 것을 보여주다)‘ 형태의 4형식 구문을 이루어야 하므로, what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다. 참고로, 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 불완전한 절을 이끌어 명사절을 이룬다.)
오답
ⓑ 완전한 절(he used to live)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the castle을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 쓴 ’전치사+관계대명사‘인 in which는 알맞다.
본문변형 where → in which

choices: Film directors maintain consistent colors regardless of changes in their characters’ lives.

solution:
가위손을 가진 한 남자는 항상 검은 옷을 입고 있고, 마을 사람들은 다채로운 옷을 입고 있다고 했으므로, ② ‘영화에서 마을 사람들은 가위손을 가진 남자와 대조적으로 밝은 옷을 입는다.’는 일치 내용이다.
남자가 오해받고 미움을 받게 되면서 영화의 색깔은 점점 더 어두워진다고 했으므로, ③ ‘마을 사람들이 남자에게 등을 돌리면서, 더 어두운 색상이 점차 영화를 지배하기 시작한다.’는 일치 내용이다.

① 영화감독들은 캐릭터들의 삶의 변화와 관계없이 일관된 색상을 유지한다. (→영화감독들은 색상의 변화를 통해 캐릭터들의 삶의 변화를 포착해낸다.)
④ 성 주변의 변화는 그 남자의 정서적 고통이 과거에 그랬던 것보다 더 악화되었음을 나타낸다. (→성의 변화들을 통해 감독은 관객들에게 그의 삶이 훨씬 더 행복해졌음을 보여준다.)
⑤ 일부 영화에서 색상을 사용하는 목적은 명확하지 않으며, 이는 영화를 이해하기 어렵게 한다. (→영화를 볼 때 특정 장면에서 왜 특정 색상이 사용되는지 생각해 본다면, 정답을 모를 수도 있지만 영화에 대한 이해는 더욱 깊어질 것이다.)

body:
Colors help audiences grasp the connections between characters, places, and important objects in films, making complex stories easier to understand. There is a film from the 1930s that shows the adventures of a girl attempting to return home after being swept away in a flash by a tornado to a land of magic. The director uses colors to effectively communicate with the audience. The girl’s life in a boring village is shown in black and white, and the world of magic is expressed in various colors in the movie. With such color differences, the audience can ______. Audiences watching this film are immersed in the world of magic as if they were the girl when watching the scenes that turn to color in a flash.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: lose track of where the events in the story are happening
overlook the visual contrast between the two different worlds
easily identify which of the two worlds each event occurs in
interpret both worlds as having nearly the same visual atmosphere
notice and distinguish the characters’ various psychological changes
solution:
글의 초반에 색상은 영화 속 캐릭터, 장소, 중요한 물건들 간의 연관성을 이해하도록 도와 복잡한 이야기를 이해하기 더 쉽게 만든다고 했으며, 그 예시로 제시된 영화에서 지루한 마을에서의 소녀의 생활은 흑백으로, 마법의 세계는 다양한 색상으로 표현되어 있다고 했으므로, 이러한 색상의 차이 덕분에 관객은 사건들이 어느 세계에서 일어나는지를 구분할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ③ ‘각 사건이 두 세계 중 어디에서 일어나고 있는지 쉽게 파악하다’가 알맞다.
본문변형 빈칸은 원래 ‘distinguish which world the events take place in’이었음

① 이야기의 사건들이 어디에서 일어나고 있는지를 놓치다
② 두 개의 다른 세계 사이의 시각적 대비를 간과하다
④ 두 세계가 거의 동일한 시각적 분위기를 지닌 것으로 해석하다
⑤ 등장인물들의 다양한 심리적 변화를 알아채고 구분하다

While the movie was mostly in black and white, the director chose one particular thing to add color to. It was the red coat of a single lost girl, alone in a crowd of ⓑfrightening Jews. As such, ⓒit was the strong contrast of colors that enabled the director to powerfully symbolize the brutality of the Nazis. Colors strengthen the emotions of viewers due to their ability to evoke strong psychological reactions. An excellent example can be found in an animated film where an ordinary citizen becomes a superhero to defeat a villain.
(A) This shift reflects his emotional development, and viewers can grasp his mood without words. Through such a process, colors impact the emotional experience of the audience.
(B) At the beginning of the film, the male character, who was once a superhero but had to return to living an ordinary life, is surrounded by dull colors and gray tones. He is working as if he were an ordinary person, hiding his true power.
(C) However, when he returns to work as a superhero, the film fills up with bold reds, yellows, and blues. These colors represent power and happiness.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 색상은 강한 심리적 반응을 불러일으키는 능력으로 인해 관객의 감정을 강화시키며, 평범한 시민이 슈퍼히어로가 되는 한 애니메이션 영화에서 훌륭한 예시를 찾을 수 있다는 내용의 주어진 글 다음에, 앞서 언급된 영화를 the film으로 가리켜 ‘그 영화’의 초반에는 한때 슈퍼히어로였던 남성 캐릭터가 칙칙한 색상과 회색 톤으로 둘러싸여 있고 마치 보통 사람인 것처럼 일하고 있다고 설명하는 (B), However(그러나)를 사용해 그가 슈퍼히어로로 되돌아가 활동하는 반전의 상황을 제시하며, 영화는 강렬한 빨강, 노랑, 파랑으로 가득 차 있고 이 색상들은 힘과 행복을 상징한다고 설명하는 (C), 칙칙한 색상과 회색 톤에서 빨강, 노랑, 파랑으로의 색상의 변화를 This shift로 가리켜 ‘이러한 변화’는 그의 정서적 성장을 나타내며, 관객들은 말없이도 그의 기분을 이해할 수 있다고 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

solution:

(2) 영화의 장면이 흑백에서 컬러로 전환될 때 관객들이 다양한 색상으로 표현되는 마법의 세계에 몰입하게 된다는 흐름이 되도록, when 이하의 내용은 ‘관객들이 순식간에 컬러로 바뀌는 장면들을 볼 때’라는 뜻이 되도록 한다. 단어 수를 고려해 접속사가 남아있는 분사구문을 사용해 접속사 when 뒤에 분사(구)를 쓰되, 앞 절의 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 they(=audiences)가 ‘보는’ 주체이므로 동사 watch를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 watching으로 변형하고, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the scenes를 쓴다. 이어서 <조건>에 따라 주격 관계대명사 that을 사용해 선행사 the scenes를 수식하는 관계사절이 ‘that+주어가 없는 불완전한 절’ 형태로 이어지도록 한다. that 뒤의 동사 자리에 ‘~로 변하다[바뀌다]’라는 뜻의 ‘turn to ~’를 사용하되, 문장 전체의 시제와 단어 수를 고려해 현재시제를 사용하고 선행사가 복수명사구이므로 복수동사 turn으로 수일치 시킨다.

The national flags of various European countries are tricolored, with the original ⓐbeing the French flag. The flags of Bolivia, Italy, and Ireland resemble the French flag with three colors, while Germany, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, and Russia use three colors with parallel bands. The symbolism of the three colors in each country ⓑare different.
Ireland
The Irish tricolor consists of green, white, and orange. It was crafted in celebration of the French Revolution and as a wish for the success of Ireland’s own revolution. Green symbolizes the Irish Catholics, orange represents the Irish Protestants, and white ⓒsignifying harmony and peace between the two communities.
France
The French tricolor flag, a product of the declaration of the “rights of man” during the French Revolution ⓓstating, “All men are born free and equal,” has served as an example for the tricolor flags of numerous countries that followed. The French flag consists of blue, white, and red, symbolizing liberty, equality, and fellowship.
Germany
The German flag, with its colors of black, red, and gold, has evolved to symbolize unification, liberty, and democracy. These colors came from the reunification of Germany formerly without specific meanings. In modern times, black represents persistence, red represents courage and strength, and gold symbolizes generosity. This flag with three colors, ⓔintroduced in the late 18th century, became prominent in the 19th century.
Italy
Italy, influenced by the French Revolution in its unification, initially adopted a flag with green, white, and red, along with a shield and cross. However, in 1946, these symbols ⓕwere removed from the tricolor. The colors symbolize Italy’s landscape and human rights, with red representing love and the conflict from the Wars of Italian Independence and Unification, and white symbolizing faith and the snowy Alps.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓑ are → is (주어 ‘The symbolism of the three colors in each country’ 뒤에 형용사 different를 보어로 취하는 be동사가 일반적 사실을 나타내는 현재시제로 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 핵심인 The symbolism이 단수명사구이므로, 수일치를 위해 복수동사 are를 단수동사 is로 고친다.)
ⓒ signifying → signifies (완전한 절인 ‘Green symbolizes the Irish Catholics’, ‘orange represents the Irish Protestants’와 ‘A, B, and C’의 병렬 구조를 이루는 완전한 절이 연결되어야 하므로 white를 주어로 하는 동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 signifying을 단수주어인 white에 수일치한 단수동사 signifies로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 전치사 with와 명사구 the original 뒤에 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)(~가 …인 채로, ~가 …하면서)’를 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 뒤에 보어로 명사구 the French flag가 있으므로, be의 현재분사 being은 알맞다.
ⓓ 주어 The French tricolor flag와 동사구 has served 사이에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입된 동격 어구는 명사구의 형태가 되어야 하므로 흐름상 the declaration of the “rights of man”을 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 수 있으며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘명시하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 타동사 state(~라는 것을 명시하다)의 목적어로 인용부호(“ ”)와 함께 쓰인 완전한 절(“All men are born free and equal”)이 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 stating은 알맞다.
ⓔ 주어 This flag with three colors와 동사 became 사이에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 수 있으며, 부연 설명의 대상인 주어가 ‘도입된’ 대상이고 타동사 introduce(~을 도입하다)의 목적어가 뒤에 없으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 introduced는 알맞다.
ⓕ 부사구 in 1946가 나타내는 과거의 일이며, 주어 these symbols가 ‘제거된’ 대상이고, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘remove ~ from …(~을 …에서 제거하다)’의 전치사 from이 쓰였으므로, 복수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 복수동사 were를 쓴 과거시제 수동태 were removed는 알맞다.

ⓐ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was ~ life)을 이끌어 주어인 the male character를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으며, 선행사가 사람이므로 주격 관계대명사 who가 알맞다. 참고로, 계속적 용법으로 관계대명사 that은 쓸 수 없다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(He ~ person) 다음에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 주절인 ‘he ~ person’의 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 he가 ‘숨기는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구(his true power)가 이어지므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 hiding이 알맞다.
ⓒ such는 명사(구)를 수식하며 ‘such+a(n)+(형용사+)명사(구)’의 구조를 이루므로, such 뒤에 관사 a가 쓰인 어순의 such a가 알맞다.

body:
Colors strengthen the emotions of viewers due to their ability to evoke strong psychological reactions. (A)평범한 시민이 악당을 물리치기 위해 슈퍼히어로가 되는 한 애니메이션 영화에서 훌륭한 예가 발견될 수 있다. At the beginning of the film, the male character, ⓐ[who / that] was once a superhero but had to return to living an ordinary life, is surrounded by dull colors and gray tones. He is working as if he were an ordinary person, ⓑ[hid / hiding] his true power. However, when he returns to work as a superhero, the film fills up with bold reds, yellows, and blues. These colors represent power and happiness. This shift reflects his emotional development, and viewers can grasp his mood without words. Through ⓒ[a such / such a] process, colors impact the emotional experience of the audience.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 적절한 관계부사와 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 맨 앞에 주어진 어구를 제외하고 17단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
find, defeat, become, an ordinary citizen, a villain, a superhero, an animated film
→ An excellent example can ______.
answer: be found in an animated film where an ordinary citizen becomes a superhero to defeat a villain
solution:
⦁주어인 An excellent example이 ‘발견되는’ 대상이므로 ‘조동사+be+p.p.’ 형태의 수동태를 사용해 조동사 can 뒤에 be를 쓰고 find를 과거분사 found로 변형한다.
⦁적절한 전치사 in을 추가한 뒤 명사구 an animated film을 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 적절한 관계부사로 where를 사용해 선행사인 an animated film을 수식하는 관계사절을 ‘where+완전한 절’ 형태로 쓴다. 관계사절의 주어로 an ordinary citizen을 쓰고, 단수주어에 수일치하도록 become을 단수동사 becomes로 변형한 뒤, 보어로 명사구 a superhero를 쓴다.
⦁<조건>에 따라 부사적 용법 중 목적을 나타내는 to부정사를 사용해 defeat를 to defeat로 변형하고, 목적어로 명사구 a villain을 쓴다.

body:
Like the saying “A picture is worth a thousand words,” colors get a film’s message across (A)[more / less] strongly than words. A good example is the red coat in a movie about the true story of a German businessman who saved thousands of Jews from the Nazis during World War II. While the movie was mostly in black and white, the director chose one particular thing to add color to. It was the red coat of a single lost girl, alone in a crowd of (B)[delighted / terrified] Jews. As such, it was the strong contrast of colors that enabled the director to powerfully symbolize the brutality of the Nazis. The young girl represents (C)[innocence / hope] while also representing the violence of the Nazis. So, what happened to this young girl? The movie never tells us for sure, but later in the film we see a dead girl in a red coat being loaded into a cart.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: more / delighted / innocence
less / terrified / innocence
more / terrified / innocence
less / delighted / hope
more / terrified / hope
solution:
(A) ‘그림은 천 마디 말의 가치가 있다.’라는 속담을 인용하고 있으므로, 색상은 영화의 메시지를 말보다 더 강력하게 전달한다는 흐름이 되는 more(더)가 알맞다.
less 덜
(B) 강렬한 색상의 대비가 감독으로 하여금 유대인에 대한 나치의 잔혹성을 상징할 수 있게 했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 길을 잃은 한 유대인 소녀가 겁에 질린 유대인 군중 속에 있는 장면을 언급하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 terrified(공포에 질린, 두려움에 떠는)가 알맞다.
본문변형 frightened(겁먹은, 무서워하는) → terrified(공포에 질린, 두려움에 떠는)
delighted 매우 기쁜
(C) 감독이 나치의 잔혹성을 강력하게 상징하기 위해 강렬한 색상의 대비를 사용했으며, 영화 후반부에 붉은 외투를 입은 죽은 소녀가 수레에 실리고 있는 장면을 볼 수 있다고 했으므로, 붉은 외투를 입은 어린 유대인 소녀는 나치의 폭력성과 동시에 무고하게 희생되는 소녀의 순수성을 상징한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 innocence(무죄, 결백, 순수함)가 알맞다.
hope 희망

body:
Colors help audiences (A)grasp the connections between characters, places, and important objects in films, making complex stories easier to understand. There is a film from the 1930s that shows the adventures of a girl attempting to return home after being swept away (B)in a flash by a tornado to a land of magic. The director uses colors to effectively communicate with the audience. The girl’s life in a (C)boring village is shown in black and white, and the world of magic is expressed in various colors in the movie. With such color differences, the audience can distinguish which world the events (D)take place in. Audiences watching this film are (E)immersed in the world of magic as if they were the girl when watching the scenes that turn to color in a flash.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)를 아래와 같이 바꾸어 쓸 때 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): comprehend
(B): in an instant
(C): dull
(D): occur
(E): detached from
solution:
(E) immersed in은 ‘~에 몰입한’을 뜻하므로, absorbed in(~에 몰두한) 등으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으며, ‘~로부터 분리된’을 뜻하는 detached from과는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.
오답
(A) grasp ~ ‘~을 이해하다’ = comprehend ~ ‘~을 이해하다’
(B) in a flash ‘순식간에’ = in an instant ‘순식간에’
(C) boring ‘지루한’ = dull ‘따분한, 재미없는’
(D) take place ’일어나다’ = occur ’발생하다, 일어나다’

solution:
색상은 강한 심리적 반응을 불러일으키는 능력으로 인해 관객의 감정을 강화시킬 수 있다고 했으며, 예시로 든 영화에서 한때 슈퍼히어로였으나 평범한 삶으로 돌아와야 했던 캐릭터는 칙칙한 색상과 회색 톤으로 둘러싸여 있지만, 그가 슈퍼히어로로 되돌아가 활동할 때 영화는 힘과 행복을 상징하는 강렬한 빨강, 노랑, 파랑으로 가득 차며, 이러한 색상의 변화는 그의 정서적 성장을 나타내고 관객들은 말없이도 그의 기분을 이해할 수 있다고 했으므로, 이러한 과정을 통해 영화에 사용된 색이 관객의 정서에 영향을 미친다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ① ‘관객들의 정서적 경험’이 알맞다.

body:
Good evening, everyone. Welcome to the November Book Concert. I’m especially excited to introduce tonight’s author, who is known as the queen of winter. When I read her books, I was fascinated by her descriptions of the winter landscape. (A) They are so vivid and alive that I felt like I was in a world of snowflakes. (B) She has written a number of best-selling novels. (C) Into the Aurora is a story about a young girl who goes on a journey to see the Northern Lights. (D) While enjoying the snow and the stars, they learn about the beauty of nature. (E) Starry Starry Nights has been translated into five languages. We’re honored to have her here tonight to talk about her works. Please join me in welcoming the gifted and inspiring author Alice Lee.
주어진 문장: Another novel, Starry Starry Nights, is about a family that moves to Alaska.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘또 다른 소설인 “별이 빛나는 밤”은 알래스카로 이주하는 한 가족에 관한 이야기입니다.’라는 뜻으로, Another(또 다른)로 또 다른 소설을 추가 설명하는 흐름이므로, Alice Lee의 베스트셀러 소설 중 북극광을 보러 여행을 떠나는 어린 소녀의 이야기인 “오로라 속으로”을 설명하는 문장의 뒤이자, they로 주어진 문장의 ‘a family that moves to Alaska(알래스카로 이주하는 한 가족)’를 가리켜 그들이 눈과 별을 즐기면서 자연의 아름다움에 대해 알게 된다며 소설의 내용을 소개하는 문장 앞인 (D)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

body:
Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him ⓐsincerely, but the Colonel won’t let them marry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds.
One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very ⓑmiserable face. His clothes were old and worn out.
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his ⓒasset?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a ⓓreasonable share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“ⓔExactly, exactly! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ Exactly, exactly(바로 그거야, 바로 그거야) → Nonsense, nonsense(말도 안 돼, 말도 안 돼)

body:
That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and ⓐfinding Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture ⓑfinished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who ⓒare you, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I ⓓcould do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, ⓔfell to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes (A)______. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “(B)An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, ⓕnot to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
기호      어색한 표현         알맞은 표현
(1) ( ______ )      ______      →      ______
(2) ( ______ )      ______      →      ______
(3) ( ______ )      ______      →      ______
answer:
(1) ⓐ finding → found
(2) ⓒ are you → you are
(3) ⓔ fell → falling
solution:
ⓐ 주어 he에 연결된 과거형 동사 walked와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 finding을 과거형 동사 found로 고친다.
ⓒ know의 목적어 자리에서 의문사 who가 간접의문문(의문사+평서문)을 이루어야 하므로 의문사 who 뒤에 are you를 ’주어+동사‘의 어순인 you are로 고친다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(His ~ worn)에 접속사 없이 콤마로 과거형 동사가 연결될 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이끄는 분사 자리가 되어야 한다. 의미상 주어인 His clothes가 해어지는 주체이며 fall은 자동사이므로 현재분사 falling으로 고친다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)An artist’s heart is his head가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?

body:
After a while, the servant came in and told Alan that the frame-maker wanted to see him. Alan said, “I will be back in a moment,” as he went out. The old beggar took advantage of Alan’s absence to rest for a moment on a chair. He looked so sad and lonely. Hughie couldn’t help pitying him and felt his own pockets to see what money he had. All he could find, however, was a few coins. “Poor old fellow, he wants them more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks,” he thought to himself. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar’s hand. The old man was surprised and smiled faintly. “Thank you, sir,” he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at what he had done.
Hughie spent the day with Laura, received a gentle scolding for his actions, and had to walk home.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: The old beggar remained standing throughout Alan’s absence.
The old beggar’s sorrowful and lonely appearance aroused Hughie’s sympathy for him.
Hughie gave the beggar his coins despite the inconvenience it would cause him.
The beggar reacted with surprise and a slight smile but declined to accept the coins from Hughie.

“You don’t mean to say you talked to him about her?” said Hughie.
“Sure I did. He knows all about the Colonel, Laura, and the 10,000 pounds,” replied Alan.
“You told that old beggar all my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and angry.
“My dear boy,” said Alan, smiling, “that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest ⓐman in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and asked me a month ago to paint him as a beggar.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie, feeling ⓑembarrassed. “Good heavens! I gave him some coins,” he said, sinking into an armchair.
“What? You gave him coins?” cried Alan, bursting into laughter. He went on, “Well, it never occurred to me ⓒwhat you would distribute money in that way. Besides, (A)네가 들어왔을 때 나는 Hausberg 남작이 자신의 이름이 언급되는 것을 좋아할지 아닐지 몰랐어. You know he wasn’t in full dress.”
“Oh no, what did I do? The best thing I can do is to go to bed, and, my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone,” said Hughie, and he went home, ⓓfeeling very unhappy.
The next morning, when Hughie was having breakfast, an old gentleman visited his house. The man said, “I have come from Baron Hausberg,” and continued, “The Baron ....” Hughie interrupted, “I beg you, sir, ⓔto offer him my sincerest apologies.” Then, with a smile, the old gentleman said, “The Baron has asked me to bring you this letter,” and gave Hughie a sealed envelope. On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar,” and inside ⓕwere a check for 10,000 pounds.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ man → men (’가장 ~한 …들 중 하나‘라는 뜻의 ’one of the+최상급+복수명사(구)‘ 형태가 되어야 하므로 단수명사 man을 복수명사 men으로 고친다.)
ⓒ what → that (가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리에서 완전한 절(you ~ way)을 이끌고 있으므로, what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓕ were → was (장소 등을 나타내는 부사(구)가 강조를 위해 문두에 오면서 절의 주어와 동사가 도치되어 be동사가 먼저 나온 것으로, 주어가 단수명사구 a check이므로 복수동사 were를 단수동사 was로 고친다.)

body:
Throughout history, people have always tried to understand themselves and the world ⓐ[which / where] they live in, and these efforts are reflected in the stories they tell. An interesting example of such stories is the pourquoi tales, which aim to explain the origins or reasons behind various phenomena. As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. These imaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, ⓑ[provide / providing] creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots. According to this story, leopards were originally plain brown like the desert. However, in order not to reveal themselves while hunting animals in the forest, leopards decided to paint spots on their skins. This story explains that leopards developed spots as a means of survival.
Pourquoi tales serve several purposes. They engage readers with imaginative stories, ⓒ[teach / teaches] lessons, and serve as a means of passing on knowledge to future generations. These stories explore the complexity of the world around us.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ      ⓑ      ⓒ
choices: which providing teach
which provide teaches
where provide teach
where providing teaches
which provide teach
solution:
ⓐ 전치사의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they live in)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the world를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.
ⓑ 명사구 These imaginative stories와 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 명사구를 부연 설명하는 분사구 뒤에 있으며, 뒤에 이어진 다른 동사(구)가 없이 명사구(creative explanations ~)만 이어지므로 문장의 동사 자리이다. 따라서 현재동사 provide가 알맞다.
ⓒ 주어인 복수대명사 They에 수일치한 복수 동사 engage, serve와 함께 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬 연결되어 있으므로, 복수 동사 teach가 알맞다.

body:
One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

Feeling (A)______ for Alan’s poor-looking model and learning about the large difference in their earnings, Hughie argues that the model deserves a fairer share, while Alan emphasizes the (B)______ required of the painter.
(A)      (B)
choices: compassion ease
disgust labor
sympathy exertion
admiration patience
pity idleness
solution: 정답은 ③ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
How does Hughie feel about Alan’s attitude toward the old model’s worn clothes?
choices: He disapproves of Alan’s lack of sympathy for the old man.
He commends Alan for valuing artistic appeal over the model’s hardship.
He objects to Alan’s view that the worn clothes diminish the old man’s appeal as a model.
He feels indifferent to Alan’s opinion because the model‘s appearance does not concern him.
He finds Alan’s artistic response to the model fully understandable from a painter’s perspective.
solution: Alan은 Hughie가 낡은 옷이라고 부르는 것을 자신은 낭만이라고 부르며 또한 그 옷들이 낭만적이고 매력적이라고 생각한다는 말에, Hughie가 진지하게 “너희 화가들은 냉정해.”라고 그의 반응이 무정하다고 말했으므로, Alan의 태도에 대한 Hughie의 태도로 ❶ ‘그는 그 노인에 대한 Alan의 동정심 부족을 못마땅하게 여긴다.’가 알맞다.

hunt, paint, reveal, decide, spots, in order, while

solution:

One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar ⓐhim was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “ⓑHow an unfortunate-looking man he is! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, ⓒwould you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that,” cried Hughie, ⓓlaughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you ⓔdo.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and ⓕstanding in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

4개

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ him → himself (명사 바로 뒤에서 그 명사를 강조할 때는 인칭대명사의 목적격이 아닌 재귀대명사를 써야 하므로, 주어인 명사구 the beggar 뒤에서 강조하는 역할을 하도록 him을 재귀대명사 himself로 고친다.)
ⓑ How → What (감탄문으로 뒤에 명사구 an unfortunate-looking man이 이어지므로 ‘What+a/an+형용사+명사+주어+동사!’의 감탄문을 이루도록 How를 What으로 고친다. 참고로, How로 시작하는 감탄문은 ‘How+형용사/부사+주어+동사!’의 구조이다.)
ⓕ standing → stand (‘it takes ~ to부정사‘ 구문을 이루는 to부정사 to draw의 to 뒤에서 동사원형 draw, paint와 ’A and B and C‘의 구조로 병렬 연결되므로, standing을 동사원형 stand로 고친다.)

W: A friend invites you to a party, but you don’t want to attend. So you make up an excuse to decline the invitation. Or you receive a gift from your friends that you don’t like, but you pretend that you do so that you don’t disappoint them.
(A) In contrast, John Stuart Mill said that it’s morally okay to lie if lying increases overall happiness. The point is that handling this type of dilemma requires careful consideration.
(B) But isn’t it morally wrong to lie? Immanuel Kant argued that lying is always immoral regardless of the circumstances.
(C) These situations show how people sometimes face ethical dilemmas about whether to tell white lies. People often tell white lies to avoid harming their relationships.
Ultimately, the choice depends on your values and the situation. What would be your choice in such a dilemma?
위 주어진 담화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 친구가 파티에 초대하지만 참석하고 싶지 않아 거절할 핑계를 대거나, 마음에 들지 않는 선물을 받고도 친구들을 실망시키지 않기 위해 좋아하는 척한다는 주어진 글 뒤에 앞선 두 가지 상황들을 These situations(이러한 상황들)로 이어받아, 이것이 선의의 거짓말에 관한 윤리적 딜레마임을 설명하는 (C), 사람들이 관계에 해를 끼치는 것을 피하기 위해 선의의 거짓말을 한다는 마지막 문장에 이어, 거짓말을 하는 것은 도덕적으로 잘못된 것 아니냐는 질문과 함께 거짓말은 어떤 상황에서도 도덕적으로 그르다는 Immanuel Kant의 주장을 소개하는 (B), In contrast(그와 반대로)를 통해 Immanuel Kant의 주장과 반대되는, 거짓말이 전체적인 행복을 증가시킨다면 도덕적으로 허용될 수 있다는 John Stuart Mill의 주장을 소개하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments using multimedia and Internet platforms. (A)반면, 전통적 교육은 일반적으로 교사와 학생이 함께 있는 교실 환경에서의 전통적인 교수-학습 과정을 의미한다.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
teaching-learning process, to, and, present, be, refer, generally, conventional
→ ______ ______, on the other hand, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ in a classroom setting ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ together.
answer: Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are present together.
solution:
• 주어 Traditional education을 쓰고, 연결어 on the other hand 뒤에 ‘일반적으로’를 뜻하는 부사 generally와 generally의 수식을 받는 구동사 refers to(~을 의미하다)와 목적어 the conventional teaching-learning process를 쓴다.
• 명사구 a classroom setting을 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 써야 하며, 이 뒤에는 완전한 절이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 어울리는 전치사 in과 관계대명사 which를 함께 쓴 뒤, 관계사절의 주어 teachers and students를 쓰고, 복수로 수일치한 be동사 are, ‘존재하는’을 뜻하는 형용사 present를 쓴다.

Which one do you think is better? We decided to explore this topic by considering the perspectives of our readers. The following represents two sides of the debate.
[1]
Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. ⓐLiving in an era in which we enjoy technical innovations and boundless connectivity, we should take advantage of ⓑwhat is available in education as well. In the following, I will explore the reasons ⓒwhy online education is a better choice.
First, online education breaks down the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program ⓓprovides free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living far away. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
[2]
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter ⓔwhat advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable that online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks that education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, which traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven more successful in providing an educational environment where students can concentrate and learn better. According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. It seems that it is much easier for students ⓕpay attention and understand the content taught in a traditional classroom because they are learning together.

solution:
어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓓ provides → providing (동사 take의 목적어 Khan Academy와 동격을 이루는 명사구 an online education program을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, an online education program이 무료 강의를 ‘제공하는’ 주체이므로 provides를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 providing으로 고친다.)
ⓕ pay → to pay (명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 that절에서 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리이며, 앞에 to부정사의 의미상 주어를 나타내는 for students가 있으므로 pay를 to부정사 to pay로 고친다.)

famous, virtual reality programs, realistic details, historical sites, by, allow, travel back, use, can

answer: students can learn history more effectively by using virtual reality programs, which can show them realistic details of famous historical sites or allow them to travel back in time.
solution:

• virtual reality programs를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 콤마(,) 뒤에 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 쓰고 ‘보여줄 수 있다’를 뜻하는 can show와 간접목적어 them을 이어 쓴다. 직접목적어 ‘유명한 유적지의 실제 같은 세부 양식’을 쓰기 위해 realistic details와 전치사 of를 쓰고 famous historical sites를 이어 쓴다.

body:
It is certainly not easy to judge which form of education is better. Online education has advantages such as accessibility, personalized instruction, and innovative teaching materials based on advanced technology. Traditional education, on the other hand, provides a more dynamic learning environment, based on the relationships students and teachers build together.
(A) At present, what seems to be the most effective approach to this debate is to take advantage of each method by combining them. (B) For example, teachers in a traditional education environment can introduce personalized online programs using AI technology or make use of VR as part of their classroom activities. (C) With AI capable of delivering tailored instruction, the role of the classroom as a physical learning space is expected to gradually disappear. (D) Combining methods this way can benefit students by making up for what seems to lack in each method. (E) Selecting the best resources and methods for learners will lead us to the most successful and fulfilling educational outcomes.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 온라인 교육과 전통적 교육이 각각 장점을 가지고 있기에 어느 하나가 더 낫다고 판단할 수 없으며, 두 교육 방법을 결합하여 서로의 부족한 점을 보완하는 것이 효과적인 접근법임을 설명하는 글이지만, (C) ‘AI가 맞춤형 수업을 제공할 수 있기 때문에, 물리적인 학습 공간으로서 교실의 역할은 점차 사라질 것으로 예상된다.’는 AI의 발전으로 전통적 교육인 물리적인 교실의 역할이 점차 사라질 것이라는 내용으로 두 교육 방법의 결합이라는 전체 글의 흐름과 반대되기에 흐름상 관계없는 문장은 (C)이다.

body:
by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments using multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are present together.
다음 글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Margie learns alone at home with the help of a computer-like teacher. (T/F)
(B) After discovering an old book, Margie becomes interested in attending a school where students spend time together. (T/F)
(C) Margie wishes she could attend a real school, studying different subjects individually in the same classroom. (T/F)
(D) Online education uses digital tools and the Internet to teach students. (T/F)
(E) Traditional education generally involves teachers and students being together in a classroom as part of the teaching and learning process. (T/F)
choices: T-T-T-T-T
T-F-T-T-F
F-T-T-F-T
T-T-F-F-T
T-T-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-T-F-T-T이다.
(A) Margie는 컴퓨터와 같은 교사의 도움을 받아 집에서 혼자 학습한다. (일치)
(B) 오래된 책을 발견한 후, Margie는 학생들이 함께 시간을 보내는 학교에 다니는 것에 관심을 갖게 된다. (일치)
(C) Margie는 학생들이 같은 교실에서 서로 다른 과목을 개별적으로(→모두 같은 과목을 함께) 공부하는 실제 학교에 다닐 수 있기를 바란다. (불일치)
(D) 온라인 교육은 학생들을 가르치기 위해 디지털 도구와 인터넷을 사용한다. (일치)
(E) 전통적 교육은 일반적으로 교수와 학습 과정의 일부로 교사와 학생들이 교실에서 함께 있는 것을 포함한다. (일치)

G: (A)Are you aware that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
B: No, what is it?
G: It’s the kangaroo rat, and it lives in the desert in North America.
B: Really? How does it manage to survive without water?
G: Apparently, it obtains all the moisture it needs from the seeds it eats.
B: That’s fascinating! Do you know why it is called the kangaroo rat?
G: Yes, that’s because it has really long legs that help it jump really high like a kangaroo.

G: It can jump up to about 2.75 m in a single leap!

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 흐름상 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Are you sure there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Is it true that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Have you heard that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Do you know that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Did you realize that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
solution:
밑줄 친 (A) ‘물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 것을 알고 있니?’는 ‘Are you aware that ~?(~라는 것을 알고 있니?)’을 사용해 상대방이 어떤 정보나 사실에 대해 알고 있는지 묻고 있는 것이므로, 확실성 여부를 묻는 ‘Are you sure (that) ~?(~라는 것이 확실하니?)’을 사용한 ① ‘물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 것이 확실하니?’와 진위 여부를 묻는 ‘Is it true (that) ~(~라는 것이 사실이니?)’을 사용한 ② ’물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 것이 사실이니?‘와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.
오답

body:
(A)많은 식물들은 동물들에게 먹이를 제공함으로써 자신들의 씨앗을 흩뿌리는 것을 선택하지만, 그들 모두가 그런 것은 아닙니다. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading ⓐthem without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. ⓑIts blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, ⓒthey become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals.
As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to ⓓtheir fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like the devil is scratching them with ⓔits horrifying claws. That is how devil’s claw became known as (B)the worst free rider.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• (1)에는 ‘by+동명사’를 사용할 것
• (2)에는 부분 부정 표현과 대동사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• (1)은 10단어, (2)는 5단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
all, opt, seeds, food, scatter, provide, to animals
Many plants (1)______, but (2)______.
answer:
(1) opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals
(2) not all of them do
solution:
(1) • ‘~하는 것을 선택하다’라는 뜻의 ‘opt+to부정사’를 사용해 동사 opt를 쓴 뒤, scatter를 to부정사인 to scatter로 변형하고 목적어로 명사구 their seeds를 쓴다.
• <조건>에 따라 ‘by+동명사’를 사용해 by 뒤에 provide를 동명사 providing으로 변형한다. 이어서 ‘provide ~ to …(~을 …에게 제공하다)’의 구조를 사용해 providing의 목적어인 명사 food와 전치사구 to animals를 쓴다.
(2) • <조건>에 따라 부분 부정 표현을 사용해 ‘모두가 ~한 것은 아닌’이라는 뜻의 not all을 쓴다. all 뒤에 인칭대명사가 쓰일 때는 전치사 of를 사용해 연결하므로 all 뒤에 전치사 of와 대명사 them을 쓴다.
• <조건>에 따라 대동사를 사용하되, 흐름상 일반동사를 포함한 동사구 opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals를 대신해야 하므로, 대동사 do를 쓴다.

body:
Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world’s tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning “the highest one.” However, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park ______. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making it nearly impossible to identify from the ground. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: are fairly high
are slim to none
are difficult to predict
are worth taking seriously
are greater than those of other redwoods
solution:
공원은 방문객들로 인한 잠재적 피해로부터 나무를 보호하기 위해 나무의 정확한 위치를 비밀로 유지한다고 했으며, Hyperion과 인접한 redwood 간의 높이 차이가 단지 몇 미터에 불과해 지상에서 식별하는 것이 거의 불가능하다고 설명하므로, 공원에서 실제로 Hyperion을 보게 될 가능성이 매우 낮다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘거의 희박한’이 알맞다.

③ 예측하기 어려운
④ 진지하게 생각해볼 가치가 있다
⑤ 다른 redwood를 볼 가능성보다 훨씬 크다

body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants ______. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: release their seeds only after the fruits have fully developed
only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience
require the help of animals such as birds to release their seeds effectively
continuously release their seeds throughout the year regardless of the weather conditions
release their seeds gradually over an extended period of time to maximize their chances of survival
solution:
사례로 든 eucalyptus의 경우, 씨앗이 강한 껍질로 보호되어 있어 새들이 먹을 수 없으나 덥고 건조한 날씨에 잎에 불이 붙으면 강한 열로 인해 단단한 껍질이 갈라지고, 그때 씨앗이 껍질에서 나와 땅에 떨어지고 자라기 시작하며, 타고 남은 재가 그것들을 가혹한 환경에서 보호하는 한편 다른 경쟁 식물들을 태운다고 설명했으므로, 성숙한 씨앗이 자동으로 모체 식물에서 분리되는 대부분의 식물과 달리 eucalyptus와 같은 일부 식물은 극한의 환경 조건을 거쳐야만 씨앗을 방출한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘극심한 경험을 견딘 후에야 씨앗을 방출합니다’가 알맞다.

③ 씨앗을 효과적으로 방출하기 위해 새와 같은 동물의 도움을 필요로 합니다

body:
Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and ⓐbury it in the ground to eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are ⓑquite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓒwere antelope dung. That is why dung beetles ⓓoften spot rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the ⓔconfusing beetles will realize ⓕthey cannot. They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓓ often spot → are often spotted (why가 이끄는 절의 주어 dung beetles가 ‘발견되는’ 대상이며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’spot+목적어+목적격보어(현재분사)(~가 …하는 것을 발견하다)‘의 목적격보어에 해당하는 현재분사구(rolling ~ balls)가 이어져 있으므로, 수동태 ’be spotted+현재분사(…하는 것이 발견되다)‘를 이루도록 often spotted를 are often spotted로 고친다.)
ⓔ confusing → confused (정관사 the와 명사 beetles 사이에 뒤의 명사를 수식하는 형용사가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 수식받는 명사가 ’혼란스럽게 하는‘ 주체가 아니라 ’혼란스럽게 된‘ 대상이므로, 능동의 의미를 가진 현재분사 형태의 형용사 confusing을 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 형태의 형용사 confused로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ as if가 이끄는 조건절이 현재 사실의 반대를 가정해야 하므로, ‘as if+주어+were/동사의 과거형 ~(마치 ~인 것처럼)’ 형태의 가정법 과거 표현을 이루는 동사 were는 알맞다.
ⓕ 동사 realize의 목적어이므로 명사절 접속사 that이 생략된 완전한 절의 형태가 되어야 하나, 조동사 뒤에 반복을 피하기 위해 동사구의 나머지 부분을 생략할 수 있으므로, ’they cannot eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them’에서 반복되는 ‘eat ~ them’을 생략한 형태인 they cannot은 알맞다.

solution:

쇠똥구리들이 씨앗을 먹거나 그 안에 알을 낳으려고 할 때 그럴 수 없다는 것을 깨달을 것이라고 했으므로, ⑤ ‘쇠똥구리들은 영양의 배설물에 그렇게 하듯이 silver arrow-reed의 씨앗을 먹거나 그 안에 알을 낳을 수 있다.’ 또한 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 남아프리카의 silver arrow-reed는 씨앗을 퍼뜨리기 위해 쇠똥구리를 이용한다.
② 쇠똥구리는 영양의 배설물을 굴려 그것을 땅에 묻는 습성을 가지고 있다.
③ silver arrow-reed의 씨앗은 영양의 배설물처럼 짙은 갈색이고 둥글다.

body:

choices: a comparison among the root systems of diverse plant species around the world
a description of specific ways plants use their seeds for survival and reproduction
a discussion of how climate change has altered the migration patterns of various plant species
an explanation of how photosynthesis allows plants to convert sunlight into energy for growth
an overview of how animals help plants by pollinating flowers and spreading pollen across ecosystems

body:
Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks.
Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. (A) Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. (B) Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. (C) Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. (D) Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. (E) As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘분홍색 트럼펫을 닮은 이 식물의 꽃은 결국 많은 갈고리가 있는 열매로 변합니다.’라는 뜻으로, Its가 가리키는 devil’s claw를 날카로운 갈고리나 바늘을 갖춘 식물의 예시로 소개하며 그것의 서식지를 설명한 다음이자, 주어진 문장에 언급된 fruits를 these fruits로 가리켜, 꽃이 열매로 변한 이후의 과정에 해당하는 내용으로서 이 열매들이 마르는 동안 단단해지고 갈고리들이 동물의 몸에 달라붙을 만큼 단단해진다고 설명하는 문장 앞인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for (A)[distributing / storing] their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts (B)[untouched / decomposed]. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a (C)[satisfying / dissatisfying] meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: distributing untouched satisfying
distributing untouched dissatisfying
distributing decomposed satisfying
storing untouched dissatisfying
storing decomposed satisfying
solution:
(A) 달콤한 향기로 동물들을 유혹해 과육과 함께 씨앗을 먹게 하고, 씨앗들이 배변을 통해 내보내져 발아하고 자라며 퍼진다고 설명하므로, 식물들이 씨앗을 퍼뜨리는 대가로 동물들에게 맛있는 먹이를 제공한다는 흐름이 되는 distributing(~을 퍼뜨리는)이 알맞다.
storing ~을 보관[저장]하는
(B) 씨앗들이 배변을 통해 내보내져 발아하고 자라기 시작한다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 씨앗이 소화되지 않고 훼손되지 않은 원래의 상태 그대로 동물들의 소화관을 통과한다는 흐름이 되는 untouched(훼손되지 않은, 원래 그대로의)가 알맞다.
decomposed 분해된
(C) jackfruit의 달콤한 향기에 이끌려 동물들이 그것의 맛있는 과육을 먹고, 함께 섭취한 씨앗이 배변으로 내보내져 발아하고 자란다고 설명하므로, 만족스러운 식사의 대가로 동물들이 씨앗을 퍼뜨린다는 흐름이 되는 satisfying(만족스러운)이 알맞다.
dissatisfying 만족을 주지 못하는

body:
Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and ⓐflies farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air ⓑusing their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed ⓒelevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel ⓓmuch farther from the parent tree. The rotation also ⓔslows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps ⓕreducing the damage to the seed during the fall.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓐ 주어 This rotation이 아니라 makes의 목적어인 the seed(씨앗)가 ‘날아가는’ 주체이므로, ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)(~가 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구문에서 첫 번째 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 동사원형 stay와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어야 한다. 따라서 flies를 동사원형 fly로 고친다.
ⓒ 동사 allows와 목적어 the maple seed에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식 구문에 쓰일 때 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로, elevate를 to부정사인 to elevate로 고친다.
ⓕ ‘~하는 것을 돕다, ~하는 데 도움이 되다’라는 뜻으로 ‘help+동사원형/to부정사’를 쓰므로, helps 뒤의 reducing을 동사원형 reduce 또는 to부정사인 to reduce로 고친다.
*원래 지문에는 reduce가 쓰였음
오답
ⓑ 앞의 동사구 get lifted and stay in the air에 접속사 없이 연결되므로 흐름상 동시동작(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사가 쓰일 수 있으며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 helicopters가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 their propellers가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 using은 알맞다.
ⓓ 훨씬’이라는 의미의 비교급 강조 부사로 much, still, even 등이 쓰일 수 있으므로, 비교급 farther을 강조하기 위해 앞에 온 much는 알맞다.
ⓔ ‘~의 속도를 늦추다’라는 뜻으로 ‘타동사+부사’ 구조의 구동사 ‘slow ~ down’을 쓸 수 있으며, 이때 목적어는 동사와 부사 사이 또는 부사 뒤에 올 수 있고, 목적어인 명사구 the speed of the fall이 뒤에 이어져 있으므로, 단수명사구인 주어 The rotation에 수일치한 slows 뒤에 부사 down이 바로 이어진 slows down은 알맞다.

body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell (A)[cracking / to crack] open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. ⓐ떨어진 씨앗들은 편리하게도 화재 후 남은 부드러운 재 속에 감춰지는데, 이것은 그것들을 가혹한 환경으로부터 보호합니다. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also (B)[burns / burning] practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided (C)[that / what] there is fire.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: cracking burning that
to crack burning what
to crack burns that
cracking burns that
to crack burns what
solution:
(A) 동사 causes와 목적어 the shell에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, ‘cause+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 유발하다)’의 5형식 구문에 쓰일 때 cause는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로, to부정사인 to crack이 알맞다.
(B) 주어 Wildfire와 두 개의 콤마(,) 사이에 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 과거분사구(often started ~ tree)에 이어져 있으며, 뒤에 다른 동사구 없이 destroying 이하의 분사구문이 이어지므로, 주어에 대한 동사가 올 자리이다. 따라서 단수인 주어에 수일치한 단수동사 burns가 알맞다.
(C) ‘만약 ~한다면, ~라는 것을 조건으로’라는 뜻의 ‘provided (that)+완전한 절’ 형태의 부사절을 이루어야 하므로 that이 알맞다.

body:

Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell (A)[cracking / to crack] open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. ⓐ떨어진 씨앗들은 편리하게도 화재 후 남은 부드러운 재 속에 감춰지는데, 이것은 그것들을 가혹한 환경으로부터 보호합니다. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also (B)[burns / burning] practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided (C)[that / what] there is fire.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 분사구와 적절한 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>에 주어진 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• (1)과 (2) 각각 7단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
leave, protect, conceal, over, the harsh environment, in the soft ash
The fallen seeds are conveniently (1)______ after the fire, (2)______.
answer:
(1) concealed in the soft ash left over
(2) which protects them from the harsh environment
solution:
(1) • 주어 The fallen seeds가 ‘감춰지는’ 대상이므로, are와 함께 수동태(be동사+p.p.)를 이루도록 conceal을 과거분사 concealed로 변형한다.
• 부사구 in the soft ash를 쓴 뒤, <조건>에 따라 명사구 the soft ash를 수식하는 분사구를 쓰되, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘남겨진’ 대상이므로, 수동 표현인 be left over(남겨지다)를 사용해 leave를 과거분사 left로 변형하고 뒤에 부사 over를 쓴다.
(2) • <조건>에 따라 적절한 관계대명사를 사용하되, 콤마(,) 뒤에 선행사인 앞 절을 부연 설명하는 관계사절이 이어져야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which를 사용한다.
• 주격 관계대명사 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어져야 하며, 선행사인 앞 절이 ‘보호하는’ 주체이고 절 전체가 선행사일 때는 단수 취급하므로, protect를 능동태이자 단수동사로 수일치한 protects로 변형한다.
• ‘~을 …로부터 보호하다’라는 뜻의 ‘protect ~ from …’을 사용해, protects의 목적어로 대명사 them을 쓰고, from과 명사구 the harsh environment를 연결한다.

body:
As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly ⓐattached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The ⓑattached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them ⓒto feel like the devil is scratching ⓓthem with its horrifying claws. That is ⓔhow devil’s claw became known as the worst free rider.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ to feel → feel (현재분사 형태로 쓰인 making과 목적어 them에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, make가 사역동사로 쓰여 ‘~가 …하게 만들다’를 뜻하는 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문을 이룰 때, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동인 경우 목적격보어로 동사원형이 쓰이고, 목적어 them이 가리키는 the animals가 ‘느끼는’ 주체이므로, to feel을 능동 관계를 나타내는 동사원형 feel로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘~가 계속 …하게 하다’라는 뜻의 5형식 구문인 ‘keep+목적어+목적격보어‘에서 목적격보어 자리에 분사(구)가 올 수 있으며, 목적어인 the dried fruit이 attach(~을 붙이다)의 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’attach ~ to …(~을 …에 붙이다)‘의 전치사 to가 바로 이어졌으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 attached는 알맞다. 참고로, 부사 firmly가 앞에서 수식하고 있다.

body:
Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts untouched. body:
Grandma Moses
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, ⓐfills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats ⓑgrazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known ⓒfigure in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while ⓓraising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, ⓔbring about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. (A) She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. (B) Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. (C) Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. (D) The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. (E) The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.

Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그는 그녀 작품의 아름다움을 깨닫고 그녀의 그림 전시회들을 열었는데, 이는 모두 대중에게 큰 인기를 끌었고, 그 후의 일은 다들 아는 대로이다.’라는 뜻으로, 이 문장에서 he(그)가 쓰였으며, he(그)가 그녀의 작품의 아름다움을 깨달았다고 했으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 he를 가리키는 남자가 그녀의 작품을 보거나 발견했다는 내용이 와야 하며, 뒤에는 그녀의 전시회에 대한 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 Louis Calder라는 이름의 미술품 수집가가 약국 창문에 걸린 그녀의 그림들을 발견했다는 문장 뒤이자, 주어진 문장의 exhibitions of her drawings를 The exhibitions로 이어받아, 그 전시회들이 Grandma Moses의 작품을 대중에게 알렸다는 문장 사이인 (D)에 들어가야 한다.

body:
Lee Jungseop
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work ⓐdealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork (A)[what / that] reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems ⓑlighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children (B)[is / are] a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took ⓒrefuge on Jejudo. Although they were ⓓfleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the ⓔseparation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, (C)[which / that] was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.

<보기>
ⓐ deal with: to do business with someone or have a business connection with someone
ⓑ lighthearted: cheerful and not worried about anything
ⓒ refuge: shelter or protection from someone or something
ⓓ flee: to leave a place quickly because you are in danger or are afraid
ⓔ separation: an occasion when people who have not met each other for a long time meet again

body:
Alfonse Mucha
Finding the light at the end of the long tunnel
(A)Alfonse Mucha(1860-1939)는 최초의 아르 누보 예술가들 중 한 명이었으며, 이것이 이러한 형태의 예술이 ‘Mucha 양식’이라고 불리는 것으로 이어졌다.
His style became famous later on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, did not happen overnight.
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, ⓐwhich he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, ⓑhe produced a life-sized poster, portrayed Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only (B)______, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

body:
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an (A)[ordinary / unusual] day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder (B)[overlooked / noticed] her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to (C)[accomplish / give up] our dreams.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: unusual / overlooked / accomplish
ordinary / noticed / give up
ordinary / noticed / accomplish

ordinary / overlooked / give up

unusual 특이한
(B) 뒤에서 그(=Louis Calder)가 그녀 작품의 아름다움을 깨닫고 그녀의 그림 전시회를 열었다고 했으므로, 약국 창문에 걸린 그녀의 그림을 발견했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 noticed(~을 알아채다, 발견하다)가 적절하다.

Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why did Mucha move to Vienna at the age of 19?
How did Mucha support himself while studying in Vienna?
What opportunity gave Mucha his big break in Paris?
How long did Mucha spend creating the poster for Gismonda?
What does Mucha’s story suggest about the relationship between preparation and opportunity?
solution:
Mucha가 크리스마스이브 늦게 혼자 작업하던 중 의뢰를 받았다는 내용만 언급되었을 뿐, 포스터 제작에 실제로 얼마나 시간이 걸렸는지는 언급되지 않았으므로, ④ ‘Mucha는 Gismonda 포스터를 제작하는 데 얼마나 많은 시간을 들였는가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.
오답
① Mucha는 왜 19세의 나이에 비엔나로 이주했는가? (→예술가가 되겠다는 꿈을 이루기 위해 교육을 계속하고자 비엔나로 이주했다.)
② Mucha는 비엔나에서 공부하는 동안 어떻게 자신을 부양했는가? (→잡지에 삽입 광고와 삽화를 그리며 돈을 벌었다.)
③ 어떤 기회가 파리에서 Mucha에게 큰 성공의 계기를 주었는가? (→연극 ‘Gismonda’의 포스터를 그릴 기회를 얻으면서 큰 성공의 계기를 맞았다.)
⑤ Mucha의 이야기는 준비와 기회의 관계에 대해 무엇을 시사하는가? (→성공은 준비가 기회를 만날 때 이루어질 수 있다는 것을 보여 준다.)

Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the separation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, which was his way of ______.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting is the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability to express this hope through art brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of comfort to people to this day.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: erasing the painful scars of the war
hiding his deep sorrow from the public
escaping from the harsh reality of poverty
remembering the memories he had with his family
forgetting the pain of being separated from his family
solution:

G: Theo, are you reading again?
B: I just couldn’t help it. I want to know what happens next!
G: But you seem to read all the time. Why do you like reading so much?
B: Well, it allows me to imagine things that I can’t experience in real life. For example, the main character in this book goes on a trip to Mars. When would I be able to enjoy something like that?
G: You certainly have a good point about reading! I wish I could read as much as you do. It’s on my New Year’s resolution list every year, but I just cannot find the time for it.
B: Hmm, ______?
G: No, I haven’t.
B: They’re useful for people who don’t have enough time. You can read them on your phone anywhere at your convenience.
G: Oh, I’ve never thought of that. I’ll give it a try.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: have you tried pocket books
have you ever tried reading e-books
have you thought about changing your reading habits
have you considered listening to audiobooks instead
have you ever tried using time-management apps to make more time
solution:
소녀가 ‘No, I haven’t.‘로 대답했으므로 빈칸은 현재완료 의문문이 되어야 하고, 소년이 자신이 빈칸에서 언급한 것의 장점으로 시간이 충분하지 않은 사람들에게 유용하며 편한 시간에 어디에서든 휴대폰으로 그것들을 읽을 수 있다고 덧붙이고 있으므로 빈칸에는 휴대폰으로 읽을 수 있는 책이 언급되는 ② ‘전자책을 읽어 본 적이 있니’가 알맞다.

① 포켓북 읽어 봤니
③ 독서 습관을 바꾸는 것에 대해 생각해 본 적이 있니
④ 대신 오디오북을 듣는 것을 고려해 본 적이 있니

solution:

body:
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How ⓐunfortunately he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, ⓑwould you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that,” cried Hughie, ⓒlaughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you ⓓare.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and ⓔstand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Hughie supposed that the beggar’s miserable appearance might be an advantage to him as a painter’s model.
Alan believed that a beggar serving as a model should appear miserable.
According to Alan, the model’s payment was not fixed.
Alan told Hughie that he would earn a total of two thousand pounds for the painting.
Alan rejected Hughie’s suggestion and stressed the considerable effort involved in producing a painting.
solution:
모델은 시간당 1실링을 받는다고 했으므로, ③ ‘Alan에 따르면, 모델의 보수는 고정된 것이 아니었다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
Alan은 이 그림으로 2천을 받으며, 파운드가 아닌 기니로 받는다고 했으므로, ④ ‘Alan은 Hughie에게 자신은 그 그림의 대가로 총 2천 파운드를 벌게 될 것이라고 말했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① Hughie는 그 거지의 비참한 외모가 화가의 모델로서 그에게 유리한 점이 될 수 있다고 생각했다.
② Alan은 모델 역할을 하는 거지는 비참해 보여야 한다고 생각했다.
⑤ Alan은 Hughie의 제안을 받아들이지 않았고 그림을 제작하는 데 수반되는 상당한 노력을 강조했다.

After a while, the servant came in and told Alan that the frame-maker wanted to see ⓐhim. Alan said, “I will be back in a moment,” as he went out. The old beggar took advantage of Alan’s absence to rest for a moment on a chair. ⓑHe looked so sad and lonely. Hughie couldn’t help pitying ⓒhim and felt his own pockets to see what money he had. All he could find, however, was a few coins. “Poor old fellow, ⓓhe wants them more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks,” he thought to himself. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar’s hand. ⓔThe old man was surprised and smiled faintly. “Thank you, sir,” he said. body:
That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan ⓐsitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture ⓑto finish?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
(A) When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is ⓒto show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how ⓓis Laura. The old model was quite interested in her.”
(B) “But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “ⓔThat you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
(C) “My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I ⓕcould do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ to finish → finished (got의 목적어 that picture에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, ‘get+목적어+목적격 보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식에서 목적어와 목적격 보어가 수동 관계일 때 목적격 보어로 과거분사를 취하며 목적어 that picture가 ‘마무리된’ 대상이므로 to finish를 과거분사 finished로 고친다. 참고로, 목적어와 목적격 보어가 능동 관계일 경우 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취한다.)
ⓓ is Laura → Laura is (동사 tell의 직접목적어인 간접의문문으로 how 이하는 의문사(how) 뒤 평서문의 어순이 되어야 하므로, is Laura를 ’주어+동사‘의 어순인 Laura is로 고친다.)
ⓔ That → What (’call+목적어+목적격 보어’의 5형식을 이루는 두 번째 동사 call과 목적격 보어인 romance 사이에서 강조를 위해 문장 앞으로 이동하여 목적어를 이루어야 하므로, 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you call worn clothes)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루도록 That을 ‘~한 것’의 의미로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 What으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ find는 ‘find+목적어+목적격 보어(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다)’의 5형식에 쓰일 때 목적어와 목적격 보어 사이가 능동 관계일 경우 목적격 보어로 현재분사를 취하며, 목적어 Alan이 앉아 있는 주체이며 sit은 자동사이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 sitting은 알맞다.
ⓒ be동사 is의 보어 자리로, ‘보여주는 것’이라는 뜻의 명사적 용법의 to부정사 to show는 알맞다.

“You don’t mean to say you talked to him about her?” said Hughie.
“Sure I did. He knows all about the Colonel, Laura, and the 10,000 pounds,” replied Alan.
“You told that old beggar all my (A)[public / private] affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and angry.
“My dear boy,” said Alan, smiling, “that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the (B)[poorest / richest] men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and asked me a month ago to paint him as a beggar.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie, feeling embarrassed. “Good heavens! I gave him some coins,” he said, sinking into an armchair.
“What? You gave him coins?” cried Alan, bursting into (C)[cheers / laughter]. He went on, “Well, it never occurred to me that you would distribute money in that way. Besides, when you came in, I didn’t know if Hausberg would like his name mentioned. You know he wasn’t in full dress.”

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: continued to bring rare enough
continuing to bring rare enough
continued to bring enough rare
continuing bring enough rare
continued bring rare enough
solution:
ⓐ 앞의 과거시제 동사 said와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되는 동사 자리이므로, 과거시제 동사 continued가 알맞다.
ⓑ asked와 목적어 me에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, 5형식 ask가 ‘~에게 …할 것을 요청하다’를 뜻하는 ‘ask+목적어+목적격 보어’의 5형식 구문에 쓰일 때 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, to부정사 to bring이 알맞다.
ⓒ enough가 부사로 쓰여 형용사나 부사를 수식할 때 형용사/부사의 뒤에서 수식하므로, 형용사 rare 뒤에 enough가 위치한 어순의 rare enough가 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 전치사 on으로 시작하는 부사구로 시작할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
to, from, write, wedding present, old beggar, the outside
______ ______ ______ ______ ______, “A ______ ______ ______ Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, ______ ______ ______ ______,“
answer: On the outside was written, wedding present to, from an old beggar
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 전치사 on으로 시작하는 부사구 On the outside로 시작하되, 장소 등을 나타내는 부사(구)가 강조를 위해 문두에 오면 절의 주어와 동사가 도치되며, be동사가 있는 경우 ‘be동사+주어 ~‘의 어순이 되어야 한다. 주어인 따옴표(“”) 안의 문구는 ‘쓰여진’ 대상이고 따옴표는 하나의 문구로 취급되어 단수 취급되며 흐름상 과거의 상황을 묘사하므로, 주어진 동사 write를 단수로 수일치한 과거시제 수동태 was written으로 변형한다.
• 관사 A 다음에 wedding present를 쓰고 이어서 ‘~에게’를 뜻하는 전치사 to를 쓰고, 마지막에 ‘~로부터’를 뜻하는 전치사 from과 목적어 an old beggar를 쓴다.

That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”

윗글의 두 번째 문단에서 네 번째 문단까지의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Hughie’s genuine concern for the old model’s worn clothes
the importance of proper clothing in creating a successful painting
the contrast between Hughie’s compassion and Alan’s artistic perspective
a disagreement over whether poor people should serve as models for artists
Alan’s effort to persuade Hughie to appreciate the artistic value of poverty
solution:
늙은 모델의 낡은 옷을 생각하며 자신의 옷을 주겠다며 연민을 느끼는 Hughie와 그 낡은 옷은 그림의 소재로서 낭만적이고 매력적이라고 생각하며 화가는 세상을 보는 그대로 세상을 보여 주는 거라는 견해를 가진 Alan의 상반된 시각을 보여주므로, 글의 주제로 ③ ‘Hughie의 동정심과 Alan의 예술적 관점 사이의 대조’가 알맞다.
오답

② 성공적인 그림을 만드는 데 있어 적절한 의상의 중요성
