Most people use their cell phone everywhere. But research shows that cell phones are far dirtier than most people think, and the more germs they collect, the more germs you touch. In fact, our hands are to blame. Americans check their phones about 47 times a day, and this spreads germs from hands to the phone. A recent study found more than 17,000 bacterial gene copies on the phones of high school students. Scientists at the University of Arizona have found that cell phones carry 10 times more bacteria than most toilet seats. While most germs on phones aren't harmful, some can be. One of the worst places to use your phone is in the bathroom. When toilets flush, they spread bad germs everywhere. Keeping your phone out of the bathroom will help. You can wipe it with a soft towel, which will remove many of the germs. For a deeper clean, use a mix of 60% water and 40% alcohol. Still, the best advice has more to do with you than the phone. Wash your hands several times a day, and you'll likely be fine.

As the new school year begins, many students are turning to energy drinks to stay awake and alert. Studies show that as many as 70% of European adolescents and 30% of U.S. adolescents regularly consume these drinks. Colorful packaging, sweet flavors, and marketing, often tied to popular figures like SNS influencers, contribute to this trend. However, these energy drinks can be harmful to adolescents' health, as they contain high levels of caffeine and added sugars, which can lead to side effects like increases in heart rate and blood pressure. Adolescents can even become dependent on these drinks. Experts recommend that adolescents aged 12-18 consume less than 100mg of caffeine per day, while energy drinks can have 100-200mg per serving. To ensure a healthier choice, teens ______ when purchasing drinks with caffeine. Natural sources of caffeine like plain tea without added sugars are better options.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: should choose drinks with sweet flavors
should follow the popular SNS influencers
should ignore the advice from many experts
should exercise regularly and get enough sleep
should check caffeine levels and avoid added sugars

body:
It appears that viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated to have killed 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, affecting almost every aspect of human life worldwide.
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter human bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in ______, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: more frequent contact between humans and wild animals
a decrease in the number of wild animals living near humans
stronger natural barriers separating humans from wild animal habitats
an increase in the spread of viruses among different animal species
fewer opportunities for viruses to enter human bodies without immunity
solution: 정답은 ① 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. (A) About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. (B) If viruses did not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. (C) Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. (D) Because plankton serve as food for many organisms, from small marine creatures to fish and whales, a decline in plankton can lead to a decrease in marine animal populations. (E) In short, without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans to survive.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 지구에 산소를 공급하는 바이러스의 역할과 관련해, 바이러스가 박테리아를 감염시켜 죽이지 않는다면 죽은 박테리아에서 나온 영양소를 주 먹이로 하는 플랑크톤이 부족해지고, 지구 산소의 약 절반을 생산하는 플랑크톤이 부족하면 산소가 부족해져 인류의 생존이 불가능할 것이라고 설명하는 흐름이므로, 플랑크톤의 감소가 해양 생물 개체 수에 미치는 영향에 대한 내용인 (D) ‘플랑크톤은 작은 해양 생물부터 물고기와 고래에 이르기까지 많은 생물의 먹이가 되므로, 플랑크톤 감소는 해양 생물의 개체 수 감소로 이어질 수 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 무관하다.

body:
(A)[That / What] is less commonly known is that viruses play crucial roles in supporting much of life on Earth. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses that ⓐsustain us and the planet, instead of just those (B)[who / which] harm us. Therefore, scientists have much more to learn about viruses than they currently know. What they do know is (C)[that / which] viruses act as the primary ⓑfacilitators of bacterial and insect populations.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, they ⓒaid the reproductive functions of other organisms to multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses go on to ⓓinfect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses ⓔcontrol the excessive growth of certain bacteria.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: What which that
That who which
What which which
What who that
That who that
solution:
(A) 불완전한 절 ‘is less commonly known’을 이끌어 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 What이 알맞다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절 ‘harm us’를 이끌어 those를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 주격 관계대명사 자리이며, 선행사 those가 the viruses를 가리키므로, 사물 선행사와 쓰이는 which가 알맞다.
(C) is의 보어 자리에서 완전한 절 ‘viruses act ~ insect populations’를 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.

body:
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution is their role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ that helps the fetus grow securely inside its mother’s body. It facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while protecting the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, making them vulnerable to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to carry their young inside their bodies safely from one location to another. Viruses that infected our remote ancestors more than 130 million years ago have been reported to have served a key function in the development of this vital organ.
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Placenta as a Defense Against Viral Infections
Viruses as a Major Threat to Mammalian Reproduction
The Evolutionary Benefits of Carrying Young Inside the Body
Ancient Viruses and the Spread of Diseases Among Mammals
How Viruses Helped Mammals Evolve a Safer Way to Carry Their Young

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is ⓐthat they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients ⓑreleasing from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses ⓒdid not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans ⓓsurvive.
Insect species populations ⓔare also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses ⓕthat infect those insects also increase, reducing their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects ⓖto flourish. (A)자연의 먹이사슬을 고려할 때, 바이러스가 다른 종을 조절하는 중요한 기능을 수행한다고 가정하는 것은 어렵지 않을 것이다. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓑ releasing → released (is의 보어인 명사 nutrients를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 수 있으나, 수식받는 명사가 타동사 release(~을 방출하다)의 주체가 아니라 대상이고, 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 releasing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 released로 고친다.)
ⓓ survive → to survive (make 뒤에 가목적어 it과 목적격보어인 형용사 impossible이 쓰였으며, to부정사의 의미상 주어로 쓰이는 ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 for humans가 이어졌으므로, ‘make+가목적어(it)+목적격보어+진목적어(for+목적격+to부정사)(-가 ~하는 것을 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구조를 이루는 to부정사를 써야 한다. 따라서 동사 survive를 to부정사인 to survive로 고친다.)

body:
As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing them in the battle against diseases are arising. Of notable interest ⓐare the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment. Genes can be compared to instruction guides that govern how our bodies function. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, which can lead to health problems. Gene therapy steps in ⓑto fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering corrected genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, ⓒenables them to function properly. In this process, specially modified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, it can potentially help the body fight off certain diseases.
ⓓUsing viruses to treat cancer, another use of viruses, is based on the notion of utilizing their natural ability to infect and kill cells. If successful, viruses can be manipulated to specifically target and ⓔdestroying cancer cells while leaving healthy cells unharmed. The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment is still in the early stages. However, many researchers are involved in hundreds of projects with the goal of discovering cures for diseases that ⓕonce thought to be incurable.
We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. (A)하지만 바이러스에 대해 더 많이 알수록 특정 바이러스를 유익한 목적으로 사용하고 다음 팬데믹으로 이어질 수 있는 바이러스에 대한 방어책을 개발하는 데 더 잘 대비할 수 있을 것이다. More than that, learning more about viral diversity will help us ⓖreach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓒ enables → enabling (동사(lies)가 있는 완전한 절(The essence of ~ cells)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 뒤에 목적어 them과 목적격보어인 to부정사구가 이어져 ‘enable+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …하는 것을 가능하게 하다)’의 능동태 5형식을 이루므로, enables를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 enabling으로 고친다.)
ⓔ destroying → destroy (to와 부사 specifically에 이어진 동사원형 target과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 목적(~하기 위해서)을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사구를 이루어야 하므로, destroying을 동사원형 destroy로 고친다.)
ⓕ once thought → were once thought (주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절의 동사 자리에 흐름상 과거시제가 쓰인 것과 동사 앞에 ‘한때’라는 의미의 부사로 once가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 선행사 diseases가 과거 ‘여겨졌던’ 대상이고, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’think+목적어+(to be+)보어(~을 …라고 생각하다)‘의 to부정사 to be와 보어 incurable이 이어져 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ’be thought+(to be+)보어(…라고 생각되다)‘를 이루어야 한다. 따라서 복수명사인 선행사에 수일치한 과거형 be동사 were를 사용하고, 부사는 보통 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 위치하므로, once thought를 were once thought로 고친다.)

윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Scientific knowledge about viruses is widely used in the medical field.
Gene therapy removes specific genes from a patient's cells.
Cancer treatment can make use of viruses' natural ability to infect and destroy cells.
Viruses can be manipulated to selectively attack and kill cancer cells.
Thanks to the efforts of many researchers, the characteristics of each virus and the existence of almost all types of viruses have now been identified.

바이러스를 이용한 암 치료는 세포를 감염시키고 죽이는 바이러스의 자연적인 능력을 활용한다는 개념에 기반을 두고 있다고 했으므로, ❸ ‘암 치료는 세포를 감염시키고 파괴하는 바이러스의 자연적인 능력을 활용할 수 있다.’는 일치하는 내용이다.
성공한다면 건강한 세포는 손상시키지 않으면서 암세포만 명확히 표적으로 삼아 파괴하도록 바이러스가 조작될 수 있다고 했으므로, ❹ ‘바이러스는 선택적으로 암세포를 공격해 죽이도록 조작될 수 있다.’ 또한 일치하는 내용이다.

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses did not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, without viruses, ______.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: bacteria would continue to provide nutrients for ocean plankton
the amount of carbon in the atmosphere would greatly increase
the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans to survive
humans would have difficulty finding enough food in the oceans
ocean plankton would be able to produce more oxygen for marine animals
solution: 바이러스가 박테리아를 감염시켜 죽이지 않는다면 박테리아의 사체도 없을 것이고 그 결과 죽은 박테리아에서 방출된 영양소를 주 먹이로 삼는 플랑크톤이 부족해지며, 플랑크톤이 없다면 지구 산소의 절반이 사라진다고 했으므로, 바이러스가 없다면 지구의 산소가 부족해져 인류 생존이 위협을 받게 될 것이라고 요약하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❸ ‘산소의 부족이 인류가 생존하는 것을 불가능하게 할 것이다’가 알맞다.

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. (A) They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick. (B)
But they were wrong. (C) The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. (D) The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague. (E)
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘흑사병은 동물에서 사람으로 퍼질 수 있는 박테리아에 의해 발생했다.’라는 뜻으로, 흑사병의 실제 원인을 설명하고 있으므로, 흑사병의 원인에 대한 당시 의사들의 믿음과 그들이 사용한 방법을 기술하고 나서 그들이 틀렸음을 밝힌 뒤이자, also(또한)을 사용해 박테리아가 벼룩에 물리거나 아픈 사람과의 접촉을 통해서도 퍼질 수 있었다는 또 다른 확산의 원인을 추가 설명하는 문장 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
G: Dad, we don’t have any shampoo at home. Let’s buy this brand. I saw it advertised on TV.
M: I think it’s better for the environment to buy one with this logo on it!
G: What do you mean by that? What does this logo have to do with the environment?
M: It indicates that the product is guaranteed not to contain microplastics.
G: Oh, I read an article about the negative impact of microplastics on the environment. They are especially harmful to marine habitats because they eventually end up in places like rivers, lakes, and oceans.
M: That’s why we should consider purchasing products with this logo. It can encourage more companies to think about how they develop their products.
G: I never thought about it that way. From now on, I will be more conscious about what I buy.
M: Great! Why don’t you check out other products with this logo?

다음 대화의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the significance of brand value in shaping consumer behavior
the importance of choosing products labeled as free of microplastics
the environmental consequences of plastic waste in aquatic ecosystems
the growing importance of environmentally conscious product development
recent methods companies are taking to promote environmentally responsible products
solution: 샴푸를 사야 한다는 딸의 말에 아빠는 환경을 위해 미세 플라스틱이 들어있지 않다는 것을 보증하는 로고가 있는 제품을 사자고 제안하며 그것이 더 많은 기업들이 제품 개발 방식에 관해 고민하도록 장려할 수 있다고 설명하고, 딸은 미세 플라스틱의 환경적 영향에 관련된 기사를 읽었다고 말하며 이제부터 물건을 살 때 더욱 신중해야겠다고 답하고 있으므로, 대화의 주제로 ❷ ‘미세 플라스틱이 없는 것으로 표시된 제품을 선택하는 것의 중요성’이 알맞다.

body:

body:
What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials ⓐcontaining in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year ⓑis increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year ⓒwhen data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually ⓓwill have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, ⓔmost of them are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
*metric ton 메트릭톤(1,000kg을 1톤으로 하는 중량 단위)

윗글의 바로 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the alarming growth of e-waste production around the world
researches addressing the environmental impact of electronic waste
practical difficulties of reducing e-waste through consumer awareness
various policies designed to regulate the disposal of electronic devices
repair policies and initiatives in different countries and regions to reduce e-waste

body:
On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously ⓐ[damaged / damaging] it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it ⓑ[to repair / repaired], but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. (A)______, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, (B)______, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz ⓒ[will throw / throws] her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: damaged / to repair / will throw
damaging / repaired / will throw
damaged / repaired / throws
damaging / repaired / throws
damaging / to repair / throws
solution:
ⓐ 동사(dropped)가 있는 완전한 절(Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 ’손상시키는‘ 원인이자 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어로 대명사 it이 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 damaging이 알맞다.
ⓑ have의 목적어인 대명사 it이 가리키는 her laptop이 ’수리되는‘ 대상이며, ‘have+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문에서 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동의 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 과거분사를 사용하므로, 과거분사 repaired가 알맞다. 참고로, 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동이면 목적격보어로 동사원형을 쓰고, 목적어의 행위에 진행이나 지속의 의미가 더해질 경우 현재분사를 쓴다.
ⓒ If가 이끄는 조건 부사절의 동사 자리이며, 시간·조건의 부사절에서는 미래의 일을 현재시제로 나타내므로, 주어 Liz에 수일치한 현재시제 단수동사 throws가 알맞다.

solution:

(B) 오래된 노트북을 버리고 새것을 사는 것이 더 합리적인 선택처럼 보일 수 있다는 내용 뒤에 실제로는 그것이 최선이 아닐 수 있다는 대조적 내용이 이어지므로, ‘하지만’이라는 역접의 뜻을 나타내는 though 또는 however가 알맞다.

body:
One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is ⓐwhich they are too difficult to repair. (A)예를 들어, 어떤 장치는 분해하기 어려울 수 있고, 또는 그것의 제조사가 그것이 고쳐지도록 공식 수리소로 가져와질 것을 요구할 수도 있다. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers ⓑare unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs.
The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or ⓒbringing it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as ⓓeasily as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries ⓔjoined the cause.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 두 번 사용할 것
• 명사절 접속사 that을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (중복 사용 가능하며, 필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
to an official service center, disassemble, be, bring, it, require, fix, difficult
→ For example, a device may ______ ______ ______ ______, or its manufacturer may ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed.

body:
In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.
The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to ______. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

choices: alter the standards of the repairability index
label its products according to the repairability index
take into account consumers’ trust in the repairability index
consider various repairability indexes when pricing products
assess consumers’ purchasing patterns and loyalty to products
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
*metric ton 메트릭톤(1,000kg을 1톤으로 하는 중량 단위)

We live surrounded by cloth. We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. Wearing clothes is a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. Textiles ─artificial and natural ─have shaped and changed the world ⓐwhere we live in. The history of textiles is almost as old as human civilization, and as time has passed, it has been more and more enriched. ⓑExploring how textiles have changed the world helps us understand how human civilization has evolved.
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found ⓒthat the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. ⓓBeing intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric ⓔthat was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.

We live surrounded by cloth. We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. Wearing clothes is a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. Textiles ─artificial and natural ─have shaped and changed the world ⓐwhere we live in. The history of textiles is almost as old as human civilization, and as time has passed, it has been more and more enriched. ⓑExploring how textiles have changed the world helps us understand how human civilization has evolved.
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found ⓒthat the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. ⓓBeing intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric ⓔthat was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.

body:
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk were eased, and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, prompting the development of the civilizations.

the discovery of silk in Egypt as evidence of China’s early silk production

What to Wear for Space Travel
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest ⓐchallenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits ⓑwasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses ⓒusing their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard ⓓwas the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit ⓔwas worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to ⓕhave used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

Technology Doping
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. (A) At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. (B) The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. (C) In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. (D) In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit. (E)
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. ⓐ그들은 또한 수영복을 만들기 위해 쓰이는 직물은 통기성이 있어야 한다고 규정했다.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그것은 상어의 피부를 모방한 소재로 디자인된 전신 수영복이었다.’라는 뜻으로, 대명사 It을 사용하여 앞에서 언급된 수영복이 구체적으로 어떤 종류의 수영복인지 설명하고 있다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 수영복의 존재나 종류만 언급되고, 그 수영복의 소재나 구체적인 특징은 아직 제시되지 않은 문장이 오는 것이 적절하다. (B) 앞에서 2008년 베이징 올림픽에서 새로운 유형의 수영복(a new type of swimsuit)이 많은 수영선수들에 의해 착용되었다는 사실만 언급되었을 뿐, 그 수영복이 구체적으로 어떤 수영복인지는 설명되지 않았다. 따라서 (B)에 주어진 문장이 오면 a new type of swimsuit를 대명사 It으로 이어받아, 그것이 전신 수영복(a full ~ shark skin)임을 구체적으로 설명하며, (B) 뒤의 The suit는 바로 앞에서 설명한 수영복을 다시 가리켜 그 수영복의 효과와 특징(산소 공급 향상, 물의 저항 감소, 부력 증가)에 대한 설명으로 자연스럽게 이어지므로 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (B)이다.

body:
Various styles and types of textiles can be used in art. In textile art, blue jeans, not water paints, can be used to draw pictures. Beautiful threads replace photos of scenic views. These types of textiles can be brilliant tools for expanding artistic creativity.
Ian Berry, Denim Art
Have you ever imagined painting with clothes, not on clothes? Surprisingly, Ian Berry succeeded in this and makes art out of blue jeans. His art looks like a painting, but people suddenly notice the beauty in blue jeans when they look at his art. He collects denim of every shade and uses it to create the shading and the sense of perspective in his portraits, landscapes, and other unique works of art. With just his hands, scissors, and glue, he creates almost three-dimensional pieces. He (A)[has been making / has been made] realistic installations of denim for many years. He uses discarded jeans, cuts them up into pieces, and, like a painter, sorts them according to color. At first glance, the work seems flat, but a closer look reveals different layers of denim placed on top of and over each other. They are in fact denim collages. They are almost impossible to distinguish from paintings.
Teresa Lim, Embroidery Art
People usually take pictures of scenic views, but Teresa Lim paints pictures of tourist spots with a needle and thread when she travels the world. She embroiders places (B)[what / that] she visits in surprising detail. This method of preserving memories lets her truly take in her surroundings. She spends time sitting in one place, observing details and stitching as the scene reveals itself. She says on her website that her designs “seek to erase the lines and boundaries between being an illustrator and a textile designer.” Her art is a delightful fusion of a canvas and a camera that (C)[project / projects] travel scenes onto fabric. She recreates what she sees on cloth and eliminates the need for a vacation photo album.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: has been made / that / project
has been making / that / projects
has been making / what / project
has been made / what / projects
has been making / that / project
solution:
(A) 주어 He가 사실적인 설치 미술품을 지금까지 ‘만들어 온’ 주체이자, 지금도 계속 만들고 있는 중임을 강조하기 위해, 현재완료진행(have/has been+-ing)인 has been making이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
(B) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(she ~ detail)을 이끌어 선행사 places를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치하므로, 선행사인 단수 명사구 ‘a delightful ~ camera’에 수일치한 단수동사 projects는 적절하다.

For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk (B)[eased / were eased], and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, prompting the development of the civilizations.
[3]
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to (C)[have been used / be used] to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

choices: enriched / were eased / be used
enriching / eased / have been used
enriching / were eased / be used
enriched / eased / have been used
enriched / were eased / have been used

body:
Technology Doping
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, (A)[increased / reduced] water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit.
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be (B)[airtight / breathable].
“Technology doping” in sports means the practice of gaining a competitive edge by using technology to improve performance. This can be against the spirit of fair play. However, since most sports require equipment of some sort, it can be tricky to determine what is technology doping and what is not. Some argue that it is a natural progress coming from scientific development, while others claim it undermines human spirit and effort, (C)[ensuring / denying] that rich athletes have an advantage over poor ones.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: reduced / breathable / ensuring
increased / airtight / denying
increased / breathable / ensuring
reduced / breathable / denying
reduced / airtight / ensuring
solution:
(A) 전신 수영복의 특징으로, 근육으로의 산소 공급 향상, 부력 증가와 함께 선수들이 물속에서 더 좋은 경기력을 낼 수 있도록 하는 기능이 이어져야 하므로 물의 저항을 감소시킨다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reduced(감소된)가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에서 새로운 전신 수영복이 공기를 가둬 부력을 높였고, 이 수영복을 입은 선수들이 계속해서 세계 기록을 깼다고 했으므로 이를 규제하기 위해 FINA가 수영복의 직물은 통기성이 있도록 규정한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 breathable(통기성이 있는)이 적절하다.
(C) ‘기술 도핑’이 정정당당한 경쟁에 반하는 것일 수 있다고 언급하며, 기술 도핑을 비판하는 사람들은 그것이 인간의 정신력과 노력을 약화시킨다고 주장하므로, 기술 도핑이 부유한 선수들이 가난한 선수들보다 유리하도록 보장한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ensuring(확실히 하는)이 적절하다.

body:
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many ______

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: woven around the production of silk
confirmed by researchers as historically accurate
made by accident in the field of textile engineering
developed to explain the origins of traditional tea culture
passed down to describe the invention of Chinese agriculture
solution: 앞에서 비단 생산에 대해 Leizu와 누에고치에 관한 이야기를 소개한 뒤 ‘This Chinese legend(이 중국의 전설은)이라고 시작하므로, 이 전설이 비단 생산의 기원을 둘러싼 여러 전설 중 하나라는 내용이 이어지는 것이 가장 자연스럽다. 따라서 ❶ '비단 생산을 둘러싸고 만들어진'이 적절하다.

On July 21, 1969, 528 million people ⓑtuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest ⓒchallenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s ⓓsurprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. It remains the most ⓔsimple space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

G: Dad, I’ve been thinking about participating in the underwater cleanup program.
M: Really? How does that program actually work?

solution: 수중 정화 프로그램에 참여할까 생각중이라는 딸의 말에 아버지가 그 프로그램이 실제로 어떻게 진행되는지를 묻는 주어진 대화에 이어, 프로그램 진행 방식에 대해 참가자들이 바다로 나가 수중 쓰레기를 수거한다고 설명하는 (D), 딸이 수중 활동 경험이 많지 않다는 점을 걱정하며 안전에 대한 우려를 나타내는 (B), 수영과 다이빙 경험에 따라 참가자들에게 서로 다른 역할이 주어지므로 누구나 참여할 수 있다고 설명하며 걱정하지 말라고 아빠를 안심시키는 (A), 딸의 설명에 ‘I see.(그렇구나.)’라며 수긍한 뒤 참여하기 전에 프로그램에 대해 더 알아보고 안전을 최우선시하라고 한 번 더 조언하는 (E), 아빠의 조언에 ‘You’re right, Dad.(맞아요, 아빠.)‘라고 말하며 동의한 뒤 참여 전에 프로그램에 대해 꼭 더 조사해보겠다고 말하는 (C)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, ⓐincreases its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in (A)capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes ⓑhave been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times (B)more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and ⓒstored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that ⓓhas dissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, (C)accelerating global warming.
Nevertheless, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet saving function ⓔdepending on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and ⓕaid in the planet’s decarbonization. Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, rethinking industrial fishing practices, (D)restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution ⓖentered the sea. By (E)prioritizing ocean health, we can unlock its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.

body:
Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to ______. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean’s conservation.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: strengthening marine law enforcement
monitoring changes in marine environments
prioritizing ocean research and conservation
strengthening cooperation with marine scientists
advancing technological innovation in marine industries
solution: Earle의 노력에도 불구하고 그녀는 정부 고위 관리로서 표현과 행동의 자유에 대한 제약에 직면해 보다 적극적인 환경 운동가가 되고자 2년 후 미국 국립해양대기청(NOAA)에서 사임했고, 민간 부문에서 해양 보호 캠페인을 위해 자신의 전문 지식과 경험을 활용했다고 설명하고 있으므로, NOAA의 첫 여성 과학자가 된 후 해양 자원 개발에서 해양의 연구와 보호로 NOAA의 초점을 바꾸고자 노력했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❸ ‘해양 연구와 보전에 우선순위를 두는 것’이 알맞다.

body:
When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there?” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life ⓐwhich I see.” Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.
Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. ⓑHaving moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is ⓒdive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake ⓓworn the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle (A)______. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine ⓔscientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation.

choices: was relieved to return safely to the surface
was surprised to find the water extremely cold
was curious to discover what lay beyond the familiar shoreline
was concerned to notice the limited visibility below the surface
was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the importance of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.”
With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and preserve the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.

In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and ⓐwalking on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” (A) As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. (B) Among them were some species she had studied but ⓑnever seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend ⓒit. (C) She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. (D) The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet ⓓto explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” (E) Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day ⓔwhen human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration.

Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support.
Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for maintaining ocean health.

(A)그렇게 함으로써, 그녀는 상황들을 더 나쁘게 만들었는데 왜냐하면 그녀는 그녀의 어려운 과학 수업을 견디며 집중해야 하기 때문이다. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. ⓒ[Embarrassed / Embarrassing] and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny?
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: finishing / catch / Embarrassing
finishing / to catch / Embarrassed
finished / catch / Embarrassing
finishing / to catch / Embarrassing
finished / to catch / Embarrassed
solution:
ⓐ 완전한 절(Jenny ~ night)에 접속사와 주어 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 Jenny가 과제를 ‘끝내는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 finishing이 적절하다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(She ~ rush)에 동사원형이 바로 이어질 수 없으며, 흐름상 ‘등교 버스를 타기 위해’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로 ‘목적’의 의미를 갖는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to catch가 적절하다.
ⓒ 뒤에 완전한 절(she ~ friends)이 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 she가 ‘당황하게 된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 Embarrassed가 적절하다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 대동사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
bad, on, have to, matter, sit through, focus, by, difficult
______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ because ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class.
solution:
• ‘그렇게 함으로써’를 영작하기 위해 do so(그렇게 하다)를 사용하여 ‘~함으로써’를 뜻하는 ‘by+동명사’를 결합하여 By doing so를 쓴다. 참고로 do so는 앞 문장에 쓰인 ‘skip ~ school’을 가리킨다.
• ‘~을 …하게 만들다’의 뜻을 갖는 5형식 'make+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)‘를 사용하여 시제에 맞게 made, 목적어 matters를 쓰고, 형용사 bad의 비교급 worse를 목적격보어 자리에 쓴다.
• 접속사 because 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어져야 하므로, ’~해야 한다‘를 뜻하는 'have to+동사원형’을 주어 she에 수일치하여 has to sit through(~에서 끝까지 앉아 있다)를 쓰고, 등위접속사 and 뒤에는 반복되는 has to를 생략하고 동사원형 focus로 시작하여 focus on 뒤에 her difficult science class를 이어 쓴다.

body:
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Having a delicious meal can make people feel comfortable and happy.
Hunger often brings physical weakness and negative feelings.
A well-known candy bar used the slogan “You’re not you when you’re hungry” in its ads a few years ago.
The slogan shows that hunger can affect both a person's emotional state and their overall performance.
Getting annoyed because of hunger is too rare for the word “hangry” to be officially added to dictionaries.
solution:
배고픔으로 인해 짜증이 나고 예민해지는 현상은 너무 흔해서 ’hangry‘라는 단어가 사전에 실렸다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘배고픔으로 인해 짜증이 나는 것은 너무 드물어, 'hangry'라는 단어가 공식적으로 사전에 추가될 수 없다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 맛있는 식사를 하는 것은 사람들이 편안하고 행복하게 느끼도록 만들 수 있다.
② 배고픔은 종종 신체적인 쇠약과 부정적인 감정들을 가져온다.
③ 한 유명한 초코 바는 몇 년 전 광고에서 “배고플 땐 너답지 않아.”라는 문구를 사용했다.
④ 그 문구는 배고픔은 한 사람의 감정 상태와 전반적인 수행 능력 모두에 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 보여 준다.

윗글의 바로 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the history of famous commercial slogans and examples of their marketing strategies
the physical effects of hunger and how they lead to irritation and anger
why people choose to eat candy bars when they feel stressed
how dictionary editors decide to add new words like “hangry”

solution:
hangry라는 단어를 소개하면서 배고픔이 사람의 기분과 수행 능력을 변화시키고 짜증과 분노를 일으킬 수 있으며 이런 현상이 사전에 실린 정도로 너무 흔하다고 언급한 뒤 마지막 문장에서 ‘그렇다면 그것은 어떻게 일어나는 걸까?’라고 질문을 던졌으므로, 배고픔으로 인해 짜증이 나고 예민해지는 현상이 일어나는 과정, 즉 배고픔이 신체와 감정에 미치는 영향, 그리고 그것이 짜증과 분노로 이어지는 과정에 관한 내용이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 ② ‘배고픔의 신체적 영향과 그것들이 짜증과 분노로 이어지는 방식’이 적절하다.
오답
① 유명한 광고 문구들의 역사와 마케팅 전략의 예시들
③ 사람들이 스트레스를 느낄 때 초코바를 먹는 것을 선택하는 이유
④ 사전 편집자들이 “hangry”와 같은 새로운 단어를 추가하기로 결정하는 방식
⑤ 바쁜 근무 시간 동안 배고픔을 느끼지 않게 하는 간단한 방법들

body:
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or ⓐeating a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management ⓑbeing recorded and analyzed. The results showed ⓒthat participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name ⓓprinted in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem ⓔto suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓐ eating → eat (상관접속사 'either A or B(A 또는 B)'의 구조로, either 앞의 to와 함께 쓰여 to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 skip과 병렬 구조를 이뤄야 하므로, eating을 동사원형 eat로 고친다.)
ⓑ being → were (해당 문장에 동사가 없으므로 동사 자리이며, 전치사구 at varying ~ management의 수식을 받는 주어 Their performance and behavior가 ‘기록되고 분석되는’ 대상이므로 뒤의 두 과거분사 recorded and analyzed와 함께 수동태를 이루는 be동사가 쓰여야 한다. 따라서 주어가 A and B의 형태로 복수 취급하여, being을 복수 동사 were로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 완전한 절(participants ~ beforehand)을 이끌어 동사 showed의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓓ 앞의 명사구 a color name을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a color name이 ‘출력된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 printed가 적절하다.
ⓔ 동사 seem은 to부정사와 함께 쓰여 ‘~하는 것 같다’를 뜻하므로 seem 뒤에 to부정사 to suggest는 적절하다.

body:
Hunger and Hormones
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know ⓐthat hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets ⓑabsorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing ⓒthat they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body ⓓcope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects ⓔincluding anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ that → what (to do의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they ~ do)을 이끌어 선행사 없이 동명사 performing의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, that을 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(hunger ~ too)을 이끌어 동사 know의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓑ 동사 gets의 보어 자리이며, 주어 It(=glucose)이 ‘흡수되는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 absorbed는 적절하다.
ⓓ 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절의 동사 helps는 준사역동사로 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 구조로 쓰여 목적격보어로 항상 동사원형 또는 to부정사를 취하므로, 목적격보어로 동사원형 cope이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
ⓔ ‘~를 포함하여’의 의미로 구체적 예시(anxiety, irritation, and depression)를 나타내는 명사구를 이끌어 앞의 명사구 many psychological effects를 수식할 수 있는 전치사 including은 적절하다.

body:
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop.
(A) These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly altered.
(B) When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity.
(C) Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being.
Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 코르티솔 수치가 높아지면 뇌 속 세로토닌 수치가 감소한다는 주어진 글 뒤에는, 앞에서 언급된 세로토닌의 개념과 신경계에서의 역할을 설명하는 (C), (C)에서 설명한 세로토닌의 역할을 바탕으로, 세로토닌 수치의 불균형이 감정 조절을 방해하여 슬픔, 짜증, 불안 등을 유발한다는 인과관계를 설명하는 (B), (B)에서 언급한 뇌 영상 기법에서의 뇌 활동 사진들(pictures of brain activity)을 These images로 받아, 배고플 때 위협 및 부정적 감정 관련 영역 활동이 증가하는 반면, 자기 통제나 의사 결정과 같은 인지 기능을 담당하는 영역이 크게 변화한다는 구체적인 결과를 제시하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
You Are in Control
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. (A)______, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you’re just hangry.
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. (B)______, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: Furthermore / In short
In addition / Nevertheless
For example / That is
However / In other words
For instance / Nonetheless
solution:

(B) 앞 문장에서 ‘외로움에서 오는 허기(lonely hunger)’가 외로움에서 신체적 영양 섭취에 대한 욕구로 이어지는 현상이라고 했고, 다음 문장에서 그 현상이 구체적으로 어떤 현상인지를 다시 설명하므로 That is(다시 말해), In other words(다시 말해서)가 적절하다.

body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. (A) Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. (B) Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. (C) For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. (D) Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control. (E)
The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그 결과는 식사를 거른 참가자들이 미리 식사를 했던 참가자들보다 수행 능력이 더 낮았다는 사실을 보여 주었다.’라는 의미로, 앞에는 두 유형의 참가자들과 관련된 실험 내용과 과정 등이 언급되어야 한다. (A) 뒤에서 참가자들의 두 가지 다른 유형을 설명하고 있고, (B) 뒤에서는 다양한 과제에서 참가자들의 수행과 행동을 기록하고 분석했다고 설명했다고 언급하고 있으므로, 그 기록과 분석의 결과를 주어진 문장의 The result가 가리키고 있으므로 주어진 문장은 (C) 이후에 들어가는 것이 자연스러우며, 뒤에 For example(예를 들어)로 시작하여, 주어진 문장에서 언급한 ‘poorer performance’의 구체적인 예로 식사를 거른 참가자들이 Stroop 과제에서 더 많은 실수를 했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 주어진 문장은 실험 결과를 기록하고 분석했다는 내용과 구체적인 사례 사이인 (C)에 들어가야 한다.

solution:

body:
Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your (A)[genes / environment] if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as (B)[common / unique] as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, creating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired (C)[similarly / differently] when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact that we are all different and share a plate of understanding.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: environment / unique / differently
genes / unique / similarly
genes / common / differently
environment / common / similarly
genes / unique / differently
solution:
(A) 오이와 같이 특정 음식에 대한 강한 혐오감이 기호보다는 유전일 수 있으며, 오이가 생성하는 쓴맛의 물질을 매우 민감하게 느끼는 특정 유전자가 있다는 사실을 밝혀냈다는 내용이 언급되었으므로, 그러므로 어떤 음식을 싫어한다면 자신의 ‘유전자’를 탓할 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 genes(유전자)가 적절하다.
environment 환경
(B) 뒤에서 400가지가 넘는 후각 수용체가 존재하여 다양성을 만들어낸다고 했으므로, 후각은 우리 자신만큼이나 ‘독특하다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 unique(독특한)가 적절하다.
common 흔한
(C) 특정 음식을 싫어하는 원인이 유전자와 타고난 후각 수용체에 따라 다를 수 있다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로, 음식 취향에 있어서 우리 모두 타고나게 ‘다른’ 것처럼 보인다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 differently(다르게)가 적절하다.
similarly 유사하게

body:
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry ⓐrefers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works ⓑthe other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical ⓒnourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in ⓓexcessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. (A)연구는 또한 외로움이 배고픔과 비슷한 신호로 작용한다는 견해를 지지하는데, 이는 해결될 필요가 있는 결핍 상태를 나타낸다는 것이다. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be ⓔaddressed.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
<보기>
ⓐ refer to: to mention or speak about somebody or something
ⓑ the other way around: the opposite of what you have just mentioned
ⓒ nourishment: the food and other substances that people and other living things need to live, grow, and stay healthy
ⓓ excessive: even less than is reasonable or necessary
ⓔ address: to say something directly to somebody
solution:
ⓑ 반대로: 당신이 방금 말한 것과 반대인
ⓒ 영양분: 사람과 다른 생명체가 살아가고 성장하며 건강을 유지하는 데 필요한 음식과 기타 물질들
오답
ⓐ ~을 나타내다: 누군가 또는 무언가를 언급하거나 이야기하다 (→to describe or be connected to somebody or something 누군가 또는 무언가를 묘사하거나 연관되다)
ⓓ 지나친, 과도한: 합리적이거나 필요한 것보다도 훨씬 더 적은 (→much more less than is reasonable or necessary 합리적이거나 필요한 것보다도 훨씬 더 많은)
ⓔ ~을 다루다, 해결하다: 누군가에게 무언가를 직접 말하다(→to think about a problem or a situation and decide how you are going to deal with it(문제나 상황에 대해 생각하고 그것을 어떻게 처리할지 결정하다))

Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry ⓐrefers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works ⓑthe other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical ⓒnourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in ⓓexcessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. (A)연구는 또한 외로움이 배고픔과 비슷한 신호로 작용한다는 견해를 지지하는데, 이는 해결될 필요가 있는 결핍 상태를 나타낸다는 것이다. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be ⓔaddressed.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 동격 접속사를 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• 형용사구 후치 수식을 사용할 것
• 관계대명사 that을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 22단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
similar to, a signal, the notion, serve, also support, as, studies, address, indicate, need
→ ______
answer: Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed.
solution:
• 주어 Studies와 부사 also의 수식받는 동사 support 뒤에 목적어 the notion을 쓰고 the notion과 동격을 나타내는 절을 영작하기 위해 동격 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• 동격절의 주어 loneliness와 ‘~으로 작용한다, ~로서 역할을 하다’를 뜻하는 자동사구 serves as와 목적어 a signal을 이어 쓴다.
• 명사구 a signal을 후치 수식하는 형용사구를 영작하기 위해 ‘~와 비슷한’을 뜻하는 similar to와 명사 hunger를 차례대로 쓴다.
• 콤마(,) 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문을 영작해야 하며, 의미상 주어인 a signal similar to hunger가 결핍 상태를 ‘나타내는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 indicating을 쓴다.
• ’결핍 상태’를 뜻하는 a lack과 a lack을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계대명사 that을 쓴다. ‘~할 필요가 있다’를 뜻하는 ‘need+to부정사’를 사용하되, 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치하므로 a lack에 수일치한 단수동사 needs를 쓰고, to부정사의 의미상 주어인 a lack이 ‘해결될’ 필요가 있는 대상이므로 to부정사의 수동태 to be addressed를 차례대로 쓴다.

The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves ⓐcomparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs ⓑto consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, ⓒvoted either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, ⓓwas preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes (A)______. This is especially true in elections that ⓔcontains numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over ⓕothers.

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.

ⓔ contains → contain (주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사 that에 대한 동사 자리로, 주격 관계대명사는 선행사에 수와 태를 일치시키므로 선행사인 복수명사 elections에 수가 일치되도록 복수동사 contain으로 고친다.)

unified 일치되는

body:
(A)이상적인 투표 방법을 선택하는 것은 복잡하고 도전적인 일이라는 것은 분명하다. No voting system is ㉠flawless or clearly superior to ⓐanother. ⓑWhich we choose will have pros and cons. Some people believe that it is best ⓒto keep the process ㉡simple by not ranking our choices at all. Others ㉢continue to develop and test new ways of voting, ⓓargue that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and ㉣inefficient, but ⓔhelp us make better decisions as a society. Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and ㉤neglecting their pros and cons allows us ⓕto better understand the process of decision-making. When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ⓖourselves.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.

• ‘It(가주어) ~ that(진주어)’ 구문을 사용할 것
• 동명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 15단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
task, obvious, challenging, choose, complex, an ideal voting method
→ ______
answer: It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task.
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 가주어 It을 문장의 주어로 쓰고 동사와 보어인 is obvious를 연결한 뒤 진주어인 that절을 이어 쓴다.
• 동명사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라, that절의 주어를 동명사구로 영작한다. 주어진 단어 choose를 동명사 choosing으로 변형한 뒤 제시된 표현인 an ideal voting method를 목적어로 써서 주어를 완성한다. 동명사(구) 주어는 단수 취급하므로 동사 is를 연결하고 보어 자리에 a complex and challenging task를 써서 문장을 완성한다.

solution:
ⓑ 선행사 없이 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we choose)을 이끌어 문장 전체의 주어 역할을 해야 하며, 흐름상 우리가 선택하는 것은 무엇이든지 장단점이 있다는 뜻이므로, ‘~하는 어느 것이든지’라는 뜻의 복합관계대명사 Whichever로 고친다. 참고로, 이때 Whichever는 명사절을 이끌므로 Anything that[which]으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.

I’m thrilled to see
I’m curious to see
I’m reluctant to see

solution:
‘I can’t wait+to부정사‘는 ‘~하기를 무척 기대하다’라는 의미로, 어떤 일이나 경험에 대해 기대감과 설렘을 강하게 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현이다. ‘I’m curious to see ~’는 ‘~이 어떨지 궁금하다’라는 뜻이고, ‘I’m reluctant to see ~’는 ‘~을 보는 것이 꺼려진다’를 뜻하므로 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은 ③ ‘~이 어떨지 궁금하다’, ④ ‘~을 보는 것이 꺼려진다’이다.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been the subject of much discussion and controversy for many decades, with many experts (A)[predicting / predicted] that it will revolutionize our way of life. From healthcare to finance, the implementation of AI is transforming a wide range of sectors. (B)[Embrace / Embracing] AI means tapping into the potential of tomorrow in unprecedented ways. From self-driving cars to personalized medical treatments, AI is shaping our future and pushing the envelope like never before. As we stand on the brink of a new era, it is crucial that each of us (C)[understand / to understand] the rise of AI and its impacts on our world.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

choices: predicting / Embrace / to understand
predicted / Embracing / understand
predicted / Embrace / understand
predicting / Embracing / to understand
predicting / Embracing / understand
solution:
(A) 전치사 with, 명사구 many experts와 함께 ‘with+명사(구)+현재분사/과거분사(~가 …하면서/한 채로)’의 부대상황을 나타내는 with분사구문을 이루고 있으며, many experts가 ‘예측하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 predicting이 알맞다.
(B) 뒤에 동사 means가 있으므로 주어 역할을 할 수 있는 동명사 Embracing이 알맞다.
(C) ‘중요성, 의무, 필요’ 등을 나타내는 형용사가 보어로 쓰인 ‘가주어(it) - 진주어(that절)’에서 that절 안의 동사는 주어의 인칭이나 시제에 관계없이 동사원형을 사용하며, ‘~해야 한다’는 의미의 조동사 should가 동사원형 앞에서 생략된다. 형용사 crucial(매우 중요한)은 ‘중요성’을 나타내므로 that절 안의 동사는 조동사 should가 생략된 동사원형 understand가 알맞다.

solution:

solution:

body:
Advocates of AI argue ⓐwhat these advancements will lead to a more efficient, productive, and technical society, ⓑwhich individuals have more time and resources to focus on more meaningful work.
(A) Automation, they argue, will lead to widespread job losses, as machines and robots replace human workers in many industries.
(B) This could lead to ⓒfinding solutions to climate change and cures for untreatable illnesses much quicker. Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment.
(C) They also argue that AI has the potential to solve complex problems, such as climate change and disease, in ways that ⓓwere previously impossible. For example, AI can analyze huge amounts of data quickly ⓔto find patterns in weather changes or the spread of a disease.
This ⓕcould lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: AI의 지지자들은 이러한 발전이 더 효율적이고 생산적인 사회를 만들어, 개인이 더 의미 있는 일에 집중할 시간과 자원을 늘릴 것이라고 주장한다는 주어진 글 뒤에, AI의 지지자들(Advocates of AI)을 They(그들)로 이어받아 also(또한)과 함께 AI가 기후 변화나 질병과 같은 복잡한 문제를 해결할 잠재력이 있다고 AI에 대한 긍정적 견해를 추가로 제시하는 (C), (C)의 마지막에서 AI가 날씨 변화나 질병 확산의 양상을 찾기 위해 많은 양의 데이터를 빠르게 분석할 수 있다고 언급한 뒤, 앞서 언급한 AI의 데이터 분석 능력을 This로 이어받아 이것이 기후 변화와 질병 문제의 해결로 이어질 수 있다고 설명하는 (B), (B)의 마지막에서 Meanwhile(한편)을 통해 AI에 대한 긍정적 견해에서 비판자들의 우려로 전환한 뒤, 앞서 제기된 AI의 고용에 대한 우려를 구체적으로, 자동화로 인해 기계와 로봇이 노동자를 대체하여 대규모 일자리 상실을 초래할 것이라고 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
Advocates of AI argue ⓐwhat these advancements will lead to a more efficient, productive, and technical society, ⓑwhich individuals have more time and resources to focus on more meaningful work.

(B) This could lead to ⓒfinding solutions to climate change and cures for untreatable illnesses much quicker. Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment.
(C) They also argue that AI has the potential to solve complex problems, such as climate change and disease, in ways that ⓓwere previously impossible. For example, AI can analyze huge amounts of data quickly ⓔto find patterns in weather changes or the spread of a disease.
This ⓕcould lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ what → that (완전한 절(these ~ work)을 이끌어 동사 argue의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓑ which → where (콤마 뒤에서 완전한 절(individuals ~ work)을 이끌어, 콤마 앞의 명사구 a more efficient, productive, and technical society를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절이므로 관계부사 where로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 구동사 ‘lead to(~으로 이어지다)‘의 to는 전치사이므로 lead to의 목적어 자리의 동명사 finding은 적절하다.
ⓓ 복수명사 ways를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절의 동사이며, 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사와 수일치하므로, 복수동사 were는 적절하다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(AI ~ quickly)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ’날씨 변화나 질병 확산의 양상을 찾기 위해‘라는 의미로 목적을 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to find는 적절하다.
ⓕ 과거 시제가 아니라 가능성을 나타내는 could이므로 적절하다.

body:
This argument is not without merit. Automation has already displaced workers in several industries, and ⓐit is likely that this trend will continue as AI becomes more widespread. (A)______, it is also important to consider ⓑthat automation has been a driving force behind economic growth for centuries and has consistently created new job opportunities, even as it has decreased existing ones.
(B)______, the rise of the automobile industry in the early 20th century led to the displacement of carriage drivers, but it also created new jobs in manufacturing, sales, and service. The same can be said for the rise of the computer industry in the late 20th century, which displaced workers in manual labor industries, but also created new jobs in software development, information technology, and related fields.
Therefore, it is likely that the rise of AI will also give rise to new job opportunities. There will be a growing demand for data scientists, machine learning engineers, and AI ethics experts, among others. These jobs will allow individuals ⓒcontributing to society in meaningful ways. At the same time, since they require new skills, education and training will need to evolve to help people ⓓprepare for these new opportunities. By adapting and learning, people can find paths in a world ⓔwhere AI plays a major role.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ contributing → to contribute (동사 allow의 목적격보어 자리로, 동사 allow는 ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 contributing을 to부정사 to contribute로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 진주어절 ‘this trend ~ widespread’가 있으므로 이에 상응하는 가주어 it은 적절하다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(automation ~ ones)을 이끌어 to consider의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓓ help의 목적격보어 자리로, 동사 help는 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어 자리의 동사원형 prepare는 적절하다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(AI ~ role)을 이끌어 장소를 나타내는 선행사 a world를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 관계부사 where는 적절하다.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: In contrast / Thus
Furthermore / Nevertheless
Moreover / As a result
Therefore / For instance

solution:

body:
Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to maintain existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as (A)[objective / subjective]. However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely (B)[eliminate / reproduce] those biases in its output.
For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones. As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police. This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to (C)[amplify / diminish] the potential negative impacts of AI.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: objective / reproduce / amplify
objective / eliminate / diminish
subjective / reproduce / amplify
subjective / eliminate / diminish
objective / reproduce / diminish
solution:
(A) 다음 문장이 However(그러나)로 연결되어 AI 시스템은 그것이 훈련된 데이터가 편향되지 않는 만큼만 편향되지 않을 수 있다고 했으므로, 사람들이 컴퓨터 시스템을 ‘객관적’이라고 여긴다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 objective(객관적인)가 적절하다.
subjective 주관적인
(B) 앞에서 AI 시스템은 그것이 훈련된 데이터가 편향되지 않는 만큼만 편향되지 않을 수 있다고 했으며, 뒤에 언급된 예시에서 안면 인식 알고리즘이 편향된 데이터로 인해 특정 피부색을 가진 사람의 인식 정확도가 떨어진다고 언급되었으므로, 데이터에 편향이 있다면 AI 시스템의 산출물에도 그러한 편향을 ‘재현할’ 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reproduce(재현하다)가 적절하다.
eliminate ~을 없애다
(C) AI 시스템이 기존의 편향과 차별을 지속 시킬 가능성에 대한 윤리적 우려에 대한 글로, 안면 인식 알고리즘이 편향된 데이터로 인해 소수 인종에 속하는 사람들이 부당하게 체포되는 사건이 있었던 것처럼, 사회는 AI의 이런 잠재적인 부정적 영향을 ‘줄일’ 대책을 취하는 것이 중요하다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 diminish(줄이다)가 적절하다.
amplify ~을 증폭시키다

solution:

body:
Merging with AI: We may be able to merge with AI in the future, enhancing our intelligence and life expectancy. What would it be like to be able to access the Internet with your mind? Then we might be able to think and learn at extraordinary speeds and control machines with our thoughts.
Bots taking the lead: Many traditional jobs might fade away, but exciting new roles may pop up. People might be trained to be mediators between AI and humans. Schools might teach teamwork among humans and bots rather than traditional subjects. Kids may attend “fusion schools” where AI instructor bots might collaborate with human creativity. Here, students can design artworks and invent games alongside their AI friends.
Scientific leaps: Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) can solve complex problems, allowing for phenomenal achievements in physics, medicine, climate science, and other fields at an unprecedented pace. For example, the spacecraft of the future may be capable of traveling to other planets at unimaginable speeds. They may also be equipped with advanced life support systems that will allow humans to live there for extended periods of time.
The technological singularity is a potentially dangerous event, but it is also one that could lead to incredible advances for humanity. We need to be aware of the risks and prepare for them as best we can, so that we can make sure that the singularity is a positive event for us all.
