answer: there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police
solution:
• ‘사건들이 있어왔다’를 영작하기 위해 ‘~이 있다’라는 뜻의 ‘there+be동사+주어‘와 현재완료시제를 사용해야 하며, 주어인 복수명사 incidents와 수일치하여 there have been incidents를 쓴다.
• 추상적인 의미에서 공간을 뜻하는 명사 incidents를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계부사 where를 쓴다.
• ’소수 인종의 사람들‘을 뜻하도록 주어 people of racial minorities를 쓴다. 주어 people of racial minorities가 잘못 ‘식별된‘ 대상이므로 ’identify ~ as …(~을 …로 식별하다)’의 수동태 ’~ be identified as …(~가 …로 식별되다)’와 현재완료시제를 사용하여 복수주어 people of racial minorities에 이어지는 현재완료수동태 have been mistakenly identified와 as wanted criminals를 쓴다. 주어 people of racial minorities가 ‘체포된‘ 대상이므로 등위 접속사 and 뒤에 have been을 생략하고 부사 wrongfully와 과거분사 arrested를 쓴다.

M: The Concorde was the first commercial airplane that could travel faster than the speed of sound. It could fly from Paris to New York in half the time of other planes. The Concorde was a technological (A)marvel, but today it is nowhere to ⓐbe seen. What happened? In fact, the Concorde’s failure was (B)inevitable from the start. Its production costs were excessive, and it consumed a lot of fuel. Also, it was able to carry only a small number of passengers. In other words, it was never a (C)profitable airplane. Despite these problems, large sums of money continued to be invested in the Concorde. The governments and airline companies ⓑfunded it were (D)reluctant to admit that it was a failure. They were worried about wasting the money and other resources ⓒthat they had already spent on it. Eventually, after many years of huge losses, the Concorde made its last flight in 2003. The decision to keep operating the Concorde was the result of the “sunk cost fallacy.” Why do people fall for the sunk cost fallacy? Perhaps it’s the human instinct ⓓto avoid losses. However, sunk costs are costs that you’ll never (E)lose, regardless of what decisions you make in the future. If you realize your past decision was a mistake, accept the fact and move on. Don’t let sunk costs ⓔaffect your decisions.
위 담화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓑ funded → funding (뒤에 문장의 본동사인 과거동사 were가 있으므로 접속사 없이 과거동사가 올 수 없고, were 앞에서 주어부를 이루도록 명사구 The governments and airline companies를 수식하는 분사구의 분사가 와야 한다. 뒤에 목적어인 it이 있으며 정부와 항공사들이 자금을 지원하는 주체이므로 funded를 능동 관계를 나타내는 현재분사 funding으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they ~ on it)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the money and other resources를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ 사역동사 let과 목적어 sun costs에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, 사역동사 let은 목적격 보어로 동사원형을 취하므로 동사원형 affect는 적절하다.

body:
We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to ⓐwhat career to pursue. However, there are many situations ⓑwhich we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with ⓒdiffering opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and ⓓmore efficiently, and various voting methods ⓔhave been developed over time. The following story illustrates ⓕhow do these different voting methods work.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ which → where (완전한 절(we ~ group)을 이끌어 추상적 장소를 나타내는 명사구 many situations를 수식해야 하므로, 관계대명사 which를 관계부사 where로 고친다.)
ⓓ more efficiently → more efficient (make의 목적어 group decisions에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, 5형식 동사로 쓰인 make는 목적격 보어로 형용사를 취하여 ‘~을 ...하게 만들다’라는 뜻을 나타내므로 목적격 보어 자리에서 앞의 비교급 형용사 fairer와 등위 접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 형용사구를 이루도록 비교급 부사 more efficiently를 비교급 형용사 more efficient로 고친다.)
ⓕ how do these different voting methods work → how these different voting methods work (동사 illustrates의 목적어 자리이므로 의문사 how가 이끄는 간접의문문이 와야 한다. 간접의문문은 ‘의문사+평서문’의 어순을 따르므로 how do these different voting methods work를 의문사 how, 주어 these different voting methods, 동사 work의 어순으로 쓰인 how these different voting methods work로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 전치사 to의 목적어 자리이므로 ‘의문사(구)+to부정사’의 명사구를 이루는 what career to pursue는 알맞다.

body:
Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making.
It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another. (A) Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. (B) Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. (C) Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. (D) All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society. (E) When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: ‘결국, 모든 가능한 투표 방법을 이해하고 장단점을 따져 보는 것은 우리가 의사 결정 과정을 더 잘 이해할 수 있게 한다.’라는 뜻의 주어진 문장은, Ultimately(결국, 궁극적으로)를 사용하여 투표 방식을 이해하고 비교하는 행위의 핵심을 제시하고 있으므로, 이러한 모든 노력, 곧 모든 투표 방식은 의사 결정을 어렵고 비효율적으로 만들기 위한 것이 아니라, 우리가 집단으로서 더 나은 의사 결정을 내릴 수 있게 돕기 위해 고안된 것이라는 문장 뒤이자 주어진 문장에 언급된 ‘의사 결정을 더 잘 이해하는 것’을 다시 언급하며 의사 결정을 더 잘 이해할 때 우리는 더 나은 의사 결정자가 될 가능성이 더 높다는 내용으로 주어진 문장의 결과를 진술하기 전인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote.
When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, ⓐ그녀는 그들에게 익숙한 투표 방법을 사용하지 말고, 대신 다른 것을 시도해 보라고 권장했다. After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results.
On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.”
Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference. For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA.
After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted. The results were as follows:

Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was ⓐ[required / optional].
Option A, the art show, received the ⓑ[fewest / most] first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were ⓒ[added to / subtracted from] the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner.
Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. (A)그것은 때때로 2지망 표가 1지망 표보다 더 큰 영향력을 갖게 하기도 한다. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.

The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters are given ⓐseveral options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes (A)[win / wins]. The student council quickly ⓒdetermined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
The FPTP method is uncomplicated and ⓓtricky to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. body:
The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves ______ In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: giving different scores to options based on their ranked position
choosing the most popular option without ranking any choices
comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options
repeating the vote until an option secures a majority of the total votes
holding a second vote strictly among the options who received equal votes

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것은?
solution:
ⓓ ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’가 ‘~가 ...하면서’라는 뜻의 부대상황을 나타내며, 명사구 5 council members가 그것에 ‘투표하는’ 주체이자 vote가 전치사 for와 함께 자동사로 쓰였으므로 with와 목적어인 명사구 only 5 council members에 이어 능동 관계를 나타내는 분사 voting이 쓰인 with only 5 council members voting for it은 알맞다.

ⓐ used → using (완전한 절(the council ~ votes)에 접속사 없이 이어져야 하므로 동사가 올 수 없고 분사구문을 이끄는 분사가 와야 한다. 의미상 주어 the council members가 사용하는 주체로 목적어 the AV method가 이어지므로 used를 능동 관계를 나타내는 현재분사 using으로 고친다.)
ⓑ what → that (타동사 meant의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(option B ~ only 9)을 이끌어야 하므로, what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)

by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie living in 2155 ⓐreceives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school ⓑwhere all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
[2]
Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. Living in an era ⓒwhen we enjoy technical innovations and boundless connectivity, we should take advantage of what is available in education as well. In the following, I will explore the reasons why online education is a better choice.
First, online education breaks down the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living far away. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
[3]
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter what advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable that online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks that education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, which traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven more successful in providing an educational environment ⓓin which students can concentrate and learn better. According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. It seems that ⓔwhat is much easier for students to pay attention and understand the content taught in a traditional classroom because they are learning together.
Traditional education also fosters the development of students’ social and interpersonal skills. Beyond classroom instruction, students interact during their lunch breaks and extracurricular activities. While spending time together and being engaged in various types of interaction, students are exposed to valuable opportunities to learn how to communicate with each other. Consequently, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ what → it (뒤에 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사구(to ~ classroom)와 의미상 주어(for students)가 있으므로 이에 상응하는 가주어가 와야 한다. 따라서 what을 it으로 고친다.)

Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
Second, online education caters to (A)______. One of the criticisms of traditional education is that it takes a one-size-fits-all approach that ⓓfail to address the various needs of students. In contrast, online learning can offer a customized learning path for each learner. To achieve this, a computer learning program first assesses each learner’s current level and weaknesses. Based on the assessment, each learner is offered personalized online lessons and more detailed explanations when necessary. This kind of personalized feedback process can be highly interactive and motivate learners to reach higher levels of achievement.
Finally, online education uses advanced technology such as multimedia materials or virtual simulations to provide more engaging and impactful learning experiences. For example, students can learn history more effectively by using virtual reality programs, ⓔwhich can show them realistic details of famous historical sites or allow them to travel back in time.

choices: ways traditional education addresses the problems of a one-size-fits-all approach
key features that make online education an effective learning choice
how technology is changing the way online education is provided
the differences between traditional and online education methods
the growing use of online education in the digital age

body:
Dear Editor,
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter what advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable that online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks that education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, which traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven more successful in providing an educational environment where students can concentrate and learn better. According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. It seems that it is much easier for students to pay attention and understand the content taught in a traditional classroom because they are learning together.
Traditional education also fosters the development of students’ social and interpersonal skills. Beyond classroom instruction, students interact during their lunch breaks and extracurricular activities. ⓐ함께 시간을 보내고 다양한 유형의 상호 작용에 참여하는 동안, 학생들은 서로 소통하는 방법을 배울 수 있는 귀중한 기회에 노출됩니다. Consequently, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What does online education mainly focus on?
How was the study on students’ levels of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes conducted?
Why do students in traditional classrooms tend to pay attention and understand the content better?
When do students have opportunities to interact with one another beyond classroom instruction?
What specific social skills do students acquire through traditional education?
solution: 전통적 교실과 온라인 수업에서의 학생들의 집중도와 이해도에 관한 연구에 따르면, 전통적 교실의 학생들이 학업을 더 잘 수행했으며, 이는 학생들이 함께 학습하기 때문이라고만 언급되었을 뿐, 연구 방식에 대해서는 제시된 바가 없으므로, ② ‘전통적 교실과 온라인 수업에서의 학생들의 집중도와 이해도에 관한 연구는 어떻게 진행되었는가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.

body:
by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments using multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are present together.

다음 글을 읽고 아래 질문에 대한 답을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸을 완성하시오.
(1) What is the “real school” that Margie imagines like?
→ Margie imagines a “real school” as a place ______.
(2) What does traditional education generally mean?
→ It generally means ______.
answer:
(1) Margie imagines a “real school” as a place where other students and she learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
(2) It generally means the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are present together.
solution:
정답은 (1) Margie imagines a “real school” as a place where other students and she learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
(2) It generally means the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are present together. 이다. (해설 없음)

Colors are an important aspect of films. They look visually attractive and can be used to convey various emotions and messages to the audience. Film directors carefully select colors like bright yellow to bring a sense of hope, calm blue for peace, and intense red for violence. These color choices are not random; they are intentionally made to impact your experience while you watch the film, even if you don’t consciously notice them. Below are several outstanding examples of how skillfully film directors can use color to add richness to the story and evoke specific emotions from the audience.

body:
Colors (A)[strengthen / weaken] the emotions of viewers due to their ability to evoke strong psychological reactions. An excellent example can be found in an animated film where an ordinary citizen becomes a superhero to defeat a villain. At the beginning of the film, the male character, who was once a superhero but had to return to living an ordinary life, is surrounded by (B)[dull / vivid] colors and gray tones. ⓐ그는 자신의 진정한 힘을 숨기면서, 마치 보통 사람인 것처럼 일하고 있다. However, when he returns to work as a superhero, the film fills up with bold reds, yellows, and blues. These colors represent power and happiness. This shift (C)[reflects / inhibits] his emotional development, and viewers can grasp his mood without words. Through such a process, colors impact the emotional experience of the audience.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

choices: strengthen / dull / reflects

solution:

weaken ~을 약화시킨다
(B) However(하지만) 뒤에 슈퍼히어로로 되돌아가 활동할 때 영화는 강렬한 빨강, 노랑, 파랑으로 가득 찬다는 내용이 대조적으로 이어지므로, 평범한 삶은 단조롭거나 칙칙한 색깔들과 회색 톤으로 둘러싸여 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 dull(흐릿한, 탁한)이 알맞다.
vivid 선명한, 강렬한
(C) 관객들은 말없이도 영화 속 캐릭터의 기분을 이해할 수 있다는 내용이 이어지므로, This shift(이러한 변화)가 가리키는 영화 속 색의 변화가 그의 정서적 성장을 나타낸다는 흐름이 되는 reflects(~을 반영한다)가 알맞다.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
It was the red coat of a single lost girl, alone in a crowd of frightened Jews.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그것은 겁에 질린 유대인 군중들 속에서 홀로 길을 잃은 한 소녀의 붉은 외투였다.’라는 뜻으로, It(그것)이 가리키는 것과 관련해 감독이 대부분 흑백으로 된 영화에 색을 더할 한 가지를 선택했다고 언급하는 내용 뒤이자, As such(그렇기 때문에)를 사용해 앞에 언급된 내용을 근거로 감독이 나치의 잔혹성을 강력하게 상징할 수 있게 해 준 것이 바로 강렬한 색상의 대비였다고 설명하는 문장 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Like the saying “A picture is worth a thousand words,” ⓐcolors get a film’s message across more strongly than words. (A) A good example is the red coat in a movie about the true story of a German businessman who saved thousands of Jews from the Nazis during World War II. (B) While the movie was mostly in black and white, the director chose one particular thing to add color to. (C) As such, it was the strong contrast of colors that enabled the director to powerfully symbolize the brutality of the Nazis. (D) The young girl represents innocence while also representing the violence of the Nazis. (E) So, what happened to this young girl? The movie never tells us for sure, but later in the film we see a dead girl in a red coat being loaded into a cart.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ‘colors get a film’s message across more strongly than words’가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Colors can diminish the impact of the message a film director intends to convey.
A film’s message becomes far clearer when colors and words convey the same information.
Colors function as aesthetic devices that enhance a film’s visual appeal rather than communicate meaning.
The deliberate use of color can communicate meaning with greater impact than verbal expression alone.
The function of colors in films is to make cinematic images visually engaging and emotionally pleasing.
solution:
예시로 든 영화에서 감독은 흑백과 대비되는 소녀의 붉은 외투를 부각하여 소녀의 순수함과 동시에 나치의 폭력성을 상징한다고 설명하고 있으므로, 밑줄 친 ⓐ ‘색상은 영화의 메시지를 말보다 더 강하게 전달한다’는 색의 사용을 통해 말로 설명할 필요 없이 영화가 전달하려는 메시지를 더 효과적으로 관객에게 각인시킬 수 있다는 의미라고 볼 수 있다. 따라서 밑줄 친 ⓐ가 의미하는 바로 ④ ‘의도적인 색상의 사용은 언어적 표현만이 전달하는 것보다 더 큰 영향력을 가지고 의미를 전달할 수 있다.’가 알맞다.
오답
① 색상은 영화감독이 전달하고자 하는 메시지의 영향력을 약화시킬 수 있다.
② 영화의 메시지는 색상과 말이 동일한 정보를 전달할 때 훨씬 더 분명해진다.
③ 색상은 의미를 전달하기보다는 영화의 시각적인 매력을 높이는 미적 장치로 기능한다.
⑤ 영화에서 색상의 기능은 영화적 이미지를 시각적으로 매력 있고 정서적으로 기분 좋게 만드는 것이다.

body:
Film directors capture the changes in their characters’ lives through changes in color. Another film from the 1990s follows the dramatic experience of a man with scissor hands ⓐwhich comes down to a town to live with ordinary folks. He always wears black, and the castle where he used ⓑto live was a gray and gloomy place. However, in the town ⓒwhere he came to live with his lover, each house is painted differently, and the people wear colorful clothes. At first, he is welcomed by the people in town, but as he becomes ⓓmisunderstood and disliked, the film’s colors gradually become darker. Eventually, he returns to his castle, but he fills his garden with green grass and beautiful, blooming flowers. Moreover, ice powder from his ice sculpture ⓔblowing in the wind like snow. With such changes, the director shows the audience that (A)______.
Film directors choose colors to give us the best possible experience. When ⓕwatching movies, consider why specific colors are used in a scene. You may not know the answer, but your understanding of the film will be deeper.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ which → who 또는 that (주어가 없는 불완전한 절(comes down ~ folks)을 이끌고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사가 올 자리이며, 관계사절이 수식하는 선행사가 scissor hands가 아니라 a man with scissor hands이므로, 사물 선행사와 쓰이는 which를 사람 선행사와 쓰이는 주격 관계대명사 who 또는 that으로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 who가 쓰였음
ⓔ blowing → blows (뒤에 다른 동사가 없으므로 주어 ice powder from his ice sculpture에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 글의 전체 시제를 고려해 현재시제를 써야 하고, 주어의 핵심이 단수명사구 ice powder이므로 blowing을 단수동사로 수일치한 blows로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ ‘(과거에) ~했었다(지금은 아니다)’를 뜻하는 ‘used to+동사원형’을 이루어야 하므로, used 뒤에 쓰인 to live는 알맞다.
ⓕ 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사 when을 남겨둔 ‘접속사+분사(구)’ 형태의 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 명령문인 주절(consider ~ a scene)의 생략된 주어 you와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 ‘보는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사 movies가 이어지므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 watching은 알맞다.

Colors help audiences grasp the connections between characters, places, and important objects in films, ⓐmaking complex stories easier to understand. With such color differences, the audience can distinguish which world the events take place in. *원래 지문에는 that이 쓰였음

The national flags of various European countries are tricolored, with the original being the French flag. The flags of Bolivia, Italy, and Ireland ⓐresemble the French flag with three colors, while Germany, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, and Russia use three colors with parallel bands. ㉠______
Ireland
The Irish tricolor (A)[comprises / is comprised] of green, white, and orange. It was crafted in celebration of the French Revolution and as a wish for the success of Ireland’s own revolution. Green symbolizes the Irish Catholics, orange represents the Irish Protestants, and white signifies ⓑconcord and peace between the two communities.
France
The French tricolor flag, a product of the declaration of the “rights of man” during the French Revolution stating, “All men are born free and equal,” has served as an example for the tricolor flags of numerous countries (B)[that / what] followed. The French flag consists of blue, white, and red, symbolizing ⓒoppression, equality, and fellowship.
Germany
The German flag, with its colors of black, red, and gold, has evolved to symbolize unification, liberty, and democracy. These colors came from the reunification of Germany formerly without specific meanings. In modern times, black represents persistence, red represents courage and strength, and gold symbolizes generosity. This flag with three colors, introduced in the late 18th century, became ⓓprominent in the 19th century.
Italy
Italy, (C)[influencing / influenced] by the French Revolution in its unification, initially adopted a flag with green, white, and red, along with a shield and cross. However, in 1946, these symbols were removed from the tricolor. The colors symbolize Italy’s ⓔlandscape and human rights, with red representing love and the conflict from the Wars of Italian Independence and Unification, and white symbolizing faith and the snowy Alps.

(B) 앞에 선행사로 명사구 numerous countries가 있고, 뒤에는 주어 없이 동사 followed가 이어져 있으므로, 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. 참고로, 관계대명사 what은 선행사를 포함한다.
(C) 주어 Italy에 대한 동사로 부사 initially의 수식을 받는 adopted가 있으므로, 주어와 동사구 사이에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어인 명사 Italy를 부연 설명하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리이다. 부연 설명의 대상인 Italy가 ‘영향을 받는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’by+명사구‘가 바로 이어져 있으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 influenced가 알맞다.

body:
Film directors capture the changes in their characters’ lives through changes in color. Another film from the 1990s follows the dramatic experience of a man with scissor hands who comes down to a town to live with ordinary folks.
(A) At first, he is welcomed by the people in town, but as he becomes misunderstood and disliked, the film’s colors gradually become darker. Eventually, he returns to his castle, but he fills his garden with green grass and beautiful, blooming flowers.
(B) Moreover, ice powder from his ice sculpture blows in the wind like snow. With such changes, the director shows the audience that his life has become much happier.
(C) He always wears black, and the castle where he used to live was a gray and gloomy place. However, in the town where he came to live with his lover, each house is painted differently, and the people wear colorful clothes.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 영화감독들은 색상의 변화를 통해 캐릭터들의 삶의 변화를 포착해낸다는 설명과 함께 가위손을 가진 한 남자가 평범한 사람들과 함께 살기 위해 마을로 내려오는 1990년대의 영화를 사례로 언급하는 주어진 글 다음에, 가위손을 가진 남자를 He로 가리켜, 그는 항상 검은 옷을 입고 있고 예전에 살던 성은 회색빛의 우울한 장소였으나, 그가 살기 위해 온 마을은 집마다 다른 색으로 색칠되어 있고 사람들이 다채로운 옷을 입고 있다는 대조적 분위기를 설명한 (C), At first(처음에)를 사용해 그가 처음 마을에 왔을 때는 환영받았음을 언급한 뒤, 이후 오해와 미움을 받으면서 영화의 색깔이 점점 더 어두워지고 결국 성으로 다시 돌아와 자신의 정원을 초록빛 풀과 아름답고 활짝 핀 꽃들로 채운다는 내용의 (A), Moreover(또한)를 사용해 얼음 조각상에서 나오는 얼음 가루는 눈처럼 바람에 날린다는 변화된 성의 모습을 추가 설명하며, 이러한 변화를 통해 감독이 관객들에게 그의 삶이 더 행복해졌음을 보여준다고 마무리하는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Colors are an important aspect of films. They look visually attractive and can be used to ⓐconveying various emotions and messages to the audience. Film directors carefully select colors like bright yellow to bring a sense of hope, calm blue for peace, and intense red for violence. These color choices are not random; they are intentionally made ⓑto impact your experience while you watch the film, even if you don’t consciously notice them. Below ⓒis several outstanding examples of how skillfully film directors can use color to add richness to the story and evoke specific emotions from the audience.
Like the saying “A picture is worth a thousand words,” colors get a film’s message across more strongly than words ⓓare. A good example is the red coat in a movie about the true story of a German businessman who saved thousands of Jews from the Nazis during World War II. While the movie was mostly in black and white, the director chose one particular thing to add color to. It was the red coat of a single lost girl, alone in a crowd of frightened Jews. As such, it was the strong contrast of colors ⓔthat enabled the director to powerfully symbolize the brutality of the Nazis. The young girl represents innocence while also representinging the violence of the Nazis. So, what happened to this young girl? The movie never tells us for sure, but later in the film we see a dead girl in a red coat ⓕbeing loaded into a cart.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
answer:
(1) ⓐ → convey
(2) ⓒ → are
(3) ⓓ → do 또는 are 삭제
solution:
ⓐ Colors를 가리키는 주어 They가 메시지를 전달하는 데 사용될 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 하므로, ‘~하는 데 사용되다’라는 뜻의 ‘be used+to부정사(구)’를 이루도록 동명사 conveying을 동사원형 convey로 고친다. 참고로, ‘be used to+동명사(구)’는 ‘~하는 것에 익숙하다, ~하는 것이 당연하다고 여기다’라는 뜻으로 쓰인다.
ⓒ 문두에 온 부사 Below에 의한 도치로 주어 앞에 be동사가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 이어진 주어 several outstanding examples가 복수명사구이므로, 수일치를 위해 단수 동사 is를 복수 동사 are로 고친다.
ⓓ ‘비교급+than ~’ 구문에서 접속사로 쓰인 than이 이끄는 비교절의 동사 자리로, 앞 절(colors get a film’s message across more strongly)에 쓰인 일반동사를 포함한 구동사 ‘get ~ across(~을 이해시키다)’에 상응하는 대동사가 와야 하므로, are를 do로 고치거나, 비교구문에서 중복되는 부분은 대용형으로 대체되거나 흔히 생략될 수 있으므로 are를 삭제한다.)
*원래 지문에는 do가 생략되어 있음
오답
ⓔ it was 뒤에 온 명사구 the strong contrast of colors가 이어지는 동사 enabled의 주어에 해당하므로, 주어를 강조하기 위해 쓰인 ‘it ~ that’ 강조 구문을 이루는 that은 알맞다.

영화감독들이 색을 얼마나 능숙하게 사용하여 이야기에 풍성함을 더하고 관객에게 특정한 감정을 불러일으킬 수 있는지에 대한 뛰어난 예들이 있다고 했으므로, ② ‘감독들은 색상을 사용하여 자신들의 이야기를 더욱 풍부하게 만들고 관객에게 특정한 감정을 불러일으킬 수 있다.’는 일치 내용이다.
한 독일 사업가의 실제 이야기를 다룬 한 영화의 대부분은 흑백으로 되어 있었지만, 감독은 색을 더할 특정한 한 가지로 한 소녀의 붉은 외투를 선택했다고 했으므로, ③ ‘한 독일 사업가에 관한 영화는 붉은 외투가 두드러진 채로 대체로 흑백으로 표현되었다.’는 일치 내용이다.
*두 번째 단락 위에 소제목 ‘Colors Convey a Film’s Message with Intensity‘ 생략되었음
오답
① 색상의 정서적 의미는 영화감독들이 계획하지 않은 우연한 결과이다. (→영화감독들의 색상 선택은 무작위가 아니라 의도적으로 이루어진다.)
④ 두드러진 색상 대비를 통해 감독은 나치의 잔혹성에 대한 묘사를 완화했다. (→ 감독이 나치의 잔혹성을 강력하게 상징할 수 있게 해준 것은 바로 강렬한 색상의 대비였다.)
⑤ 영화 후반부에서 나치가 붉은 외투를 입은 소녀에게 한 일이 명확해진다. (→영화는 어린 소녀에게 무슨 일이 있었는지 확실히 알려주지 않고, 붉은 외투를 입은 죽은 소녀가 수레에 실리고 있는 장면만을 보여준다.)

G: Yes! René Magritte's paintings are so unique.

ⓐ I think it symbolizes peace and harmony within a family. It makes me feel good.
ⓑ It really does! But I focused on the meaning of the bird.
ⓒ Yes, I find it fascinating. I love the way the bird's body is bright blue and covered in clouds. The contrast in brightness with the dark ocean creates a mysterious atmosphere.
ⓓ Why is that?
G: That's an interesting point of view! Maybe the dark ocean represents life's challenges, then.
B: Yes, possibly. The more we discuss the painting, the more interesting it gets!
G: I agree!

다음 주어진 대화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 르네의 그림 ‘The Great Family’가 인상적이지 않은지 묻는 소년의 질문에 Katherine이 동의하며 그림이 매력적이라고 말하고, 밝은 새와 어두운 바다의 대비에 대한 자신의 의견을 말하는 ⓒ, 이에 소년이 Katherine의 의견에 동의하며 자신은 새의 의미에 주목했다고 말하는 ⓑ, 그러자 Katherine이 소년에게 왜 새의 의미에 주목했는지 묻는 ⓓ, Katherine의 질문에 소년이 새가 가족 간의 평화와 화합을 상징하며 자신에게 좋은 기분을 느끼게 한다고 답하는 ⓐ로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

W: Welcome to the world of shadow art! Shadow art is a unique form of art that uses light and shadow to create visual effects. Let’s start with Vincent Bal’s works of art. This artist transforms everyday items into amazing creations with his imagination. For example, the shadow of a leftover apple becomes an angry owl. And a bottle is turned into a swimming pool. Another amazing shadow artist is Rashad Alakbarov. By projecting light upon materials of different shapes and colors, he creates incredible shadow images of beaches, cities, and people. Take a look at these bottles. What kind of shadow will appear when we shine light on them? A man’s face! These examples show how ordinary objects can become incredible works of art with some help from the artists’ imagination.

Grandma Moses
When it seems too late
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, ⓐsold homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren.
(A) Then, one day in 1939, an art collector ⓑnaming Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which ⓒwas all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history.
(B) She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention.
(C) The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, ⓓallowed people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life.
The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late ⓔaccomplish our dreams.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Many works of art bring us happiness or comfort by their existence alone. Take, for example, the work of Arthur Elsley. His paintings of children and their pets have made people smile for over a century. The work of another artist, Mark Rothko, might be more recognizable. The solid colors in his paintings bring to mind the diversity of human emotions, helping those who view them feel a sense of warmth and comfort.
Artwork, however, is more deeply appreciated with a deeper understanding of the artist and the experiences that helped produce it. We are going to explore the lives of three artists whose art has inspired people from different cultures and generations. As their life experiences became the inspiration for their art, understanding the stories behind their work will not only help us better appreciate their work but also inspire us.

solution: 정답은 deeper, understanding, inspiration 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Lee Jungseop
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. body:
Alfonse Mucha
Alfonse Mucha (1860-1939) was one of the first Art Nouveau artists, which led to this form of art being referred to as the “Mucha Style.” His style became famous later on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, did not happen overnight.
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

body:
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.

How Art Exhibitions Support Unknown Artists
Late in Life but Not Too Late to Succeed

Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. (A)Grandma Moses의 이야기는 우리의 꿈을 이루는 데 결코 너무 늦은 때란 없다는 것을 상기시켜 준다.

a reminder, never, accomplish, too, the story

body:
Alfonse Mucha
Alfonse Mucha (1860-1939) was one of the first Art Nouveau artists, which led to this form of art being referred to as the “Mucha Style.” His style became famous (A)[early / later] on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, did not happen overnight.
As a younger artist, Mucha was (B)[rejected / accepted] when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His (C)[big break / major setback] came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: early / rejected / big break
later / rejected / big break
later / accepted / major setback
early / accepted / big break
later / rejected / major setback
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 Mucha의 명성이 하룻밤 사이에 이루어진 것이 아니었다고 했고, 마지막 단락에서도 Mucha는 자신의 경력을 시작했을 때 즉각적인 성공을 거두지는 못했다고 했으므로 그의 양식은 생애 후반에 유명해졌다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 later(후반에)가 적절하다.
(B) 바로 뒤에서 그러나 Mucha는 포기하지 않았다고 했으므로 지역 미술 학교에 지원했다가 거절당했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 rejected(거절당한)가 적절하다.
(C) 연극 ‘Gismonda’의 포스터를 그릴 기회를 얻었고 이로 인해 Mucha는 아르누보 양식 발전의 주요 인물로 알려지게 되었다고 했으므로 큰 기회가 찾아왔다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 big break(큰 기회)가 적절하다.

body:
When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there?” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see.” Long before others, this person recognized that not only ⓐthe ocean is full of life, but that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.
Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and ⓑobserving the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is ⓒdived in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
At 17, she took her first deep dive, ⓓdescended 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle was thrilled ⓔto observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become (A)______.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a skilled diver and instructor
a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation
a researcher specializing in predicting changes in ocean currents
a leading scientist devoted to designing advanced diving equipment
an environmentalist who led efforts to protect coastal waters from illegal activities
solution: Sylvia Earle은 다른 사람들보다 훨씬 먼저 바다의 매력을 알아보고 바다가 생명으로 가득할 뿐 아니라 보호해야 할 대상이라는 사실을 깨달은 전설적인 해양 생물학자로서, 어린 시절 다이빙의 짜릿함을 경험하면서 스쿠버 장비를 사용한 최초의 해양 과학자 중 한 명이 되었다고 했으므로, 그녀의 타고난 모험심과 호기심이 학문적 여정을 이끌었다는 내용 뒤에 해양을 탐구하고 보호하는 데 있어 선두적인 인물이 되었다는 결과가 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❷ ‘해양 탐험과 보전의 선구자’가 알맞다.

body:
Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge just couldn’t cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater,” she said. (A)이듬해, 그녀는 전부 여성으로 구성된 텍타이트 II 프로젝트를 이끌도록 선정되어, 다른 해양학자 네 명과 함께 해저 15미터에서 생활하며 2주를 보냈다. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes.
Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts’ historic moon landing.

the ocean’s surface, lead, choose, live, two weeks, beneath

answer: The following year, having been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers.

body:
For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its (A)[preservation / development]. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species. There are (B)[more / less] whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the (C)[importance / danger] of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.”
With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and preserve the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: preservation more danger
development less danger
preservation less importance
preservation more importance
development more importance
solution:
(A) Earle이 해양학자이자 작가, 강연가로서 사람들이 해양의 중요성을 인식하도록 지속적으로 영감을 주고 있다는 설명이 이어지므로, 미션 블루가 바다에 대한 열정 및 바다 보존에 대한 헌신을 바탕으로 하는 운동이라는 흐름이 되는 preservation(보존)이 알맞다.
(B) 멸종 위기에 처한 해양 생물을 보호할 희망이 있다는 내용 뒤에 이어져 있으며, 뒤에 대부분의 국가가 고래와 거북이를 보호하고 있다는 이유를 언급하므로, 자신이 어렸을 때보다 오늘날 더 많은 고래와 거북이가 있다는 흐름이 되는 more(더 많은)가 알맞다.
(C) 바다가 중요하지 않다고 생각한다면 바다가 없는 지구를 상상해 보라고 하며, 바다가 없으면 생명도 없다는 그녀의 말이 인용되므로, 이를 통해 그녀가 바다의 중요성을 상기시켜준다는 흐름이 되는 importance(중요성)가 알맞다.

body:
In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

윗글을 읽고 다음 질문에 대한 답을 아래와 같이 쓸 때 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것)
(1) What historic achievement did Sylvia Earle accomplish in 1979?
→ She went down ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ without being connected to anything for ______ ______.
(2) What was the purpose of her planting a flag on the seafloor while diving?
→ It was to show that ______ ______ is just as important as ______ ______.
answer:
(1) She went down 381 meters and walked on the ocean floor without being connected to anything for two hours.
(2) It was to show that ocean exploration is just as important as space exploration.

Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, increasing its temperature and acidity. (A)______, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. ⓐCovered 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes ⓑhave found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon ⓒis commonly knowing as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide ⓓthat has dissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming.
(B)______, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet saving function ⓔdepends on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and aid in the planet’s decarbonization. Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, rethinking industrial fishing practices, restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and ⓕreduce pollution entering the sea. By prioritizing ocean health, we can unlock its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)

solution:
(A) 기후 변화가 바다의 온도와 산성도를 증가시키며 해양에 심각한 피해를 입히고 있다는 문제점 뒤에 최근의 과학적 통찰에 따르면 바다가 이러한 글로벌 위기의 잠재적 해결책일 수 있다는 대조적 내용이 이어지므로, 역접을 나타내는 However(하지만) 또는 Nonetheless(그럼에도 불구하고)가 알맞다.
(B) 해양은 육지보다 16배 많은 탄소를 보유하고 있으며, 해양에 저장된 블루카본이 지구 온난화를 방지한다는 순기능에 대한 설명 뒤에, 지구 보호 기능을 수행하는 해양의 능력은 해양의 건강에 달려 있다는 문제를 언급하므로, '그럼에도 불구하고‘라는 뜻으로 역접을 나타내는 Nevertheless 또는 Nonetheless가 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개

solution:
ⓐ Covered → Covering
(콤마(,) 뒤에 완전한 절(the ocean plays ~ the atmosphere)이 접속사 없이 이어지므로, 콤마(,) 앞은 주절 앞에 쓰여 흐름상 주절 주어를 부연 설명하는 분사구문의 형태가 되어야 한다. 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상의 주어 the ocean이 ‘차지하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 70% of Earth가 이어지므로, Covered를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Covering으로 고친다.)
ⓑ have found → have been found
(부사구 For thousands of years와 함께 과거부터 현재까지 수천 년 동안 ‘밝혀져 왔다’는 의미를 나타내기 위해 핵심주어인 복수명사구 marine ecosystems에 수일치한 복수 조동사(have)를 사용해 현재완료가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주어가 ‘밝혀진’ 대상이고, 뒤에 수동 표현인 ‘be found+to부정사(~라는 것이 밝혀지다)’의 to부정사가 이어져 있으므로, 현재완료 능동태(have[has]+p.p.)가 아닌 현재완료 수동태(have[has] +been+p.p.)를 사용해 have found를 have been found 로 고친다.)
ⓒ is commonly knowing → is commonly known
(주어 This captured carbon이 단수명사구이므로 단수동사로 수일치하는 것과 be동사와 분사 사이에 부사 commonly가 위치한 것은 모두 알맞으나, 주어가 “blue carbon”으로 ‘알려진’ 대상이며, 뒤에 ‘know ~ as …(~을 …로 알다)’의 목적어 없이 전치사 as와 명사구 “blue carbon”이 바로 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘~ be known as …(~가 …로 알려지다)’를 사용해 is commonly knowing을 is commonly known으로 고친다.)
ⓕ reduce → reducing
(타동사 include(~을 포함하다)의 목적어 자리에 쓰인 동명사 protecting, rethinking, restoring과 ’A, B, C and D’ 구조로 병렬 연결되며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사 pollution이 있으므로, reduce를 능동형 동명사 reducing으로 고친다.)

Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean.
(A) At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater.
(B) Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
(C) As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

body:
It appears that viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated ⓐto kill 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, affecting almost every aspect of human life worldwide.
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses ⓑentering human bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests ⓒpreventing animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, ⓓmeant more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern ⓔwhich pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지 못한 것은?
choices: ⓐ to kill → to have killed
ⓑ entering → to enter
ⓒ preventing → prevented
ⓓ meant → meaning
ⓔ which → what
solution:
ⓔ which → that (추상명사 concern(걱정, 우려)의 구체적 내용을 나타내는 완전한 절(pandemics may increase in the future)을 연결하고 있으므로, which를 what이 아닌 동격 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘~한 것으로 추정되다’라는 뜻의 ‘be estimated+to부정사(구)’에서 추정되는 시점이 현재이므로 현재시제 is estimated가 쓰였으나 사람들이 사망한 것은 과거의 일이며, to부정사(구)의 내용이 본동사의 시제보다 이전 상황이면 완료부정사(to have p.p.)를 사용하므로, to kill을 to have killed로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …하게 하다)’의 5형식에서 allow의 목적격보어로 to부정사(구)가 쓰이므로 entering을 to enter로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓒ 주어 natural barriers such as mountains and forests에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 흐름상 과거의 일을 나타내야 하고, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 animal viruses가 있으므로, preventing을 과거시제 능동태인 prevented로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓓ 앞의 완전한 절(These changes ~ wild animals)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사구가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절을 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 ‘의미하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 완전한 절 형태의 명사절이 이어져 있으므로, meant를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 meaning으로 고친 것은 알맞다.

body:
(A)덜 일반적으로 알려진 것은 바이러스들이 지구상의 많은 생명체를 지탱하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 것이다. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses that sustain us and the planet, instead of just those that harm us. Therefore, scientists have much more to learn about viruses than they currently know. What they do know is that viruses act as the primary regulators of bacterial and insect populations.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, (B)they steal the reproductive functions of other organisms to multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses go on to infect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses control the excessive growth of certain bacteria.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.

• 관계대명사 what을 사용할 것
• 명사절 접속사 that을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 18단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
play, know, support, crucial, on Earth, life, roles, much of, less commonly
→ ______
answer: What is less commonly known is that viruses play crucial roles in supporting much of life on Earth.
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 관계대명사 what을 사용하여, ‘~한 것은 바로 …이다’라는 뜻으로 보어를 강조하는 ‘What절+be동사 ~’ 형태로 쓴다.
• What은 보통 단수 취급하므로 관계사절의 동사 자리에 단수동사인 is를 쓴 뒤, 주어 역할을 하는 What이 ‘덜 알려진’ 대상이므로, less commonly 뒤에 know를 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 known으로 변형한다.
• What절 주어는 보통 단수 취급하므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is를 쓰고, 이어지는 보어절에 <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사를 사용해 ‘that+완전한 절’ 형태의 명사절을 쓴다.
• ‘~하는 데 있어 …한 역할을 하다’라는 뜻의 ‘play … roles in+동명사’를 사용한다.

The greater significance of viruses ⓐinfected bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth ⓑis produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses ⓒdid not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, (A)바이러스들이 없다면, 산소의 부족이 인류가 생존하는 것을 불가능하게 만들 것이다.
Insect species populations are also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses that infect those insects also increase, ⓓreduced their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects ⓔflourish. Considering the chain of food in nature, it would not be difficult ⓕto assume that viruses fulfill important functions in regulating other species. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ infected →infecting (전치사 of의 목적어인 명사 viruses를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사 자리이며, 수식받는 명사가 ‘감염시키는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사 bacteria가 있으므로, infected를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 infecting으로 고친다.)
ⓓ reduced → reducing (완전한 절(the viruses ~ increase) 뒤에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이끄는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 ‘줄이는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 their numbers가 있으므로, reduce를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 reducing으로 고친다.)
ⓔ flourish → to flourish (앞에 to부정사의 의미상 주어로 쓰이는 ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 for other types of insects가 있으며, 흐름상 명사 room을 ‘다른 종류의 곤충들이 번성할 (여지)’라는 뜻으로 수식하는 형용사구를 이루어야 하므로, 동사 flourish를 to부정사인 to flourish로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 주절에 조동사 과거형 would와 동사원형 be가 쓰였으며, 주절과 조건절이 모두 현재 사실의 반대를 가정해야 하므로, ‘If+S+과거동사 ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …(만약 ~한다면, …할 텐데[…할 것이다])’ 형태의 가정법 과거를 사용해 If절에 과거형 조동사 did와 부정어 not이 쓰여 동사구 infect and kill의 부정형을 이룬 것은 알맞다.

The greater significance of viruses ⓐinfected bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth ⓑis produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses ⓒdid not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, (A)바이러스들이 없다면, 산소의 부족이 인류가 생존하는 것을 불가능하게 만들 것이다.

We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• without으로 시작하여 쓰고, 가정법을 사용할 것
• 가목적어 it을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 14단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
will, survive, humans, impossible, the lack
→ ______
answer: without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans to survive
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 without으로 시작하고 가정법을 사용해야 하며, 내용상 현재의 사실을 가정해야 하므로, ‘without+명사(구), 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 ~(…가 없다면, ~할 텐데[~할 것이다])’ 형태의 가정법 과거를 사용한다.
• ‘~의 부족’이라는 뜻의 ’the lack of ~’를 사용하여 주어 the lack of oxygen을 쓰고, will을 과거형 would로 변형한 뒤 동사원형 make를 쓴다.
• <조건>에 따라 가목적어 it을 사용하고 진목적어 자리에는 to부정사(구)를 쓰되, 주절 주어와 to부정사의 의미상 주어가 다르므로 ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 의미상 주어를 to부정사(구) 앞에 위치시켜 ‘make+가목적어(it)+목적격보어+(형용사)+for+목적격+진목적어(to부정사(구))(~가 …하는 것을 -하게 만들다)’ 형태로 쓴다.

body:
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution (A)[is / are] ⓐtheir role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ that helps the fetus (B)[grow / growing] securely inside ⓑits mother’s body. ⓒIt facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while protecting the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, making ⓓthem vulnerable to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to carry their young inside ⓔtheir bodies safely from one location to another. Viruses that infected our remote ancestors more than 130 million years ago have been reported (C)[to serve / to have served] a key function in the development of this vital organ.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: is / grow / to serve
is / grow / to have served
are / grow / to have served
are / growing / to serve
is / growing / to have served
solution:
(A) 주어 One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution의 핵심단어가 단수명사 example이므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 알맞다.
(B) ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식 구문에서 준사역동사 help의 목적격보어로 to부정사나 동사원형이 쓰이므로, 동사원형 grow가 알맞다.
(C) ‘be reported+to부정사(~한 것으로 보고되다, ~라고 한다)’의 to부정사가 올 자리이며, 주어 Viruses가 ‘역할을 했던’ 것이 보고된 상태(have been reported)인 현재시점보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로, 완료부정사(to have p.p.)인 to have served가 알맞다.

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
But they were wrong. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What did the costume worn by doctors treating the plague look like?
Why did doctors treating the plague use sticks?
What beliefs did doctors in the 1600s have about the cause of the plague?
What medicines did doctors in the 1600s give to patients with the plague?
What contributions has modern medicine made to combating infectious diseases?
solution:
흑사병이 발병했던 1600년대 당시 의사들이 전염을 막기 위해 허브를 가득 채운 마스크를 착용했고 허브가 공기를 걸러내고 병에 걸리지 않도록 보호해 주기를 바랐다고 했으나, 환자들을 치료하기 위해 사용했던 약에 관련해 언급된 바가 없으므로, ④ ‘1600년대의 의사들은 흑사병에 걸린 환자들에게 어떤 약을 투여했는가?’에는 답할 수 없다.
오답
① 흑사병을 치료한 의사들이 입은 의상은 어떤 모습이었는가? (→광택이 나는 긴 코트와 하나로 연결된 바지와 부츠로 이루어졌으며, 셔츠가 끝까지 채워졌고 그들은 염소 가죽으로 만든 모자와 장갑을 착용했다.)
② 흑사병을 치료한 의사들은 왜 막대기를 사용했는가? (→그들은 아픈 사람들을 만지거나 밀치기 위해 막대기를 사용했다.)
③ 1600년대의 의사들은 흑사병의 원인에 대해 어떤 믿음을 가지고 있었는가? (→그들은 흑사병이 몸의 내부 균형을 깨뜨릴 수 있는 나쁜 공기 때문에 발생한다고 생각했다.)
⑤ 현대 의학은 전염병을 퇴치하는 데 있어 어떤 기여를 했는가? (→현대 의학은 우리가 박테리아와 바이러스를 신속하게 탐지하고 대응할 수 있게 해 주었다.)

What is less commonly known is that viruses play crucial roles in supporting much of life on Earth. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses that sustain us and the planet, instead of just those that harm us. Therefore, scientists have much more to learn about viruses than they currently know. What they do know is that viruses act as the primary regulators of bacterial and insect populations.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, they steal the reproductive functions of other organisms to multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses go on to infect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses ______ of certain bacteria.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

support the survival
spread through the cells
control the excessive growth

As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing them in the battle against diseases are arising. Of notable interest are the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment. Genes can be compared to instruction guides that govern how our bodies function. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, which can lead to health problems. Gene therapy steps in to fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering corrected genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, enabling them to function properly. In this process, specially modified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, ______.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: it may cause new health problems
it will affect the body's normal biological functions
it is likely to spread genetic changes to other cells
it can potentially help the body fight off certain diseases
it could increase the risk of unexpected immune reactions
solution:
유전자 치료는 유전적 장애를 가지고 태어난 환자의 세포에 수정된 유전적 지침을 전달하여 세포가 제대로 기능하게 하는 것을 핵심으로 하며, 이 과정에서 특수하게 변형된 바이러스가 유전적 지시를 전달하는 매개체 중 하나로 사용된다고 했으므로, 환자의 세포가 정상적으로 기능하게 될 경우, 해당 유전적 질병을 치료하는 데 도움이 될 수 있을 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ④ ‘그것은 신체가 특정 질병을 퇴치하는 데 잠재적으로 도움이 될 수 있다’가 알맞다.

① 그것은 새로운 건강 문제를 야기할지도 모른다
② 그것은 신체의 정상적인 생물학적 기능에 영향을 미칠 것이다
③ 그것은 유전적 변화를 다른 세포로 확산시킬 가능성이 높다

body:
Imagine you are at a restaurant with a menu ⓐthat has hundreds of items on it. You feel (A)excited at first, but it quickly becomes overwhelming. You do not know what ⓑto choose. Your choice ⓒwould be much (B)easier if you could pick between beef steak and mushroom spaghetti. This simple example (C)illustrates “the paradox of choice.” Having too many choices actually ⓓmake it harder to make a decision. When we have (D)numerous options, we feel like we have to compare them all, and we can never be sure which would be the best choice. Plus, ⓔwhichever we choose may leave us (E)satisfied because we have missed out on so many other options. The paradox of choice can affect our decisions in all areas of our lives, from choosing the color of our socks to deciding on a major.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ make → makes (문장의 동사 자리로, 주어가 동명사구 Having ~ choices이며, 동명사구 주어는 단수 취급하므로 make를 단수동사 makes로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ know의 목적어 자리로, ‘의문사+to부정사’ 형태의 명사구를 이루도록 의문사 what 뒤에 쓰인 to부정사 to choose는 적절하다.
ⓒ if절에 과거시제(could pick)가 쓰여 앞에서 현재 상상하고 있는 상황(수백 개의 항목이 있는 메뉴를 보는 상황)과 반대로 선택지가 소고기 스테이크와 버섯 스파게티라는 2개인 상황을 가정하고 있으므로 가정법 과거(주어+과거형 조동사+동사원형 ~ if+S+과거형 동사 ...)를 이루도록 주절에 과거형 조동사 would와 동사원형 be가 쓰인 것은 적절하다.

We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue. However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time. The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work.

The First-Past-The-Post Method
The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters (A)[give / are given] several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. Neither the second nor third preference (B)[matter / matters] at all, so they are ⓐ[ignored / considered]. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world.
The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
The FPTP method is ⓑ[complicated / uncomplicated] and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is ⓒ[possible / impossible] to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which (C)[equaling / equaled] 40% of the total votes.

(A) (B) (C)
choices: give / matters / equaled
are given / matters / equaled
are given / matters / equaling
give / matter / equaled

solution:
(A) 맥락상 주어인 Voters(투표자들)가 여러 선택지를 ‘받는’ 대상이므로, ‘give+A(간접목적어)+B(직접목적어)’(A에게 B를 주다)의 4형식에서 A가 주어 자리로 나가 수동태로 전환된 ‘A be given B’(A에게 B가 주어지다)가 되어야 한다. 따라서 수동태(be+p.p.)인 are given이 알맞다.
(B) 상관접속사 ‘neither A nor B’(A도 B도 아닌)가 주어 자리에 올 때 동사는 B에 수를 일치시키므로, 단수 주어 third preference에 일치한 단수동사 matters가 알맞다.
(C) which는 콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끄는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로, 관계사절 안에 동사가 없으므로 which에 대한 동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 동사로 쓰일 수 있는 과거형 동사 equaled가 알맞다.

The Alternative Vote Method
Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. (A)어떤 선택지가 1차 집계에서 승리하기 위해서는, 1지망 표의 50% 이상을 얻어야 한다. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required.
Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner.
Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. (B)It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.

body:
The First-Past-The-Post Method
The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters are given several options, and whichever ⓐgetting the most first-preference votes wins. ⓑNeither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. This method ⓒis commonly used in political elections around the world.
The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to ⓓunderstand it, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible ⓔto win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was ⓕto hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, ⓖthat equaled 40% of the total votes.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ getting → gets (동사 wins 앞의 주어 자리로, 복합관계대명사 whichever가 주어부인 명사절을 이루도록 관계사절 내에서 동사가 와야 한다. 뒤에 동사가 이어지지 않고, whichever가 가장 많은 1지망 표를 얻은 주체로 주어 역할을 하므로 이에 이어진 동사가 되도록 getting을 3인칭 현재 능동태 gets로 고친다.)
ⓓ understand it → understand (주어인 The FPTP method가 understand의 의미상 목적어이므로 understand it을 중복되는 목적어 it을 삭제한 understand로 고친다.)
ⓖ that → which (콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(equaled ~ votes)을 이끌어야 하므로 계속적 용법으로 쓰일 수 없는 that을 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ ‘A도 B도 아닌’은 상관접속사 ‘neither A nor B’로 나타내며, A와 B에는 서로 대등한 어구가 연결되어야 한다. 따라서 두 개의 명사구 the second (preference)와 third preference가 연결된 Neither the second nor third preference는 알맞다.
ⓕ be동사 was의 보어 자리이며 뒤에 목적어 a charity concert를 취해야 하므로 명사적 용법으로 쓰인 능동형 to부정사 to hold는 적절하다.

body:
The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
(A) They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
(B) Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9.
(C) Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB.
다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 콩도르세 방식으로 표를 집계할 때, 이 경우에는, A와 B, B와 C, A와 C의 고려해야 할 세 쌍이 있었다는 주어진 글에 이어, 이 방식을 통해 학생 자치회는 구성원들이 A:B 비교에 대해서 11대 9로 11명이 ABC, ACB, 또는 CAB에 투표하여 선택지 B보다 선택지 A를 선호한다는 사실을 발견했다는 (C), Meanwhile(한편)을 써서 A:B 비교에서 9명은 BAC, BCA, 또는 CBA에 투표함으로써 A보다 B를 선호했다는 내용과 흥미로운 점으로 the same count를 써서 앞서 언급된 집계 수와 같이 동일하게 11대 9로 투표자들은 선택지 C보다 선택지 B를 선호했다는 B:C를 비교하는 내용의 (B), (B)의 the voters(투표자들)를 They(그들)로 지칭하여 also(또한)를 써서 그들(=투표자들)은 11대 9로 선택지 C보다 선택지 A를 선호했다는 A:C를 비교하는 내용과 이 비교 과정에 의해 미술 전시회인 선택지 A가 승자로 간주되는 결과가 제시된 (A)의 순서로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
The Alternative Vote Method
Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required.
Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner.
Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.
While the Alternative Vote method eliminates the option with the fewest first-preference votes and (A)______ its votes based on second preferences when no option secures a majority, this system has a drawback in that second-preference votes can sometimes (B)______ the final outcome compared to first-preference choices.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: reallocates / minimize
reassigns / overpower
discards / weaken
cancels / dictate
retains / equalize

better decisions, help, make, design, inefficient, a society, difficult, all of these efforts
→ ______
answer: All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society.
solution:

• <조건>에 따라 상관접속사 ‘not A, but B’(A가 아니고 B)와 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 사용하여 ‘~ 만들기 위한 것이 아니라 ... 돕기 위해’에 해당하는 부분을 영작한다. 상관접속사는 A와 B에 같은 문법 요소가 오므로 to부정사끼리 연결되도록 ‘not to부정사, but to부정사’ 형태로 영작한다. not 뒤에 to make를 연결하고 make의 5형식(make+목적어+목적격 보어(형용사))을 사용하여 목적어 decision-making과 목적격 보어 difficult and inefficient를 쓴다.

body:
W: Every day, the world throws away billions and billions of plastic bottles. That's a problem. Of course, the real solution is to use less plastic. But it's cool that, even while we work to reduce plastic, some companies are turning trash into stuff we actually like. Drink it. Drop it in the bin. Take it to a recycling factory. Chop it up. Weave it. Wear it. Wash it. Wear it again. Wash it again. Seems like a great solution, right? But there's also a little problem that contributes to one big mess. Every time we wash synthetic fabrics, whether they are made from recycled bottles or brand-new materials, super tiny pieces of plastic, called microfibers, wash off and flow down the drain, up to hundreds of thousands each wash. The older our clothes get, the worse the problem can become! Yikes! These fibers are so tiny that water treatment plants don't catch them all. So they end up in rivers, lakes, and even the ocean.
위 담화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Although turning trash into useful products is helpful, the real solution is to use less plastic.
We as individuals are actively turning plastic bottles into new things to solve the plastic problem.
Brand-new clothes wash off more microfibers in the wash than old clothes.
Making clothes from recycled bottles involves many steps, such as chopping, weaving, and washing.
Water treatment plants cannot catch all of the tiny plastic fibers from our laundry.
solution:
쓰레기를 우리가 좋아할 만한 물건으로 바꾸고 있는 것은 기업들이라고 했으므로 ② ‘우리 개인들은 플라스틱 문제를 해결하기 위해 플라스틱병을 새로운 물건으로 적극적으로 바꾸고 있다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
옷이 오래될수록 미세섬유가 씻겨 나와 하수구로 흘러가는 문제가 더 심각해진다고 했으므로 ③ ’새 옷은 세탁할 때 오래된 옷보다 더 많은 미세섬유를 씻어 내보낸다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 쓰레기를 유용한 제품으로 바꾸는 것이 도움이 되기는 하지만, 진정한 해결책은 플라스틱을 덜 사용하는 것이다.
④ 재활용된 병으로 옷을 만드는 것은 자르고, 짜고, 씻는 것과 같은 많은 단계를 포함한다.

Every time we wash synthetic fabrics, whether they are made from recycled bottles or brand-new materials, super tiny pieces of plastic, called microfibers, wash off and flow down the drain, up to hundreds of thousands each wash. The older our clothes get, the worse the problem can become! Yikes! These fibers are so tiny that water treatment plants don't catch them all. So they end up in rivers, lakes, and even the ocean.

We live surrounded by cloth. (A) We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. (B) Wearing clothes is a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. (C) Textiles ─ artificial and natural ─ have shaped and changed the world we live in. (D) Modern clothing companies heavily rely on digital marketing strategies and social media influencers to boost sales. (E) The history of textiles is almost as old as human civilization, and as time has passed, it has been more and more enriched. Exploring how textiles have changed the world helps us understand how human civilization has evolved.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 인간의 삶과 문명에서 직물이 지닌 중요성과 직물의 역사에 대해 설명하는 글로, 직물은 인간의 삶과 함께해 왔으며, 인간 문명의 발전에도 영향을 미쳤으며, 따라서 직물의 역사를 살펴보는 것은 인간 문명의 발전을 이해하는 데 도움이 된다는 것이 글의 핵심 내용이다. (A)에서는 옷이 인간의 삶에서 태어날 때부터 죽을 때까지 함께한다는 점을, (B)에서는 옷을 입는 것은 인간의 특징이며 대부분의 인간 사회에서 옷을 사용한다는 점을, (C)에서는 직물이 우리가 사는 세계를 형성하고 변화시켰다는 점을, (E)에서는 직물의 역사가 인류 문명만큼 오래되었으며, 직물의 변화를 통해 인간 문명의 발전을 이해할 수 있다는 점을 설명하므로 글의 핵심 내용과 자연스럽게 연결된다. 그러나 (D) ‘현대의 의류 회사들은 판매를 늘리기 위해 디지털 마케팅 전략과 소셜 미디어 인플루언서들에게 크게 의존한다.‘는 직물의 역사와 인간 문명의 발전이라는 흐름에서 벗어나므로, (D)는 글의 흐름과 관계없다.
