body:
What to Wear for Space Travel
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest challenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─ a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. ⓐ모두가 놀랍게도, 아폴로 우주복 계약을 따낸 업체는 다른 업체만큼 크지도 않은 데다 여성 속옷 제품군 덕분에 명성을 얻은 업체였다. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 관계대명사 which를 사용할 것
• 원급 비교를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
⦁(1)은 3단어, (2)는 16단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
the contract, win, for, surprise, everyone
the others, the company, the Apollo suits, to
(1)______, (2)______ and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear.
answer:
(1) To everyone’s surprise
(2) the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others
solution:
(1) ‘모두가 놀랍게도’를 뜻하는 ‘to one's+감정명사‘의 구조가 되도록, 전치사 to, ‘모두’의 소유격 everyone’s, ‘놀람’을 뜻하는 감정 명사 surprise를 차례대로 쓴다.
(2) • 주어 the company를 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계대명사 which를 쓰고, ‘win the contract(계약을 따내다)’를 과거형 won the contract로 변형하여 쓴다. the contract를 수식하는 전치사구 for the Apollo suits를 이어 쓴다.
• 단수주어 the company에 수일치한 be동사의 과거형 was의 부정형 wasn’t를 쓰고, ‘~만큼 크지 않은’을 뜻하도록 원급 비교를 사용하여 as big as를 쓴다. 8개의 업체들 중 한 회사를 제외한 나머지 모든 업체를 가리키는 대명사 the others를 이어 쓴다.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) A space suit to withstand extreme conditions was needed for the first moon mission. (T/F)

solution:

body:
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were ⓐset. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. It was a full body swimsuit ⓑdesigned with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to (A)[increase / reduce] buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers ⓒwear this type of suit.
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to (B)[prohibit / permit] all full body swimsuits. They also dictated ⓓthat the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.
“Technology doping” in sports means the practice of gaining a competitive edge by using technology to improve performance. This can be against the spirit of fair play. However, since most sports require equipment of some sort, it can be (C)[easy / difficult] to determine what is technology doping and what is not. Some argue that it is a natural progress ⓔcoming from scientific development, while others claim it undermines human spirit and effort, ⓕensure that rich athletes have an advantage over poor ones.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓒ wear → wearing (명사 swimmers를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, swimmers가 ‘착용하는’ 주체이므로 wear를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 wearing으로 고친다.)
ⓕ ensure → ensuring (콤마(,) 앞의 완전한 절(it ~ effort)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사 구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절(it ~ effort)이 ‘확실하게 하는’ 주체이므로 ensure를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 ensuring으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주어 25 new swimming world records가 ‘수립된“ 대상이므로, 앞의 be동사 were와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 set는 적절하다.
ⓑ 명사구 a full body swimsuit를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a full body swimsuit가 ’설계된‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 designed는 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(the fabric ~ breathable)을 이끌어 동사 dictated의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ 명사구 a natural progress를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a natural progress가 과학 발전으로부터 ’기인한‘ 주체이자 자동사 come이 쓰여 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 coming은 적절하다.

body:
Various styles and types of textiles can be used in art. In textile art, blue jeans, not water paints, can be used to draw pictures. Beautiful threads replace photos of scenic views. These types of textiles can be brilliant tools for expanding artistic creativity.
Ian Berry, Denim Art
Have you ever imagined painting with clothes, not on clothes? Surprisingly, Ian Berry succeeded in this and makes art out of blue jeans. His art looks like a painting, but people suddenly notice the beauty in blue jeans when they look at his art. He collects denim of every shade and uses it to create the shading and the sense of perspective in his portraits, landscapes, and other unique works of art. With just his hands, scissors, and glue, he creates almost three-dimensional pieces. He has been making realistic installations of denim for many years. He uses discarded jeans, cuts them up into pieces, and, like a painter, sorts them according to color. At first glance, the work seems flat, but a closer look reveals different layers of denim placed on top of and over each other. They are in fact denim collages. They are almost impossible to distinguish from paintings.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Ian Berry creates artworks by using blue jeans instead of traditional art materials.
Berry gathers denim in different shades to create shading and perspective in his artworks.
Berry uses his hands, scissors, and glue to create almost three-dimensional pieces.
Berry cuts used jeans into pieces and arranges them by color like a painter.
Berry's denim collages have different layers, and they can be easily distinguished from paintings.
solution:
Berry의 작품에는 서로 겹쳐진 다른 층의 데님이 드러나는데, 그것들은 실제로 데님 콜라주이며, 그림과 구별하기가 거의 불가능하다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘Berry의 데님 콜라주에는 서로 다른 층이 있으며, 그것들은 그림과 쉽게 구별될 수 있다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① Ian Berry는 전통적인 미술 재료 대신 청바지를 사용하여 작품을 만든다.
② Berry는 자신의 작품에서 명암과 원근감을 만들어 내기 위해 다양한 색조의 데님을 모은다.
③ Berry는 거의 입체적인 작품을 만들기 위해 자신의 손, 가위, 그리고 접착제를 사용한다.
④ Berry는 사용된 청바지를 조각으로 자르고 화가처럼 색깔에 따라 배열한다.

body:
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. (A) Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. (B) What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. (C) Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. (D) The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. (E) This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, ㉠비단을 입고 사용할 수 있는 사람에 대한 제한이 느슨해졌고, 점점 더 많은 사람들이 비단옷을 입고 집을 비단 장식으로 꾸미는 것이 보이게 되었다. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, prompting the development of the civilizations.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘호기심이 동한 그녀는 고치를 풀기 위해 나무에서 더 가져와 실로 옷감을 만들었다’는 뜻으로, 문장의 맨 앞에 Intrigued가 쓰였으므로 이 문장 앞에는 그녀가 호기심을 갖게 된 계기가 제시되어야 한다. 또한 more cocoons(더 많은 고치들)라는 표현을 통해 이미 고치 하나를 가지고 무언가를 해 본 내용이 앞에 제시되어 있음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 차가 고치의 막을 녹인 뒤에 남은 부드러운 섬유 덩어리를 발견한 뒤, 그 고치를 풀어 600m가 넘게 늘어뜨린 내용 이후인 (D)에서, 호기심이 생겨 더 많은 고치를 모아 풀고 그 실로 천을 만들었다는 주어진 문장이 연결된다. 또한 (D) 뒤에서 The result(그 결과)가 쓰여, 고치를 더 가져와 풀고 그 실로 옷감을 만든 결과를 가리키고 있으므로 그 앞에 주어진 문장이 들어가야 자연스럽게 이어지므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (D)이다.

dress up, see, use, wear, ease, can, clothing, on, wear, homes, the restrictions

solution:

body:
Eight companies ⓐpresented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and ⓑowed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more ⓒflexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and ⓓcomponents involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the ⓔcraftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
<보기>
ⓐ present: to offer your thoughts, ideas, plans, etc., to others for them to consider
ⓑ owe: to need to pay or give something to someone because they have lent money to you, or in exchange for something they have done for you
ⓒ flexible: able to bend or be bent easily without breaking
ⓓ component: the center or most important part of something
ⓔ craftsmanship: skill at making things, or the skill with which something was made or done
solution:
ⓐ ~을 제시하다: 다른 사람들이 그것을 고려하도록 자신의 생각, 아이디어, 계획 등을 그들에게 제안하다
ⓒ 유연한: 부러지지 않고 쉽게 구부리거나 구부러질 수 있는
ⓔ 솜씨: 무언가를 만드는 기술, 또는 무언가가 만들어지거나 행해진 방식의 기술
오답
ⓑ …은 ~ 덕분이다: 누군가가 당신에게 돈을 빌려주었기 때문에, 또는 그들이 당신을 위해 한 일에 대한 대가로, 그 사람에게 무언가를 지불하거나 주어야 하다
(→to have something or achieve something because of what someone else has done 다른 사람이 한 일 때문에 무언가를 가지거나 무언가를 성취하다)
ⓓ 구성 요소: 어떤 것의 중심이 되거나 또는 가장 중요한 부분
(→a part that combines with other parts to form something bigger 다른 부분들과 결합하여 더 큰 것을 형성하는 부분)

On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest challenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─ a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.

the psychological challenges faced by astronauts during the first space mission

body:
Teresa Lim, Embroidery Art
People usually take pictures of scenic views, but Teresa Lim paints pictures of tourist spots with a needle and thread when she travels the world. She embroiders places she visits in surprising detail. This method of preserving memories lets her truly take in her surroundings. She spends time sitting in one place, observing details and stitching as the scene reveals itself. She says on her website that her designs “seek to erase the lines and boundaries between being an illustrator and a textile designer.” Her art is a delightful fusion of a canvas and a camera that projects travel scenes onto fabric. She recreates what she sees on cloth and eliminates the need for a vacation photo album.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Teresa Lim uniquely preserves her travel memories by (A)______ tourist spots in detail with a needle and thread, (B)______ illustration and textile design to replace traditional photo albums.
(A) (B)
choices: embroidering separating
embroidering fusing
unraveling combining
unraveling fusing

During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit.
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, ______. They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: allowed athletes to choose any swimsuit as long as it improved performance
formally permitted all athletes to wear shark-skin suits
established strict safety rules to protect swimmers
banned the use of any natural fabrics in races
decided to ban all full body swimsuits

W: Hey, everyone. Welcome back to AI Talks. Today, let’s explore a fascinating subject: machine learning. You know when you use a music streaming app and it magically suggests songs you might like? Or when a camera app has those fun filters that can turn you into a movie character or place virtual sunglasses on you? That’s the magic of machine learning in action. Picture this: You have a robot, and at first, it’s nothing but a machine. Now, you show it a lot of photos of pizza. After a bit, you show it a random picture, and it can tell you if it’s pizza or not. That’s machine learning ― it’s all about helping machines learn from information. Think about your favorite game. The first time? Maybe a bit tricky. But play it again and again, and you’ll beat it, right? Machines do something similar; they learn from errors, getting smarter over time using a lot of data. And it’s not just fun and games. From healthcare to self-driving tech, machine learning is changing our world. It’s like giving computers their own set of cool skills! Stay curious, keep exploring, and until next time, happy learning!

choices: the basic concept and practical applications of machine learning
the historical development and future challenges of machine learning
the differences between machine learning and traditional algorithms
the advantages of replacing human workers with robots in everyday life
the growing popularity of entertainment apps using artificial intelligence

G: Have you heard about the latest developments in AI?
B: Yes, it’s concerning how fast technology is evolving.
G: What are you worried about?
B: Well, AI systems need an enormous amount of data, and that includes personal data. So there might be privacy concerns.
G: You’re right. I’m worried about how they will use the data without taking away our privacy.
B: The thing is, it’s not just about privacy. It’s about morality because AI can’t tell right from wrong.
G: Absolutely. There’s another issue. AI may help in healthcare, but it could give wrong diagnoses sometimes.
B: That’s worrying. Wrong diagnoses will lead to wrong treatments.
G: Definitely. It’s a tricky area with lots of things to think about.

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The rapid growth of AI technology is causing some concerns.
AI systems may raise privacy issues because they require a large amount of personal data.
The speakers agree that AI can clearly distinguish between right and wrong.
Using AI in healthcare can pose a risk of wrong diagnoses and incorrect treatments.
Both speakers are worried about the ethical and medical problems associated with AI.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) ⓐhas been the subject of much discussion and controversy for many decades, with many experts predicting ⓑthat it will revolutionize our way of life. From healthcare to finance, the implementation of AI is transforming a wide range of sectors. Embracing AI ⓒmeans tapping into the potential of tomorrow in unprecedented ways. From self-driving cars to personalized medical treatments, AI is shaping our future and ⓓpushing the envelope like never before. As we stand on the brink of a new era, it is crucial ⓔwhat each of us understand the rise of AI and its impacts on our world.
AI is the ability of computers and machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, decision-making, and language translation. Recent developments have also seen AI taking on more creative roles; AI art generators, for example, are able to take a human’s description in words and transform it directly into art. AI has been around for several decades, but recent advancements in computing power, data storage, and machine learning algorithms have fueled its rapid growth.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ what → that (완전한 절(each ~ world)을 이끌어 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 과거부터 지금까지 수십 년 동안 인공 지능[AI]이 많은 논의와 논란의 대상이었다는 뜻이므로 현재완료형 has been은 적절하다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(it ~ life)을 이끌어 predicting의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
ⓒ 동명사구 주어 ‘Embracing AI’에 이어지는 동사 자리로, 동명사구 주어는 단수 취급하므로 단수동사 means는 적절하다.
ⓓ be동사 is와 함께 쓰여 현재진행형을 이루는 현재분사 shaping과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되며, 주어 AI가 ‘한계를 초월하는’ 주체이므로 is와 함께 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 pushing은 적절하다.

body:
Some of the most significant impacts of AI are ⓐincreased efficiency and productivity. Through automation, AI systems and robots can perform repetitive, boring, and dangerous tasks easily, freeing up humans ⓑto focus on more innovative and strategic work. In the healthcare sector, AI is being used to analyze vast amounts of medical data to improve diagnoses. In finance, AI algorithms ⓒare being used to automate administrative tasks, detect fraud, and make investment decisions.
Advocates of AI argue that these advancements will lead to a more efficient, productive, and technical society, ⓓwhich individuals have more time and resources to focus on more meaningful work. They also argue that AI has the potential to solve complex problems, such as climate change and disease, in ways ⓔhow were previously impossible. For example, AI can analyze huge amounts of data quickly to find patterns in weather changes or the spread of a disease. This could lead to finding solutions to climate change and cures for untreatable illnesses ⓕmuch quicker.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓓ which → where (완전한 절(individuals ~ work)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 a more efficient, productive, and technical society를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where로 고친다.)
ⓔ how → that 또는 which (선행사 ways와 관계부사 how는 원래 함께 쓸 수 없을 뿐만 아니라, 여기서는 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(were previously impossible)을 이끌어 선행사 ways를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.)
*본문에는 that이 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 명사구 efficiency and productivity를 수식하는 분사 자리로, efficiency and productivity가 ‘증진된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 increased는 적절하다.
ⓑ 구동사 free up은 ‘free up+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(…에게 ~할 시간적 여유를 주다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 분사 freeing up의 목적격보어로 쓰인 to부정사 to focus는 적절하다.
ⓒ 주어 AI algorithms이 ‘활용되는’ 대상이자, 지금 ‘활용되고 있는 중’이므로, 수동과 진행을 동시에 나타내는 수동진행형(be being p.p.)을 주어에 수일치하여 are being used로 쓴 것은 적절하다.
ⓕ 비교급 quicker를 강조 수식하는 much가 쓰인 것은 적절하다.

body:
Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to maintain existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as objective.
(A) As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police.
(B) For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones.
(C) However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely reproduce those biases in its output.
This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to diminish the potential negative impacts of AI.
In conclusion, the rise of AI is shaping the future of society in profound ways, and it is important that we consider both the potential benefits and challenges this technology presents. While AI has the potential to increase efficiency and productivity and solve complex problems, it also has the potential to cause job losses and continue existing biases. However, as with any revolutionary technology, it is likely that the rise of AI will also create new job opportunities and contribute to economic growth. ⓐAI의 개발과 활용이 신뢰할 수 있는 윤리적인 방식으로 이루어지도록 보장하는 것은 사회의 책임이다. This will require collaboration between governments, corporations, and individuals to establish regulations and standards, provide education and training programs, and ensure that the benefits of AI are shared equally. The future is now, and the way we shape the role of AI in our lives will have a profound impact on the future of humanity.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 일부 비평가들이 AI가 기존의 편향과 차별을 지속시킬 수 있다는 윤리적 문제를 우려하고, 사람들이 종종 컴퓨터 시스템을 객관적이라고 여긴다는 주어진 글 뒤에, However(그러나)를 통해 AI 시스템도 학습 데이터에 편향이 포함되어 있다면 그 편향을 결과에 그대로 반영할 수 있다는 상반된 내용을 제시하는 (C), For example(예를 들어)을 통해 (C)에서 설명한 AI의 편향 문제에 대한 구체적인 사례로 특정 유형의 피부색에 대해 얼굴 인식 알고리즘의 정확도가 낮아지는 현상과 그 원인을 설명하는 (B), As a result(그 결과)를 통해 (B)에서 설명한 편향의 결과로 미국에서 소수 인종이 얼굴 인식 시스템에 의해 범죄자로 잘못 식별되어 부당하게 체포된 사례를 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

③ AI의 부상은 고용과 경제에 어떤 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있는가? (→새로운 취업 기회를 만들고 경제 성장에 기여할 것이다.)
④ AI의 개발과 활용을 올바른 방향으로 이끌기 위해 어떤 협력이 필요한가? (→ 사회는 규제와 기준을 확립하고, 교육 및 훈련 프로그램을 마련해야 하며 AI의 혜택이 동등하게 나누어지도록 정부와 기업, 그리고 개인 간의 협력이 요구될 것이다.)

body:
Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to maintain existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as objective.
(A) As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police.
(B) For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones.
(C) However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely reproduce those biases in its output.
This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to diminish the potential negative impacts of AI.
In conclusion, the rise of AI is shaping the future of society in profound ways, and it is important that we consider both the potential benefits and challenges this technology presents. While AI has the potential to increase efficiency and productivity and solve complex problems, it also has the potential to cause job losses and continue existing biases. However, as with any revolutionary technology, it is likely that the rise of AI will also create new job opportunities and contribute to economic growth. ⓐAI의 개발과 활용이 신뢰할 수 있는 윤리적인 방식으로 이루어지도록 보장하는 것은 사회의 책임이다. This will require collaboration between governments, corporations, and individuals to establish regulations and standards, provide education and training programs, and ensure that the benefits of AI are shared equally. The future is now, and the way we shape the role of AI in our lives will have a profound impact on the future of humanity.

The technological singularity is the point at which ㉠______. This could lead to a future ⓐ[which / in which] humans and machines merge, creating a new form of intelligence. Either way, the technological singularity is likely to have a profound impact on the future of humanity. According to futurist Ray Kurzweil, the singularity will occur when technological development becomes unstoppable and unalterable, resulting in unanticipated changes to human civilization. Here are a few potential scenarios:
Merging with AI: We may be able to merge with AI in the future, ⓑ[enhancing / enhance] our intelligence and life expectancy. What would it be like ⓒ[to be / being] able to access the Internet with your mind? Then we might be able to think and learn at extraordinary speeds and control machines with our thoughts.
Bots taking the lead: Many traditional jobs might fade away, but exciting new roles may pop up. People might be trained to be mediators between AI and humans. Schools might teach teamwork among humans and bots rather than traditional subjects. Kids may attend “fusion schools” where AI instructor bots might collaborate with human creativity. Here, students can design artworks and invent games alongside their AI friends.
Scientific leaps: Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) can solve complex problems, allowing for phenomenal achievements in physics, medicine, climate science, and other fields at an unprecedented pace. For example, the spacecraft of the future may be capable of traveling to other planets at unimaginable speeds. They may also be equipped with advanced life support systems that will allow humans to live there for extended periods of time.
The technological singularity is a potentially dangerous event, but it is also one that could lead to incredible advances for humanity. We need to be aware of the risks and prepare for them as best we can, so that we can make sure that the singularity is a positive event for us all.

Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment. Automation, they argue, will lead to widespread job losses, as machines and robots replace human workers in many industries. (A)이는 실직한 이들이 이미 경쟁이 치열한 취업 시장에서 새로운 일자리를 찾느라 어려움을 겪음에 따라 증가된 빈곤과 소득 격차로 이어질 수 있다.
This argument is not without merit. Automation has already displaced workers in several industries, and it is likely that this trend will continue as AI becomes more widespread. However, it is also important to consider that automation has been a driving force behind economic growth for centuries and has consistently created new job opportunities, even as it has decreased existing ones.
For example, the rise of the automobile industry in the early 20th century led to the displacement of carriage drivers, but it also created new jobs in manufacturing, sales, and service. The same can be said for the rise of the computer industry in the late 20th century, which displaced workers in manual labor industries, but also created new jobs in software development, information technology, and related fields.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 가능성의 could를 사용할 것
• 주격 관계대명사 who를 사용할 것
• to부정사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것

<보기>
find, struggle, lose, lead to, those, poverty, new, as, increased, one's jobs, income gap, employment
→ This ______ in an already competitive job market.
answer: could lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment
solution:
• 주어 This 뒤에 조동사 could와 ‘~으로 이어지다’를 뜻하는 구동사 lead to를 이어 쓴다. lead to의 목적어를 영작하기 위해 ‘빈곤과 소득 격차’를 뜻하는 poverty and income gap을 쓰고, poverty and income gap가 ‘증가된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 increased를 poverty and income gap 앞에 쓴다.
• ‘~함에 따라’를 뜻하는 접속사 as 뒤에 ‘사람들’을 뜻하는 복수대명사 those를 쓰고 those를 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 주격 관계대명사 who를 이어 쓴다.
• 관계사절의 동사 lose와 목적어 their jobs를 쓴다. 관계사절 who lose their jobs의 수식을 받는 주어 those에 이어지는 동사 자리에 ‘~하느라 어려움을 겪다’를 뜻하는 ‘struggle+to부정사‘를 쓰고, to 뒤에 ’새로운 일자리를 찾다‘를 뜻하는 find new employment를 이어 쓴다.

Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to maintain existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as objective. However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely ______.
For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones. As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police. This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to diminish the potential negative impacts of AI.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: generate results that reflect the data without reproducing its biases
produce results that improve upon the information in its training data
prevent biased information from affecting its decisions
correct pre-existing biases in the data on its own
reflect the same biases in its generated results
solution:
앞에서 AI 시스템은 자신이 훈련된 데이터가 편향되지 않은 만큼만 편향되지 않게 된다고 설명하고 있으며, 뒤의 예시에서는 편향된 데이터, 즉 밝은 피부색의 얼굴이 주로 포함된 데이터로 학습한 얼굴 인식 알고리즘이 특정 피부색을 인식할 때 정확성이 떨어져 소수 인종의 사람들을 잘못 식별하여 잘못된 체포로 이어진 사례를 제시하고 있으므로 데이터에 편향이 있다면 AI 시스템이 그 편향을 산출물에 재현한다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘생성된 결과에 동일한 편향을 반영한다’가 적절하다.
본문변형 reproduce those biases in its output → reflect the same biases in its generated results
오답

③ 편향된 정보가 자신의 결정에 영향을 미치는 것을 막는다

AI is the ability of computers and machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, decision-making, and language translation. Recent developments have also seen AI taking on more (A)[repetitive / innovative] roles; AI art generators, for example, are able to take a human’s description in words and transform it directly into art. AI has been around for several decades, but recent advancements in computing power, data storage, and machine learning algorithms have (B)[boosted / hindered] its rapid growth.
Some of the most significant impacts of AI are increased efficiency and productivity. Through automation, AI systems and robots can perform repetitive, boring, and dangerous tasks easily, (C)[allowing / forbidding] humans to focus on more innovative and strategic work. In the healthcare sector, AI is being used to analyze vast amounts of medical data to improve diagnoses. In finance, AI algorithms are being used to automate administrative tasks, detect fraud, and make investment decisions.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: innovative boosted forbidding
repetitive hindered allowing
repetitive boosted forbidding
innovative boosted allowing
innovative hindered allowing
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 AI 미술 작품 생성기는 인간이 말로 묘사한 내용을 가지고 바로 미술 작품으로 변환할 수 있다고 했으므로 AI가 단순한 작업을 넘어 창의적인 영역까지 맡는다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 innovative(혁신적인, 창의적인)이 적절하다.
본문변형 creative → innovative
repetitive 반복적인
(B) 앞에서 AI가 수십 년 동안 존재해 왔지만, 최근 연산력, 데이터 저장, 머신 러닝 알고리즘의 발전을 바탕으로 빠르게 성장했다고 설명하고 있으므로, 이러한 발전이 AI의 성장을 촉진했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 boosted(증진했다)가 적절하다.
hinder ~을 방해하다
본문변형 fueled → boosted
(C) 앞에서 AI 시스템과 로봇이 반복적이고, 지루하며, 위험한 작업을 대신 수행한다고 했으므로, 인간은 보다 더 혁신적이고 전략적인 업무에 집중할 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 allowing(가능하게 하는)이 적절하다.
본문변형 freeing up → allowing
forbid ~을 못 하게 하다

Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment. Automation, they argue, will lead to widespread job losses, as machines and robots replace human workers in many industries. This could lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market.
This argument is not without merit. Automation has already displaced workers in several industries, and it is likely (A)[what / that] this trend will continue as AI becomes more ⓐwidespread. However, (B)[what / it] is also important to consider that automation has been a ⓑdriving force behind economic growth for centuries and has consistently created new job opportunities, even as it has decreased existing ones.
For example, the rise of the automobile industry in the early 20th century led to the displacement of carriage drivers, but it also created new jobs in manufacturing, sales, and service. The same can be said for the rise of the computer industry in the late 20th century, (C)[which / that] displaced workers in manual labor industries, but also created new jobs in software development, information technology, and related fields.
Therefore, it is ⓒunlikely that the rise of AI will also give rise to new job opportunities. There will be a growing demand for data scientists, machine learning engineers, and AI ethics experts, among others. These jobs will allow individuals to contribute to society in meaningful ways. At the same time, since they require new skills, education and training will need to ⓓevolve to help people prepare for these new opportunities. By adapting and learning, people can find paths in a world where AI plays a ⓔmajor role.

In 1918, as "World WarⅠ" was ending, a very deadly flu called the "Spanish Flu" spread around the world. It infected many people, causing the deaths of around 50 million, even more than the number of people who died in the war.
(A) This resulted in the mistaken belief that the 1918 flu emerged in Spain. In reality, scientists still don't know where it came from, but some think it might have begun in France, China, Britain, or even the United States.
(B) The flu reached places like the United States, Europe, and even remote areas like Greenland and the Pacific islands. Some people thought it was called the Spanish Flu because it started in Spain, but that's not true.
(C) Spain was the only country hit by the virus that was not involved in "World WarⅠ." Therefore it was the only country to report the true extent of the pandemic.
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 1918년 스페인 독감이 전 세계로 퍼져 많은 사망자를 냈다는 내용의 주어진 글 다음에, 스페인 독감을 The flu로 가리켜 이 독감이 여러 지역으로 퍼졌으며, 일부 사람들의 생각과 달리 스페인에서 시작되었다는 것은 사실이 아님을 언급한 (B), 스페인이 제1차 세계대전에 관련되지 않은, 바이러스의 타격을 입은 유일한 국가로서 팬데믹의 실상을 보도했기 때문에 스페인에서 유래했다는 오해가 생겼다는 구체적 사실을 설명한 (C), 앞에서 설명한 내용을 This로 가리켜 이것이 스페인에서 독감이 발생했다는 잘못된 믿음을 낳았으며, 실제로는 그 기원이 불분명하다는 내용의 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

ⓐWhat less commonly knows is that viruses play crucial roles in supporting much of life on Earth. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses ⓑthat sustain us and the planet, instead of just those that harm us. Therefore, scientists have much more to learn about viruses than they currently know. ⓒWhat they do know is that viruses act as the primary regulators of bacterial and insect populations.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, they steal the reproductive functions of other organisms to multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses ⓓgoing on to infect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses ⓔto control the excessive growth of certain bacteria.

Viruses have harmful effects on living organisms in various ways.
Viruses and bacteria have a mutually dependent symbiotic relationship.
Viruses benefit ecosystems by regulating the populations of bacteria.
Much scientific research is being conducted on the beneficial roles of viruses.

It appears that viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. ⓐ1918년 인플루엔자 대유행은 5천만 명에서 1억 명의 사람들의 목숨을 빼앗아간 것으로 추정된다. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, affecting almost every aspect of human life worldwide.
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. (A) Such contacts allow new viruses to enter human bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. (B) Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. (C) Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. (D) These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. (E) Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 현재시제를 사용할 것
• 완료부정사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 14단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
kill, estimate, 50 to 100, the 1918 influenza pandemic
→ ______
answer: The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated to have killed 50 to 100 million people.
solution:
• 주어인 The 1918 influenza pandemic이 ‘추정되는’ 대상이므로, ‘~한 것으로 추정되다’라는 뜻의 ‘be estimated+to부정사’를 사용하되, 추정되는 시점은 현재이므로 <조건>에 따라 현재시제를 사용해 단수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 현재 단수형 be동사 is를 쓰고, estimate를 과거분사 estimated로 변형한다.
• 사람들이 사망한 것은 과거의 일이므로, is estimated 뒤에 <조건>에 따라 완료부정사(to have p.p.)를 사용하며 to have killed를 쓰고, 목적어로 50 to 100 million people을 연결한다.

body:
Another less recognized role of viruses is their contribution to the evolution of life on Earth. When a virus infects a reproductive cell of its host, such as an egg or sperm, the viral DNA may be passed down to the host’s offspring. The insertion of new DNA into genomes ⓐis a significant mechanism of evolution. Without viruses, in other words, the evolutionary potential for all life on the planet would be impacted.
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution is their role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ ⓑwhat helps the fetus grow securely inside its mother’s body. It facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while ⓒprotecting the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, ⓓmade them vulnerable to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to (A)______. Viruses that infected our remote ancestors more than 130 million years ago have been reported ⓔto serve a key function in the development of this vital organ.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(helps ~ body)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 a complex organ을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what을 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.
*원래 지문에는 that이 쓰였음
ⓓ 완전한 절(female animals had to leave their offspring in one location)과 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입된 전치사구(like eggs in a nest) 뒤에 접속사 없이 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절이 ‘만드는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어인 them이 이어져 있으므로, made를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 making으로 고친다.
ⓔ ‘be reported+to부정사(~한 것으로 보고되다, ~라고 한다)’의 to부정사가 올 자리이며, 주어 Viruses가 핵심적인 ‘역할을 했던’ 것이 보고된 상태(have been reported)인 현재와 같은 시점이 아닌 그보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로, to serve를 완료부정사(to have p.p.)인 to have served로 고친다.
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 보어로 명사구(a significant mechanism)가 있으며, 주어 The insertion of new DNA into genomes의 핵심단어가 단수명사 insertion이므로 단수형 be동사로 수일치한 is는 알맞다.
ⓒ 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사를 남겨 둔 ‘접속사+분사(구) ~’ 형태의 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 it(=a placenta)이 ‘보호하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the fetus가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 protecting은 알맞다.

body:
As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing ⓐthem in the battle against diseases are arising. Of notable interest (A)[is / are] the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment. Genes can be compared to instruction guides that govern how (B)[our bodies function / do our bodies function]. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, (C)[what / which] can lead to health problems. Gene therapy steps in to fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering corrected genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, enabling ⓑthem to function properly. In this process, specially modified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, it can potentially help the body fight off certain diseases.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: is / our bodies function / which
is / do our bodies function / what
are / our bodies function / which
is / do our bodies function / which
are / our bodies function / what
solution:
(A) 보어 역할의 전치사구 Of notable interest가 강조를 위해 문두에 쓰이면서 도치에 의해 주어(the areas ~ treatment) 앞에 be동사가 쓰인 것으로, 주어의 핵심단어인 areas가 복수명사이므로, 복수동사로 수일치한 are가 알맞다.
(B) how 이하는 동사 govern의 목적어로 쓰인 명사절이므로 ‘의문사+평서문(주어+동사~)’의 어순이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ’주어+동사‘ 어순인 our bodies function이 알맞다.
(C) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can lead ~ problems)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 genetic disorders를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.

body:
Using viruses to treat cancer, another use of viruses, ⓐare based on the notion of utilizing their natural ability to infect and kill cells. If ⓑsuccessfully, viruses can be manipulated to specifically target and destroy cancer cells while ⓒleaving healthy cells unharmed. The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment ⓓis still in the early stages. (A)______, many researchers are involved in hundreds of projects with the goal of discovering cures for diseases that were once thought ⓔbeing incurable.
We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. The more we learn about viruses, however, ⓕthe better equipped we will be to use certain viruses for beneficial purposes and to develop defenses against viruses that could lead to the next pandemic. (B)______, learning more about viral diversity will help us ⓖreach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 총 4개이다.
ⓒ 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사를 남겨 둔 ‘접속사+분사(구)’ 형태의 분사구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어인 healthy cells와 목적격보어인 형용사 unharmed가 이어져 ‘leave+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)(~을 …한 상태로 남겨두다)’의 능동태 5형식 구문을 이루므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 leaving은 알맞다.
ⓓ 주어 The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment의 핵심단어가 단수명사 use이므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is는 알맞다.
ⓕ ’the+비교급‘이 쓰인 앞 절(The more ~ viruses)에 상응해 ’the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 …(~ 할수록, 더 …하다)‘을 이루어야 하며, 주어 we가 ’equip+목적어+to부정사(~에게 …할 능력[기술]을 키워주다)‘의 동사 equip의 대상이므로, ’the+비교급‘인 the better 뒤에 수동 표현인 ’be equipped+to부정사‘의 equipped가 쓰인 the better equipped는 알맞다.
ⓖ ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식 구문에서 준사역동사 help의 목적격보어로 to부정사나 동사원형이 쓰이며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 a deeper understanding이 이어져 있으므로, help와 목적어 us 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 타동사 reach(~에 이르다)가 능동태 동사원형으로 쓰인 것은 알맞다.
오답
ⓐ are → is (주어인 동명사구 Using viruses to treat cancer와 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입된 동격 어구 another use of viruses 뒤에 문장의 동사로 ’be based on ~(~에 근거하다, ~에 기반을 두다)‘의 be동사가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 동명사(구) 주어는 단수 취급하므로 수일치를 위해 복수동사 are를 단수동사 is로 고친다.)
ⓑ successfully → successful (부사절 접속사 If 뒤에 ’주어+be동사‘인 it is가 생략되었으므로 생략된 be동사(is)의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 올 자리이다. 보어 자리에 부사는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사 successfully를 형용사 successful로 고친다.)
ⓔ being incurable → to be incurable (’~을 …라고 생각하다‘라는 뜻의 ’think+목적어+(to be+)보어‘의 수동 표현인 ’be thought+(to be+)보어(…라고 생각되다)‘를 이루어야 하므로, being incurable을 to be incurable로 고친다.)

body:

If ⓑsuccessfully, viruses can be manipulated to specifically target and destroy cancer cells while ⓒleaving healthy cells unharmed. The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment ⓓis still in the early stages. (A)______, many researchers are involved in hundreds of projects with the goal of discovering cures for diseases that were once thought ⓔbeing incurable.
We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. The more we learn about viruses, however, ⓕthe better equipped we will be to use certain viruses for beneficial purposes and to develop defenses against viruses that could lead to the next pandemic. (B)______, learning more about viral diversity will help us ⓖreach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.
윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: However / What’s more
Namely / Unfortunately
Nevertheless / In contrast
That is to say / Conversely
For example / More than that
solution:
(A) 유전자 치료와 암 치료에 바이러스를 사용하는 것은 아직 초기 단계에 머물러 있다는 내용 뒤에 많은 연구자들이 치료법을 발견하기 위해 수백 개의 프로젝트에 참여하고 있다는 대조적인 내용이 이어지므로, 역접을 나타내는 However(그러나) 또는 Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)가 알맞다.
(B) 바이러스에 대해 더 많이 알게 되는 것은 특정 바이러스를 유익한 목적으로 사용하고 다음 팬데믹으로 이어질 수 있는 바이러스에 대한 방어책을 개발하는 데 더 잘 대비할 수 있게 한다는 이점 뒤에, 지구와 생태계, 우리 몸의 작용에 대해 더 깊이 이해할 수 있도록 도움을 준다는 또 다른 이점을 추가하므로, What’s more(게다가) 또는 More than that(그 이상으로, 뿐만 아니라)이 알맞다.
*원래 지문에는 More than that이 쓰였음
오답
② 즉, 다시 말해서 / 불행히도, 유감스럽게도
③ 그럼에도 불구하고 / 대조적으로
④ 즉, 다시 말해서 / 반대로, 역으로
⑤ 예를 들어 / 그 이상으로, 뿐만 아니라

body:
ⓐIt appears that viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. ⓑThe 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated to have killed 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, ⓒaffecting almost every aspect of human life worldwide.
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter ⓓhuman bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, ⓔmeaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: Viruses appear to exist solely to bring suffering to humanity.
ⓑ: It is estimated that the 1918 influenza pandemic kills 50 to 100 million people.
ⓒ: and it affects almost every aspect of human life worldwide
ⓓ: human bodies which have no prior immunity to such viruses
ⓔ: which means more opportunities for the viruses that are present in wild animals to spread to humans
solution:
ⓑ ‘be estimated+to부정사(구)(~할 것으로 추정되다)’는 가주어 It과 진주어인 that절을 사용해 ‘It+be estimated+that절’ 구조로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으나, is estimated 뒤에 추정되는 시점보다 이전의 과거에 발생한 일을 나타내는 완료부정사(to have killed)가 쓰였으므로 진주어인 that절에 현재시제 kills가 아닌 과거시제 killed를 사용해야 한다. 따라서 ‘It is estimated that the 1918 influenza pandemic killed 50 to 100 million people.’로 전환해야 한다.
오답
ⓐ ‘~한 것처럼 보인다’라는 뜻의 가주어-진주어 구문인 ‘It appears+that절’은 that절의 주어를 주절 주어 자리로 이동시켜 ’주어+appear+to부정사(구)‘로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으므로, that 뒤의 viruses를 주절 주어로 하고, 복수명사인 주어에 수일치 시켜 복수동사 appear를 쓴 뒤, 동사 exist를 to부정사로 바꿔 ’Viruses appear to exist solely to bring suffering to humanity.‘로 전환한 것은 알맞다.
ⓒ 앞의 완전한 절(the recent ~ lives)에 콤마(,)로 이어져 흐름상 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문이므로 접속사 and를 사용해 ’and+대명사(주어)+동사~‘로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 주절 주어인 단수명사구 the recent COVID-19 pandemic과 동일하므로 and 뒤에 이를 가리키는 단수대명사 it을 사용하고, 분사구문의 내용이 현재의 일반적 사실에 해당하므로 현재시제이자 it에 수일치한 단수동사 affects를 써서 ’and it affects almost every aspect of human life worldwide‘로 전환한 것은 알맞다.
ⓓ enter의 목적어인 명사구 human bodies를 관계사절인 ’that ~ viruses’가 수식하고 있으며 human bodies를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 that은 which로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으므로, that 대신 which를 사용해 ‘human bodies which have no prior immunity to such viruses’로 전환한 것은 알맞다.
ⓔ 앞의 완전한 절(These changes ~ wild animals)에 콤마(,)로 이어져 앞 절을 부연 설명하는 분사구문이므로 동일한 기능을 가지는 계속적 용법의 관계사절로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으며, 명사구 the viruses를 수식하는 형용사구 ‘present in wild animals’는 앞에 ‘주격 관계대명사+be동사’가 생략된 것으로 설명할 수 있다. 관계사절의 내용이 일반적 사실을 나타내고 선행사가 앞 절인 경우 단수 취급하므로, which 뒤에 현재시제이자 단수로 수일치한 means를 사용하고, present 앞에 선행사 the viruses에 어울리는 주격 관계대명사 which 또는 that 중 that을 사용하고, 선행사인 복수명사구에 수일치한 복수동사 are를 사용해, ‘which means more opportunities for the viruses that are present in wild animals to spread to humans’로 전환한 것은 알맞다.

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could (A)[keep / disrupt] the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
But they were (B)[right / wrong]. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and (C)[counter / multiply] bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: keep / right / counter
disrupt / wrong / multiply
keep / wrong / counter
disrupt / wrong / counter
disrupt / right / multiply
solution:
(A) 당시의 의사들이 흑사병의 원인이라고 생각했던 나쁜 공기에 대한 설명이므로, 몸의 내부 균형을 깨뜨린다는 흐름이 되는 disrupt(~에 지장을 주다, ~을 방해하다)가 알맞다.
keep ~을 유지하다
(B) they가 가리키는 1600년대 흑사병을 치료했던 의사들이 흑사병의 원인이 나쁜 공기라고 생각하고 마스크의 허브가 공기를 걸러내 병에 걸리지 않게 보호해 주길 바랐다고 했으나, 뒤에 흑사병이 실제로는 동물에서 사람으로 퍼질 수 있는 박테리아에 의해 발생했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 당시 의사들의 생각이 틀렸었다는 흐름이 되는 wrong(틀린, 잘못된)이 알맞다.
right 옳은
(C) 1600년대에 의사들이 사용한 의복과 방법은 실제로 흑사병으로부터 그들을 보호하지 못했지만 이후 상황이 크게 바뀌었다고 했으므로, 현대 의학으로 인해 이제 우리는 박테리아와 바이러스를 신속하게 탐지하고 그것을 예방할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 counter(~을 저지하다, ~에 대응하다)가 알맞다.
multiply ~을 증식시키다

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 바이러스에 대한 과학적 지식의 확장에 따라 질병과의 전쟁에 바이러스를 활용할 기회가 생겨나고 있으며 주목할 분야로 유전자 치료와 암 치료를 언급한 주어진 글에 이어, 유전자가 우리 몸이 기능하는 방식을 규정하는 지침서와 같다는 개념적인 설명과 함께 때로 사람들이 유전적 장애를 가지고 태어나며 이것이 건강 문제를 일으킬 수 있다고 언급하는 (A), 앞에 언급된 문제 상황을 these issues(이러한 문제들)로 가리켜 유전자 치료가 이 문제들을 해결하기 위해 개입하고, 치료의 핵심은 환자의 세포에 수정된 유전적 지침을 전달해 세포가 제대로 기능하게 하는 것이라고 설명한 (C), 앞서 설명한 유전자 치료의 과정을 this process(이러한 과정)로 가리켜, 이 과정에서 특수하게 변형된 바이러스가 유전적 지시를 전달하는 매개체 중 하나로 사용된다고 부연 설명한 (B)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses did not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans to survive.
Insect species populations are also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses that infect those insects also increase, reducing their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects to flourish. Considering the chain of food in nature, it would not be difficult to assume that viruses fulfill important functions in regulating other species. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.

body:
Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created diverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques (A)[which / by which] they have developed. Let’s discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds.
Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby (B)[gets / getting] them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin (C)[sprouting / to sprout] and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: which / gets / sprouting
which / getting / sprouting
by which / gets / sprouting
which / getting / to sprout
by which / getting / to sprout
solution:
(A) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they have developed)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the strongest survival techniques를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고로, ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 뒤에는 완전한 절이 온다.
본문변형 (A)는 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
(B) 동사가 있는 완전한 절(It tempts ~ flesh)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로, thereby 이하는 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문의 형태가 되어야 한다. 뒤에 목적어인 them과 목적격보어인 to부정사구(to eat the seeds)가 이어져 ’get+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …하게 하다)‘의 능동태 5형식 구문을 이루고 있으므로, 현재분사 getting이 알맞다.
(C) begin의 목적어로 동명사나 to부정사가 둘 다 쓰일 수 있으나, 뒤에 등위접속사 and로 to가 생략된 동사원형 grow가 병렬로 연결되어 있으므로, to부정사인 to sprout가 알맞다.

body:
Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil's claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil's claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. (A)As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals. (B)As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. (C)As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. (D)Fallen seeds can germinate when they are exposed to enough moisture and sunlight. (E)The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is how devil’s claw became known as the worst free rider.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 날카로운 갈고리나 바늘을 사용해 지나가는 동물에게 씨앗을 붙여 그것을 퍼뜨리는 식물의 사례로 devil’s claw를 소개하며 분홍색 트럼펫을 닮은 그것의 꽃이 많은 갈고리가 있는 열매로 변한다고 설명을 시작한 뒤에, 열매가 마르는 동안 갈고리들이 동물들의 털에 달라붙을 만큼 단단해지고, 동물들이 이동하면서 여러 장소에 씨앗이 흩어지게 되며, 그 과정에서 동물들은 갈고리로 인해 심한 통증을 느낀다는 내용으로 이어지는 것이 자연스러우므로, devil’s claw의 씨앗이 퍼지는 방식과 무관하게 씨앗이 발아하기 위한 환경 조건을 언급하는 (D) ‘떨어진 씨앗은 충분한 수분과 햇빛에 노출될 때 발아할 수 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world’s tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. (A)______, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning “the highest one.” (B)______, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, (C)______. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
choices: In short / Actually
However / Consequently
Moreover / For example
However / In fact
Furthermore / As a result
solution:
(A) Hyperion이 발견되기 전에는 Helios가 가장 높은 나무로 여겨졌다는 내용 뒤에, 2006년에 두 명의 자연학자가 Helios보다 더 높은 나무를 발견했다는 내용이 이어져 흐름이 반전되므로, 역접을 나타내는 However(하지만)가 알맞다.
(B) Helios보다 더 높은 나무가 발견되어 그리스 신화의 Titan 중 ‘가장 높은 자’를 의미하는 Hyperion의 이름을 따서 그 나무의 이름이 지어졌다는 내용 뒤에, 공원에서 Hyperion을 볼 가능성은 희박하다는 예상과 다른 대조적인 사실을 연결하므로, In fact(사실은)가 알맞다.
본문변형 (B)는 원래 지문에서 However였음
오답
① 요컨대 실제로는, 사실은
② 하지만 그 결과, 따라서
③ 게다가, 더욱이 예를 들어
⑤ 게다가, 더욱이 그 결과로

윗글의 빈칸 (C)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 쓰시오.
<조건>
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• 가목적어 it을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)

impossible, from the ground, identify, nearly, make
→ ______
answer: making it nearly impossible to identify from the ground
solution:

body:
Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground to eat or ⓐlay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size.
(A) That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and ⓑsmell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of ⓒthem, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot.
(B) They cannot help aborting and ⓓsearch for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.
(C) Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓔhad been antelope dung.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓓ search →searching (aborting과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 ‘~할 수밖에 없다’라는 뜻의 ‘cannot help -ing‘ 구문을 이루어야 하므로, search를 -ing 형태의 searching으로 고친다.)
본문변형 have no choice but to abort and search → cannot help aborting and searching
ⓔ had been → were (현재시제로 쓰인 앞의 완전한 절(they carefully roll the seed away)에 이어진 as if가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이며, 흐름상 앞 절과 동일한 현재 시점에서 반대의 사실을 가정해야 하므로, ‘as if+주어+were/과거동사 ~(마치 ~인 것처럼)’ 형태의 가정법 과거 표현을 이루어야 한다. 따라서 had been을 were로 고친다. 참고로, ‘as if+주어+had been ~’은 ‘마치 ~였던 것처럼’이라는 뜻으로 과거 사실의 반대를 가정할 때 쓰인다.
오답

body:
Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground to eat or ⓐlay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size.
(A) That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and ⓑsmell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of ⓒthem, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot.
(B) They cannot help aborting and ⓓsearch for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.
(C) Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓔhad been antelope dung.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 먹거나 안에 알을 낳기 위해 영양의 배설물을 굴리는 선천적인 쇠똥구리의 습성과 silver arrow-reed 씨앗의 색과 모양, 크기를 설명하는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, silver arrow-reed의 씨앗을 가리키는 their를 사용해 그것들의 겉모습과 냄새가 영양의 배설물과 흡사하기 때문에 씨앗이 땅에 떨어지면 쇠똥구리가 곧 그것에 접근해 그것이 영양의 배설물인 것처럼 굴린다고 설명하는 (C), 앞에 언급된 이유에 대해, ‘That is why ~(이것이 ~한 이유이다)를 사용해 쇠똥구리들이 silver arrow-reed의 씨앗을 굴리는 모습이 자주 발견된다는 결과가 이어지고, 쇠똥구리들이 씨앗을 먹으려고 하거나 그 안에 알을 낳으려고 할 때 그럴 수 없다는 것을 깨닫게 된다는 점을 설명하는 (A), the confused beetles를 They로 가리켜 그들은 포기하고 진짜 배설물 덩어리를 찾을 수밖에 없다는 최종적인 결과를 설명하는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically ⓐseparated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they ⓑare bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally ⓒcatching fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, ⓓhitting the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often ⓔstarted by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight ⓕneeding for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce ⓖprovided there is fire.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓒ catching → catch (주어 eucalyptus leaves에 수일치한 복수동사 rub과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되며 부사 naturally의 수식을 받는 동사가 올 자리이므로, catching을 복수동사 catch로 고친다.)
ⓓ hitting → hit (주어 the seeds에 수일치한 복수동사 come, begin과 ‘A, B, and C’의 형태로 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, hitting을 복수동사 hit으로 고친다.)
ⓕ needing → needed (for의 목적어로 쓰인 명사구 the water and sunlight을 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘필요로 하는’ 주체가 아니라 ‘필요시되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 needing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 needed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 주어 they가 가리키는 Eucalyptus seeds가 ‘타동사+부사’ 구조의 구동사 ‘bind ~ together(~을 묶다)‘의 대상이며, 목적어 없이 부사 together만 뒤에 쓰였으므로, 수동태인 ’be bound together‘를 사용한 are bound는 알맞다.
ⓖ ‘만약 ~한다면, ~라는 것을 조건으로’라는 뜻으로 뒤의 완전한 절(there is fire)을 이끌어 ‘provided (that)+완전한 절’ 형태의 조건 부사절을 이루고 있으며, provided that에서 that은 생략 가능하므로, provided는 알맞다.
본문변형 provided that → provided

Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. ⓐ그것은 헬리콥터가 그것의 프로펠러를 사용하여 떠오르고 공중에 머무는 방식과 유사합니다. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, ⓑ______. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 적절한 관계부사를 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
propellers, helicopters, in the air, stay, similar, lift, use, get
It ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: is similar to how helicopters get lifted, stay in the air using their propellers
solution:
• It에 수일치한 단수형 be동사 is 뒤에 보어로 형용사 similar를 쓰고, ‘~와 유사한’이라는 뜻의 ‘similar to ~’를 사용해 전치사 to를 추가한다.
• <조건>에 따라 적절한 관계부사를 사용하되, ‘~하는 방식[방법]’이라는 뜻으로 선행사 the way를 생략한 관계부사 how를 쓰고 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지도록 한다.
• how가 이끄는 절의 주어로 helicopters를 쓰고, ‘get+p.p.’ 형태의 수동태를 사용해 get 뒤에 타동사 lift(~을 올리다)를 과거분사 lifted로 변형한다.
• 복수동사 get과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되도록 복수동사 stay를 쓰고, 부사구 in the air를 연결한다.
• <조건>에 따라 흐름상 동시동작(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 사용하되, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 helicopters가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이므로 use를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 using으로 변형하고, 목적어로 명사구 their propellers를 써서 완성한다.

body:
M: Jessica, I went to the Gustav Klimt exhibition you recommended.
W: Great! What did you think, Tom?
M: It was very impressive! I especially liked the way the paintings were projected on the walls. I felt like I was inside the art itself.
W: I felt the same way. It is very well organized. Which painting did you like the most?
M: I loved The Tree of Life. The spiral shapes of the branches made the tree seem alive and showed the power of life.
W: That was my favorite, too! The gold tree trunk was gorgeous.
M: I think the artist tried to show the strong connection between nature and spirituality.
W: Indeed! It’s amazing how art can express such powerful messages.

위 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Both Tom and Jessica picked The Tree of Life as their favorite painting in the exhibition.
Tom thought that the branches’ swirling forms made the tree appear lively and represented the strength of life.
Tom believed Gustav Klimt intended to highlight the connection between nature and spirituality.
solution:
Tom은 자신이 예술 작품 그 자체 속에 들어가 있는 것처럼 느꼈다고 말했을 뿐, 실제로 그 안에 들어간 것이 아니므로 ② ‘Tom은 그 전시를 좋아했고, 특히 작품 그 자체 안에 들어가 있는 것을 즐겼다.‘는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

① Jessica는 Gustav Klimt 전시회를 Tom에게 추천했다.
③ Tom과 Jessica는 둘 다 전시에서 The Tree of Life를 가장 좋아하는 그림으로 꼽았다.
④ Tom은 나뭇가지의 나선형 모양이 나무를 살아 있는 것처럼 보이게 하고 생명의 힘을 보여 준다고 생각했다.

Alfonse Mucha (1860-1939) was one of the first Art Nouveau artists, which led to this form of art ⓐwas referred to as the “Mucha Style.” His style became famous later on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, (A)______.
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day ⓑbecoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money ⓒdrawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he ⓓwas commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept ⓔworking on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

오답
ⓑ 전치사 of의 목적어로 쓰였으므로 동명사 becoming은 적절하다. 참고로 one day(언젠가)는 부사구로 becoming을 수식하고 있다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(Mucha made money)에 접속사와 주어 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 Mucha가 그림을 ‘그리는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 drawing은 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어 he(=Mucha)가 ‘의뢰를 받는’ 대상이므로 수동태(be+p.p.) was commissioned는 적절하다.
ⓔ 동사 kept는 동명사를 목적어로 취해 ‘~을 계속하다’라는 뜻으로 쓰이므로 동명사 working은 적절하다.

body:
Alfonse Mucha
Alfonse Mucha (1860-1939) was one of the first Art Nouveau artists, which led to this form of art being referred to as the “Mucha Style.” His style became famous later on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, did not happen overnight.
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris. (A)
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. (B) He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. (C) Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. (D) This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form. (E)
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
His big break came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그의 큰 기회는 훨씬 나중인 1894년에 찾아왔는데, 그때 그는 연극 ‘Gismonda’의 포스터를 그릴 기회를 얻었다.’라는 뜻이다. ‘큰 기회(big break)’가 훨씬 나중에 찾아왔다고 했으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 Mucha가 아직 큰 성공을 거두지 못하고 자신의 예술 활동을 이어 가던 상황이 언급되어야 하며, 뒤에는 연극 포스터를 기회를 얻는 일에 대한 내용이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 피리에서 Mucha가 잡지의 삽입 광고와 삽화를 그리며 돈을 벌고 있었다는 문장 뒤이자, 연극 포스터를 위해 배우 Sarah Bernhardt의 그림을 제작해 달라는 의뢰를 받았다는 문장 앞인 (B)에 들어가야 한다.

body:
Grandma Moses
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received (A)______. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were (B)______ with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: little or no attention / complete failures
hardly any notice / complete failures
little or no attention / wildly successful
widespread acclaim / public triumphs
widespread acclaim / wildly successful
solution:
(A) 앞 절에서 Grandma Moses가 지역 시장에서 자신의 그림들을 판매하려고 시도했다고 했고, 빈칸이 있는 절은 상반된 내용을 나타내는 but으로 연결되어 있으므로, 그림들이 판매에 성공하지 못했다는 흐름이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ‘거의 또는 전혀 관심을 받지 못한’, ‘거의 어떠한 주목도 받지 못한’이 적절하다.
(B) 뒤에서 Louis Calder가 열었던 전시회들이 Grandma Moses의 작품을 대중에게 알리고, 각계각층의 사람들이 그녀의 일상생활이 지닌 평온한 아름다움을 감상할 수 있게 했다고 했으므로, 전시회들이 대중에게 큰 인기를 끌었다는 흐름이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ‘매우 성공적인’, ‘대중적인 성공’이 적절하다.
본문변형 all a big hit → wildly successful
오답

② (A) 거의 어떠한 주목도 받지 못한 (B) 완전한 실패작들
④ (A) 폭넓은 찬사를 받은 (B) 대중적인 성공
⑤ (A) 폭넓은 찬사를 받은 (B) 매우 성공적인

[1]
Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the ⓐreliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their ⓑreferences based on only their text. (A)[Being read / Having read] a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the ⓒlandscape in which people write and publish, making (B)[it / them] necessary to change reading strategies.
[2]
Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to ⓓnavigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called “lateral reading,” which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight.
For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information that (C)[is being / being] presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general ⓔassertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
<보기>
ⓐ reliability: the state of depending on or trusting in something or someone
ⓑ reference: a book, article, etc. from which information has been obtained
ⓒ landscape: a picture showing an area of countryside or land
ⓓ navigate: to find your way around on a particular website, or to move from one website to another
ⓔ assertion: something that you say or write that you strongly believe
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

solution:
(A) 완전한 절(a reader ~ the text) 앞에 콤마로만 연결되어 있으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 문맥상 주절의 내용인 독자가 검토하거나, 살펴보거나, 화인하는 것보다 책을 읽는 것이 더 먼저 일어난 일이며, 의미상 주어인 a reader가 책을 ‘읽는’ 주체이므로 완료분사구문의 능동태(having p.p.)로 써야 한다. 따라서 Having read가 적절하다.
(B) 분사구문을 이루는 현재분사 making의 목적어 자리이며 ‘make+가목적어+목적격보어+for+의미상주어+진목적어(to부정사)(~하는 것을 …하게 만들다)’ 형태의 5형식 구문을 이루고 있으므로 진목적어인 to부정사에 상응하는 가목적어 역할을 하는 it이 적절하다.
(C) 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 주격 관계대명사절의 동사구를 이루는 자리로, 선행사 any type of information은 단수명사구이며 ‘제시되고 있는’ 대상이므로 뒤의 과거분사 presented와 함께 진행수동태(be being p.p.)를 이루는 is being이 적절하다.

body:
Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. For this reason, ______. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: vertical reading remains the most reliable evaluation strategy
readers should prioritize speed over thorough verification
authors and publishers are held responsible for verification
information evaluation ought to be completed in a single step
lateral reading requires ongoing and repeated evaluation of information

Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. (A)예를 들어, 책을 읽은 후 독자는 그 원문에 제시된 주장이 충분한 근거로 뒷받침되고 있는지 검토하거나, 저자나 출판사가 누구인지 살펴보거나, 원문에 인용된 참고 문헌을 확인할 수 있다. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 완료형 분사구문을 사용할 것
• 명사를 수식하는 분사를 사용할 것
• 간접의문문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
present, cite, read, the arguments, look at, check, support, the references, if, the author, the publisher
→ ______ ______ ______ ______, for example, a reader can review ______ ______ ______ ______ in the text ______ ______ by enough evidence, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, or ______ ______ ______ ______ in the text.
answer: Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text.
solution:
• ‘책을 읽은 것‘이 주절의 내용인 독자가 ’검토하는 것‘보다 먼저 발생한 일이므로 <조건>에 제시된 완료형 분사구문으로 써야 한다. 의미상 주어인 a reader가 책을 ’읽는‘ 주체이므로 동사 read를 능동의 의미를 갖는 완료형 분사 Having read로 변형하고 목적어 a book을 이어서 쓴다.
• 동사 review의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 ’~인지 아닌지‘를 뜻하는 명사절 접속사 if를 쓰고 if가 이끄는 절의 주어 자리에는 the arguments를 쓴다.
• the arguments가 ’제시된‘ 대상이므로 명사를 수식하는 분사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 presented를 쓴다. 부사구 in the text 뒤에 복수주어 the arguments에 이어지는 동사를 써야 하며, the arguments가 ’뒷받침되는’ 대상이므로 수동태 are supported로 쓴다.
• 조동사 can에 이어지는 동사원형 review와 ‘A, B, or C’의 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 등위접속사 or 뒤에 동사원형 look을 쓰고 전치사인 at을 이어서 쓴 다음 전치사의 목적어 자리에 <조건>에 제시된 간접의문문(의문사+평서문)인 who the author or the publisher is를 이어서 쓴다. 접속사 or 뒤에는 동사원형 check를 쓰고, 목적어 자리에 the references를 쓰고, 이를 수식하는 과거분사 cited를 이어서 쓴다.

body:
[1]
Numerous surveys consistently highlight the growing trend of teenagers spending extensive hours on social media. This increased usage comes with potential risks, including addiction and exposure to misinformation and inappropriate content. Many adolescents struggle with managing their time and interactions on social media. To address these concerns, certain authorities are implementing legal restrictions on minors’ access to social media. For example, in some countries, like China, limits for social media have been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or maintain social media accounts and the other granting parents full access to their children’s online activities.
[2]
Despite these concerns, it is crucial to maintain a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, making it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving.
[3]
As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers’ social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever-changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?
