(A) Surveys indicate that teenagers are increasingly spending long periods on social media, which may expose them to various risks. (T/F)
(B) Some governments have introduced restrictions on minors’ social media use to address problems related to their online activities. (T/F)
(C) Social media can help teenagers develop a sense of identity and receive emotional support, especially when such support is limited in their communities. (T/F)
(D) Social media has little educational value beyond personal expression and social interaction. (T/F)
(E) The debate over teenagers’ social media use has begun to prioritize the benefits of social media over its potential risks. (T/F)

(A) 설문 조사들은 십 대들이 소셜 미디어에서 점점 더 오랜 시간을 보내고 있으며, 이는 그들을 다양한 위험에 노출시킬 수 있음을 보여 준다. (일치)
(B) 몇몇 정부는 청소년들의 온라인 활동과 관련된 문제를 해결하기 위해 미성년자의 소셜 미디어 사용에 대한 제한을 도입했다. (일치)
(C) 소셜 미디어는 청소년들이 정체성을 형성하고 정서적 지원을 받도록 도울 수 있으며, 특히 그들의 지역 사회에서 그러한 지원이 제한적일 때 그러하다. (일치)
(D) 소셜 미디어는 개인적 표현과 사회적 상호 작용을 넘어서는 교육적 가치가 거의 없다(→시사 문제에 대한 정보를 얻고 다양한 주제에 대한 지식을 습득하는 데 유용하다). (불일치)
(E) 청소년의 소셜 미디어 사용에 관한 논쟁은 소셜 미디어의 잠재적 위험보다 그 이점에 우선순위를 두기 시작했다.(→소셜 미디어 사용 규제가 개인의 문제인지, 공공의 문제인지에 관한 질문은 여전히 진행 중이다.) (불일치)

body:
[1]
Numerous surveys consistently highlight the growing trend of teenagers spending extensive hours on social media. This increased usage comes with potential risks, including addiction and exposure to misinformation and inappropriate content. Many adolescents struggle with managing their time and interactions on social media. To address these concerns, certain authorities are implementing legal restrictions on minors’ access to social media. For example, in some countries, like China, limits for social media have been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or maintain social media accounts and the other granting parents full access to their children’s online activities.
[2]
Despite these concerns, it is crucial to maintain a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, making it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving.
[3]
As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers’ social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever-changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?
윗글의 단락 [2]의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the influence of online trends on teenagers’ social interaction styles
the correlation between online participation and youth identity development
fostering teenagers’ face-to-face communication skills through group activities
improving teenagers’ academic focus through modern digital learning tools
the benefits of social media for teenagers’ personal, social, and intellectual development
solution: 소셜 미디어가 십 대에게 자신의 생각과 재능을 표현하고 자아 정체성을 형성할 기회를 제공하며, 또래와의 유대감 형성과 정서적 지원에 도움을 주고, 시사 정보를 접하거나 다양한 주제에 관한 지식을 습득하는 데 유용하다고 언급하며 소셜 미디어가 제공하는 다양한 이점을 설명하고 있으므로 이 글의 주제로 ❺ '십 대들의 개인적, 사회적, 지적 발달에 대한 소셜 미디어의 기여‘가 적절하다.

This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also ______. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.
[2]
Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called “lateral reading,” which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: encourages readers to create their own content
simplifies the process of checking factual accuracy
maintains consistent standards for online publications
prevents unverified information from circulating too widely
makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information
solution: 인터넷에서는 정보를 찾은 것은 비교적 쉽지만 이를 검증하거나 그 타당성을 확인하는 것은 그렇지 않다고 언급했으며, 과거에는 저자들이 충족해야 하는 출판 기준이 있었지만, 오늘날에는 인터넷이 수많은 사람의 출판 장벽을 없앴다는 내용과 역접의 however(하지만)으로 연결되어 있으므로 그들이 올린 정보의 신뢰성을 판단하기 어려워졌다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ❺ ‘독자들이 신뢰할 수 있고 타당한 정보를 찾는 일을 더 어렵게 만든다’가 적절하다.

body:
Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. (A)우리는 세계, 그러므로 정보 그 자체가 끊임없이 변화하고 있다는 것을 이해할 필요가 있다. 정보는 정체되어 있지 않으며, 독자 역시 그래서는 안 된다. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 도치구문을 사용할 것

need, should, neither, constantly evolve, the world, the reader, understand

body:
In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today’s words, one could say that the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s (A)[endorsement / skepticism] gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was (B)[authentic / fabricated]. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.
Single-Source Reading
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more (C)[prevalent / limited], readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer’s credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as “vertical reading.”
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: skepticism / fabricated / limited
endorsement / fabricated / limited
skepticism / authentic / prevalent
endorsement / authentic / limited
endorsement / fabricated / prevalent
solution:
(A) 앞에서 Doyle이 요정들과 함께 찍은 사진들이 초자연적 현상의 증거라고 주장하는 기사를 썼다고 했으므로, 그의 지지가 소녀들의 사진들에 신뢰성을 부여했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 endorsement(지지)가 적절하다.
(B) 이 사진과 관련된 사건을 유명한 작가가 관련된 가짜 뉴스의 한 일화로 소개하고 있으므로 소녀들이 그 사진이 진짜라고 주장하다가 거의 70년이 지나서야 꾸며낸 것이었다고 인정했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 fabricated(꾸며낸)가 적절하다.
(C) 인쇄기의 등장으로 책이 지식 전달 수단이 되었다고 설명하고 있으므로 문서 자료들이 더 널리 보급되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 prevalent(널리 퍼진)가 적절하다.

body:
Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author’s claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently.
As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire “fact-checkers” to evaluate their writers’ claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What does digital lateral reading enable readers to do to check the credibility of an author’s claims?
Why do many people and companies adopt lateral reading as their reading strategy?
What information helps readers decide which online sources are worth examining?
What specific role do "fact-checkers" play in media companies before publishing content?
What did recent research reveal about lateral reading compared to vertical reading?
solution: 가로 읽기를 하는 독자들이 저자의 주장의 신뢰성을 검토하기 위해 인터넷의 정보를 이용할 수 있는데, 브라우저를 사용하여 여러 웹사이트를 동시에 검토할 수 있다고 하였으나 출처를 비교하여 선택하는 것에 대해서는 언급하지 않았으므로 ❸ ‘어떤 정보가 독자들이 어떤 온라인 출처를 살펴볼 가치가 있는지 결정하는 데 도움이 되는가?‘라는 질문에는 답할 수 없다.

body:
Multiple-Source Reading
Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called “lateral reading,” which involves verifying information while (A)[reading / read] by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something (B)[what / that] you have read and gain insight.
For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information (C)[presenting / being presented], such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: read / that / presenting
reading / that / being presented
read / what / presenting
reading / what / being presented
reading / that / presenting
solution:
(A) 접속사 while 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 접속사 while을 생략하지 않은 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 you가 ‘읽는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 reading이 적절하다.
(B) 동사 read의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you have read)을 이끌어 선행사 something을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
*(B)는 본문에서 생략되었음
(C) 앞의 명사구 any type of information을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, 수식을 받는 any type of information이 ‘제시되고 있는’ 대상이므로 현재분사의 수동태(being p.p.)인 being presented가 적절하다.

body:
W: Good morning, everyone. My name is Mia and I’ll be your tour guide for today. Today we are going to visit three famous attractions in Barcelona. Right now, you are standing at the entrance of our first destination, Park Güell, (A)[designed / was designed] by Antoni Gaudi. Before I let you (B)[to look / look] around, I’m going to explain some of the park’s most notable features. Originally, this place was very dry with little rainfall. It also lacked water because it was on a slope. However, Gaudi was able to build systems to collect and store water. He believed (C)[what / that] it was possible to build a water system and even a fountain in an area with little water. As you explore the park, be sure to check out the little holes in the benches. When it rains, the rainwater filters down through the holes and is stored for later use.
위 담화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: designed / to look / what
was designed / look / that
was designed / to look / that
designed / look / what
designed / look / that
solution:
(A) 명사구 our first destination과의 동격을 나타내는 고유명사 Park Güell을 부연 설명하는 분사 자리이며, Park Güell이 ‘설계된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 designed가 적절하다.
(B) 동사 let은 ‘let+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 동사 let의 목적격보어 자리에 동사원형 look이 적절하다.
(C) 완전한 절(it ~ water)을 이끌어 동사 believed의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.

W: Good morning, everyone. My name is Mia and I’ll be your tour guide for today. Today we are going to visit three famous attractions in Barcelona. body:
Have you ever wondered, “What if I could run so fast that nobody could see me?” If you have asked this kind of question, you may be ready to become the next Galileo. The Italian scientist Galileo Galilei is famous for a thought experiment, which is an imaginary experiment designed to explore a mathematical or scientific hypothesis. With only his thoughts, (A)그는 다른 질량들을 지닌 물체들이 공기 저항 없이 같은 높이로부터 떨어뜨렸을 때 같은 속도로 떨어진다는 것을 입증하였다. With a hypothesis based on creativity and imagination, anyone can become a great scientist.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
drop, with, height, demonstrate, different masses, objects, should fall,
he ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ at the same speed when ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ in the absence of air resistance
answer: demonstrated that objects with different masses should fall, dropped from the same height
solution:
• 주어 he에 이어지는 동사 demonstrated를 쓰고, 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• ‘다른 질량들을 지닌 물체들’을 뜻하는 that절의 주어 objects with different masses를 쓰고, 당위성을 의미를 지닌 조동사 should와 동사 fall을 이어 쓴다.
• 분사구문을 사용해야 하므로 부사절 접속사 when 뒤에 주어와 동사 없이 분사를 써야 하며, 의미상 주어인 they(=objects with different masses)가 ‘떨어진’ 대상이므로 동사 drop을 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 dropped로 변형하여 쓰고 ‘같은 높이로부터’를 뜻하는 전치사구 from the same height를 이어 쓴다.

body:
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is (A)[what / that] it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height (B)[increases / increased] ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. However, the area of the feet supporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means that his feet (C)[will / would] be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased far more than the area of his feet.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: that / increases / will
what / increases / would
what / increased / would
that / increased / will
that / increased / would
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(it ~ effect)을 이끌어 be동사 is에 이어지는 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.
(B) 사람의 키가 10배가 되는 것은 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황 또는 실현 가능성이 희박한 상황이므로, 가정법 과거 ‘If+주어+과거동사 ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …’의 구조가 되어야 하므로, if절의 동사로 과거동사 increased가 알맞다.
(C) 그의 발이 증가된 무게를 지탱하느라 지나치게 많은 압력을 받을 것이라는 that절의 내용은 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황 또는 실현 가능성이 희박한 상황(무게가 1000배, 발의 면적이 100배가 되는 것)을 가정하고 있으므로, 가정을 나타내는 조동사 would가 알맞다.

body:
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, ⓐif there is no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. ⓑThis could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially made summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ에서 어법상 어색한 부분을 한 군데씩 찾아 각각 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
어색한 표현     알맞게 고친 표현

ⓑ ______ → ______
solution:
ⓐ ‘달이 없다면’은 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하고 있으므로 ‘If+주어+과거형 동사 ~, 주어+과거형 조동사+동사원형’의 가정법 과거를 써야 하며, 특히 be동사는 주어의 수에 관계없이 were을 쓰는 것이 원칙이므로, is를 were로 고친다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(This ~ patterns)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어 summers와 winters가 있으므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 making으로 고친다.

3. What if the oxygen concentration in the atmosphere doubled?
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, making up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil ⓐto generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would ⓑit be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
While more oxygen may seem ⓒbeneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are (A)______. Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially ⓓdisrupting the food chain. Dragonflies, for example, may become ⓔas largely as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.
Fortunately, you wouldn’t need to worry about giant insects chasing after you if this were to occur. If the oxygen concentration were to double, you would be able to run faster than you can right now. Considering that oxygen is used to break down energy so that muscles can use it, the increase in oxygen would help to use energy more efficiently and improve our capability for physical exercise. This leads us to expect that athletes would set new world records at the Olympics.
While these three thought experiments offer interesting possibilities, it is important to consider that they are simply based on imagination and have not been tested through scientific research.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ as largely as → as large as (‘~만큼 …한’의 의미를 갖는 원급 비교 'as+형용사/부사의 원급+as'의 구조가 쓰였으며, 동사 become의 보어가 as 사이에 들어가야 하므로, 부사 largely를 형용사 large로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(It ~ oil)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 동사가 아닌 준동사 자리이며, ‘열과 빛을 내기 위해’라는 뜻의 목적을 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to generate는 적절하다.
ⓑ 진주어인 to부정사구 to have~ atmosphere에 상응하는 가주어 자리이므로 it이 적절하다.
ⓒ 형용사 보어를 취하는 2형식 동사 seem의 보어 자리이므로 형용사 beneficial은 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(This ~ environment)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 This increase in insect size가 먹이 사슬을 ‘교란하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 disrupting은 적절하다.

Have you ever heard the expression “I love you to the moon and back”? This expression conveys a deep extent of love, and uses the great distance between the Earth and the Moon as a metaphor. While this expression is easily understood, there ⓐare idioms with a scientific background that may not be so obvious. One example is the phrase “once in a blue moon.” Although people may have seen a magnificent full moon ⓑbrightened the night sky or a tiny crescent resembling a clipped fingernail, ⓒwhat is highly unlikely that they have seen a blue moon. Surprisingly, this extraordinary event does occur. Normally, there is only one full moon in a month. However, every 2.5 years, there can be two full moons in the same month. The second moon ⓓis called a “blue moon,” and it occurs because the Moon completes its cycle of phases in only about 29.5 days. From this rare phenomenon of a blue moon emerged the use of the expression “once in a blue moon.” It describes something that ⓔhappens exceptionally infrequently.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓑ brightened → brightening (명사구 a magnificent full moon을 수식하는 분사 자리이며 a magnificent full moon이 밤하늘을 ‘밝히는’ 주체이므로, 과거분사 brightened를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 brightening으로 고친다.)
ⓒ what → it (진주어절(that ~ moon)에 상응하는 가주어 자리이므로 what을 가주어 it으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 절의 맨 앞에 있는 유도부사 there에 의해 주어와 동사가 도치되므로 뒤에 위치한 복수주어 idioms에 수일치한 복수동사 are는 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어 The second moon에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, The second moon이 a “blue moon”이라 ‘불리는’ 대상이므로 수동태(be동사+p.p.) is called는 적절하다.
ⓔ something을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 단수명사 something에 수일치한 단수동사 happens는 적절하다.

2. What if there were no Moon?
“O, swear not by the moon, the inconstant moon.” This is a famous line from Romeo and Juliet. Juliet warns Romeo not to swear his love by the Moon as it may change just as the Moon changes its shape. Although its appearance changes, the Moon is always present in the night sky and plays a crucial role in regulating the length of the day on Earth as well as the Earth’s seasons and weather patterns. Then, what would happen if there were no Moon?
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. (A)하지만 달이 없다면, 지구의 자전은 느려지지 않을 것이고 하루의 길이에 변화를 가져올 것이다. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• without을 사용한 가정법으로 시작할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
rotation, a change, the Earth‘s, slow down, result in, will
______ ______ ______, however, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ in the length of a day.
answer: Without the Moon, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change
solution:
• 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황(달이 없다면)을 가정하므로 without을 사용한 가정법 과거 구문 ‘Without+명사(구), 주어+과거형 조동사+동사원형’을 써야 한다. 따라서 Without the Moon을 쓰고 however 뒤에 주어 the Earth’s rotation, 조동사 will을 과거형 would로 변형하여 would not slow down을 차례대로 쓴다.
• 완전한 절(the ~ down)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지는 분사구문을 영작해야 하며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절 전체(the ~ down)가 변화를 ‘가져오는’ 주체이므로 ‘(어떤 결과)를 가져오다’를 뜻하는 구동사 result in을 현재분사 resulting in으로 변형하고 목적어 a change를 이어 쓴다.

While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as efficient as lungs at taking in air. (A)
Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. (B) If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. (C) However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. (D) This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain. (E)
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘예를 들면, 잠자리는 독수리만큼 커질 수 있으며, 이것은 생태계에서 포식자와 먹이의 균형을 변화시킨다.’라는 뜻으로, 연결어 for example(예를 들어)로 시작하므로, 이 문장 앞에는 곤충의 크기 증가가 생태계에 미치는 영향과 같은 일반적인 내용이 먼저 제시되어야 한다. (C) 앞에서 산소 농도가 두 배가 되면 곤충이 더 크게 자랄 수 있다고 했고, (D) 앞에서 이러한 곤충의 크기 증가가 생태 환경에 큰 영향을 미치며 먹이 사슬을 교란할 수 있다고 설명하고 있으므로, 이와 같은 일반적인 영향에 이어 구체적인 사례를 제시하는 주어진 문장이 (E)에 들어가면 자연스럽게 이어진다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (E)이다.

The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this ⓐhypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to ⓑsurface. However, the area of the feet supporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to ⓒsupport the increased weight because the mass would have increased far more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from ⓓaccumulating in the body. If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s ⓔvolume. However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. This shows that while we may wish to grow as tall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.

solution: ⓑ surface(표면적) → volume(용적)

body:
[1]
Have you ever wondered, “What if I could run so fast that nobody could see me?” If you have asked this kind of question, you may be ready to become the next Galileo. The Italian scientist Galileo Galilei is famous for a thought experiment, which is an imaginary experiment designed to explore a mathematical or scientific hypothesis. With only his thoughts, he demonstrated that objects with different masses should fall at the same speed when dropped from the same height in the absence of air resistance. With a hypothesis based on creativity and imagination, anyone can become a great scientist.
[2]
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would ______.
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth.
(A) The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially making summers hotter and winters colder.
(B) We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt.
(C) However, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees.
If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 달의 부재가 지구의 기후 패턴을 완전히 바꿔 놓을 것이라는 주어진 글 뒤에 서로 다른 계절이 나타나는 이유가 지구의 자전축 기울기 때문이며 달의 중력이 그 기울기를 안정시킨다고 설명하는 (B), However(그러나)를 통해 달이 없다면 자전축의 기울기가 0도에서 85도 사이에서 크게 변할 수 있다는 상반된 내용을 가정하는 (C), (C)의 마지막 문장에서 지구가 60도로 기울어졌다고 가정한 뒤, 60도일 때 지구의 한쪽 반구가 다른 반구보다 훨씬 많은 태양 에너지를 받게 되어 극심한 날씨 변화가 나타날 수 있다고 구체적으로 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
Have you ever heard the expression “I love you to the moon and back”? This expression conveys a deep extent of love, and uses the great distance between the Earth and the Moon as a metaphor. While this expression is easily understood, there are idioms with a scientific background that may not be so obvious. One example is the phrase “once in a blue moon.” (A) Although people may have seen a magnificent full moon brightening the night sky or a tiny crescent resembling a clipped fingernail, it is highly unlikely that they have seen a blue moon. (B) The Moon’s gravity also causes ocean tides to rise and fall regularly, affecting coastal environments around the world. (C) Surprisingly, this extraordinary event does occur. (D) Normally, there is only one full moon in a month. (E) However, every 2.5 years, there can be two full moons in the same month. The second moon is called a “blue moon,” and it occurs because the Moon completes its cycle of phases in only about 29.5 days. From this rare phenomenon of a blue moon emerged the use of the expression “once in a blue moon.” It describes something that happens exceptionally infrequently.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 관용 표현 ‘I love you to the moon and back’으로 흥미를 유발한 뒤, 약 2.5년마다 한 달에 보름달이 두 번 뜨는 희귀한 현상인 Blue Moon과 여기에서 유래한 ‘once in a blue moon’이라는 관용 표현을 예로 들어 설명하는 글이다. (A)에서는 파란 달을 실제로 보는 것이 매우 드물다고 설명하고, (C)에서는 이러한 현상이 실제로 발생한다고 이어서 설명한다. (D)에서는 일반적으로 한 달에 보름달이 한 번 나타난다고 설명하고, (E)에서는 약 2.5년마다 한 달에 두 번의 보름달이 나타날 수 있으며 두 번째 보름달을 파란 달이라고 설명한다. 그러나 (B) ‘달의 중력은 또한 해양의 조수가 규칙적으로 오르내리게 하여, 전 세계의 해안 환경에 영향을 미친다’는 파란 달의 발생과 관용 표현의 유래를 설명하는 흐름과 자연스럽게 연결되지 않으므로 (B)는 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world ⓐcuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was a rare and expensive luxury item that ⓑpeasants could not afford. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. So desired was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.” There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to ⓒreduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it elaborated one’s ⓓsocial status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such an ⓔundervalued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
it, seem, walk, from rocks, collect, women, harvest, the sea
→ Gim ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ in the past ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ during low tide ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: seems to have been harvested, by women who walked into the sea, to collect it from rocks
solution:
⦁‘보이는’ 것은 현재의 사실이므로 현재시제를 사용하되, seem을 단수주어 Gim에 수일치한 현재형 단수동사 seems로 변형한다. ‘~인 것 같다, ~인 것으로 보이다’라는 뜻의 ‘seem+to부정사’를 사용하되, 주어 Gim이 ‘채취되었던’ 대상이며, seems가 나타내는 현재보다 이전 과거의 일이므로, 수동형 완료부정사(to+have+been+p.p.)를 사용해 to have been을 쓴 후, harvest를 과거분사 harvested로 변형한다. 시간의 부사구 in the past 뒤에 행위자를 ‘by+명사’ 형태인 by women으로 쓴다.
⦁<조건>에 따라 관계대명사 who를 사용해 선행사 women을 수식하는 관계사절을 ‘who+주어가 없는 불완전한 절’ 형태로 쓴다. who가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리에 walk를 시제에 맞게 과거형 walked로 변형하고, ‘~로 걸어 들어가다’라는 뜻의 ‘walk into ~’를 사용해 전치사 into와 명사구 the sea를 쓴다.
⦁<조건>에 따라 부사적 용법 중 목적을 나타내는 to부정사를 사용해 ‘모으기 위해’라는 뜻으로 collect를 to부정사인 to collect로 변형한다. 목적어로 Gim을 가리키는 단수 지시대명사 it을 쓰고, 부사구 from rocks를 써서 완성한다.

body:
Gim in the Past
(A)김은 과거에 바위들에서 김을 모으기 위해 썰물 때 바다로 걸어 들어간 여인들에 의해 채취되었던 것으로 보입니다. It was so precious and scarce that only royalty, like kings and queens, and the very wealthy had the privilege to afford it. During the Joseon period, ten sheets of gim were said to cost twenty cotton rolls, which cost a lot at the time. So you can imagine how expensive gim was. You might be wondering how gim became more affordable and readily available in recent years. Two figures are behind the striking popularity of gim today.

various traditional recipes using gim during the Joseon period
modern technological advances in processing and packaging gim
two key figures who contributed to making gim widely accessible
historical records of trade conflicts caused by the high price of gim
solution:

body:
ⓐIt is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man named Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with ⓑsome seaweed attaching to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and found (A)it to be delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea ⓒwhere he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people to enjoy gim, but (B)it was not ⓓenough productive to cultivate as much gim as we consume today.
ⓔTo us surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. ⓕWhile researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, ⓖwhich function like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching (C)them to cultivating frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓑ attaching → attached (전치사 with 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 some seaweed가 온 뒤, 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)(~가 …한 상태로)’를 이루는 분사구 또는 ‘~가 있는’이라는 뜻으로 쓰인 전치사 with의 목적어인 명사구 some seaweed를 수식하는 분사구가 이어지는 것은 알맞으나, 앞의 명사구가 ‘부착된’ 대상이므로, ‘attach ~ to …(~을 …에 부착하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘~ be attached to …(~가 …에 부착되다)’를 사용해 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 attaching을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 attached로 고친다.)
ⓓ enough productive → productive enough (enough가 부사로 쓰여 형용사나 부사를 수식할 때, 형용사/부사의 뒤에 위치하므로, enough productive를 productive enough의 어순으로 고친다. 그 외, was의 보어로 형용사 productive가 쓰인 것과, ‘형용사/부사+enough+to부정사(구)(~할 만큼 충분히 …한/…하게)’를 이루는 to부정사 to cultivate는 모두 알맞다.)
ⓔ us → our (‘~에게 …하게도’라는 뜻은 ‘to+소유격+추상명사’로 나타내므로, 전치사 To와 추상명사 surprise 사이에 쓰인 목적격 형태의 us를 소유격인 our로 고친다.)
오답
ⓕ 주절(she discovered ~) 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 분사구문이 쓰일 수 있으며, 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사를 남겨둔 ‘접속사+분사~’ 형태로 쓸 수 있고, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 she가 타동사로 쓰인 research(~을 연구하다)의 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the annual life cycle of seaweed가 있으므로, 접속사 While 뒤에 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 researching이 쓰인 While researching은 알맞다.

body:
Did you know that gim is also eaten in South Africa? In the first half of 2017, Korean gim accounted for approximately 43% of the South African market. Not surprisingly, Korea is the world’s largest gim producer and exporter, dominating roughly 70% of the global gim market. According to Graph 1, gim exports overseas were only $100 million in 2010, but have steadily increased year after year, and reached $600 million in 2020. To where is gim exported? In 2019, the top three export destinations for Korean gim were the United States, Japan, and China. Furthermore, the number of export destinations is continuously increasing. According to Graph 2, gim was only exported to 64 countries in 2010, but by September 2021, gim exports had expanded to 112 countries worldwide.
As more countries begin to eat gim, it is being consumed in new ways depending on the country. For example, in the United States, as Americans are paying more attention to gim as a healthy food, they enjoy roasted gim snacks with almonds and coconut added. Also, Thailand is producing its own gim snacks by importing gim from Korea and processing it with popular Thai flavors, such as tom yam kung (a sweet and sour flavor) and grilled squid. What is more, gim can be easily added to a variety of dishes. For example, the Culinary Institute of America, an internationally famous culinary university, published a recipe book titled Fabulous and Flavorful Gim. It includes gim recipes, such as gim flavored popcorn, gim fried chicken, and even gim ice cream. It is quite clear that gim is being used to create new and delicious types of food and to give new flavors to old favorites.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Global Rise of Korean Gim
Amazing Seaweed Snacks in the World
How Korean Dishes Captivate the World
The Secret to the Success of Korean Seafood Exports
Why Korean Gim is Replacing Traditional Snacks in the West

This is a NASA satellite image of the area near Wando, ⓐ[taking / taken] from space. NASA initially wondered what the black lines were and later discovered they are farms ⓑ[that / where] grow gim. From this picture, you can guess that Korea is currently producing a lot of gim. It is relatively cheap and is frequently used in various Korean dishes, such as gimbap (a type of seaweed rice roll), gimjaban (roasted seaweed), and gimbugak (a type of crispy seaweed and rice chip). However, it ⓒ[used / was used] to be very expensive in the past, so not everyone could enjoy it as much as people can today.

다음 글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: taken that was used
taking that used
taken that used
taking where was used
taken where used
solution:
ⓐ 완전한 절(This ~ Wando) 뒤에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로 이어져 흐름상 앞의 명사구 a NASA satellite image of the area near Wando를 부연 설명하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사 자리이며, 부연 설명의 대상인 앞의 명사구가 ‘촬영된’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 taken이 알맞다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(grow gim)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사 farms를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
ⓒ 흐름상 주어 it이 가리키는 gim이 과거에 매우 비쌌다는 의미가 되어야 하므로, ‘used to+동사원형(~했었다(지금은 아니다))’의 used가 알맞다. 참고로, 뒤에 이어진 to부정사구(to be ~ past)가 목적을 나타내지 않으므로 ‘be used+to부정사(~하는 데 사용되다)’는 어색하다.

body:
Gim in the Future
The future of the gim industry appears bright, ⓐas global demand for gim is expecting to rise in the coming years for a couple of reasons. First of all, gim is a highly valued product on the global market as a healthy food due to its nutritional properties. One hundred grams of gim ⓑcontain sixteen times more dietary fiber than the same amount of cabbage, two times more protein than beans, and four times more calcium than milk. Gim’s high nutrient content will make it a popular choice among consumers ⓒwho are keenly interested in a healthy diet. Second, gim is (A)______. A French magazine once published an article titled “Koreans who cook seaweed for Earth,” ⓓwhich listed seaweed, including gim, as one of the most valuable food for future generations, along with Spanish tomatoes, Latin American beans, and Canadian salmon. In fact, research shows ⓔthat seaweed has been shown to capture and store CO₂ as it grows. For example, one ton of seaweed absorbs three times ⓕas much CO₂ as a maple tree. As demonstrated here, gim has many benefits. Who knows? There may come a day ⓖwhen gim is found on every dinner table around the world.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ expecting → expected (주절 뒤에 콤마(,)로 as가 이끄는 부사절이 이어진 것은 알맞으나, 주어인 global demand for gim이 오를 것으로 ‘기대되는’ 대상이므로 ‘expect+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …할 것으로 예상하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘be expected+to부정사(…할 것으로 예상되다)’를 써야 한다. 따라서 is와 to부정사인 to rise 사이의 현재분사 expecting을 과거분사 expected로 고친다.)
ⓓ food → foods (콤마(,) 뒤에 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 an article titled “Koreans who cook seaweed for Earth”를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이룬 것과 as가 ’~로서‘라는 뜻의 전치사로 쓰여 목적어로 명사구가 이어진 것 또한 모두 알맞으나, ‘가장 ~한 …들 중 하나’라는 뜻으로 ‘one+of+the+최상급+복수명사’를 쓰므로 one of the most valuable 뒤의 단수명사 food를 복수명사 foods로 고친다.)
오답
ⓔ shows의 목적어 자리에 명사절 접속사 that이 쓰여 완전한 절을 이끄는 것은 알맞다. 또한, 목적어절의 주어 seaweed가 현재 ‘입증된’ 상태임을 나타내기 위해 단수인 주어에 단수 조동사로 수일치한 현재완료수동태(have[has]+been+p.p.)로 has been shown이 쓰인 것과 수동 표현인 ‘be shown+to부정사(~한다는 것이 입증되다)’의 to부정사구가 쓰여 to 뒤에 두 개의 동사원형 capture와 store가 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결된 후 공통의 목적어로 CO₂가 이어진 것은 모두 알맞다.

body:
Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. So desired was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.” There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it elaborated one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: In the past, black pepper was an expensive luxury that ordinary working people could not purchase.
Black pepper served as a payment method for rents and taxes in certain regions.
Before modern oral hygiene tools appeared, black pepper was used to alleviate bad breath.
People in the past believed that black pepper could help cure various medical conditions like sleep troubles and skin irritation.
It was believed that if someone placed black pepper on their desk, something ominous would happen to their social status and wealth.

Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching them to cultivating frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

choices: so it completely replaced natural collection methods in a very short period
but it was not productive enough to cultivate as much gim as we consume today
but it led to severe conflicts among local fishermen over farming territories

and it immediately made gim one of the most exported items to neighboring countries
solution:
다음 단락에 영국 과학자 Kathleen Drew-Baker의 포자를 통한 번식 방법 덕에 김의 대량 생산이 가능해져서 김이 더욱 저렴해지고 널리 보급되었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 김여익의 양식법 덕분에 더 많은 사람이 김을 즐길 수 있게 되었지만, 그 방법을 통해 김을 대량 생산하는 것에는 한계가 있었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘하지만 그것은 오늘날 우리가 소비하는 만큼의 많은 김을 재배하기에 충분히 생산적이지 않았다’가 알맞다.

body:
It is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man named Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with some seaweed attached to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and found it to be delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea where he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people to enjoy gim, ______.
To our surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. While researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, which function like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching them to cultivating frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

윗글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 각각 쓰시오.
During the reign of King Injo, Yeoik Gim successfully cultivated gim using ______ planted along the sea, and later, British scientist Kathleen Drew-Baker developed a method of reproducing seaweed through ______, enabling mass production of gim and making gim more ______ and readily ______.
solution: [요약문] 인조 통치기에 김여익은 바다를 따라 심은 기둥을 이용해 성공적으로 김을 양식했고, 이후 영국인 과학자 Kathleen Drew-Baker는 포자를 통해 해조류를 번식시키는 방법을 개발했으며, 이는 김의 대량 생산을 가능하게 해 김을 더 저렴하고 쉽게 구할 수 있게 만들었다.

(A) What is more, gim can be easily added to a variety of dishes. For example, the Culinary Institute of America, an internationally famous culinary university, published a recipe book titled Fabulous and Flavorful Gim.
(B) Also, Thailand is producing its own gim snacks by importing gim from Korea and processing it with popular Thai flavors, such as tom yam kung (a sweet and sour flavor) and grilled squid.
(C) It includes gim recipes, such as gim flavored popcorn, gim fried chicken, and even gim ice cream. It is quite clear that gim is being used to create new and delicious types of food and to give new flavors to old favorites.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 김이 각 나라에 따라 새로운 방식으로 소비되고 있다는 것과 미국의 사례를 설명한 주어진 글에 이어, Also(또한)를 사용해 태국의 사례를 추가 설명한 (B), What is more(게다가)를 사용해 김은 다양한 요리에 쉽게 곁들여질 수도 있다는 또 다른 측면과 함께 그 예시로 The Culinary Institute of America의 <Fabulous and Flavorful Gim>이라는 요리책을 언급한 (A), 앞의 요리책을 It으로 지칭해 그 책에는 김 맛 팝콘, 김 프라이드 치킨, 심지어 김 아이스크림 같은 다양한 김 요리법이 포함되어 있다고 구체적으로 설명한 (C)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. (A)후추는 너무 열망되어 그것은 ‘블랙 골드’와 ‘향신료의 제왕’ 같은 화려한 별명을 얻었습니다. There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it elaborated one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, (B)both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• So로 시작하고, 접속사 that을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 16단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
and “king of spices”, fancy, pepper, earn, desired, “black gold”, it, like
→ ______
answer: So desired was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.”
solution:
⦁‘…할 정도로 매우 …한/…하게, 매우 ~해서 …하다’를 뜻하는 ‘so+형용사/부사+that+완전한 절‘ 구문을 활용하되, <조건>에 따라 So로 시작하여 보어인 형용사구 So desired를 먼저 쓰고 이어지는 절에 동사 도치를 적용해 ’be동사+주어‘ 어순으로 was pepper를 쓴다.
⦁‘so+형용사/부사+that+완전한 절‘ 구문에서 that은 생략될 수 있으나 <조건>에 따라 접속사 that을 쓴 후, 완전한 절을 연결한다. that이 이끄는 절의 주어로 pepper를 가리키는 지시대명사 it을 쓰고, 시제에 맞게 동사 earn을 과거형 earned로 변형한 후, 형용사 fancy를 사용해 목적어인 명사구 fancy nicknames를 쓴다. 이어서 ’~와 같은‘을 뜻하는 전치사 like와 명사구 “black gold” and “king of spices”를 쓴다.

It was so precious and scarce that only royalty, like kings and queens, and the very wealthy had the privilege to afford it. During the Joseon period, ten sheets of gim were said to cost twenty cotton rolls, which cost a lot at the time. So you can imagine how (B)[expensive / cheap] gim was. You might be wondering how gim became more affordable and readily available in recent years. Two figures are behind the striking (C)[popularity / decline] of gim today.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)

low expensive decline
low expensive popularity
high cheap popularity
high cheap decline
solution:

high 높은
high tide 만조(滿潮)
(B) 조선 시대에 김 10장이 면포 20필과 같은 값이었으며 면포는 당시 매우 비쌌다고 설명하므로, 이를 통해 김이 얼마나 비쌌는지 상상할 수 있을 것이라는 흐름이 되는 expensive(비싼)가 알맞다.
cheap 값싼, 저렴한

decline 쇠퇴, 감소

body:
Gim in the Future
The future of the gim industry appears bright, as global demand for gim is expected to rise in the coming years for a couple of reasons. First of all, gim is a highly valued product on the global market as a healthy food due to its nutritional properties. One hundred grams of gim contain sixteen times more dietary fiber than the same amount of cabbage, two times more protein than beans, and four times more calcium than milk. Gim’s high nutrient content will make it a popular choice among consumers who are keenly interested in a healthy diet. Second, gim is environmentally friendly. A French magazine once published an article titled “Koreans who cook seaweed for Earth,” which listed seaweed, including gim, as one of the most valuable foods for future generations, along with Spanish tomatoes, Latin American beans, and Canadian salmon. In fact, research shows that seaweed has been shown to capture and store CO₂ as it grows. For example, one ton of seaweed absorbs three times as much CO₂ as a maple tree. As demonstrated here, gim has many benefits. Who knows? There may come a day when gim is found on every dinner table around the world.

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What are the prospects of the gim industry in the coming years?
How much protein does gim contain compared to beans?
Among which consumers will gim become popular?
What was the name of the French magazine that published an article on gim?
What is the impact of gim on the environment?

body:
W: What would happen if all the fish in the world suddenly vanished? First, people around the world would face food shortages. Millions of people living near coastal areas live on fish. If all fish were gone, people might face starvation due to lack of food. Second, Earth’s carbon levels would increase. The oceans store a huge amount of carbon. Tiny marine plants absorb carbon, and fish eat them. Fish then swim down and store the carbon deep in the ocean. Without fish, Earth’s carbon levels would increase, worsening climate change.

It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was ⓑcharmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. solution:
ⓑ does → is
(상관 접속사 ‘not only A but (also) B(A뿐만 아니라 B도 역시)’ 구문에서 부정어 not only에 의해 이어지는 절의 주어와 동사가 도치되어 단수주어인 the ocean에 수일치한 단수동사가 주어 앞에 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 형용사 full을 보어로 취하는 ‘be full of ~(~로 가득하다)’의 be동사를 써야 하므로, does를 is로 고친다.)
ⓒ naming → named
(앞의 명사구 the legendary marine biologist를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 수 있으나, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘이름이 지어진’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’name+목적어+목적격보어(이름)(~에게 …라는 이름을 지어주다)‘의 목적격보어에 해당하는 Sylvia Earle이 이어져 있으므로, naming을 수동 표현인 ’be named+이름(…라는 이름이 지어지다)‘의 과거분사 named로 고친다.)

(B) Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. (C) Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. 다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: Earle은 NOAA의 첫 여성 수석 과학자로서 해양 연구와 보전에 우선순위를 두는 것으로 NOAA의 초점을 전환하려고 했으나 표현과 행동의 자유에 대한 제약으로 사임했고, 민간 부문에서 표현의 자유를 얻어 제약 없이 자신의 전문 지식과 경험을 활용하여 해양 보호 캠페인을 했다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로, 민간 기업에서 일할 때 발생할 수 있는 어려움을 깨달았다는 내용인 (D) ‘그녀는 과학적 우선순위가 상업적 이해관계와 항상 일치하는 것이 아니기 때문에 민간 기업에서 일하는 것이 어려울 수 있다는 것 또한 깨달았다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats ⓐsituated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge just couldn’t cope with ⓑthe idea of men and women living together underwater,” she said. The following year, ⓒhaving been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and (A)______.
Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts’ historic moon landing.
In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures ⓓthat flashed like stars against the darkness. (B)그것들 중에는 자신을 방어하기 위해 빛나는 액체를 내뿜는 심해 오징어와 같이 그녀가 연구했지만 한 번도 본 적이 없는 몇몇 종들도 있었다.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day ⓔwhen human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: which were situated in the Virgin Islands
ⓑ: the idea of men and women’s living together underwater
ⓒ: as she was chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project
ⓓ: which flashed like stars against the darkness
ⓔ: that human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater
solution: ⓒ 분사구문은 흐름상 적절한 접속사를 사용해 부사절로 전환할 수 있으므로 접속사 as와 주절 주어와 동일한 부사절의 주어로 she를 사용해 부사절로 바꾸는 것은 알맞으나, 수동형 완료 분사구문(having+been+p.p.)인 having been chosen을 사용해 주절의 동사 spent가 나타내는 과거 시점보다 더 먼저 일어난 일을 나타내며 수동의 의미를 포함하는 것이므로, 부사절에 단순 과거 수동태(was/were+p.p.)가 아닌 과거완료 수동태(had+been+p.p.)를 써서 as she had been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project로 전환해야 한다.

For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, ______. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. body:
In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Earle walked on the seafloor at a depth of 381 meters for two hours without a cable.
As Earle moved deeper into the ocean, she was captivated by the creatures that glittered like stars in the darkness.
Earle confirmed that the deep-sea squid she had studied released a glowing liquid to attract prey.
Earle placed a flag on the ocean floor to highlight the importance of ocean exploration, linking the moment to Neil Armstrong’s first step on the Moon.
Earle’s accomplishment paved the way for humanity to appreciate and value life beneath the sea.
solution: Earle이 매료된 생물들 중에는 자신을 방어하기 위해 빛나는 액체를 내뿜는 심해 오징어와 같이 이전에 연구했지만 한 번도 본 적이 없는 종들도 있었다고 했으므로, ❸ ‘Earle은 그녀가 연구했던 심해 오징어가 먹이를 유인하기 위해 빛나는 액체를 방출했다는 것을 확인했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

body:
Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, increasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis.
(A) Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, rethinking industrial fishing practices, restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution entering the sea. By prioritizing ocean health, we can ⓐ[constrain / unlock] its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.
(B) Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes have been found to ⓑ[surpass / fall behind] plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean.
(C) Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that has dissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a ⓒ[beneficial / detrimental] material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming. Nevertheless, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet saving function depends on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and aid in the planet’s decarbonization.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 기후 변화로 인해 해양은 심각한 피해를 입기도 하지만, 동시에 이러한 글로벌 위기의 잠재적 해결책이 될 수 있다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 바다가 기후 위기의 해결책이 될 수 있다는 내용에 대해 바다가 대기 중 이산화탄소를 포집하고 저장하는 데 중요한 역할을 하며, 육지보다 훨씬 많은 탄소, 흔히 ‘블루 카본’이라는 것을 보유한다는 구체적인 근거를 제시하는 (B), 앞서 언급된 ‘블루 카본’의 의미를 ‘블랙 카본’과 비교해 설명한 뒤, 지구 보호 기능을 수행하는 해양의 능력이 그것의 건강에 달려 있으며 그에 따라 Duarte 박사와 그의 팀은 해양 건강의 회복 및 지구의 탈탄소화를 돕기 위한 실행 가능한 행동 계획을 제안한다는 내용의 (C), Duarte 박사와 그의 팀을 Their로 가리켜 그들이 제안하는 긴급한 권고 사항이 포함하는 내용을 구체적으로 설명하고 기후 변화에 대한 해결책으로서 해양 건강을 우선시해야 할 필요성을 강조하면서 마무리한 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: constrain surpass detrimental
unlock surpass detrimental
constrain fall behind beneficial
unlock surpass beneficial
unlock fall behind detrimental
solution:
ⓐ 해양이 기후 변화로 인한 글로벌 위기의 잠재적 해결책이라고 했으므로, 해양을 건강하게 유지함으로써 기대되는 효과로서, 기후 변화에 대한 해결책으로서 해양의 잠재력을 이끌어 낼 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 unlock((잠재력 등)을 끌어내다)이 알맞다.
ⓑ 지구의 70%를 차지하는 바다는 대기 중 이산화탄소를 포집하는 데 중요한 역할을 하며, 육지보다 16배나 많은 탄소를 보유하고 있다고 설명하므로, 해양 생태계가 탄소를 포집하고 저장하는 데 있어 육지 식물을 능가한다는 흐름이 되는 surpass(~을 능가하다, ~보다 뛰어나다)가 알맞다.
ⓒ 블루 카본은 해양에 저장되어 지구 온난화를 방지한다는 사실과 대조되는 내용이 While(~한 반면)에 의해 이어져야 하며, 화석 연료를 태울 때 발생한다는 설명이 함께 언급되므로, 블랙 카본은 해로운 물질로서 기후 변화의 주요 원인이 된다는 흐름이 되는 detrimental(유해한)이 알맞다.

We live surrounded by cloth. We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. Wearing clothes (A)[is / are] a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. Textiles ─ artificial and natural ─ have shaped and changed the world (B)[which / where] we live in. The history of textiles is almost as old as human civilization, and as time has passed, it has been more and more enriched. Exploring how textiles have changed the world helps us (C)[understand / understanding] how human civilization has evolved.

is / which / understanding

(B) 전치사 in의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we live in)을 이끌어 선행사 the world를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.

body:
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. ⓐ당연히 그녀는 그 불쾌한 물체를 건져 냈고, 그녀는 놀랍게도 그 차가 고치의 막을 녹였다는 것을 알게 되었다. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk were eased, and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 과거완료를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
dissolve, to, fish, find, the tea, the coating, amazement, of, the offending object
Naturally, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ out, and ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: she fished the offending object, to her amazement, she found that the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon
solution:
• 주어 she 뒤에 ‘~을 건져내다’를 뜻하는 구동사 fish ~ out을 쓰되, 뒤에 부사 out이 있으므로 시제를 맞춰 동사 fished를 쓰고 목적어 the offending object를 쓴다.
• ‘to one’s+감정 명사‘를 사용하여 ’그녀가 놀랍게도‘를 뜻하도록 to her amazement를 쓴다.
• 주어 she, 동사 found를 쓰고 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• 그녀(she)가 알게 된(found) 것보다 차(the tea)가 고치의 막(the coating of the cocoon)을 녹인 것이 더 이전에 일어난 일이므로 that절의 주어 the tea에 이어 과거완료 had dissolved를 쓰고 목적어 the coating of the cocoon을 이어 쓴다.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Silk production is believed to have started when a cocoon accidentally fell into Leizu’s cup of tea. (T/F)
(B) After discovering a lump of soft fibers, Leizu unwound it into a thread more than 600 meters long. (T/F)
(C) The fabric made from silk was smooth and shiny, while also feeling cool when touched. (T/F)
(D) At first, silk was widely available to ordinary people, but its use was later limited to the Emperor and his close associates. (T/F)
(E) Silk clothing and decorations became less common among Chinese people. (T/F)
choices: F-T-T-T-F
F-T-T-F-F
T-T-T-F-F
T-F-T-T-F
T-T-T-T-F
solution:
차례대로 T-T-T-F-F이다.
(A) 비단 생산은 고치 하나가 우연히 Leizu의 찻잔에 떨어지면서 시작된 것으로 여겨진다. (일치)
(B) 부드러운 섬유 덩어리를 발견한 후, Leizu는 그것을 풀어 600미터가 넘는 길이의 실로 만들었다. (일치)
(C) 비단으로 만들어진 직물은 매끄럽고 반짝였으며, 만졌을 때 시원한 느낌이 났다. (일치)
(D) 처음에는(→나중에는) 비단이 일반 사람들에게 널리 이용 가능했지만, 나중에는(→처음에는) 그것의 사용이 황제와 그의 가까운 사람들에게만 제한되었다. (불일치)
(E) 비단으로 만든 옷과 장식품은 중국인들 사이에서 덜(→더) 흔해졌다. (불일치)

It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. ⓐ당연히 그녀는 그 불쾌한 물체를 건져 냈고, 그녀는 놀랍게도 그 차가 고치의 막을 녹였다는 것을 알게 되었다. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk were eased, and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the results of efforts to create comfortable and soft fabrics
the discovery of silk and the growth of China’s silk industry
the step-by-step process of extracting silk threads from cocoons
the use of silk as a means of displaying wealth by the ruling class
the historical relationship between tea culture and textile production
solution:
Leizu가 차를 마시던 중 고치에서 부드러운 섬유를 발견한 일화를 통해 비단의 기원을 설명하고, 이후 제한된 비단의 사용에서 점차 범위가 점차 확대되면서 중국에서 비단 생산이 하나의 큰 산업으로 발전했음을 설명하고 있으므로 이 글의 주제로 ② ‘비단의 발견과 중국 비단 산업의 성장’이 적절하다.

On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission ⓐto take humans to the moon. One of the greatest challenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and ⓑbe able to withstand extreme temperatures ─ a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company ⓒwhich won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear.
(A) Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. ⓓWhat made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved.
(B) The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit ⓔmaking almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines.
(C) In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time.
It remains the most complex space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: NASA에 솔루션을 제안한 8개사 중, 아폴로 우주복 계약을 따낸 곳은 다른 업체만큼 크지도 않은 여성 속옷으로 명성을 얻은 업체였다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 이 회사를 The company로 이어받아, 이 회사가 개발한 우주복의 특징(직물로 만들어진 더 부드럽고 유연한 우주복)을 소개하는 (B), (B)에서 언급한 여자 재봉사들(seamstresses)을 Their로 받아 이들의 기술이 여성 속옷을 만들면서 습득한 것임을 설명하는 (A), (A)의 마지막 문장에서 관련된 층과 구성 요소의 수 때문에 우주복 제작 작업이 매우 어려웠다고 언급한 뒤 우주복이 실제로 얼마나 복잡하게 만들어졌는지 구체적인 수치를 제시하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk were (A)[eased / tightened], and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the (B)[earliest / latest] evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, (C)[prompting / hindering] the development of the civilizations.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: tightened / earliest / prompting
eased / latest / prompting
eased / earliest / hindering
tightened / after / hindering
eased / earliest / prompting
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 점점 더 많은 사람들이 비단옷을 입고 집을 비단 장식으로 꾸미는 것이 보이게 되었다고 했으므로 비단의 사용 제한이 느슨해졌다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 eased(느슨해진)가 적절하다.
tighten (규정∙법 등)을 강화하다
(B) 비단 교역은 실크로드가 기원전 2세기에 공식적으로 열리기 이전에 실제로 시작된 것으로 여겨지므로, 기원전 1070년경의 이집트 미라의 머리카락에서 비단실이 발견된 것은 비단 교역의 ‘최초의’ 증거라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 earliest(최초의)가 적절하다.
latest 최근의
(C) 실크로드를 통해 비단뿐만 아니라 향신료, 희귀 금속, 이국적인 동물들 그리고 종교, 예술 양식, 기술까지도 공유되었다고 했으므로 문명의 발달을 촉진했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 prompting(~을 촉진하는)이 적절하다.
hinder 방해하다

body:
Technology Doping
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material ⓐwhat imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once ⓑto increase buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit.
In later competitions, swimmers ⓒwearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. (A)______, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. They also dictated that the fabric used ⓓto make the suits must be breathable.
“Technology doping” in sports means the practice of gaining a competitive edge by using technology to improve performance. This can be against the spirit of fair play. (B)______, since most sports require equipment of some sort, ⓔit can be tricky to determine what is technology doping and what is not. Some argue that it is a natural progress coming from scientific development, while others claim it undermines human spirit and effort, ensuring that rich athletes have an advantage over poor ones.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓐ what → that (주어가 없는 불완전한 절(imitated shark skin)을 이끌어 선행사 a material을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 주격 관계대명사 that으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 완전한 절(some ~ once)에 접속사 없이 이어져 ‘부력을 늘리기 위해’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로 목적의 의미를 갖는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to increase는 적절하다.
ⓒ 명사 swimmers를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, swimmers가 수영복을 ‘입는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 wearing은 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(They ~ used)에 접속사 없이 이어져 ‘만들기 위해’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로 목적의 의미를 갖는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to make는 적절하다.
ⓔ 주격보어 tricky 뒤에 이어지는 진주어 to determine에 상응하는 가주어 자리이므로 it은 적절하다.

For example / Moreover
Therefore / Furthermore

solution:

(B) 빈칸 앞 문장에서 기술 도핑이 스포츠의 정정당당한 경쟁 정신에 반할 수 있다는 견해를 제시한 뒤, 빈칸 뒤에서는 대부분의 스포츠가 어느 정도 장비를 필요로 하기 때문에 무엇이 기술 도핑이고 무엇이 아닌지를 구분하기 어렵다는 상반된 견해를 제시하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 But(그러나), However(그러나)가 적절하다.

body:
Various styles and types of textiles can be used in art. In textile art, blue jeans, not water paints, can be used to draw pictures. Beautiful threads replace photos of scenic views. These types of textiles can be brilliant tools for expanding artistic creativity.
Ian Berry, Denim Art
Have you ever imagined painting with clothes, not on clothes? Surprisingly, Ian Berry succeeded in this and makes art out of blue jeans. His art looks like a painting, but people suddenly notice the beauty in blue jeans when they look at his art. He collects denim of every shade and uses it to create the shading and the sense of perspective in his portraits, landscapes, and other unique works of art. With just his hands, scissors, and glue, he creates almost three-dimensional pieces. He has been making realistic installations of denim for many years. He uses discarded jeans, cuts them up into pieces, and, like a painter, sorts them according to color. At first glance, the work seems flat, but a closer look reveals different layers of denim placed on top of and over each other. They are in fact denim collages. They are almost impossible to distinguish from paintings.

다음 글을 읽고 아래 질문에 대한 답을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸을 완성하시오.
(1) Why does Ian collects denim of every shade and uses it?
→ He does so to ______.
(2) What are the four things Ian uses to create realistic installation art?
→ He uses ______, ______, ______ and, ______.
answer:
(1) create the shading and the sense of perspective (in his portraits, landscapes, and other unique works of art)
(2) his hands, scissors, glue, discarded jeans
solution:
질문
(1) Ian은 왜 모든 색조의 데님을 수집하는가?
→ 그는 (자신의 초상화, 풍경화 그리고 다른 독특한 예술 작품에서) 음영과 원근감을 만들기 위해 그렇게 한다.
(2) Ian이 사실적인 설치 미술 작품을 만들기 위해 사용하는 네 가지는 무엇인가?
→ 그는 손, 가위, 풀, 그리고 버려진 청바지를 사용한다.

body:
Teresa Lim, Embroidery Art
People usually take pictures of scenic views, but Teresa Lim paints pictures of tourist spots with a needle and thread when she travels the world. She embroiders places she visits in surprising detail. This method of preserving memories ⓐlet her truly take in her surroundings. She spends time sitting in one place, observing details and ⓑstitching as the scene reveals itself. She says on her website ⓒwhere her designs “seek to erase the lines and boundaries between being an illustrator and a textile designer.” Her art is a delightful fusion of a canvas and a camera that ⓓprojects travel scenes onto fabric. She recreates ⓔwhat she sees on cloth and eliminates the need for a vacation photo album.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓐ 주어의 핵이 단수명사 method이므로 단수주어와 수일치하도록 let을 단수동사 lets로 고친다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(her ~ designer.”)을 이끌어 동사 says의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 where를 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다. 참고로 장소를 나타내는 부사구 on her website가 동사와 목적어절 사이에 삽입되어 있다.

solution:

오답
① Teresa Lim은 사진을 찍는 대신, 자수를 이용하여 장소의 이미지를 만든다.
② Teresa Lim은 자신이 방문한 장소를, 천에 그것의 세부적인 모습들을 바느질하면서 주의 깊게 관찰한다.
③ 한 장소에서 시간을 보내는 것은 Teresa Lim이 주변 풍경에 더 세심하게 주의를 기울일 수 있게 한다.

body:
Cloth That Connected the Worlds
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk were eased, and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, ______.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: making China fall behind other countries culturally
prompting the development of the civilizations
accelerating the isolation of Eastern empires
helping people preserve their local religions
leading to the monopoly of silk production
solution:
빈칸 앞에서 실크로드를 통해 비단뿐만 아니라 향신료, 희귀 금속, 이국적인 동물이 교환되고 종교, 예술 양식, 기술이 공유되었다고 설명하고 있으므로, 이러한 다양한 물질적·문화적 교류의 결과로 문명의 발전이 촉진되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ② ‘문명들의 발전을 촉진했다’가 적절하다.
오답
① 중국이 문화적으로 다른 나라들에 뒤처지게 만들다
③ 동방 제국들의 고립을 가속했다
④ 사람들이 자신들의 지역 종교를 보존하도록 도왔다
⑤ 비단 생산의 독점으로 이어졌다

Technology ⓐDoping
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. (A) At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. (B) It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin. (C) The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water ⓑresistance, and added ⓒbuoyancy by trapping air. (D) In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit. (E)
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.
“Technology doping” in sports means the practice of gaining a competitive ⓓedge by using technology to improve performance. This can be against the spirit of fair play. However, since most sports require equipment of some sort, ㉠무엇이 기술 도핑이고 무엇이 아닌지를 판단하는 것은 까다로울 수 있다. Some argue that it is a natural progress coming from scientific development, while others claim it ⓔundermines human spirit and effort, ensuring that rich athletes have an advantage over poor ones.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘실제로 몇몇 수영 선수들은 부력을 늘리기 위해 이 수영복을 한 번에 두 벌 혹은 그 이상 입었다.’라는 뜻으로, 앞에서 설명한 내용을 실제 사례나 구체적인 사실로 뒷받침하거나 강조할 때 사용하는 연결어인 In fact(실제로)와 앞에서 언급한 수영복을 가리키는 these suits가 쓰였으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 부력을 증가시키는 이 수영복에 대한 일반적인 설명이 와야 한다. 따라서 물의 저항을 줄이고 공기를 가둬 부력을 높이는 전신 수영복의 기능을 설명한 뒤 부력을 높이는 이 수영복(these suits)의 실제 착용 사례로 연결되도록 (D)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.
