body:
As a loyal companion, the dog accompanies us everywhere. Sometimes we have a responsibility to help others understand our pets in public spaces. How can we do that?
(A) On the other hand, if your dog doesn’t like other dogs, you can buy an orange collar to warn other pet owners. Lastly, if your dog has vision or hearing problems, use a white collar to let everyone know.
(B) Writing phrases like “friendly” or “no dogs” can make this communication even more effective. Even though our dogs can’t speak, we can still help them express themselves.
(C) Well, did you know that choosing the right color for your dog collar can help this? If your dog has a friendly personality, it’s best to use a green collar.
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 공공장소에서 다른 사람들이 우리의 반려동물을 이해할 수 있도록 도와야 한다는 주제를 제시하며 그 방법이 무엇일지를 묻는 주어진 글에 이어, 올바른 색상의 반려견 목줄을 선택하는 것이 도움이 된다는 새로운 정보를 소개하면서 그 예로 친근한 성격의 반려견에게는 초록색 목줄을 사용하는 것이 좋다고 설명하는 (C), On the other hand(반면에)를 사용해, 친근한 성격의 반려견과 대조적으로 다른 개를 좋아하지 않는 반려견에게는 경고를 의미하는 주황색 목줄을 사용할 수 있으며, 시각이나 청각 문제가 있는 반려견에게는 흰색 목줄을 사용할 수 있다고 조언하는 (A), 색의 사용에 이은 또 다른 방법으로서 문구를 적어 소통을 더욱 효과적으로 만들 수 있다고 추가 설명한 뒤, 우리는 여전히 반려견들이 자신을 표현할 수 있도록 도울 수 있다고 실천을 강조하며 마무리하는 내용의 (B)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

body:
As a loyal companion, the dog accompanies us everywhere. Sometimes we have a responsibility to help others understand our pets in public spaces. How can we do that?
(A) On the other hand, if your dog doesn’t like other dogs, you can buy an orange collar to warn other pet owners. Lastly, if your dog has vision or hearing problems, use a white collar to let everyone know.
(B) Writing phrases like “friendly” or “no dogs” can make this communication even more effective. Even though our dogs can’t speak, we can still help them express themselves.
(C) Well, did you know that choosing the right color for your dog collar can help this? If your dog has a friendly personality, it’s best to use a green collar.
윗글의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to criticize pet owners who fail to control their pets in public spaces
to compare the advantages of different types of collars for keeping dogs physically safe
to show how dog owners can communicate with their dogs more effectively in public
to suggest ways for pet owners to make their pets better understood by others in public places
to inform people that dogs with health problems are not allowed in public spaces and must remain in designated areas only
solution: 공공장소에서 다른 사람들이 자신의 반려동물을 이해할 수 있도록 돕는 방법으로 반려견의 성향이나 상태를 목줄의 색이나 문구를 통해 전달할 수 있다는 점을 알려주는 내용이므로, 글의 목적으로 ❹ ‘반려견 주인들이 공공장소에서 자신의 반려동물이 다른 사람들에게 더 잘 이해되도록 하는 방법을 제안하기 위해’가 알맞다.

body:
Colors strengthen the emotions of viewers due to their ability to evoke strong psychological reactions. An excellent example can be found in an animated film where an ordinary citizen becomes a superhero to defeat a villain. At the beginning of the film, the male character, who was once a superhero but had to return to living an ordinary life, is surrounded by dull colors and gray tones. He is working as if he were an ordinary person, hiding his true power. However, when he returns to work as a superhero, the film fills up with bold reds, yellows, and blues. These colors represent power and happiness. This shift reflects his emotional development, and ______. Through such a process, colors impact the emotional experience of the audience.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the colors interfere with viewers’ understanding of his feelings
viewers can understand his feelings even without verbal explanation
viewers grasp the director’s intention through the character’s monologue
viewers can achieve emotional healing through exposure to a wider range of colors
the director can freely change his mood by adjusting the soundtrack of each scene
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

Colors help audiences grasp the connections between characters, places, and important objects in films, making complex stories ⓐmore easily to understand. (A) There is a film from the 1930s that shows the adventures of a girl attempting to return home after ⓑsweeping away in a flash by a tornado to a land of magic. (B) The director uses colors ⓒto effectively communicate with the audience. (C) With such color differences, the audience can distinguish which world ⓓdo the events take place in. (D) Audiences watching this film are immersed in the world of magic as if they ⓔwere the girl when watching the scenes ⓕthat turn to color in a flash. (E)
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
answer:
(1) ⓐ → easier to understand
(2) ⓑ → being swept away
(3) ⓓ → the events take
solution:
ⓐ ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(형용사(구))(~을 …하게[…한 상태로] 만들다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, 보어로 부사(구)는 쓸 수 없으므로, 비교급 형태의 부사 more easily를 비교급 형태의 형용사 easier로 고친다. ‘이해하기에 (더 쉬운)’라는 뜻으로 형용사를 수식하는 부사적 용법의 to부정사가 이어질 수 있으며, 앞의 명사구 complex stories가 의미상 목적어이므로, 타동사 understand 뒤에 목적어 없이 쓰인 to understand는 알맞다.
ⓑ 전치사 after의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사구가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 의미상 주어인 a girl이 ‘휩쓸린’ 대상이므로, sweeping away을 수동형 동명사(being+p.p.)를 사용한 being swept away로 고친다.
ⓓ which world 이하는 동사 distinguish의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이므로 의문사구(which world) 뒤는 평서문의 어순이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ‘조동사+주어+동사원형’의 직접의문문 어순인 do the events take를 ‘주어+동사’의 평서문 어순인 the events take로 고친다.

body:
Film directors capture the changes in their characters’ lives through changes in color. Another film from the 1990s follows the dramatic experience of a man with scissor hands who ⓐcome down to a town to live with ordinary folks. He always wears black, and the castle where he used to live ⓑwas a gray and gloomy place. However, in the town ⓒwhere he came to live with his lover, each house is painted differently, and the people wear colorful clothes. At first, he ⓓis welcomed by the people in town, but as he becomes misunderstood and disliked, the film’s colors gradually become darker. Like the saying “A picture is worth a thousand words,” colors get a film’s message across more strongly than words. A good example is the red coat in a movie about the true story of a German businessman who saved thousands of Jews from the Nazis during World War II. While the movie was mostly in black and white, the director chose one particular thing (A)[added / to add] color to. It was the red coat of a single lost girl, (B)[who / which] was alone in a crowd of frightened Jews. As such, ⓐ감독이 나치의 잔혹성을 강력하게 상징할 수 있게 해준 것은 바로 색상의 강렬한 대비였다. The young girl represents innocence while also representing the violence of the Nazis. So, what happened to this young girl? The movie never tells us for sure, but later in the film we see a dead girl in a red coat (C)[loading / being loaded] into a cart.

choices: added who being loaded
added which being loaded
added which loading
to add who loading
to add who being loaded

(A) 동사(chose)가 있는 완전한 절(the director chose ~ thing)에 접속사 없이 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 준동사 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사 color가 있으므로, 흐름상 명사구 one particular thing을 ‘더할 (특정한 한 가지)’이라는 뜻으로 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사구를 이루는 능동형 to부정사 to add가 알맞다.

[1]
In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of ⓐ[them / themselves] near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today’s words, one could say that the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s endorsement gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years ⓑ[did / was] the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news ⓒ[involving / involved] a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.

[2]
Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it’s understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now?
(A) This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not.
(B) In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information.
(C) In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don’t know how to verify information.
In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 주어진 글의 마지막 문장 ‘첨단 기술은 오늘날 사람들이 속지 않도록 막아 주는가?’ 다음에, 이 질문에 대한 답변으로 In fact(사실)를 통해 첨단 기술이 오히려 더 속기 쉽게 만들 수도 있다는 반대되는 내용을 제시하는 (C)가 가장 먼저 온다. 다음으로 (C)의 마지막 문장에서 많은 사람들이 정보 검증 방법을 몰라 속아 넘어가거나 거짓 주장을 받아들인다고 언급한 뒤, 이 내용을 This로 이어받아 이것이 다음에 이어질 질문을 야기한다고 언급하며 온라인의 방대한 정보를 어떻게 검증할 수 있는지 묻는 (A), (A)의 마지막 문장에서 인터넷의 정보를 검증하거나 타당성을 확인하는 것이 쉽지 않다고 언급한 뒤, 그 이유로 과거에는 출판 기준이 있었지만 오늘날 인터넷은 출판의 장벽을 없애 독자들이 신뢰할 수 있는 정보를 찾기 어렵게 만들었다고 설명하는 (B)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not ⓐwhat was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and ⓑwritten materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer’s credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as “vertical reading.”
Vertical reading involves relying on the text ⓒto determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. ⓓHaving read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text ⓔis supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, so this ⓕmaking it necessary to change reading strategies.

ⓕ making → makes (접속사 so, 주어 this에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, 앞 절의 내용인 ‘기술이 사람들이 글을 쓰고 출판하는 환경을 변화시킨 것’이 읽기 전략을 바꾸게 하는 주체이고 변화로 인한 현재 시점의 필요성을 언급하고 있으므로 현재시제로 써야 한다. 따라서 making을 현재시제 makes로 고친다.)

ⓓ 정보가 정체되어 있지 않다는 부정문 ‘information does not remain still’에 이어지고 있으며 ‘조동사+주어’의 어순으로 도치된 should the reader가 이어지고 있으므로 부정문의 뒤에서 ‘…도 또한 ~하지 않는다’라는 뜻을 이루는 neither는 적절하다.
ⓔ 접속사 while 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 접속사 while을 생략하지 않은 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 readers가 ‘애쓰는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 trying은 적절하다.

Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither ⓐdoes lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. ⓑNo matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand ⓒthat the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so ⓓneither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while ⓔtrying to make sense of it.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Lateral reading is more reliable for evaluating online information than any other reading strategy.
Authors and publishers have a responsibility to maintain complete neutrality in all content.
Readers should habitually cross-check multiple sources and keep re-evaluating claims as information changes.
Consulting a wide range of sources removes the need to verify individual authors.
Combining vertical reading for books with lateral reading for news is the most effective approach.
solution:
가로 읽기가 현대 기술을 잘 활용하는 전략이지만, 중립성을 보장하는 매체는 없으므로 신뢰성 판단은 독자의 몫이므로, 많은 정보를 교차 확인하는 평가 습관을 들여야 하고, 정보가 끊임없이 변하는 만큼 이 과정을 반복하며 정보와 능동적으로 상호작용해야 한다는 내용의 글이므로, 이 글의 요지로 ③ ‘독자들은 습관적으로 여러 출처의 정보를 교차 검증하고, 정보가 변화함에 따라 주장들을 계속해서 재평가해야 한다.’가 적절하다.
오답
① 가로 읽기는 온라인 정보를 평가하는 데 있어 다른 어떤 읽기 전략보다 더 신뢰할 수 있다.
② 저자와 출판사는 모든 콘텐츠에서 완전한 중립성을 유지해야 할 책임이 있다.
④ 다양한 출처를 참고하면 개별 저자의 신뢰성을 검증할 필요가 없어진다.
⑤ 책에는 세로 읽기를, 뉴스에는 가로 읽기를 결합하여 사용하는 것이 가장 효과적인 접근법이다.

Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, (A)기술은 사람들이 쓰고 출판하는 환경을 변화시켜 왔고, 읽기 전략들을 바꾸는 것을 필요하게 만들었다.
Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it’s understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don’t know how to verify information.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 주절의 주어로 시작하고 ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• ‘가목적어-진목적어’ 구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 18단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
strategy, make, change, necessary, reading, in, the landscape, technology, publish
→ ______
answer: technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 주절의 주어인 technology를 가장 먼저 쓰고, 기술이 과거부터 현재까지 환경을 변화시켜 온 것이므로 현재 완료를 사용하여 has changed로 쓰고 목적어 자리에는 the landscape를 이어 쓴다.
• 명사구 the landscape를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절은 <조건>에 따라 ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용해야 하며, <보기>에 제시된 전치사 in을 사용하여 in which로 쓰고 관계사절의 주어 people, 동사 write와 publish를 등위접속사 and를 사이에 두고 병렬로 연결하여 쓴다.
• 주절의 뒤에 <조건>에 명시된 분사구문이 이어지도록 콤마(,)로 연결한 다음 의미상 주어인 앞 절 전체가 변화가 필요하도록 ‘만드는’ 주체이므로 make를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 making으로 변형하여 쓴다.
• <조건>에 따라 가목적어와 진목적어를 사용해야 하므로 ‘make+가목적어(it)+목적격보어+진목적어(to부정사)’의 어순이 되도록 making 뒤에 가목적어 it, 목적격보어 necessary, 진목적어 to change reading strategies를 차례대로 쓴다.

In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today’s words, one could say that the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s endorsement gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale ______ in the digital age.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: representing the influence of technology on the spread of false information
illustrating the benefits of sharing information with a wider audience
suggesting the importance of trusting information endorsed by experts
explaining how digital tools can help distinguish fact from fiction
emphasizing the necessity of critically evaluating information
solution:
유명 작가인 Arthur Conan Doyle이 사진을 초자연적 현상의 증거라고 주장하면서 사진에 신뢰성을 부여했지만, 오랜 시간이 지난 후 소녀들이 사진이 조작된 것이었음을 인정했으므로, 유명 인사의 지지가 있더라도 정보를 무조건 신뢰해서는 안 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘정보를 비판적으로 평가할 필요성을 강조하는’이 적절하다.
본문변형 demonstrating the importance of media literacy → emphasizing the necessity of critically evaluating information

① 기술이 거짓 정보의 확산에 미치는 영향을 보여주는

Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, ⓐit may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don’t know how to verify information.
This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating ⓑit is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, ⓒit also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.

[2]
Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author’s claims. (A)They can utilize Internet browser tools that helps review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows ⓓthem to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently.
As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire “fact-checkers” to evaluate ⓔtheir writers’ claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, (B)after they have utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.

choices: Limited early-20th-century technology explains why a few pictures easily convinced a famous writer and the public.
Modern technology does not stop people from being deceived if they cannot verify information properly.
While finding digital content takes minimal effort, assessing its reliability remains significantly harder.
Internet publishing helps readers identify trustworthy content because strict editing standards are still enforced online.
Since anyone can upload content today, critical evaluation is crucial for finding accurate information.

body:
It is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man named Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with some seaweed attached to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and found it to be delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea where he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people to enjoy gim, but it was not productive enough to cultivate as much gim as we consume today.
To our surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. While researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, which function like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching them to cultivating frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

The Life and Scientific Legacy of Kathleen Drew-Baker in Korea
The Advantages of Traditional Seaweed Farming Methods Over Modern Techniques
Early Gim Cultivation and the Development of a Spore-Based Mass Production Method
The Influence of Yeoik Gim’s Gim Farming on Kathleen Drew-Baker’s Seaweed Research

However, it used to be very expensive in the past, so not everyone could enjoy it as much as people can today.
Gim seems to have been harvested in the past by women who walked into the sea during low tide to collect it from rocks. It was so precious and ⓑ[scarce / plentiful] that only royalty, like kings and queens, and the very wealthy had the privilege to afford it. During the Joseon period, ten sheets of gim were said to cost twenty cotton rolls, which cost a lot at the time. So you can imagine how expensive gim was. You might be wondering how gim became ⓒ[less / more] affordable and readily available in recent years. Two figures are behind the striking popularity of gim today.

solution:
⦁<보기>에 our와 surprise가 있으므로, ‘~에게 …하게도’라는 뜻의 ‘to+소유격+추상명사’를 사용해 ‘우리에게 놀랍게도’라는 뜻으로 To our surprise를 쓴다.
⦁명사구 a British scientist가 ‘이름 지어진’ 대상이고, Kathleen Drew-Baker는 ‘name+목적어+목적격보어(이름)(~을 …라고 이름 짓다)’의 목적격보어에 해당하므로, 수동 표현인 ‘be named+보어(이름)’를 사용해 name을 과거분사 named로 변형한다.
⦁콤마(,) 뒤에 <조건>에 따라 적절한 관계대명사를 사용해 부연 설명의 관계사절을 쓰되, 관계사절이 부연 설명하는 선행사인 a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker가 사람이므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 who를 사용하고, ‘기여했던’ 과거시점 이전의 경험을 나타내야 하므로, 이어지는 동사 자리에 과거완료 표현인 ’had never been to ~(~해 와 본적이 없었다)’를 쓴다.

body:
Gim in the Future
The future of the gim industry appears bright, as global demand for gim is expected ⓐ[rising / to rise] in the coming years for a couple of reasons. First of all, gim is a highly valued product on the global market as a healthy food due to its nutritional properties. One hundred grams of gim contain sixteen times more dietary fiber than the same amount of cabbage, two times more protein than beans, and four times more calcium than milk. Gim’s high nutrient content will make it a popular choice among consumers who are keenly interested in a healthy diet. Second, gim is environmentally friendly. A French magazine once published an article ⓑ[title / titled] “Koreans who cook seaweed for Earth,” which listed seaweed, including gim, as one of the most valuable foods for future generations, along with Spanish tomatoes, Latin American beans, and Canadian salmon. In fact, research shows that seaweed has ⓒ[shown / been shown] to capture and store CO₂ as it grows. For example, one ton of seaweed absorbs three times as much CO₂ as a maple tree. As demonstrated here, gim has many benefits. Who knows? There may come a day when gim is found on every dinner table around the world.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: rising title shown
to rise titled shown
rising titled shown
to rise titled been shown
rising title been shown
solution:
ⓐ 수동태인 is expected에 이어져 ‘expect+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …할 것으로 예상하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘be expected+to부정사(…할 것으로 예상되다)’를 이루어야 하므로, to부정사인 to rise가 알맞다.
ⓑ 앞의 명사구 an article을 수식하는 분사구나 형용사구를 이끌어야 하며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘title+목적어+목적격보어(제목)(~에 …라는 제목을 붙이다)’의 목적격보어에 해당하는 “Koreans ~ Earth“가 이어져 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ‘be titled+보어(제목)(…라는 제목이 붙여지다)’의 과거분사 titled가 알맞다.
ⓒ 명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 절의 주어 seaweed가 ‘입증된’ 대상이며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘be shown+to부정사(~한다는 것이 입증되다)’의 to부정사구(to capture ~ grows)가 이어지므로, 앞의 has와 함께 현재완료수동태(have[has]+been+p.p.)를 이루는 been shown이 알맞다.

Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is ⓐone of the most commonly used spice in the world. However, in the past, it was a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. ⓑSo desired was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.” There ⓒare several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, ⓓto digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it (A)______. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, ⓔnot only black pepper made food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. (B)이 모든 점을 고려하면, 흑후추가 왜 그렇게 높은 가치를 지닌 상품이었는지는 분명합니다. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, ⓕboth in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. (틀린 부분만 찾아 고칠 것)
<기호> <틀린 부분> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ : ______ → ______
(2) ______ : ______ → ______
(3) ______ : ______ → ______
answer:
(1) ⓐ: spice → spices
(2) ⓓ: to digest → digest
(3) ⓔ: black pepper made → did black pepper make
solution:
ⓐ ‘가장 ~한 …들 가운데 하나’라는 뜻의 ‘one+of+the+최상급+복수명사(구)’를 이루어야 하므로 단수명사 spice를 복수명사 spices로 고친다. 그 외, ‘향신료’가 사용되는 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 used가 앞에 쓰인 것과, 분사 used를 최상급 형태의 부사 most commonly가 수식하는 것은 모두 알맞다.
ⓓ helped와 목적어 people에 이어져 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)(~가 …하는 것을 돕다, ~가 …하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식을 이루는 첫 번째 목적격보어 자리에 동사원형 sleep이 쓰였으므로, ‘A, B, and C’의 구조로 동사원형 digest, relieve가 병렬로 연결되도록 to digest를 digest로 고친다. 그 외, 타동사 digest(~을 소화시키다)와 relieve(~을 완화시키다)의 목적어로 명사 food와 명사구 skin irritation이 각각 이어진 것은 알맞다.
ⓔ 상관접속사 ‘not only A but also B‘의 부정어 not only가 문두에 쓰이면 뒤에 이어지는 절은 ’be동사/조동사‘ 도치를 적용해야 하며, 일반동사가 쓰인 경우 조동사 do/does/did를 사용해 ‘not only+do/does/did+주어+동사원형 ~’의 어순이 되어야 한다. 따라서 not only 뒤의 black pepper made를 did black pepper make로 고쳐야 한다.
오답
ⓒ 유도부사 There 뒤에 ‘be동사+주어’의 도치된 어순으로 복수동사로 수일치한 be동사 are와 복수명사인 주어 several reasons가 쓰이고, 선행사 reason(s) 뒤에 관계부사는 생략될 수 있으므로 관계부사 why나 관계부사 대용의 that, 또는 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 for which가 생략된 완전한 절 ‘black pepper ~ in the past’가 several reasons를 수식하는 것은 모두 알맞다.

<조건>
• 가주어를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)

solution:
⦁‘~을 고려하면’이라는 뜻의 비인칭독립분사구문을 활용해 consider를 Considering으로 변형한다.

⦁why가 이끄는 명사절은 의문사 뒤 평서문의 간접의문문 어순을 이루어야 하므로, ‘주어+be동사’ 어순으로 먼저 black pepper was를 쓰고, 보어인 명사구를 ‘such+a(n)+부사+형용사+명사’의 어순에 따라 such a highly valued commodity로 쓴다.

body:
Gim in the Past
Gim seems ⓐto be harvested in the past by women who walked into the sea during low tide to collect it from rocks. It was so precious and scarce that only royalty, like kings and queens, and the very wealthy had the privilege ⓑto afford it. During the Joseon period, ten sheets of gim were said ⓒcosting twenty cotton rolls, which cost a lot at the time. So you can imagine how expensive gim was. You might be wondering (A)______. Two figures are behind the striking popularity of gim today.
It is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man ⓓnamed Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with some seaweed attached to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and ⓔfound it to be delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea where he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people ⓕenjoying gim, but it was not productive enough ⓖto cultivate as much gim as we consume today.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ to be harvested → to have been harvested
(‘~인 것 같다, ~인 것으로 보이다’라는 뜻으로 ‘seem+to부정사’를 쓰며, 주어 Gim이 ‘채취되었던’ 대상이므로 seems 뒤에 수동형 to부정사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, seems가 나타내는 현재보다 이전 과거의 일이므로, 수동형 완료부정사(to+have+been+p.p.)를 사용해 to be harvested를 to have been harvested로 고친다.)
ⓒ costing → to cost
(‘~라고 말해진다’라는 뜻으로 ‘be said+to부정사’를 사용하므로, 수동태인 were said 뒤의 costing을 to부정사인 to cost로 고친다.)
ⓕ enjoying → to enjoy
(’allow+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)‘의 5형식 구문에서 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, allowed와 목적어 more people 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 enjoying을 to부정사인 to enjoy로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 명사구 the privilege를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사로, 뒤에 목적어인 대명사 it이 있으므로, 능동형 to부정사인 to afford는 알맞다.

W: Good afternoon, students. In our last lesson, we discussed the importance of reading. However, I know that some of you may find reading quite challenging. Have you ever used any reading strategies? If not, don’t worry. Today, I’m going to give you some useful tips to improve your reading skills. First, take notes as you read. Write down important details in the margins of your book. This will help you make connections between ideas and better understand the content. Second, visualize what you are reading. For example, if you’re reading a novel, ask yourself questions like “What do the characters and the setting look like?” Drawing pictures in your mind will help you understand the book you are reading on a deeper level. These strategies will improve your reading comprehension. Now, with these strategies in mind, I want you to pick up a book and enjoy reading.

(A) All he could find, however, was a few coins. “Poor old fellow, he wants ⓐ[it / them] more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks,” he thought to himself. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar’s hand.
(B) The old man was surprised and smiled faintly. “Thank you, sir,” he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at ⓑ[that / what] he had done.
(C) The old beggar took advantage of Alan’s absence to rest for a moment on a chair. He looked so sad and lonely. Hughie couldn’t help ⓒ[pity / pitying] him and felt his own pockets to see what money he had.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 액자 제작자가 만나길 원한다는 하인의 말에 Alan이 밖으로 나갔다는 주어진 글 다음에, Alan이 자리를 비운 것을 Alan’s absence(Alan의 부재)로 가리켜 그것을 이용하여 쉬고 있는 늙은 거지의 모습에 Hughie가 측은한 마음을 느껴 자신이 가진 돈을 확인하기 위해 주머니를 더듬었다는 내용의 (C), however로 생각과는 달리 주머니에는 몇 개의 동전뿐이었으며, Hughie는 그 돈이 자신보다 그 거지에게 더 필요할 거라고 생각하며 그의 손에 그 동전들을 주었다는 내용의 (A), 동전을 받는 노인은 놀라며 감사를 표했다는 내용의 (B)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won’t let them ⓐmarry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds.
One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar ⓑhimself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “ⓒHow unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar ⓓto look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think (A)______” cried Hughie, ⓔlaughed. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes ⓕto draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

2개

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 1개이다.
ⓔ laughed → laughing (완전한 절(“Well, ~ Hughie) 다음에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어 Hughie가 ‘웃는’ 주체이자 laugh는 자동사이므로 laughed를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 laughing으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 사역동사 let은 목적격 보어로 동사원형을 취하므로 let의 목적어 them에 이어 목적격 보어 자리의 동사원형 marry는 알맞다.
ⓑ 재귀대명사는 주어, 목적어, 또는 보어를 강조하기 위해 강조하는 말 바로 뒤 또는 문장 맨 뒤에 위치하여 쓰일 수 있으므로, 주어 the beggar를 강조하기 위해 바로 뒤에 쓰인 ‘직접, 본인’이라는 뜻을 나타내는 재귀대명사 himself는 알맞다. 참고로, 강조 용법의 재귀대명사는 생략해도 문법상 문제가 없다.
ⓒ 감탄문은 ‘How+형용사/부사+주어+동사!’로 나타낼 수 있으므로 형용사 unfortunate와 주어 he 동사 looks 앞에 쓰인 감탄사 How는 알맞다.
ⓕ 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 채 선행사 the effort를 수식하는 관계사절로, ‘it+takes+시간/비용/노력 등+to부정사’ 구문이 ‘~하는 데 …이 걸리다[들다]’라는 뜻을 나타내므로 it takes와 의미상 목적어 the efforts에 이어진 to부정사 to draw는 알맞다.

As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. These imaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, ⓒprovide creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots. This story explains that leopards developed spots as a means of survival.

• ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문을 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 가주어 it을 쓰고 빈도부사 never는 일반동사 앞에 쓰므로 never를 먼저 쓴 뒤에 주어진 occur to를 과거시제로 변형한 occurred to와 목적어 me를 쓴다.
• 진주어인 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that을 쓰고 주어로 you를, 동사구로 would distribute를, 목적어로 money를, 마지막으로 ‘그런 식으로’를 뜻하는 in that way를 써서 완성한다.

“You don’t mean to say you talked to him about her?” said Hughie.
“Sure I did. He knows all about the Colonel, Laura, and the 10,000 pounds,” replied Alan.
“You told that old beggar all my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and angry.
“My dear boy,” said Alan, smiling, “that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and asked me a month ago to paint him as a beggar.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie, feeling embarrassed. “Good heavens! I gave him some coins,” he said, sinking into an armchair.
“What? You gave him coins?” cried Alan, bursting into laughter. He went on, “Well, (A)그런 식으로 네가 돈을 나눠 줄 거라고는 생각은 전혀 못 했어. Besides, when you came in, I didn’t know if Hausberg would like his name mentioned. You know he wasn’t in full dress.”
“Oh no, what did I do? The best thing I can do is to go to bed, and, my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone,” said Hughie, and he went home, feeling very unhappy.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: A Baron’s Rage at Being Mistaken for a Beggar
Hughie’s Startling Discovery of the Beggar’s True Identity
A Misunderstanding That Ended Hughie and Alan’s Friendship
Baron Hausberg: A Friend Alan Desperately Wants to Get Close to
Hughie’s Suspicion of Alan’s Intention to Conceal the Baron’s Identity
solution:
Alan은 Hughie가 늙은 거지라고 부른 사람이 사실은 유럽에서 가장 부유한 사람 중 한 명인 Hausberg 남작임을 밝혔고, 이에 Hughie는 당황하며 그 거지에게 동전 몇 개를 주었던 것을 밝히고선 이 일을 아무에게도 말하지 말라고 말하며 불행한 기분으로 집으로 돌아갔다는 내용이므로, 글의 제목으로 ② ‘거지의 진짜 정체에 대한 Hughie의 깜짝 놀랄 만한 발견’이 알맞다.

body:
That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?” and Alan replied, “(A)Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him (B)waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I (C)can do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes (D)do I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how (E)Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): 앞에 I have got it이 생략된 목적격 보어로 볼 때, 목적어 it이 완성되고 액자에 씌워지는 대상이므로 과거분사 Finished와 framed는 알맞다.
(B): find의 목적격 보어 자리로 목적어 him이 기다리는 주체이자 wait는 자동사이므로 현재분사 waiting은 알맞다.
(C): 현재 상황에 대한 아쉬움을 나타내는 I wish 가정법 과거 문장이므로, can을 could로 고쳐야 한다.
(D): ‘What ~ clothes’는 강조를 위해 문두로 이동한 call의 목적어로, ‘조동사(do)+주어(I)+일반동사(call)’의 어순은 알맞다.
(E): 간접의문문이므로 의문사 how 뒤의 ‘주어+동사’ 어순인 Laura is는 알맞다.
solution:
(D) ‘What ~ clothes’가 동사 call의 목적어로 강조를 위해 문두에 있다는 설명은 적절하나, 목적어가 문두로 나가는 경우 보통 도치가 일어나지 않으므로, ‘주어(I)+일반동사(call)’의 어순으로 고쳐야 한다.
오답
(A) 앞에 ’I have got that picture’가 생략되어 있으며, get은 ‘get+목적어+목적격 보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식에서 목적어와 목적격 보어가 수동적인 관계일 경우 목적격 보어로 과거분사를 취하므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 Finished와 framed라는 설명은 적절하다.
(E) how 이하는 동사 tell 직접목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문으로, 의문사 how 뒤에 ‘주어+동사 ~’의 평서문 어순이 되어야 하므로, ‘주어+동사’의 어순인 Laura is는 알맞다는 설명은 적절하다.

body:
The next morning, when Hughie was having breakfast, an old gentleman visited his house. The man said, “I have come from Baron Hausberg,” and continued, “The Baron ....” Hughie (A)[added / interrupted], “I beg, sir, that you will offer him my sincerest apologies.” Then, with a smile, the old gentleman said, “The Baron has asked me to bring you this letter,” and gave Hughie a sealed (B)[document / envelope]. On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar,” and inside was a check for 10,000 pounds.
When they were married, Alan was the best man, and the Baron made a speech at the wedding. “Millionaire models,” remarked Alan, “are rare enough, but (C)[stingy / model] millionaires are rarer still!”

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A)　(B)　(C)
choices: interrupted　envelope　stingy
interrupted　envelope　model
added　document　stingy
interrupted　document　model
added　envelope　model
solution:
(A) 노신사가 “Hausberg 남작님께서 보내서 왔습니다.”라고 한 뒤에 “남작께서 ....”라고 말을 이어가려 할 때, Hughie가 그의 말이 끝나기 전에 진심 어린 사과를 전해달라고 간청하는 상황이므로, Hughie가 그 노신사의 말을 끊으며 끼어들었다는 흐름으로 interrupted((남의 말을) 가로막고 끼어들어 말했다)가 알맞다.
add ~ (자신이 앞서 한 말에) ~을 덧붙이다
(B) “남작님께서 이 편지를 전해 달라고 하셨습니다.”라고 노신사가 말을 했고, 겉에는 결혼 선물이라는 문구가 있고 안에는 수표가 들어 있었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 노신사는 봉인된 봉투를 Hughie에게 건넸다는 흐름으로 envelope(봉투)가 알맞다.
document 문서
(C) Hausberg 남작이 Hughie의 집으로 한 노신사를 통해 그의 결혼 선물로 1만 파운드짜리 수표가 들어있는 봉투를 보냈으므로 Hughie의 결혼식 날에 Alan이 한 말로 ‘모범적인’ 백만장자가 더 드물다고 하는 흐름이 되는 model(모범적인)이 알맞다.
stingy 인색한

body:
Throughout history, people have always tried to understand themselves and the world they live in, and these efforts are reflected in the stories they tell. (A)그러한 이야기들의 흥미로운 한 예는 푸르쿠아 이야기인데, 이것들은 다양한 현상들의 뒤에 있는 기원이나 이유를 설명하는 것을 목표로 한다. As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. These imaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, provide creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots. According to this story, leopards were originally plain brown like the desert. However, in order not to reveal themselves while hunting animals in the forest, leopards decided to paint spots on their skins. This story explains that leopards developed spots as a means of survival.
Pourquoi tales serve several purposes. They engage readers with imaginative stories, teach lessons, and serve as a means of passing on knowledge to future generations. These stories explore the complexity of the world around us.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 계속적 용법의 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
explain, be, aim, of, behind, the origins, example, stories, phenomena, or reasons, interesting, various, such, an
______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ the pourquoi tales, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: An interesting example of such stories is, which aim to explain the origins or reasons behind various phenomena
solution:
• 주어로 An interesting example of such stories를 쓰고, 주어의 핵인 An interesting example에 수일치된 be동사를 쓰되 현재 사실을 설명하므로 is를 쓴다.
• 계속적 용법의 관계대명사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 콤마(,) 뒤에 선행사인 the pourquoi tales를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 쓴다. 선행사가 복수명사구이며 현재 사실을 설명하므로 현재형 복수동사 aim을 쓰고, ‘~하는 것을 목표로 하다’라는 뜻의 ‘aim+to부정사’를 사용하므로 이어서 to부정사 to explain을 쓴다. explain의 목적어로 the origins or reasons를 쓰고 마지막으로 부사구 behind various phenomena를 쓴다.

solution:

body:
After a while, the servant came in and told Alan that the frame-maker wanted to see him. Alan said, “I will be back in a moment,” as he went out. The old beggar took advantage of Alan’s absence to rest for a moment on a chair. He looked so sad and lonely. Hughie couldn’t help pitying him and felt his own pockets to see what money he had. All he could find, however, was a few coins. “Poor old fellow, he wants them more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks,” he thought to himself. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar’s hand. The old man was surprised and smiled faintly. “Thank you, sir,” he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at what he had done.

body:
Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to ______. People often view computer systems as objective. However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely reproduce those biases in its output.
For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones. As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police. This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to diminish the potential negative impacts of AI.

maintain existing biases and discrimination
increase privacy risks through data collection
reduce the dependence on human intelligence
cause widespread job losses through excessive automation

(A)에서는 인간과 기계가 융합하여 새로운 형태의 지능을 만들 가능성을, (B)에서는 기술적 특이점이 인류의 미래에 큰 영향을 미칠 가능성을, (C)에서는 미래학자 Ray Kurzweil이 제시한 기술적 특이점의 발생 조건과 그에 따른 변화를 설명하고 있다. 이어서 (E)에서 기술적 특이점으로 인해 나타날 수 있는 몇 가지 미래의 시나리오를 제시한다고 하여 앞의 내용과 자연스럽게 이어진다. 반면 (D) ‘이러한 이유로, 학자들과 전문가들은 미래의 사회적 추세를 예측하는 데 도움을 주기 위해 고대 문명을 연구하는 것을 강조한다.’는 기술적 특이점과 그로 인해 예상되는 미래의 변화에 관한 앞뒤 내용과 관련이 없으므로 (D)는 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

Then we might be able to think and learn at extraordinary speeds and control machines with our thoughts.
Bots taking the lead: Many traditional jobs might fade away, but exciting new roles may pop up. People might be trained (B)[to be / being] mediators between AI and humans. Schools might teach teamwork among humans and bots rather than traditional subjects. Kids may attend “fusion schools” where AI instructor bots might collaborate with human creativity. Here, students can design artworks and invent games alongside their AI friends.
Scientific leaps: Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) can solve complex problems, allowing for phenomenal achievements in physics, medicine, climate science, and other fields at an unprecedented pace. For example, the spacecraft of the future may be capable of traveling to other planets at unimaginable speeds. They may also be equipped with advanced life support systems (C)[what / that] will allow humans to live there for extended periods of time.
The technological singularity is a potentially dangerous event, but it is also one that could lead to incredible advances for humanity. We need to be aware of the risks and prepare for them as best we can, so that we can make sure that the singularity is a positive event for us all.

body:
Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to (A)[eliminate / maintain] existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as objective. However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely reproduce those biases in its output.
For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones. As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and (B)[rightfully / wrongfully] arrested by the police. This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to diminish the potential negative impacts of AI.
In conclusion, the rise of AI is shaping the future of society in profound ways, and it is important that we consider both the potential benefits and challenges this technology presents. While AI has the potential to increase efficiency and productivity and solve complex problems, it also has the potential to cause job losses and (C)[cease / continue] existing biases. However, as with any revolutionary technology, it is likely that the rise of AI will also create new job opportunities and contribute to economic growth. It is the responsibility of society to ensure that the development and implementation of AI are done in a responsible and ethical manner. This will require collaboration between governments, corporations, and individuals to establish regulations and standards, provide education and training programs, and ensure that the benefits of AI are shared equally. The future is now, and the way we shape the role of AI in our lives will have a profound impact on the future of humanity.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: eliminate rightfully cease
maintain rightfully continue
eliminate wrongfully continue
maintain wrongfully cease
maintain wrongfully continue
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 AI가 훈련된 데이터에 편견이 포함되어 있으면 그 편견을 결과에 재현할 수 있다고 했으므로 기존의 편향과 차별을 그대로 가지고 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 maintain(지속시키다)이 적절하다.
eliminate 제거하다
(B) 앞에서 안면 인식 알고리즘이 특정 피부색에 대해 낮은 정확도를 보였으며, 그 원인이 밝은 피부색의 얼굴이 주로 포함된 데이터로 학습되었기 때문으로, 미국에서 소수 인종 사람들이 안면 인식 시스템에 의해 수배 중인 범죄자로 잘못 식별되어 경찰에 체포된 사례를 제시하고 있으므로, 실제로 범죄를 저지르지 않은 사람들이 부당하게 체포됐다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 wrongfully(부당하게)가 적절하다.
rightfully 정당하게
(C) AI가 효율성과 생산성을 높이고 복잡한 문제를 해결할 가능성이 있지만, 실업을 야기할 가능성이 있다고 했으므로 이와 같은 맥락으로 AI로 인한 부정적인 측면이 언급되어야 한다. 따라서 기존의 편향을 지속시킨다는 흐름의 continue(지속시키다)가 적절하다.
cease ~을 중단하다

G: Timothy, what’s wrong? You look worried.

G: Oh, right. You’ve been looking forward to it. So what’s the matter? Aren’t you excited?
B: The thing is, I have a big exam at the end of this week. So I’m not quite certain whether it would be a wise choice to go to the concert. I was thinking about canceling the ticket and just studying at home.
G: ______
B: Really? Can you tell me why?
G: It’s just a couple of hours. After you relieve your stress at the concert, you’ll be able to focus better.
B: Hmm… I’m still not sure.
G: I know you have been studying hard for the exam. Don’t worry and go have fun!

The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide ⓐhow to raise money for children in need. (A) Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were ⓑconflicting opinions. (B) When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but ⓒtrying something different instead. (C) After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. (D) The entire council was curious to find out ⓓif the different methods would yield different results. (E)
On the day of the vote, each possible event ⓔwas given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.”

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
So they decided to put it to a vote.
solution: ‘그래서 그들은 그것을 투표에 부치기로 결정했다.’라는 뜻의 주어진 문장은, 미술 전시회, 빵 바자회, 자선 콘서트라는 세 가지 선택지에 대해 자치회 구성원들의 의견이 상충했다는 내용 뒤이자 그들이 자치회의 고문 교사인 Akers 선생님에게 조언을 구하자 선생님이 익숙한 투표 방법이 아닌 다른 것을 시도해보라고 권장했다는 내용 앞인 (B)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

On the day of the vote, each possible event ⓔwas given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ trying → to try (5형식으로 쓰인 encouraged의 목적격보어 자리의 to부정사인 to use와 상관접속사 ‘not A but B‘(A가 아니라 B)로 연결된 encouraged의 두 번째 목적격 보어 자리이며 상관접속사로 연결되는 어구는 품사가 동일하거나, 문법적으로 성격이 같아야 하므로 trying을 to부정사 to try로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ decide의 목적어 자리로, ’how+to부정사‘가 ’~하는 방법‘이라는 명사구를 이루므로 how와 to부정사 to raise는 알맞다.
ⓑ 명사 opinions를 수식하는 자리로, conflict는 자동사이므로 능동 및 진행의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 conflicting이 수식하는 것은 알맞다.
ⓓ find out의 목적어 자리에서 ’~인지 아닌지‘의 뜻으로 완전한 절(the ~ results)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루는 접속사 if는 알맞다.

body:
The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. (A)투표자들에게는 여러 가지 선택지가 주어지고, 어느 것이든 가장 많은 1지망 표를 얻은 것이 이긴다. Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world.
The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 수동태를 사용할 것
• 적절한 복합관계대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형할 것
• 13단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
win, voters, first-preference votes, several options, give, get
→ ______
answer: Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins.
solution:
• 수동태를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라, ’give+A(간접목적어)+B(직접목적어)’에서 간접목적어를 주어로 전환한 수동태(‘A be given B’(A가 B를 받다))를 활용하여, 주어 Voters에 대한 동사를 수동태 are given으로 쓰고 several options를 이어서 쓴다.
• 등위접속사 and 뒤에 복합관계대명사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 ‘~하는 어느 것이든지’라는 뜻의 복합관계대명사 whichever를 써서 두 번째 절의 주어부인 명사절을 영작한다. 흐름상 whichever 뒤에 단수명사 option이 생략된 것이므로 whichever에 대한 동사로 단수동사 gets를 쓰고 목적어 the most first-preference votes를 써서 주어부를 완성한다. 이어, 명사절은 단수 취급하며 명사절 내에서도 단수동사 gets로 ‘어느 것이든 하나’임을 나타내고 있으므로 단수동사 wins를 연결한다.

pursue, personal choices, career, who, make, have lunch, many

body:
The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method (A)[involves / excludes] comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
The Condorcet method’s (B)[weakness / strength] is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is (C)[possible / impossible] that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: involves / strength / impossible
excludes / strength / possible
involves / weakness / impossible
excludes / weakness / possible
involves / weakness / possible
solution:
(A) 뒤에 이 경우에는 고려해야 할 세 쌍, A와 B, B와 C, A와 C가 있다는 내용이 이어지므로, 가능한 선택지 쌍에 대한 투표자들의 선호도를 비교하는 것을 수반한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 involves(포함하다, 수반하다)가 알맞다.
exclude 제외하다
(B) 복잡하다는 것과 더불어 때때로 승자를 가려내지 못한다는 부정적인 특징이 이어지므로, 그것들이 콩도르세 방식의 약점이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 weakness(약점)가 알맞다.
strength 강점, 장점
(C) 콩도르세 방식은 많은 선택지를 포함하는 선거에서 특히 승자를 선출하지 못한다는 점을 언급한 뒤에 이어지므로, 어떤 선택지도 다른 선택지들보다 명확하게 선호되지 않을 가능성이 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 possible(가능한)이 알맞다.
impossible 불가능한

Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. It sometimes ⓔallows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.

The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.

Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental ⓑhazard. Experts ⓓdoubt that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that (A)they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to ⓐdisassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs.
The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by ⓑpromoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products ⓒavailable to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on (B)their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as ⓓeasy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far ⓔmore e-waste will be generated. Thanks to (C)their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause.

In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer ⓐincludes a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers ⓑsee how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it.
(A) The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company ⓒthat wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate ⓓseeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.
(B) The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when ⓔpurchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ⓕend up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future.
(C) The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means ⓖwhat repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.

(C) The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means ⓖwhat repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓐ 제안(suggest, recommend), 충고(advise), 주장(insist), 요구(require) 등을 나타내는 동사의 목적어 자리에 that절이 쓰이고, that절의 내용이 당위(~해야 한다)를 나타낼 때, that절의 동사는 ‘should+동사원형’이나 should를 생략한 동사원형을 사용한다. 동사 requires의 목적어로 온 that절이 당위를 나타내야 하므로, includes를 ‘should+동사원형’ 형태인 should include 또는 should를 생략한 동사원형 include로 고친다.
*원래 지문에는 should를 생략한 동사원형 include가 쓰였음
ⓕ 전치사 with 뒤에 ‘주어+동사~’의 완전한 절이 이어질 수 없으므로 ‘~가 …한 상태로, ~가 …한 채로’라는 뜻의 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’ 구문을 이루어야 한다. 앞의 명사구 fewer electronic and electrical items가 ‘결국 ~에 이르는‘ 주체로 능동의 관계이고, ’(특정 상태·장소 등)에 결국 있게 되다‘라는 뜻의 표현인 ’end up+부사(구)‘에서 end는 수동태나 수동을 나타내는 과거분사로 쓸 수 없는 자동사이므로, end up을 능동을 나타내는 현재분사를 사용한 ending up으로 고친다.
ⓖ 완전한 절(repairing the product will be difficult)을 이끌어 동사 means의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다. 참고로, what은 의문대명사 또는 관계대명사로 쓰일 때 주어, 보어나 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌어 명사절을 이룬다.
오답
ⓑ ’let+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)‘의 5형식 구문에서 사역동사 let의 목적격보어로 동사원형이 쓰이므로, 단수형으로 쓰인 사역동사 lets와 목적어 consumers 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 동사원형 see는 알맞다.
ⓔ 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사를 남긴 ’접속사+분사(구)‘ 형태의 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 consumers가 ’구매하는‘ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 new devices and appliances가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 purchasing은 알맞다.

body:
Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world ⓐ[where / which] repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to ⓑ[pay / paying] for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how ⓒ[fixing / to fix] it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. (A)훨씬 더 중요하게는, 그것은 사람들이 훨씬 적은 전자 쓰레기를 발생시켜, 우리의 지구를 모두를 위한 더 깨끗하고 건강한 곳으로 만들 우리의 미래이다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
e-waste, will, make, people, a future, planet, a cleaner, healthier place, far, generate
→ Even more importantly, it is ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ for everyone.
answer: a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place
solution:
• 동사 is의 보어로 명사구 a future를 쓴 후, <조건>에 따라 ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용해 a future를 수식하는 관계사절을 쓴다. 즉, 선행사 a future에 어울리는 전치사 in을 사용해 in which를 쓴 뒤, 완전한 절을 연결한다.
• 관계사절의 주어로 people, 동사 자리에 조동사 will과 동사원형 generate를 쓴 뒤, 목적어 자리에 명사구를 쓰되, ‘훨씬’이라는 뜻의 비교급 강조부사 far를 먼저 쓰고 ‘더 적은’이라는 뜻의 less와 명사 e-waste가 이어지도록 한다.
• 콤마(,) 뒤에 <조건>에 따라 앞 절(people will generate far less e-waste)의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 사용하되, 분사구문의 의미상 주어이자 원인인 앞 절의 내용(사람들이 훨씬 적은 전자 쓰레기를 발생시키는 것)이 ‘만드는’ 주체이므로 make를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 making으로 변형한다. ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …로 만들다)’의 5형식 구조를 사용해 making의 목적어로 our planet, 목적격보어로 a cleaner, healthier place를 차례로 써서 완성한다.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: where paying fixing
where pay to fix
which pay fixing
which paying to fix
where paying to fix
solution:
ⓐ 완전한 절(repairing ~ life)을 이끌어 선행사인 장소 명사구 a world를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 장소의 관계부사 where가 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘limit ~ to …(~을 …로 제한하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘~ be limited to …(~가 …로 제한되다)’의 전치사 to 뒤에 명사(구)나 동명사(구)가 목적어로 이어져야 하므로, 동명사 paying이 알맞다.
ⓒ 전치사 on의 목적어 자리에 명사 역할을 하는 ‘의문사(구)+to부정사(구)’를 이루어야 하므로, how와 함께 ‘~하는 방법’을 나타내는 ‘how+to부정사(구)’를 이루는 to부정사 to fix가 알맞다.

body:
When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that ⓐis occurred to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places ⓑin which people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés ⓒstaffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was ⓓso a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people ⓔto share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.
By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and ⓕextend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective ⓖwhich can have a huge positive impact on our future.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓑ 완전한 절(people can gather together and fix their broken devices)을 이끌어 선행사인 장소 명사구 free meeting places를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 쓴 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태의 in which는 알맞다.
본문변형 where → in which
ⓔ 동사 encourage는 ’encourage+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하도록 장려하다)’의 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어로 to부정사(구)를 취하므로, encourage와 목적어인 people 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 온 to부정사 to share는 알맞다.
ⓕ ’enable+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …할 수 있게 하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리의 to maintain과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되므로, to가 생략된 동사원형 extend는 알맞다.
ⓖ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can have a huge positive impact on our future)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 a sustainable perspective를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 주격 관계대명사 which는 알맞다.
본문변형 that → which
오답
ⓐ is occurred → occurs (주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 단수명사구인 선행사 the damage에 수일치한 단수동사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, ‘발생하다’를 뜻하는 occur는 수동태나 수동을 나타내는 과거분사로 쓰일 수 없는 자동사이므로 수동태 is occurred를 능동태인 occurs로 고친다.)
ⓒ staffed → are staffed (주어 The cafés에 대한 두 번째 동사로 현재형 복수동사 teach가 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되므로 흐름상 같은 현재시제의 첫 번째 동사가 올 자리이며, 주어가 동사 staff(~에 직원을 배치하다)의 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘by+명사구’가 이어져 있으므로, staffed를 복수동사 are로 수일치한 현재시제 수동태 are staffed로 고친다.)
ⓓ so → such (뒤에 명사구인 a success와 that절이 이어지므로, ‘such+a/an+명사+that절(대단한 ~여서 …하다)’ 구조를 이루도록 so를 such로 고친다. 부사 so는 명사(구)가 아닌 형용사나 부사를 수식해 ’so+형용사/부사+that절’ 구조를 이룬다.)

body:
One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult ⓐto repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it ⓑis brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers ⓒto take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts ⓓneed to complete repairs.
The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. ⓔTo protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products ⓕavailable to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers ⓖdesign devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, (A)______. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries ⓗjoining the cause.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓑ is brought → (should) be brought (주어 it이 가리키는 a device가 ‘가져와지는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘bring ~ to …(~을 …로 가져오다)’의 전치사 to가 바로 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘~ be brought to …(~가 …로 가져와지다)’가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 제안, 주장, 추천, 요구, 명령을 나타내는 동사(suggest, insist, recommend, ask, request, require, order, urge 등)의 목적어로 이어지는 that절이 ‘~해야 한다’라는 의미의 당위성을 전달할 때, that절의 동사는 ‘(should)+동사원형’을 써야 하므로, is brought를 should be brought나 should를 생략한 형태인 be brought로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 be brought가 쓰였음
ⓓ need → needed (동사 acquire의 첫 번째 목적어인 명사구 ‘the instructions for ~ items’에 등위접속사 or로 절이 아닌 명사구가 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, 명사구 the parts를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 수식받는 명사구가 ‘필요시 되는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 부사적 용법(목적)의 to부정사구가 이어지므로, need를 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 needed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘too+형용사/부사+to부정사(’too+형용사‘ 형태인 too difficult에 이어져 ’~하기에 너무 …한/…하게)’를 뜻하는 ‘too+형용사/부사/to부정사’를 이루는 to부정사 to repair는 알맞다.
ⓖ 요구를 나타내는 동사 demands의 목적어인 that절이 당위성(~해야 한다)을 전달하므로, ‘should+동사원형’에서 should가 생략된 형태인 동사원형 design은 알맞다.
ⓗ with와 명사구 more and more countries에 이어져 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)(~가 …하면서, ~가 …한 채로)’ 구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 앞의 명사구가 ‘~에 동참하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the cause가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 joining은 알맞다.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: more devices will reach landfills
far less e-waste will be generated
manufacturers will improve product design

solution:
고장 난 장치들이 수리하기가 너무 어려워 많은 경우 버려지는 문제를 해결하기 위해 수리할 권리 운동은 소비자들이 자신의 제품을 직접 고치거나 자신이 선택한 기술자에게 고칠 수 있는 권리를 보호할 것을 명시하는 법률 제정을 추진한다고 했으므로, 요구하는 모든 목표가 이루어질 경우 기대되는 결과로서 전자 쓰레기가 줄어들 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘훨씬 더 적은 전자 쓰레기가 발생할 것이다’가 알맞다.

body:
In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a (A)[symbol-based / color-coded] system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.
The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with (B)[fewer / more] electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is (C)[likely / unlikely] to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

choices: symbol-based fewer likely

symbol-based more unlikely

solution:
(A) 초록색 라벨의 높은 숫자는 수리가 쉽다는 것을, 밝은 빨간색 라벨의 낮은 숫자는 수리가 어렵다는 것을 나타낸다고 설명하므로, 0에서 10 사이의 점수와 함께 색상으로 표시되는 시스템을 사용한다는 흐름이 되는 color-coded(색상으로 표시되는)가 알맞다.
symbol-based 기호에 기반을 둔

Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a (A)[symbol-based / color-coded] system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.
The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with (B)[fewer / more] electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is (C)[likely / unlikely] to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

body:
Have you ever wondered, “What if I could run so fast ⓐthat nobody could see me?” If you have asked this kind of question, you may be ready to become the next Galileo. The Italian scientist Galileo Galilei is famous for a thought experiment, ⓑwhich is an imaginary experiment designed to explore a mathematical or scientific hypothesis. With only his thoughts, he demonstrated ⓒthat objects with different masses should fall at the same speed when ⓓdrop from the same height in the absence of air resistance. With a hypothesis ⓔbased on creativity and imagination, anyone can become a great scientist.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ drop → dropped (접속사 when 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 접속사를 생략하지 않은 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 objects with different masses가 ‘떨어뜨리는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 dropped로 고친다.
참고로 drop은 자동사로도 쓰일 수 있지만 해당 내용은 동일한 높이에서 물체들을 떨어뜨리는 실험 조건으로 쓰였기에 본문에는 과거분사 dropped이 쓰였다.)
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 완전한 절(nobody could see me)을 이끌고 있으므로 접속사 that은 알맞으며, 앞의 so와 함께 쓰여 ‘so+형용사/부사(fast)+that+완전한 절(매우 ~해서 …하다)’의 구문을 이루고 있다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ hypothesis)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 a thought experiment를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which는 적절하다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(objects ~ speed)을 이끌어 동사 demonstrated의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ 전치사의 목적어로 쓰인 명사구 a hypothesis를 수식하는 자리이며 수식받는 명사구 a hypothesis가 ‘근거를[기반을] 둔’ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사형 형용사 based가 쓰였다.

body:
1. What if the size of a human body became enormous?
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
(A) However, the area of the feet supporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means ⓐthat his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased far more than the area of his feet.
(B) In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is ⓑgenerated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body.
(C) One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight ⓒpushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight ⓓchanges in proportion to volume.
If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated ⓔwould have increased a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. This shows that while we may wish to grow ⓕas tall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 물체의 길이가 2배가 되면 면적은 4배, 용적은 8배로 증가하고, 이러한 변화가 거인의 생명을 위험에 빠뜨릴 많은 문제들을 만들 수 있다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 앞에서 언급한 많은 문제들(many problems) 중 첫 번째 문제(One issue)로 키가 10배가 되면 무게는 1,000배 증가하여 거인이 똑바로 서 있을 수 없다고 설명하는 (C), However(그러나)를 통해 무게가 1,000배 증가하지만, 발의 면적은 100배만 증가한다는 상반된 내용이 이어지는 (A), (A)의 마지막 문장에서 질량이 발의 면적보다 훨씬 더 많이 증가하여 발이 지나치게 많은 압력을 받게 된다고 설명한 뒤, In addition(게다가)으로 시작하여 체중으로 인한 압력 문제에 이어서 또 다른 문제인 열 배출 문제를 추가로 설명하는 (B)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

solution:
어색한 것은 총 1개이다.

body:
1. What if the size of a human body became enormous?
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
(A) However, the area of the feet supporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means ⓐthat his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased far more than the area of his feet.
(B) In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is ⓑgenerated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body.
(C) One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight ⓒpushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight ⓓchanges in proportion to volume.
If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated ⓔwould have increased a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. This shows that while we may wish to grow ⓕas tall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.

body:
“O, swear not by the moon, the (A)[constant / inconstant] moon.” This is a famous line from Romeo and Juliet. Juliet warns Romeo not to swear his love by the Moon as it may change just as the Moon changes its shape. Although its appearance changes, the Moon is always present in the night sky and plays a crucial role in regulating the length of the day on Earth as well as the Earth’s seasons and weather patterns. Then, what would happen if there were no Moon?
Without the Moon, our day ㉠[will / would] no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and ㉡[fall / falls]. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a(n) (B)[increase / decrease] in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a (C)[change / consistency] in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates ㉢[that / what] without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: inconstant increase consistency
constant increase consistency
inconstant decrease change
constant decrease change
inconstant decrease consistency
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 줄리엣이 달의 모양이 변하는 것처럼 사랑도 변할 수 있으므로 로미오에게 달을 두고 사랑을 맹세하지 말라고 경고한다고 했으므로 변덕스러운 달에 맹세하지 말라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 inconstant(변덕스러운)가 적절하다.
constant 변함없는
(B) 뒤에서 달이 없으면 지구의 자전 속도가 줄지 않는다고 했으므로 마찰이 있으면 자전 속도가 감소한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 a decrease(감소)가 적절하다.
increase 증가
(C) 뒤에 달이 없었을 때 하루 길이가 5시간이었다고 언급하고 있으므로, 달이 없어서 지구의 자전 속도가 줄지 않으면 하루의 길이에 변화가 있을 것 이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 change(변화)가 적절하다.
consistency 일관성

solution:
㉠ ‘Without+명사(구)’는 ‘만약 ~이 없다면/없었다면’이라는 뜻으로, 여기서는 ‘달이 없다면‘의 의미로 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하고 있다. 따라서 가정법 과거를 나타내는 주절이 이어져야 하므로 ‘주어+과거 조동사+동사원형 ~’이 되도록 조동사 would가 적절하다.
㉡ 동사 causes의 목적격보어 to rise와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로 to를 생략한 동사원형 fall이 적절하다.

body:
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially making summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Lunar gravity helps keep the Earth’s rotational axis from shifting dramatically.
In the Moon’s absence, Earth’s axial angle could vary far more than it does now.
With a 60-degree tilt, sunlight would be distributed more evenly between the two hemispheres.
Major changes in Earth’s orientation could intensify the contrast between summer and winter.
Prolonged climatic instability could eventually make the Earth unsuitable for human habitation.
solution:
지구가 60도의 각도로 기울어지면, 태양을 접하고 있는 지구의 반구는 다른 반구보다 태양으로부터 훨씬 더 많은 에너지를 받게 될 것이라고 했으므로 ③ ‘60도의 기울기를 가지면, 햇빛은 두 반구 사이에 더 고르게 분배될 것이다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 달의 중력은 지구의 자전축이 급격하게 바뀌는 것을 막는 데 도움을 준다.
② 달이 없는 경우, 지구의 자전축 각도는 현재보다 훨씬 더 크게 변할 수 있다.
④ 지구의 방향에 있어서의 큰 변화는 여름과 겨울의 차이를 심화할 수 있다.

body:
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, making up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as efficient as lungs at taking in air.
㉠______, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain. Dragonflies, ㉡______, may become as large as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.

윗글의 빈칸 ㉠, ㉡에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: In fact Consequently
Therefore For example
However That is to say
As a result Thus
Nonetheless For instance
solution:
㉠ 곤충들의 숨구멍이 공기를 받아들이는 데 효율적이지 않기 때문에, 현재의 산소 농도에서는 몸 깊숙한 곳까지 충분한 산소를 전달하기 어려워 곤충들이 더 크게 자랄 수 없다는 결과로 이어지므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 Therefore(그러므로), As a result(그 결과)가 적절하다.
㉡ 앞에서 설명한 산소 농도가 두 배가 되면 곤충의 크기가 커져 생태 환경에 영향을 미친다는 주장의 구체적인 사례로, 뒤에서 잠자리의 크기가 커져 생태계의 포식자와 먹이의 균형을 변화시킨다는 내용이 이어지므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 For example(예를 들어), For instance(예를 들어)가 적절하다.

solution:

(B) 완전한 절(the increase ~ exercise)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절(that ~ it)이 있으므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 Considering이 적절하다. 참고로 ’considering (that) ~’은 ‘~을 고려하면’을 뜻하는 비인칭 독립 분사구문이며, 접속사처럼 기능하는 관용 표현이다.
