body:
In movies, hackers are often shown sitting in front of a computer, ⓐtried to figure out other people’s passwords. Is your password safe? That depends on how securely it was created. According to one survey, 26% of adults use passwords ⓑthat are easy to memorize, such as birthdays or names, and surprisingly, the most common passwords used were “123456,” “password,” “12345,” “12345678,” and “qwerty.”
The passwords used for mobile phones and banks ⓒbeing often four digits, and these are not very secure. Each digit can be selected from 10 numbers from 0 to 9, so there are 10⁴ possible codes. A computer can try all 10,000 combinations in the blink of an eye.
(A) ⓓUse a passphrase with a story will make it easy to memorize, even if the phrase is long. For example, if you use a passphrase like “mathfirstenglishlater,” which means that you will study math first and English later, it will be easy to memorize but difficult to hack. You can make your password even ⓔmore securely by adding capital letters and special characters. For example, “mathfirst,Englishlater” is a very secure password.
(B) Passwords become difficult to hack when they are long and combine various characters. There can be 90²º combinations for a 20-digit password using around 90 letters, numbers, and special characters on a standard computer keyboard. However, there is a problem here as well. How will the user memorize this long password? Passwords should not be too easy but also not too ⓕcomplicated to memorize.
(C) Let’s assume that, for security purposes, you create a password with six or more letters. Choosing a word with six or more letters as a password may be more secure. Six letters from the 26-letter alphabet ⓖmake a possible 26⁶ combinations, or more than 300 million total possibilities. It’s much better than a four-digit combination, though it’s still possible for a computer to check them all in only a few seconds.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 4개이다.
ⓐ tried → trying (앞의 완전한 절(hackers are often shown sitting in front of a computer)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞의 ’sitting in front of a computer’에 연결되어 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 hackers가 비밀번호를 알아내려고 ‘노력하는’ 주체이므로, tried를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 trying으로 고친다.)
ⓒ being → are (과거분사구 ‘used for mobile phones and banks’의 수식을 받는 주어 The passwords에 대한 동사가 필요하며, 문장이 일반적 사실을 나타내므로 현재시제를 사용해야 하고, 주어가 복수명사구이므로, being을 현재형이자 복수동사로 수일치한 are로 고친다.)
ⓓ Use → Using 또는 To use (문장의 동사구 will make에 대한 주어로 동명사구나 to부정사구를 이루어야 하므로, Use를 Using 또는 To use로 고친다.)
ⓔ more securely → more secure (make와 목적어 your password에 이어져 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …하게[…한 상태로] 만들다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, 보어로 부사는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사의 비교급 more securely를 형용사의 비교급 more secure로 고친다.)

ⓒ 팀의 감독이 자신만의 기준을 사용해 다른 팀들이 돈을 지급하기를 거절한 가치 있는 선수들을 영입했고, 그 선수들은 타율은 낮았지만 볼넷을 잘 얻고 출루율이 높았다고 설명하므로, 전체 메이저리그에서 세 번째로 낮은 총 선수 연봉을 가지고 있었음에도 불구하고 2년 연속 플레이오프에 진출했다는 흐름이 되는 reached(~에 도달했다)가 알맞다.

body:
Baseball is a game of statistics. It’s essential to know how many hits a batter can get and how many bases they can reach. Traditionally, batting average, which measures how often a player gets a hit, has been considered the most important criterion. However, in baseball, there is another way to reach first base besides a hit, and that’s a walk. Nevertheless, walks aren’t included in batting average, so players who don’t get many hits but are good at getting walks could be rated too ⓐ[high / low]. If players get on base in any way, they create scoring opportunities. (A)______, recent analyses have shown that on-base percentage is much more important for winning than batting averages.
A general manager of a professional baseball team in the United States, whose team could not afford to pay the biggest star players, created his own criteria for selecting players. His system valued how many bases a player averages per at-bat. It differed from the traditional batting average by ⓑ[reflecting / neglecting] not only the number of hits but also the types of hits (singles, doubles, triples, and home runs). It gave 1 point for singles, 2 points for doubles, 3 points for triples, and 4 points for home runs. Moreover, the system considered a player’s ability to draw walks as it contributes to getting on base and overall team success.
Using such standards, the team recruited valuable players other teams declined to pay. These players had low batting averages but excelled at drawing walks and had high on-base percentages. Despite having the third-lowest total player salary in the entire Major Leagues, the team ⓒ[reached / missed] the playoffs two years in a row, all thanks to this analytical approach.
(B)______, math is a subject that we use every day, from simple calculations to more complex problem-solving. It is a powerful tool that we need to navigate the world around us and to live efficiently and conveniently. Therefore, understanding basic math concepts is essential for making informed decisions.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: Hence / To conclude
Therefore / Furthermore
For example / In conclusion
Nevertheless / In contrast
For instance / Conversely
solution:
(A) 선수들이 출루하면 어떤 식으로든 득점 기회를 만든다는 앞 내용을 근거로 최근의 분석 결과들은 출루율이 타율보다 승리에 더 중요하다는 것을 보여 주었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 인과관계를 나타내는 Hence(따라서) 또는 Therefore(그러므로)가 알맞다.
(B) 수학과 통계적 분석을 활용해 효과적으로 선수를 기용한 야구 팀 감독의 사례를 다룬 뒤, 수학은 우리가 매일 사용하는 과목이며, 주변 세계를 탐색하고 효율적이고 편리하게 생활하는 데 필요한 강력한 도구로서 현명한 의사 결정에 필수적이라고 결론을 짓고 있으므로, To conclude(마지막으로, 결론적으로 말하면) 또는 In conclusion(결론적으로)이 알맞다.

body:
Riding a swift sleigh pulled by his friend Rudolph, Santa Claus begins a spectacular journey across the globe the day before Christmas, delivering presents such as dolls and toys to children everywhere. It’s a magical adventure that sparks our imaginations, but have you ever wondered just how fast Santa would need to travel to visit all the children in just one day? Let’s use some math to explore this interesting scenario.
It is obvious that Santa Claus, playing the role of a sleigh pilot in just one day, must deliver presents to children without skipping a single house. According to the United Nations’ 2022 World Population Prospects report, our world is home to approximately eight billion people, and among them, there are roughly two billion children under 14 years old. If we assume an average of two children per household, Santa would need to visit one billion households worldwide.
If we assume a simple distance of five meters between each house, Santa would have to cover a total distance of five billion meters, which amounts to five million kilometers. To accomplish this in one Christmas day, Santa’s noble mission remains a challenge, requiring a swift motion at a speed exceeding 200,000 kilometers per hour or approximately 58 kilometers per second. This is about 200 times faster than commercial airplanes typically fly.
Of course, it’s important to remember that this scenario ______. But from a mathematical perspective, it’s truly fascinating to visualize the extraordinary task that Santa Claus and Rudolph would have to undertake to make Christmas magical for children around the world. It’s a sophisticated reminder that the spirit of the holiday season exceeds the boundaries of time and space, bringing joy to countless hearts.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: is mainly designed to explain the science of modern aviation
is a symbolic expression of the spirit of the holiday season
is increasingly realistic with modern transportation technology
is based on a realistic interpretation of Santa’s journey
is purely imaginary and impossible in the real world
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

W: Eucalyptus has an amazing ability to recover and grow again after a fire. When a fire sweeps through a eucalyptus’s habitat, the intense heat causes the protective shell that holds the eucalyptus seeds to break open and release them. These seeds scatter and fall onto the burnt ground. (A)The fire also burns away other plants that compete with eucalyptus for sunlight, water, and nutrients. (B)Eucalyptus oil is widely extracted and used in cough drops, ointments, and aromatherapy products around the world. (C)With fewer competitors and a cleared area, the eucalyptus seeds have a better chance to sprout and grow. (D)They quickly produce new branches and leaves, utilizing the nutrients released into the soil from the ashes of the fire as a resource to fuel their rapid growth. (E)This demonstrates how eucalyptus has a superior ability to renew and adapt.

다음 담화의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: eucalyptus는 화재 후에 회복하고 다시 자랄 수 있는 놀라운 능력을 가지고 있으며 산불로 발생한 극심한 열이 eucalyptus 씨앗을 담고 있는 보호 껍질을 깨 씨앗들이 방출되게 하고, 씨앗들은 불에 탄 땅에 떨어지고, 산불은 eucalyptus와 햇빛, 물, 영양분을 위해 경쟁하는 다른 식물들도 태워 없앤다고 설명하는 흐름 속에서 eucalyptus 기름이 활용되는 분야를 언급한 (B) ‘eucalyptus 기름은 널리 추출되어 전 세계적으로 기침약, 연고, 아로마테라피 제품에 사용된다.’는 담화의 흐름과 관계없다.

G: I’ve heard it’s about two to four weeks until they hatch and are ready to be released.

The male seahorse is responsible for fertilizing the eggs after they are placed in his pouch.
It takes about two to four weeks for the eggs to hatch inside the male's pouch.
The girl personally witnessed a male seahorse giving birth in the wild.

Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created ⓐdiverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques they have developed. Let’s discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds.
Plants will do anything to ⓑspread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that ⓒattracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. (A)그것은 동물들이 맛있는 과육을 먹도록 유혹하며, 그렇게 함으로써 동물들이 그 씨앗들을 먹도록 합니다. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts ⓓdamaged. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In ⓔexchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓓ damaged(손상된) → untouched(훼손되지 않은)

Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created ⓐdiverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques they have developed. Let’s discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds.
Plants will do anything to ⓑspread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In ⓔexchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• to부정사구를 두 번 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>에 주어진 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 주어진 단어를 제외하고 14단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
fruit, the seeds, get, tempt, thereby, delicious, fruit flesh, them
It ______.
answer: tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds
solution:
• '…가 ~하도록 유혹하다‘의 의미를 갖는 'tempt+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구조가 되도록 제시된 주어 It에 수일치한 단수동사 tempts, 목적어 animals, 목적격보어로 to부정사구 to eat을 이어준다.
• to eat의 목적어로 명사구 delicious fruit flesh를 이어준다.
• '그렇게 함으로써‘의 의미를 갖는 부사 thereby와 함께 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 영작하되, 앞 절의 내용이 ’~하게 시키는, ~하도록 하는‘ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 준사역동사 get의 현재분사 getting을 쓴다.
• '.…가 ~하도록 시키다[~하게 하다]의 ’get+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)‘ 구문을 사용하여 getting의 목적어로 animals를 가리키는 them, 목적격보어로 to eat the seeds를 이어준다.

body:
The Worst Free Rider
Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. (A) Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. (B) Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. (C) Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. (D) As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals. (E)
As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is how devil’s claw became known as ㉠______.

Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘구미가 당기는 달콤한 과일 대신, 이 씨앗들은 날카로운 갈고리나 바늘을 갖추고 있습니다.’라는 뜻으로, these seeds로 가리킬 수 있는 것이 위치해야 한다. 따라서 지나가는 동물들에게 씨앗들을 붙여서 아무런 보답 없이 씨앗들을 퍼뜨린다는 내용 뒤이자, devil’s claw가 이러한 식물들 중 가장 악랄한 것으로 눈에 띈다는 내용 앞인 (A)에 들어가야 한다.

body:
ⓐOut of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground ⓑto eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓒwere antelope dung. ⓓThat is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They ⓔhave no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By (A)______, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: '~ 중에서‘의 의미로, 뒤에 가산명사가 이어질 때 복수형이 온다.
ⓑ: 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 형용사적 용법으로 쓰였다.
ⓒ: as if에 이어지는 가정법으로, 실제로 영양물의 배설물이 아니기에 과거형 were이 쓰였다.

body:
ⓐOut of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground ⓑto eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓒwere antelope dung. ⓓThat is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They ⓔhave no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By (A)______, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: developing structures that attach to moving animals
helping dung beetles locate real dung more efficiently
tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying its seeds
producing sweet fruit that attracts animals to consume its seeds
protecting its seeds inside a hard outer covering until they germinate
solution:
앞에서 silver arrow-reed의 씨앗은 쇠똥구리를 속임으로써 씨앗을 퍼뜨린다고 언급되었으며, silver arrow-reed의 씨앗의 생김새와 냄새가 쇠똥구리가 먹거나 알을 낳는 영양의 똥과 매우 흡사해서, 쇠똥구리가 그 씨앗을 진짜 똥으로 착각하고 굴려서 땅에 묻게 되므로, 빈칸에는 ③ ‘쇠똥구리를 속여 자신의 씨앗을 굴려 가져가 묻게 함’이 들어가야 한다.

body:
Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. (A)날개에 의해 발생된 회전은 단풍나무 씨앗이 회전하지 않는 씨앗들보다 두 배 더 높이 올라갈 수 있게 합니다. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 분사구를 사용할 것
• 원급 비교를 사용할 것
• <보기>에 주어진 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 18단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
twice, allow, elevate, high, cause, its wings, the rotation, non-rotating
→ ______
answer: The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds.
solution:
• 주어 The rotation이 ‘발생된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사구 caused by its wings를 쓴다.
• 주어 The rotation에 수일치한 단수 동사 allows를 쓰고, ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어‘의 구조가 되도록 영작하되, to부정사를 목적격보어로 취하는 동사이므로 allows 뒤에 목적어 the maple seed, 목적격보어 to elevate을 쓴다.
• '배수사+as+원급+as ~'의 어순으로 쓰되 elevate를 수식하는 부사의 원급을 사용하여 twice as high as를 쓰고 비교 대상인 non-rotating seeds를 이어준다.

body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only (A)[retain / release] their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly (B)[flammable / nonflammable] in oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently (C)[exposed / concealed] in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: retain flammable exposed
release flammable concealed
release nonflammable concealed
retain nonflammable concealed
release flammable exposed
solution:
(A) 모체 식물에서 분리되는 경우를 말하고 있으므로, 일부 식물들은 극심한 경험을 견딘 뒤에서 씨앗을 ‘방출한다(release)'는 흐름이 자연스럽다.
retain 보유하다, 유지하다
(B) 유칼립투스 잎은 서로 마찰하면서 자연적으로 불이 붙을 정도이므로, 잎들이 아주 높은 ’flammable(가연성의, 인화성의)' 기름을 가졌다는 것이 흐름상 자연스럽다.
nonflammable 불연성의
(C) 가혹한 환경으로부터 그것을 보호한다는 내용이 이어지므로 화재 후에 남은 부드러운 재 속에 ‘concealed(감춰진)’이 흐름상 자연스럽다.
expose 노출하다

body:
Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms (A)[resembling / resembled] pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals.
As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them (B)[feel / to feel] like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is (C)[how / what] devil’s claw became known as the worst free rider.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: resembling feel how
resembling to feel how
resembled to feel what
resembling feel what
resembled feel how
solution:
(A) 뒤에 문장의 동사 transform이 있으므로 앞의 명사구 Its blossoms를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘닮은’ 주체이자 resemble은 수동태를 만들 수 없는 동사이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 resembling이 알맞다.
(B) 사역동사 make의 목적격보어로 동사원형 feel이 알맞다.
(C) 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지므로 ‘~하는 방법’의 의미를 갖는 관계부사 how가 알맞다.

body:
Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy ⓐto find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world’s tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, ⓑwhich was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height ⓒthat they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning “the highest one.” However, the odds of you ⓓseeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making ⓔthat nearly impossible to identify from the ground. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ that → it (뒤에 진목적어 to identify가 이어지므로, 'make+가목적어+목적격보어(형용사)+진목적어(to부정사)'의 구조로, that을 가목적어 it으로 고쳐야 한다.)
오답
ⓐ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사구 to find는 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘so ~ that+완전한 절(너무 ~해서 …하다)‘의 의미를 갖는 구문으로, 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사 that으로 알맞다.
ⓓ 전치사 of의 목적어 역할을 하는 동명사 seeing이며, you는 동명사의 의미상 주어로 알맞다.

body:
Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

the nutritional value of jackfruit compared to other tropical fruits

body:
Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world’s tallest tree.
(A) The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making it nearly impossible to identify from the ground. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.
(B) However, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think.
(C) Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning “the highest one.”

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 세계에서 가장 높은 나무에 대해 말하며, Hyperion이라 불리는 redwood는 세계에서 가장 높은 나무로 115m에 달한다는 주어진 글에 이어, Hyperion가 어떻게 발견되었고 이름 붙여졌는지를 설명하는 (C)에 이어, However로 이어져 정작 공원에 가더라도 Hyperion을 직접 볼 가능성은 거의 없다는 (B), redwood사이에서 그것을 쉽게 찾을 수 있을 것이라 생각하지만 어렵다고 답하는 (B)의 마지막 문장에 이어 그 이유를 설명하는 (A)의 순으로 이어져야 한다.

body:
Passwords become difficult to hack when they are long and combine various characters. There can be 90²º combinations for a 20-digit password using around 90 letters, numbers, and special characters on a standard computer keyboard. However, there is a problem here as well. How will the user memorize this long password? Passwords should not be too easy but also not too complicated to memorize.
Using a passphrase with a story will make it easy to memorize, even if the phrase is long. For example, if you use a passphrase like “mathfirstenglishlater,” which means that you will study math first and English later, it will be easy to memorize but difficult to hack. You can make your password even more secure by adding capital letters and special characters. For example, “mathfirst,Englishlater” is a very secure password.

In movies, hackers are often shown sitting in front of a computer, trying to ⓐfigure out other people’s passwords. Is your password safe? That depends on how securely it was created.
According to one survey, 26% of adults use passwords that are easy to ⓑmemorize, such as birthdays or names, and surprisingly, the most common passwords used were “123456,” “password,” “12345,” “12345678,” and “qwerty.”
The passwords used for mobile phones and banks are often four digits, and these are not very secure. Each digit can be selected from 10 numbers from 0 to 9, so there are 10⁴ possible codes. A computer can try all 10,000 combinations ⓒin the blink of an eye. Let’s assume that, for security purposes, you create a password with six or more letters. Choosing a word with six or more letters as a password may be ⓓmore secure. Six letters from the 26-letter alphabet make a possible 26⁶ combinations, or more than 300 million total possibilities. It’s much better than a four-digit combination, though it’s still ⓔimpossible for a computer to check them all in only a few seconds.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ impossible(불가능한) → possible(가능한)

body:
Baseball is a game of statistics. It’s essential to know how many hits a batter can get and how many bases they can reach. (A)전통적으로, 타율은 선수가 얼마나 자주 안타를 치는지를 측정하며, 가장 중요한 기준으로 여겨졌다. However, in baseball, there is another way to reach first base besides a hit, and that’s a walk. Nevertheless, walks aren’t included in batting average, so players who don’t get many hits but are good at getting walks could be rated too low. If players get on base in any way, they create scoring opportunities. Therefore, recent analyses have shown that (B)______ is much more important for winning than batting averages.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• 현재시제와 현재완료를 한 번씩 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
get, consider, measure, a player, often, a hit, batting average
→ Traditionally, ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ the most important criterion.
answer: batting average, which measures how often a player gets a hit, has been considered
solution:
• 주어로 제시된 명사구 batting average를 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사를 사용해 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 쓴다. 즉, 선행사에 어울리는 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사로 which를 쓰고, 관계사절의 내용은 일반적 사실이므로 <조건>에 따라 현재시제를 사용하되, 선행사가 복수명사구이므로 수일치를 위해 동사 measure를 단수동사 measures로 변형한다.
• measures의 목적어 자리에 ’얼마나 자주‘라는 뜻의 의문사구 how often으로 시작하는 의문사절을 쓰되, 간접의문문은 ’의문사구+평서문‘의 어순이 되어야 하므로 how often 뒤에 ’주어+동사+목적어‘의 순서로 a player gets a hit을 쓴다.
• 타율이 중요한 기준으로 여겨진 것은 현재까지 영향을 미치는 일이므로 주절에 <조건>에 따라 현재완료(have[has]+p.p.)를 사용하되, 주어 batting average가 ‘여겨진’ 대상이고, 명사구 the most important criterion은 consider의 목적어가 아니라 수동 표현인 ‘consider+목적어+(to be+)보어(~을 …라고 여기다)’의 보어에 해당하므로, ‘be considered+(to be+)보어(…라고 여겨지다)’를 사용해 현재완료 수동태(have[has]+been+p.p.)로 써야 한다. 따라서 단수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 단수 조동사 has와 been을 쓴 뒤, consider를 과거분사 considered로 변형한다.

Mathematics is beneficial in everyday life. We use math concepts and skills to understand patterns, define relationships, and predict the future. You would be (A)[amazing / amazed] to see the emergence of math in unexpected situations. Here are a few examples.
The Mathematics of Airplane Boarding
What is the most efficient way to (B)[board / boarding] a plane? The standard procedure starts by boarding first class, then business class, and then economy class. In the case of economy class passengers, they are divided into blocks according to their seat rows to board. This often ⓐ______. Mathematicians compared various boarding methods and found (C)[what / that] boarding a plane starting from the front row took the longest while starting from the back row took the second longest.

amazed board what
solution:

(B) ’~하는 방법‘이라는 뜻으로 ’way+to부정사(구)‘를 사용하므로, to 뒤에 to부정사(to+동사원형)를 이루는 동사원형 board가 알맞다.
(C) 완전한 절(boarding ~ second longest)을 이끌어 동사 found의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• (1)에는 적절한 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되 필요시 변형 및 추가할 것
• (1)과 (2) 각각 7단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
pay, the biggest star players, select, afford, team, his own criteria for, can, create
→ A general manager of a professional baseball team in the United States, (1)______ the biggest star players, (2)______.
answer:
(1) whose team could not afford to pay
(2) created his own criteria for selecting players
solution:
(1) • <조건>에 따라 적절한 관계대명사를 사용하되, 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어(A general manager ~ in the United States)를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이끌어야 하고, 선행사인 주어가 명사 team과 소유 관계이므로, 계속적 용법의 소유격 관계대명사 whose 뒤에 명사 team을 쓴다.

(2) • 삽입된 관계사절에 이어진 문장의 동사 자리에 create를 시제에 맞게 과거형 created로 변형하고 목적어 자리에 his own criteria for를 쓴다.
• 전치사 for의 목적어 자리에 select를 동명사 selecting으로 변형하고 동명사의 목적어로 명사 players를 써서 완성한다.

Riding a swift sleigh pulled by his friend Rudolph, Santa Claus begins a spectacular journey across the globe the day before Christmas, delivering presents such as dolls and toys to children everywhere. It’s a magical adventure that sparks our imaginations, but have you ever wondered just how fast Santa would need to travel to visit all the children in just one day? Let’s use some math to explore this interesting scenario.
(A) Of course, it’s important to remember that this scenario is purely imaginary and impossible in the real world. But from a mathematical perspective, it’s truly fascinating to visualize the extraordinary task that Santa Claus and Rudolph would have to undertake to make Christmas magical for children around the world. It’s a sophisticated reminder that the spirit of the holiday season exceeds the boundaries of time and space, bringing joy to countless hearts.
(B) If we assume a simple distance of five meters between each house, Santa would have to cover a total distance of five billion meters, which amounts to five million kilometers. To accomplish this in one Christmas day, Santa’s noble mission remains a challenge, requiring a swift motion at a speed exceeding 200,000 kilometers per hour or approximately 58 kilometers per second. This is about 200 times faster than commercial airplanes typically fly.
(C) It is obvious that Santa Claus, playing the role of a sleigh pilot in just one day, must deliver presents to children without skipping a single house. According to the United Nations’ 2022 World Population Prospects report, our world is home to approximately eight billion people, and among them, there are roughly two billion children under 14 years old. If we assume an average of two children per household, Santa would need to visit one billion households worldwide.
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 산타클로스가 크리스마스 전날 전 세계 어린이들에게 선물을 전달하려면 얼마나 빠르게 이동해야 하는지 수학을 활용해 알아보자는 주어진 글 다음에, 수학적 문제를 구체적으로 계산하기 위한 기초 자료로 세계 인구와 어린이 수를 제시하고, 가구당 평균 두 명의 어린이가 있다고 가정하여 산타가 방문해야 할 가구를 약 10억 가구로 산출한 (C), 이어서 가구 간 거리를 가정하여 총 이동 거리와 하루 안에 이동하기 위해 필요한 속도를 계산한 (B), 앞서 가정한 수학적 시나리오를 this scenario(이 시나리오)로 받아, 이러한 시나리오가 상상에 기반한 것이지만 수학적 관점에서 산타의 비범한 임무를 생각해 보는 것이 매혹적이며, 연휴 시즌의 분위기가 시공간의 경계를 초월해 수많은 마음에 기쁨을 가져다준다는 것을 세련된 방식으로 상기시켜 주는 것이라고 마무리하는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
What is the most efficient way to board a plane? The standard procedure starts by boarding first class, then business class, and then economy class. In the case of economy class passengers, they are divided into blocks according to their seat rows to board. This often results in a crowded, chaotic situation for passengers. Mathematicians compared various boarding methods and found that boarding a plane starting from the front row took the longest while ⓐstarting from the back row took the second longest.
From a mathematical point of view, the most efficient way appears ⓑbeing seating passengers by the window, starting from the back. Then, passengers in the aisle seats board next, from back to front. This way, passengers can store their bags in the overhead bins almost simultaneously without disturbing each other. Further, since the boarding starts from the back, there is no need for passengers ⓒto pass each other. Moreover, filling window seats first gets rid of the trouble of aisle seat passengers ⓓhave to stand up and move into the aisle while others take their seats. In short, the most efficient way is to start with window seat passengers and ⓔmove from back to front.
윗글의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to compare the costs of different airplane boarding procedures
to investigate the causes of congestion during conventional airplane boarding
to explain how mathematical models can predict passenger behavior during boarding
to examine the optimal airplane boarding method from a mathematical perspective
to propose practical strategies for minimizing passengers’ inconvenience during air travel

Using a passphrase with a story will make it easy to memorize, even if the phrase is long.

Passwords become difficult to hack when they are long and combine various characters. There can be 90²º combinations for a 20-digit password using around 90 letters, numbers, and special characters on a standard computer keyboard. However, there is a problem here as well. (A) How will the user memorize this long password? (B) Passwords should not be too easy but also not too complicated to memorize. (C) For example, if you use a passphrase like “mathfirstenglishlater,” which means that you will study math first and English later, it will be easy to memorize but difficult to hack. (D) You can make your password even more secure by adding capital letters and special characters. (E) For example, “mathfirst,Englishlater” is a very secure password.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이야기가 있는 암호를 사용하면 구문이 길더라도 외우기 쉬워진다.’라는 뜻으로, 비밀번호는 길고 다양한 문자들을 결합할 때 해킹하기 어려워지지만 사용자가 외우기 어렵다는 문제점과 비밀번호는 너무 쉬워서도 안 되지만 외우기 너무 복잡해서도 안 된다는 조건을 언급한 뒤이자, 수학을 먼저 공부하고 영어를 나중에 공부한다는 의미를 담은 ‘mathfirstenglishlater’와 같은 문구를 구체적인 예시로 들어 여기에 대문자와 특수문자를 추가하면 외우기 쉬우면서도 안전하게 만들 수 있다고 부연 설명하는 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

The Mathematics of Airplane Boarding

What is the most efficient way to board a plane? The standard procedure starts by boarding first class, then business class, and then economy class. In the case of economy class passengers, they are divided into blocks according to their seat rows to board. This often ⓒresults in a crowded, chaotic situation for passengers. Mathematicians ⓓcompared various boarding methods and found that boarding a plane starting from the front row took the longest while starting from the back row took the second longest.

From a mathematical point of view, the most efficient way appears to be seating passengers by the window, starting from the back. Then, (A)______. This way, passengers can store their bags in the overhead bins almost simultaneously without disturbing each other. Further, since the boarding starts from the back, there is no need for passengers to pass each other. Moreover, filling window seats first ⓔbrings about the trouble of aisle seat passengers having to stand up and move into the aisle while others take their seats. In short, the most efficient way is to start with window seat passengers and move from back to front.

Passwords become difficult to hack when they are long and (A)[lack / combine] various characters. There can be 90²º combinations for a 20-digit password using around 90 letters, numbers, and special characters on a standard computer keyboard. However, there is a (B)[problem / benefit] here as well. How will the user memorize this long password? Passwords should not be too easy but also not too complicated to memorize.

Using a passphrase with a story will make it easy to memorize, even if the phrase is long. For example, if you use a passphrase like “mathfirstenglishlater,” which means that you will study math first and English later, it will be easy to memorize but difficult to hack. You can make your password even more secure by (C)[deleting / adding] capital letters and special characters. For example, “mathfirst,Englishlater” is a very secure password.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: lack / problem / deleting
combine / benefit / adding
combine / problem / adding
lack / benefit / adding
combine / problem / deleting
solution:
(A) 표준 컴퓨터 키보드에 있는 약 90개의 문자, 숫자 및 특수문자를 사용하면 20자리 비밀번호의 조합은 90²º개가 될 수 있다는 설명이 이어지므로, 비밀번호가 길고 다양한 문자를 결합할 때 해킹하기 어려워진다는 흐름이 되는 combine(~을 결합하다)이 알맞다.
(B) 이어지는 문장에서 사용자가 긴 비밀번호를 어떻게 외울 것인가라는 문제를 제시하며, 비밀번호는 너무 쉽지도, 외우기 너무 복잡하지도 않아야 한다고 설명하므로, 긴 비밀번호에 문제가 있다는 흐름이 되는 problem(문제)이 알맞다.
(C) 이야기를 활용하면 구문이 길더라도 외우기 쉽다고 하면서 예시로 “mathfirstenglishlater”를 제시한 뒤, 여기에 대문자와 특수문자를 사용한 “mathfirst,Englishlater”를 또 다시 예로 들어 매우 안전한 비밀번호라고 말하므로, 이야기가 있는 암호에 대문자와 특수문자를 추가하여 비밀번호를 더욱 안전하게 만들 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 adding(추가함)이 알맞다.

body:
Baseball is a game of statistics. It’s essential to know how many hits a batter can get and how many bases they can reach. Traditionally, batting average, which measures how often a player gets a hit, ⓐhas considered the most important criterion. However, in baseball, there is another way to reach first base besides a hit, and ㉠that’s a walk. (A)______, walks aren’t included in batting average, so players who don’t get many hits but ⓑare good at getting walks could be rated too low. If players get on base in any way, they create scoring opportunities. Therefore, recent analyses have shown ⓒthat on-base percentage is much more important for winning than batting averages.

A general manager of a professional baseball team in the United States, ⓓwhose team could not afford to pay the biggest star players, created his own criteria for selecting players. His system valued how many bases a player averages per at-bat. It differed from the traditional batting average by ⓔbeing taken into account not only the number of hits but also the types of hits (singles, doubles, triples, and home runs). It gave 1 point for singles, 2 points for doubles, 3 points for triples, and 4 points for home runs. (B)______, the system considered a player’s ability to draw walks as ㉡it contributes ⓕto get on base and overall team success.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. (단, 다른 단어를 추가하지 말 것)
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
answer:
(1) ⓐ → has been considered
(2) ⓔ → taking
(3) ⓕ → to getting
solution:
ⓐ 주어 batting average와 두 개의 콤마(,) 사이에 삽입된 관계사절(which measures ~a hit) 뒤에 문장의 동사가 올 자리이며, 흐름상 현재까지 영향을 미치는 일을 나타내기 위해 단수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 단수 조동사 has를 사용한 현재완료(have[has]+p.p.)가 쓰일 수 있으나, 주어가 ‘여겨진’ 대상이고, 뒤의 명사구 the most important criterion은 consider의 목적어가 아니라 수동 표현인 ‘consider+목적어+(to be+)보어(~을 …라고 여기다)’의 보어에 해당하므로, ‘be considered+(to be+)보어(…라고 여겨지다)’를 사용한 현재완료 수동태(have[has]+been+p.p.)를 써야 한다. 따라서 현재완료 능동태인 has considered를 현재완료 수동태인 has been considered로 고친다.
ⓔ 전치사 by 뒤에 ’by+동명사(구)(~함으로써)‘를 이루는 동명사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, ’take ~ into account(~을 고려하다)’에서 take의 목적어인 명사구가 ‘not only A but also B(A뿐만 아니라 B도)’의 구조로 길이가 길어 into account 뒤에 위치했으므로, 수동형 동명사(being p.p.)인 being taken을 능동형 동명사인 taking으로 고친다.
ⓕ ‘~에 기여하다’라는 뜻의 표현인 ‘contribute to ~’의 전치사 to 뒤에 목적어로 명사(구)나 동명사(구)가 와야 하므로, to get을 ‘전치사+동명사’ 형태인 to getting으로 고친다.

A general manager of a professional baseball team in the United States, whose team could not afford to pay the biggest star players, (A)[created / abandoned] his own criteria for selecting players. His system valued how many bases a player averages per at-bat. It differed from the traditional batting average by taking into account not only the number of hits but also the types of hits (singles, doubles, triples, and home runs). It gave 1 point for singles, 2 points for doubles, 3 points for triples, and 4 points for home runs. Moreover, the system considered a player’s ability to draw walks as it contributes to getting on base and overall team success.

Using such standards, the team recruited valuable players other teams declined to pay. These players had low batting averages but excelled at drawing walks and had high on-base percentages. Despite having the third-lowest total player salary in the entire Major Leagues, the team reached the playoffs two years in a row, all thanks to this (B)[intuitive / analytical] approach.

In conclusion, math is a subject that we use every day, from simple calculations to more complex problem-solving. It is a powerful tool that we need to navigate the world around us and to live efficiently and conveniently. Therefore, understanding basic math concepts is (C)[essential / inessential] for making informed decisions.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Limitations and Solutions of Mathematical Analysis in Modern Baseball Management
A Quantitative Framework for Predicting the Future Performance of Baseball Players
The Mathematical Approach to Maximizing Team Revenue in Professional Baseball
Math for Problem Solving: A Case of Using a Mathematical Approach in Baseball
How Low-Cost Players Can Compete with Baseball’s Elite Stars

body:
Riding a swift sleigh ⓐpulled by his friend Rudolph, Santa Claus begins a (A)spectacular journey across the globe the day before Christmas, delivering presents such as dolls and toys to children everywhere. It’s a magical adventure that (B)sparks our imaginations, but have you ever wondered just how fast Santa would need to travel ⓑto visit all the children in just one day? Let’s use some math to explore this interesting scenario.

It is obvious ⓒwhat Santa Claus, playing the role of a sleigh pilot in just one day, must deliver presents to children without (C)dropping in a single house. According to the United Nations’ 2022 World Population Prospects report, our world is home to approximately eight billion people, and among them, there are roughly two billion children under 14 years old. If we assume an average of two children per household, Santa would need to visit one billion households worldwide.

If we assume a simple distance of five meters between each house, Santa would have to (D)cover a total distance of five billion meters, which ⓓamounts to five million kilometers. To accomplish this in one Christmas day, Santa’s noble mission remains a challenge, ⓔrequires a swift motion at a speed (E)exceeding 200,000 kilometers per hour or approximately 58 kilometers per second. This is about 200 times faster than commercial airplanes typically fly.

Of course, it’s important to remember that this scenario is purely imaginary and impossible in the real world. (F)그러나 수학적인 관점에서 볼 때, 세계 모든 어린이에게 마법 같은 크리스마스를 만들기 위해 산타클로스와 루돌프가 맡을 비범한 과업을 상상하는 것은 정말로 매혹적이다. It’s a sophisticated reminder ⓕwhich the spirit of the holiday season exceeds the boundaries of time and space, bringing joy to countless hearts.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ 흐름상 앞의 명사구 a swift sleigh를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 수 있으며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘끌리는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 행위 주체를 나타내는 ‘by+명사구’가 이어져 있으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 pulled는 알맞다.
ⓑ 앞의 동사구 would need to travel에 흐름상 ‘방문하기 위해’라는 뜻으로 이어져야 하므로, 목적(~하기 위해)을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사인 to visit은 알맞다.
ⓓ 콤마(,) 뒤에 쓰인 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이며, 관계사절이 부연 설명하는 선행사 a total distance of six billion meters가 단수명사구이므로, 단수동사로 수일치한 amounts는 알맞다. 참고로, 자동사 amount와 전치사 to가 함께 쓰인 ’amount to ~’는 ‘(총계가) ~에 달하다’라는 뜻을 나타낸다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (F)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문을 사용할 것
• 목적격 관계대명사 that을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
would, visualize, undertake, make, have to, fascinate, magical, Santa Claus and Rudolph
→ But from a mathematical perspective, ______ truly ______ ______ ______ the extraordinary task ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ Christmas ______ for children around the world.
answer: But from a mathematical perspective, it’s truly fascinating to visualize the extraordinary task that Santa Claus and Rudolph would have to undertake to make Christmas magical for children around the world.
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문을 사용하되, 빈칸 수를 고려해 가주어 it과 동사 is를 축약해 it’s를 쓴다. 진주어절의 내용이 동사 fascinate(~을 매혹하다[~의 마음을 사로잡다])의 주체이므로, 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 형태의 형용사 fascinating으로 변형해 부사 truly 뒤에 쓴다. 보어인 형용사구 truly fascinating에 이어서 진주어인 to부정사구가 이어지도록 동사 visualize를 to부정사인 to visualize로 변형한다.
• <조건>에 따라 목적격 관계대명사 that을 사용해 선행사인 명사구 the extraordinary task를 수식하는 관계사절을 ‘that+목적어가 없는 불완전한 절’의 형태로 쓴다. 관계사절의 주어로 Santa Claus and Rudolph를 쓰고, 동사 자리에 조동사 would와 ‘~해야 한다’를 뜻하는 have to를 쓴 뒤, 타동사 undertake(~을 맡다)를 동사원형으로 쓰고, 선행사가 의미상 목적어에 해당하므로 undertake 뒤에 목적어를 다시 쓰지 않는다.
• 빈칸 수를 고려해 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 활용한다. ‘만들기 위해’라는 의미로 to부정사인 to make를 쓰고, ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)(~을 …하게[…한 상태로] 만들다)’의 5형식 구문을 활용해 make 뒤에 목적어 Christmas와 목적격보어인 형용사 magical을 쓴다.

body:
What is the most efficient way to board a plane? The standard procedure starts by boarding first class, then business class, and then economy class. In the case of economy class passengers, they are divided into blocks according to their seat rows to board. This often results in a crowded, chaotic situation for passengers. Mathematicians compared various boarding methods and (A)[found / finding] that boarding a plane starting from the front row took the longest while starting from the back row took the second longest.

From a mathematical point of view, the most efficient way appears to be seating passengers by the window, starting from the back. Then, passengers in the aisle seats board next, from back to front. This way, passengers can store their bags in the overhead bins almost simultaneously without (B)[disturbing / being disturbed] each other. Further, since the boarding starts from the back, there is no need for passengers to pass each other. ⓐ더욱이, 창가 좌석을 먼저 채우는 것은 복도 좌석 승객들이 다른 사람들이 착석하는 동안 일어나서 복도로 이동해야 하는 번거로움을 없애준다. In short, the most efficient way is to start with window seat passengers and (C)[moving / to move] from back to front.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: finding / disturbing / moving
finding / being disturbed / to move
found / disturbing / moving
found / disturbing / to move
found / being disturbed / to move
solution:
(A) 주어 Mathematicians에 대한 과거동사 compared와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, 과거동사 found가 알맞다.
(B) 의미상 주어 passengers가 ‘방해하는’ 주체이며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 each other가 있으므로, 능동형 동명사 disturbing이 알맞다.
(C) is의 보어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to start와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되므로, to부정사인 to move가 알맞다.

<조건>
• 동명사의 의미상 주어로 목적격 형태를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)

<보기>

→ Moreover, ______ ______ ______ first ______ ______ ______ the trouble of ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ while others take their seats.
answer: Moreover, filling window seats first gets rid of the trouble of aisle seat passengers having to stand up and move into the aisle while others take their seats.
solution:
• 빈칸 수를 고려하여 주어 자리에 동명사구가 오도록 fill을 동명사 filling으로 변형한 뒤, 동명사의 목적어로 명사구 window seats를 써서 주어부를 구성한다.
• 동명사(구) 주어는 단수 취급하므로, 수일치를 위해 get rid of의 get을 단수동사로 변형해 gets rid of를 쓴다.
• 명사구 the trouble과 동격 전치사 of 뒤에 앞의 추상명사구의 구체적인 내용에 해당하는 동명사구를 쓰되, 동명사의 의미상 주어는 동명사 앞에 목적격이나 소유격의 형태로 쓸 수 있으나 <조건>에 따라 목적격 형태로 명사구 aisle seat passengers를 먼저 쓰고 have to를 동명사구 having to로 변형한 뒤 동사원형 stand와 up을 쓴다. 이어서 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되도록 동사원형 move와 into를 쓰고, 전치사 into의 목적어로 명사구 the aisle을 쓴다.

body:
W: Good afternoon, students! Do you want to make your lunch break more valuable? Then join our on-campus lunchtime walking group and experience the magnificent benefits of taking a casual walk during your break. Do you know the Latin phrase, “Solvitur Ambulando”? It’s all about resolving problems by merely walking. Even research backs it up! Walking after eating fires up your metabolism, helps with the breakdown of food, and increases your energy. But that’s not all! When you walk outside, your stress goes down, your mood gets a sunny boost, and your brain gets sharper. It’s like a stress-relieving and mood-boosting therapy session in nature’s playground. I hope you’ll enjoy these benefits with our walking group! So put on your sneakers and make lunchtime the highlight of your day!

다음 담화의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to advise students to exercise during their lunch break
to explain how to relieve stress through walking outside
to inform students about the benefits of walking after lunch
to encourage students to join the lunchtime walking group
to announce a new schedule for the campus walking group
solution:
담화의 초반부에 학교 점심시간 산책 모임에 참여해보라고 권유하고, 쉬는 시간에 가볍게 산책하는 것의 이점을 설명한 뒤 마지막에 다시 한 번 산책 모임에 참여할 것을 권유하고 있으므로 이 담화의 목적으로 ④ ‘학생들에게 점심시간 걷기 모임에 참여하도록 권장하기 위해’가 적절하다.

② 야외에서 걷기를 통해 스트레스를 해소하는 방법을 설명하기 위해
③ 점심 식사 후 걷기의 이점에 대해 학생들에게 알리기 위해

body:
W: Logan, how was your weekend? Did you do anything special?
M: It was good. I went to the city homeless shelter as usual.
W: Are you saying that you visit there regularly?
M: Yeah. I volunteer there every Saturday, serving meals to people at the shelter.
W: That’s amazing. It must be rewarding.
M: It really is. Every week, I feel like I’ve made a difference in people’s lives.
W: That’s awesome. Did you know that volunteering can have a positive impact on your health, too?
M: What do you mean? Like an impact on physical health?
W: Yes. It can actually decrease your blood pressure and cholesterol level. It’s called the “Mother Teresa effect.”
M: Interesting... So rather than just helping others when I volunteer, it sounds like I’m benefiting a lot, too.
W: Kindness makes a world of difference!

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Logan volunteers at a homeless shelter every weekend.
One of the reasons Logan visits the shelter is to improve his physical health.
Volunteering can lower blood pressure and cholesterol levels.
Logan was not aware of the positive health effects of volunteering called the “Mother Teresa effect.”
Logan believes volunteering has made a meaningful difference in people’s lives.
solution:
대화 후반부에 Logan은 여자의 말을 통해 자원봉사가 신체적 건강에 미치는 긍정적인 효과에 대해 알게 되었으므로, ② ‘Logan이 보호소를 방문하는 이유 중 하나는 자신의 신체적 건강을 향상시키기 위해서이다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① Logan은 매주 주말 노숙인 보호소에서 자원봉사를 한다.
③ 자원봉사는 혈압과 콜레스테롤 수치를 낮출 수 있다.
④ Logan은 ‘마더 테레사 효과’라고 불리는 자원봉사의 긍정적인 건강 효과를 알지 못했다.
⑤ Logan은 자원봉사가 사람들의 삶에 의미 있는 변화를 가져왔다고 생각한다.

body:
A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often (A)sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar (B)commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means ⓐto be hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The (C)phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common ⓑthat the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either (D)skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. body:
Hunger and Hormones
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing the thing ⓐthat they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by ⓑreleasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

Hunger and the Brain
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists ⓒhave found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, ⓓwhich can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making ⓔis greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

ⓔ is → are (while이 이끄는 부사절의 동사로, 주어 the activity patterns가 복수 명사구이므로 이에 수일치한 are로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ to do의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they ~ do)을 이끌어 명사 the thing을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 목적격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
본문변형 what → the thing that
ⓑ 전치사 by의 목적어로 동명사 releasing이 온 것은 적절하다.
ⓒ 문맥상 신경학자들이 과거에 밝혀낸 것이 여전히 지속되고 있는 상태를 나타내는 현재완료형 have found는 적절하다.

While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon (A)[called / calling] “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and (B)[isolating / isolated] from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion (C)[that / what] loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

body:
You Are in Control
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. (A) Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. (B) In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. (C) For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. (D) Some researchers are also interested in how eating habits can influence people’s daily energy levels. (E) Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you’re just hangry.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 배고픔이 감정(짜증, 분노 등)과 생리·신경학적 반응에 미치는 영향, 그리고 이를 인지하고 조절하는 방법이 글의 핵심 내용이다. (A)에서는 배고픔에 대한 사람들의 생리적·신경학적 반응이 개인마다 다를 수 있다고 설명하고, (B)와 (C)에서는 이러한 배고픔과 동물의 행동 사이의 관계를 구체적인 사례를 통해 보여 주며, (E)에서는 배고픔으로 인한 부정적 감정을 인식하고 조절하는 방법에 관한 내용으로 자연스럽게 이어진다. 그러나 (D) ‘일부 연구자들은 식습관이 사람들의 일상적인 에너지 수준에 어떻게 영향을 미칠 수 있는지에도 관심을 가지고 있다.’는 배고픔에 따른 행동 변화 및 부정적 감정을 인식하고 조절하는 방법과는 관련이 없으므로 (D)가 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, ⓐ그들은 Stroop 과제에서 더 많은 실수를 했는데, 그 과제에서는 그 참가자들은 다른 색상의 잉크로 출력된 색상 이름이 보여졌다, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to (A)[higher / lower] attention span and self-control.
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels (B)[fall / increase] when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by (C)[releasing / suppressing] cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

choices: the benefits of skipping meals for self-control
how to maintain steady glucose levels during hunger
the role of hormones in boosting concentration and reducing anger
the effects of hunger on mental performance and bodily reactions
ways to improve mental performance by controlling hunger-related hormones

body:
Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. ⓐ우리의 후각은 우리 각자만큼이나 독특하며, 400가지가 넘는 종류의 후각 수용체로 다양성을 만들어 낸다. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact that we are all different and share a plate of understanding.

unique, variations, smell, create, sense of, plentiful, be

solution:
• 주어 Our sense of smell, 동사 is를 쓴 뒤, 주격보어인 형용사 unique와 원급 비교 ‘as ~ as’를 사용하여 as unique as를 쓴다. 두 번째 as 뒤에는 비교 대상이 이어져야하며, 문장의 동사가 be동사 is이므로 as unique as 뒤에 이어지는 절에서도 be동사를 써야 하는데, 주어가 we이므로 복수동사 are로 수일치하여 we are를 쓴다.
• ‘with over 400 types of smell receptors,‘ 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문을 영작해야 하는데, 의미상 주어인 400 types of smell receptors가 다양성을 ’만드는‘ 주체이므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 creating을 쓰고 목적어 plentiful variations를 이어 쓴다.

What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, ______, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

areas connected with long-term memory can process more information at once
areas responsible for logical thinking such as judgment show heightened activity

body:
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they ______, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: feel socially disconnected and emotionally isolated
experience sudden drops in blood glucose levels
go through prolonged periods of physical exhaustion
fail to manage emotional stress through long-term solutions
develop stronger emotional connections through social interaction
solution:
문장의 맨 앞에 연결어 That is(다시 말해서)가 사용되었으므로, 빈칸을 포함한 문장은 앞 문장의 내용을 구체적으로 다시 설명하는 역할을 한다. 앞 문장에서 ‘외로움에서 오는 허기’가 외로움이라는 감정에서 신체적 영양분에 대한 욕구로 이어지는 현상이라고 설명했으므로, 외로움을 느끼고 다른 사람들과 단절되었을 때 배고픔을 느낀다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ① ‘사회적으로 단절되고 정서적으로 고립되어 있다고 느끼다’가 적절하다.
본문변형 feel lonely and isolated from others → feel socially disconnected and emotionally isolated

Grandma Moses
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. (A)그녀의 작품의 아름다움을 깨닫고 그는 그녀의 그림 전시회들을 열었는데, 이는 모두 대중에게 큰 인기를 끌었고, 그 후의 일은 다들 아는 대로이다. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.

Lee Jungseop
Hope within life difficulties
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems (A)lighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children ⓐwere the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of (B)happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the (C)reunion of his family, as he was ⓑforced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, ⓒwhich was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting ⓓis the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also (D)allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability ⓔto express this hope through art brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of (E)comfort to people to this day.

body:
Alfonse Mucha (1860-1939) was one of the first Art Nouveau artists, which led to this form of art being referred to as the “Mucha Style.” His style became famous later on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, did not happen overnight.
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also (A)[ceased / continued] working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he (B)[missed / landed] the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally (C)[move apart / come together].
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: ceased landed come together
continued missed come together
continued landed come together
ceased missed move apart
continued landed move apart
solution:
(A) 마지막 단락에서 Mucha는 처음부터 성공을 거두지는 못했지만, 기회가 생길 때까지 자신만의 양식을 계속해 나갔다고 했으므로 삽입 광고와 삽화를 그려 돈을 벌면서 자신의 예술 작업도 계속했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 continued(~을 계속했다)가 적절하다.
cease ~을 중단하다
(B) Mucha는 이때 연극 ‘Gismonda’의 포스터를 그릴 기회를 잡아 마침내 아르누보 양식 발전의 주요 인물로 알려지게 된 것이므로, landed(~을 얻었다, 잡았다)가 적절하다.
miss ~을 놓치다
(C) Mucha는 적절한 기회가 생길 때까지 자신만의 양식을 계속해 나갔고 성공은 준비가 기회와 만날 때만 이루어진다고 언급하고 있으므로, 그 두 가지가 마침내 결합할 때 아름다운 일들이 일어날 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 come together(결합하다)가 적절하다.
move apart 서로 멀어지다

(B) 동사 led는 ‘lead+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …하도록 이끌다)의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어로 to부정사구가 와야 한다. 따라서 부사가 to부정사 사이에 위치한 분리부정사의 형태 ’to+부사+동사원형’로 to eventually 뒤에 동사원형 become이 오는 것이 적절하다.
(C) 완전한 절(beautiful things ~ together)을 이끌어 4형식 동사 reminds의 직접목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.

In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, (A)[portrayed / portraying] Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually (B)[become / becoming] known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us (C)[what / that] beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the difficulties Mucha experienced before achieving success
how Sarah Bernhardt influenced the rise of Art Nouveau
the conflict between commercial illustration and personal artwork
the power of preparation when it meets the right opportunity
the role of magazine illustrations in Mucha’s early artistic career
solution:

③ 상업적인 삽화와 개인적인 예술 작품 사이의 갈등
⑤ Mucha의 초기 예술 경력에서 잡지 삽화의 역할

Artwork, however, is more deeply appreciated with a deeper understanding of the artist and the experiences that helped produce it. We are going to explore the lives of three artists whose art has inspired people from different cultures and generations. As their life experiences became the inspiration for their art, (A)그들의 작품 뒤에 숨겨진 이야기들을 이해하는 것은 우리가 그들의 작품을 더 잘 감상하도록 도와줄 뿐만 아니라 우리에게도 영감을 줄 것이다.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 동명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 19단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
only, inspire, help, behind, not, the stories, work, better appreciate, but also
→ ______
answer: understanding the stories behind their work will not only help us better appreciate their work but also inspire us
solution:
• ‘이야기를 이해하는 것’을 뜻하도록 동명사 understanding과 목적어 the stories를 쓰고 수식어 behind their work를 이어 쓴다.
• ‘우리가 그들의 작품을 더 잘 감상하도록 도와줄 것이다’와 ‘우리에게도 영감을 줄 것이다‘가 상관 접속사 not only A but also B에 의해 병렬로 연결되므로 조동사 will을 쓰고 not only 뒤에 동사 help, 목적어 us를 쓰고 동사 help는 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어로 글자 수에 맞게 동사원형 appreciate를 쓰고 appreciate를 수식하는 부사 better를 appreciate 앞에 쓴다.
• but also를 쓰고 조동사 will에 이어지는 동사원형 help와 병렬로 연결되므로 동사원형 inspire를 쓰고 목적어 us를 이어 쓴다.

body:
Lee Jungseop
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance. (A) In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. (B) Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. (C) Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. (D) Poverty from the war led to the separation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. (E) During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, which was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting is the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability ⓐ______ brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of comfort to people to this day.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그러나 겉보기에는 행복해 보이는 이 아이들의 모습 뒤에는 슬픈 이야기가 있다.’라는 뜻이며, 역접을 나타내는 연결사 However가 쓰였으므로 이 문장 앞에는 겉보기에는 행복해 보이는 대상에 대한 내용이 와야 하며, 이 문장 뒤에는 슬픈 이야기(a sad story)에 대한 설명이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 ‘두 아이와 물고기와 게’라는 그림이 언뜻 보기에 쾌활해 보인다는 문장 뒤이자 이중섭과 그의 가족이 제주도로 피난을 갔다는 문장 앞인 (A)에 들어가야 한다.

body:
Grandma Moses
When it seems too late
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day ─sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that (A)______.
윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: artistic recognition depends on starting one’s career at a young age
personal hardship motivate artists to achieve meaningful success
our early experiences determine the kind of art we will create
success comes only after years of professional training
it is never too late to accomplish our dreams
solution:
두 번째 단락에서 Grandma Moses는 70대에 그림을 시작했지만 국제적으로 인정받는 예술가가 되었고, 101세까지 1,600점이 넘는 작품을 남겼다고 설명했으므로 이야기가 우리에게 늦은 나이여도 여전히 꿈을 이룰 수 있다는 것을 상기시켜 준다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘우리의 꿈을 이루기에 결코 너무 늦은 때는 없다’가 적절하다.
오답
① 예술적 인정을 받는 것은 젊은 나이에 경력을 시작하는 것에 달려 있다
② 개인적인 고난은 예술가들이 의미 있는 성공을 이루도록 동기를 부여할 수 있다
③ 우리의 어린 시절 경험이 우리가 어떤 종류의 예술을 창작하게 될지를 결정한다
④ 성공은 오직 수년간의 전문적인 훈련 후에 찾아온다

B: I watched the latest Mission Impossible movie on a streaming service last weekend.
G: How was it?
B: It was great! You know what? After I finished watching the movie, the streaming service recommended other similar action movies.
G: I know what you mean. That’s because of the recommendation algorithms.
B: Yeah, I think they track our viewing habits and suggest similar movies.
G: Exactly. I think it’s actually quite intelligent.
B: Is that how they recommend certain products when we shop online?
G: Yes. It’s the same with music recommendations.
B: That’s amazing. It’s really convenient, but (A)I’m worried about privacy issues because that means my personal information could be stored somewhere.
G: True. We should be careful about sharing too much personal data.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: I’m concerned about
I’m anxious about
I’m excited about
I’m indifferent to
I’m scared of
solution:
‘I’m worried about ~‘은 ‘~가 걱정된다’라는 의미로, 어떤 상황이나 가능성에 대해 우려나 불안을 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현이다. ‘I’m excited about ~’는 ‘~가 기대된다’를 뜻하고, ‘I’m indifferent to ~’는 ‘~에 무관심하다’를 뜻하므로 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은 ③ ‘~가 기대된다’와 ④ ‘~에 무관심하다’이다.
오답
① ~가 걱정된다
② ~가 걱정된다
⑤ ~가 두렵다

body:
AI is the ability of computers and machines to perform tasks (A)[that / what] typically require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, decision-making, and language translation. Recent developments have also seen AI taking on more creative roles; AI art generators, for example, are able to take a human’s description in words and transform it directly into art. AI has been around for several decades, but recent advancements in computing power, data storage, and machine learning algorithms have fueled its rapid growth.
Some of the most significant impacts of AI are increased efficiency and productivity. Through automation, AI systems and robots can perform repetitive, boring, and dangerous tasks easily, (B)[free / freeing] up humans to focus on more innovative and strategic work. In the healthcare sector, AI is being used to analyze vast amounts of medical data to improve diagnoses. In finance, AI algorithms are being used to automate administrative tasks, detect fraud, and (C)[making / make] investment decisions.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: what / free / making
that / free / make
what / freeing / make
that / freeing / making
that / freeing / make
solution:
(A) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(typically ~ translation)을 이끌어 명사 tasks를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(AI systems ~ easily)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로 앞 절의 내용이 ‘인간에게 시간적 여유를 주는’ 주체이자 뒤에 목적어 humans가 이어지므로, 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 freeing이 적절하다.
(C) to부정사를 이루는 to 뒤에 이어지는 동사원형 automate, detect와 함께 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조를 이루어야 하므로 동사원형 make가 적절하다.
