Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment. Automation, they argue, will lead to widespread job losses, as machines and robots replace human workers in many industries. This could lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market.
(A) However, it is also important to consider that automation has been a driving force behind economic growth for centuries and has consistently created new job opportunities, even as it has decreased existing ones.
(B) This argument is not without merit. Automation has already displaced workers in several industries, and it is likely that this trend will continue as AI becomes more widespread.
(C) For example, the rise of the automobile industry in the early 20th century led to the displacement of carriage drivers, but it also created new jobs in manufacturing, sales, and service.
The same can be said for the rise of the computer industry in the late 20th century, which displaced workers in manual labor industries, but also created new jobs in software development, information technology, and related fields.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: AI를 비판하는 이들이 AI의 자동화로 인해 일자리가 감소하고, 이것이 빈곤과 소득 격차의 확대로 이어질 수 있다고 주장하는 주어진 글 뒤에, 이러한 주장을 This argument(이 주장)로 이어받아 일리가 있음을 인정하고 실제로 여러 산업에서 근로자가 대체되어 왔다고 언급하는 (B), However(그러나)로 시작하여 (B)에서 설명한 자동화의 부정적인 측면과 대조적으로, 자동화가 기존 일자리를 감소시키기도 했지만 수백 년 동안 경제 성장의 원동력이었으며 새로운 일자리도 지속적으로 만들어 왔다는 점을 설명하는 (A), For example(예를 들어)로 시작하여 앞에서 제시한 자동화가 기존 일자리를 감소시켰으나 새로운 일자리를 만들어 왔다는 내용을 뒷받침하는 구체적인 사례로, 자동차 산업의 발전으로 마차 운전사들은 일자리를 잃었지만 제조, 판매, 서비스 분야에서는 새로운 일자리가 생겼다는 점을 제시하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been the subject of much discussion and controversy for many decades, with many experts predicting that it will revolutionize our way of life. From healthcare to finance, the implementation of AI is transforming a wide range of sectors. Embracing AI means tapping into the potential of tomorrow in unprecedented ways. From self-driving cars to personalized medical treatments, AI is shaping our future and pushing the envelope like never before. As we stand on the brink of a new era, (A)우리 모두가 AI의 부상과 우리의 세상에 미치는 그것의 영향을 이해해야 하는 것이 매우 중요하다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• ‘가주어- 진주어‘ 구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것

<보기>
on, impacts, the rise, crucial, of, understand, each of

answer: it is crucial that each of us understand the rise of AI and its impacts on our world
solution:
• ‘가주어- 진주어’ 구문을 사용해야 하므로 it is를 쓰고 ‘매우 중요한’을 뜻하는 형용사 crucial을 이어 쓴다. 진주어절을 영작해야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that과 that절의 주어 each of us를 쓴다.
• 형용사 crucial(매우 중요한)은 ‘중요성’을 나타내므로 that절 안의 동사는 조동사 should와 동사원형 understand를 쓰거나 should가 생략된 동사원형 understand를 써야 하는데, 글자 수 제한에 따라 should를 생략하고 동사원형 understand만 쓴다. 동사 understand의 첫 번째 목적어 the rise of AI를 쓰고 등위접속사 and 뒤에 두 번째 its impacts와 전치사구 on our world를 이어 쓴다.

Some critics worry about ethical issues that ⓐare tied to AI, including its potential to maintain existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as objective. (A)______, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely reproduce those biases in its output.
For example, facial recognition algorithms ⓑhave found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets ⓒthat mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones. (B)______, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully ⓓarrested by the police. This is a valid concern, and ⓔthat is important for society to take steps to diminish the potential negative impacts of AI.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: That is / In addition
In other words / Consequently
Unfortunately / Meanwhile
However / As a result
Nonetheless / Plus
solution:
(A) 사람들이 컴퓨터 시스템이 객관적이라고 여긴다는 앞 내용과 대조적으로 빈칸 뒤에서 AI 시스템은 그것들이 훈련된 데이터가 편향되지 않은 만큼만 편향되지 않게 되며, 데이터에 편향이 있으면 산출물에 그 편향이 재현될 것이라는 상반된 내용이 이어지므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 However(그러나), Nonetheless(그럼에도 불구하고)가 적절하다.
(B) 밝은 피부색의 얼굴이 주로 포함된 데이터로 학습된 안면 인식 알고리즘의 결과로, 안면 인식 시스템에 의해 소수 인종에 속하는 사람들은 범죄자로 잘못 식별되어 부당하게 체포되었으므로, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 Consequently(결과적으로), As a result(그 결과)가 적절하다.
오답
① 다시 말해서 게다가
② 다시 말해서 결과적으로
③ 불행하게도 한편
⑤ 그럼에도 불구하고 게다가

While AI has the potential to increase efficiency and productivity and solve complex problems, it also has the potential to cause job losses and continue existing biases. The technological singularity is the point at which Artificial Intelligence will ⓐexceed human intelligence. This (A)could lead to a future in which machines can create their own technology, and humans may become useless. Alternatively, the technological singularity could lead to a future in which humans and machines merge, creating a new form of intelligence. Either way, the technological singularity is likely to have a ⓑprofound impact on the future of humanity. According to futurist Ray Kurzweil, the singularity will occur when technological development becomes unstoppable and unalterable, resulting in ⓒanticipated changes to human civilization. Here are a few potential scenarios:
Merging with AI: We may be able to merge with AI in the future, enhancing our intelligence and life expectancy. What would it be like to be able to access the Internet with your mind? Then we might be able to think and learn at extraordinary speeds and control machines with our thoughts.
Bots taking the lead: Many traditional jobs might ⓓfade away, but exciting new roles may pop up. People might be trained to be mediators between AI and humans. Schools might teach teamwork among humans and bots rather than traditional subjects. Kids may attend “fusion schools” (B)where AI instructor bots might collaborate with human creativity. Here, students can design artworks and invent games alongside their AI friends.
Scientific leaps: Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) can solve complex problems, (C)allow for phenomenal achievements in physics, medicine, climate science, and other fields at an ⓔunprecedented pace. For example, the spacecraft of the future may be capable of traveling to other planets at unimaginable speeds. They may also be equipped with advanced life support systems that will allow humans (D)to live there for extended periods of time.
The technological singularity is a potentially dangerous event, but it is also one (E)that could lead to incredible advances for humanity. We need to be aware of the risks and prepare for them as best we can, so that we can make sure (F)what the singularity is a positive event for us all.

• 주어 They 뒤에 이어지는 동사 argue와 argue를 수식하는 부사 also를 They also argue의 순서로 쓰고 argue의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• that절의 주어 AI, 동사 has를 쓰고 ‘잠재력’을 뜻하는 목적어 the potential과 ‘복잡한 문제들을 해결할’이란 뜻으로 the potential을 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사구 to solve complex problems를 이어 쓴다.
• ‘이전에는 불가능했던 방식들’을 뜻하도록 ways를 수식하는 관계사절을 영작한다. 주격 관계대명사 that을 쓰고 복수선행사 ways에 수일치하고, 과거에 불가능했던 것이므로 과거로 시제를 일치한 be동사 were를 that 뒤에 쓰고 ‘이전에는 불가능한’을 뜻하도록 previously impossible을 이어 쓴다.

body:
Therefore, it is likely that the rise of AI will also give rise to new job opportunities. There will be a growing demand for data scientists, machine learning engineers, and AI ethics experts, among others. These jobs will allow individuals to contribute to society in meaningful ways. At the same time, since they require new skills, education and training will need to evolve to help people prepare for these new opportunities. By adapting and learning, people can find paths in a world where AI plays a major role.
Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to maintain existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as objective. However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely reproduce those biases in its output.
For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to ______. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones. As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police. This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to diminish the potential negative impacts of AI.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: perform equally well regardless of people’s skin tones
be free from the biases contained in their training data
be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones
correct the unfair judgments that people tend to make based on skin color
produce inaccurate results mainly because they process an excessive amount of facial data
solution:
앞에서 AI 시스템은 자신이 훈련된 데이터에 편향이 포함되어 있을 경우 그 편향을 결과에 재현할 수 있다고 설명했으며, 그 예시로 언급된 안면 인식 알고리즘은 밝은 피부색의 얼굴 위주인 데이터로 학습되어 그 결과 소수 인종이 범죄자로 잘못 식별되어 부당하게 체포되었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 빈칸에는 안면 인식 알고리즘이 밝은 피부색이 아닌 다른 피부색을 가진 사람들을 식별할 때 덜 정확하다는 내용이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 ③ ‘특정 유형의 피부색을 가진 사람들을 인식할 때 정확성이 떨어진다’가 빈칸에 들어가야 한다.
오답
① 사람들의 피부색과 관계없이 똑같이 잘 작동하다
② 훈련 데이터에 포함된 편향에서 자유롭다[영향을 받지 않는다]
④ 사람들이 피부색을 바탕으로 흔히 내리는 불공정한 판단을 바로잡다
⑤ 주로 지나치게 많은 양의 얼굴 데이터를 처리하기 때문에 부정확한 결과를 만들어 내다

body:
However, it is also important to consider that automation has been a driving force behind economic growth for centuries and has consistently created new job opportunities, even as it has decreased existing ones.

Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment. Automation, they argue, will lead to widespread job losses, as machines and robots replace human workers in many industries. (A) This could lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market. (B) This argument is not without merit. (C) Automation has already displaced workers in several industries, and it is likely that this trend will continue as AI becomes more widespread. (D)
For example, the rise of the automobile industry in the early 20th century led to the displacement of carriage drivers, but it also created new jobs in manufacturing, sales, and service. (E) The same can be said for the rise of the computer industry in the late 20th century, which displaced workers in manual labor industries, but also created new jobs in software development, information technology, and related fields.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그러나, 자동화는 수백 년간 경제 성장의 원동력이었고, 기존의 취업 기회를 감소시키는 한편 지속적으로 새로운 취업 기회를 창출해 왔다는 점을 고려하는 것 또한 중요하다.’라는 뜻으로, However(그러나)로 시작하며 ‘it is also important to consider that(~라는 점을 고려하는 것 또한 중요하다)’라고 했으므로 자동화의 긍정적인 측면을 제시하기에 앞서 자동화의 부정적인 영향이나 우려가 언급되어야 한다. (D) 앞에서 자동화가 이미 여러 산업에서 근로자를 대체했으며, 이러한 추세가 계속될 가능성이 있다는 부정적인 영향을 언급하고 있다. 또한 (D) 뒤에서 For example(예를 들어)로 시작하여 자동차 산업의 발전이 마차 운전사의 일자리를 감소시킨 동시에 제조, 판매, 서비스 분야에서 새로운 일자리를 창출한 구체적인 사례를 제시하고 있다. 따라서 앞의 부정적인 영향과 뒤의 구체적인 사례를 자연스럽게 연결하도록 주어진 문장이 (D)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

body:
AI is the ability of computers and machines (A)[perform / to perform] tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, decision-making, and language translation. Recent developments have also seen AI (B)[taking / to take] on more creative roles; AI art generators, for example, are able to take a human’s description in words and transform it directly into art. AI has been around for several decades, but recent advancements in computing power, data storage, and machine learning algorithms have fueled its rapid growth.
Some of the most significant impacts of AI (C)[is / are] increased efficiency and productivity. Through automation, AI systems and robots can perform repetitive, boring, and dangerous tasks easily, freeing up humans to focus on more innovative and strategic work. In the healthcare sector, AI is being used to analyze vast amounts of medical data to improve diagnoses. In finance, AI algorithms are being used to automate administrative tasks, detect fraud, and make investment decisions.
Advocates of AI argue that these advancements will lead to a more efficient, productive, and technical society, where individuals have more time and resources to focus on more meaningful work. They also argue that AI has the potential to solve complex problems, such as climate change and disease, in ways that were previously impossible. For example, AI can analyze huge amounts of data quickly to find patterns in weather changes or the spread of a disease. This could lead to finding solutions to climate change and cures for untreatable illnesses much quicker.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: perform / to take / is
to perform / to take / are
perform / taking / are
to perform / taking / is
to perform / taking / are
solution:
(A) ‘수행하는 (능력)’이라는 뜻으로 명사구 the ability를 수식하므로 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to perform이 적절하다.
(B) have also seen의 목적격보어 자리로, 지각동사 see는 ’see+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이며 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 때 목적격보어로 동사원형 또는 –ing(현재분사)를 쓰고, 수동 관계일 때 목적격보어로 p.p.(과거분사)를 쓴다. 여기서는 AI가 보다 창의적인 역할을 맡는 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 taking이 적절하다.
(C) 주어의 핵이 impacts이며 복수명사이므로 이에 수일치한 복수동사 are가 적절하다.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) AI-based tools can turn a person's written ideas into visual artwork. (T/F)
(B) Giving machines repetitive and dangerous duties may leave people time for creative work. (T/F)
(C) Supporters of AI expect technological advances to give people more time and resources for meaningful activities. (T/F)
(D) AI could contribute to faster solutions to climate change and cures for currently untreatable illnesses. (T/F)
(E) Since processing large amounts of information takes considerable time, AI may slow efforts to address climate change and disease. (T/F)
choices: T-T-T-T-F
F-T-T-F-T
T-F-F-T-T
T-T-F-F-T
T-F-T-T-F
solution:
차례대로 T-T-T-T-F이다.
(A) AI 기반 도구는 한 사람의 글로 작성된 아이디어를 시각적인 예술 작품으로 바꿀 수 있다. (일치)
(B) 반복적이고 위험한 업무를 기계에 맡기는 것은 사람들이 창의적인 일에 시간을 쓸 수 있게 할 수 있다. (일치)
(C) AI의 지지자들은 기술의 발전이 사람들에게 더 많은 시간과 자원을 의미 있는 활동에 사용할 수 있게 할 것으로 예상한다. (일치)
(D) AI는 기후 변화에 대한 더 빠른 해결책과 현재 치료할 수 없는 질병에 대한 치료법에 기여할 수 있다. (일치)
(E) 대량의 정보를 처리하는 데 상당한 시간이 걸리기 때문에, AI는 기후 변화와 질병에 대처하려는 노력을 늦출 수 있다.(→AI는 날씨 변화의 양상을 찾기 위해 엄청난 양의 데이터를 빠르게 분석할 수 있다.) (불일치)

body:
W: Hello, Mr. Hopkins. I’m wondering if you can help me design a poster for the special lecture hosted by the school council.
M: Okay, what’s the lecture about?
W: It’s about ways to protect turtles from bycatch. I want to make sure that all the necessary information is on the poster.
M: Okay. (pause) It’s nice that you added extra information about the guest speaker, but I’m a bit worried that students might not know what Mission Blue is.
W: Then how about adding that Mission Blue is an organization dedicated to protecting marine ecosystems?
M: I think that would work. Also, ______.
W: I’ll do that. Thank you very much for your help.

다음 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: I suggest you mention that the event is hosted by the student council
if I were you, I would mention that the event is hosted by the student council
it was wise of you to mention that the event is hosted by the student council
you might want to mention that the event is hosted by the student council
I think you should mention that the event is hosted by the student council
solution:
앞서 학생회에서 주최하는 특별 강연 포스터 디자인과 관련해 도움을 요청한 상대방에게 몇 가지 조언을 했으며, ‘미션 블루’라는 단체명과 관련한 정보를 추가하는 것에 대해 그렇게 하는 것이 좋겠다는 의견을 제시한 뒤 Also(또한)를 사용해 말하고 있고, 이에 상대방이 그렇게 하겠다고 답하고 있으므로, 포스터 디자인과 관련해 추가 조언이나 충고를 하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 상대방이 한 일에 대해 칭찬하는 내용인 ③ ‘그 행사가 학생회에 의해 주최된다고 언급한 것은 현명했습니다’는 빈칸에 알맞지 않다.
*원래 지문에는 ‘I think you should ~ council’이 쓰였음
오답
① 그 행사가 학생회에 의해 주최된다고 언급하는 것을 제안합니다
② 제가 당신이라면, 그 행사가 학생회에 의해 주최된다고 언급하겠습니다
④ 그 행사가 학생회에 의해 주최된다고 언급하는 것이 좋겠습니다
⑤ 그 행사가 학생회에 의해 주최된다고 언급해야 한다고 생각합니다

body:
W: What would happen if all the fish in the world suddenly vanished? First, people around the world would face food shortages. Millions of people living near coastal areas live on fish. (A)If all fish were gone, people might face starvation due to lack of food. Second, Earth’s carbon levels would increase. (B)The oceans store a huge amount of carbon. (C)Carbon has long been recognized for its remarkable ability to form complex molecular structures. (D)Tiny marine plants absorb carbon, and fish eat them. Fish then swim down and store the carbon deep in the ocean. (E)Without fish, Earth’s carbon levels would increase, worsening climate change.

다음 담화의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 세계의 모든 물고기가 사라질 경우 세계 곳곳에 식량 부족과 지구의 탄소 수치 증가로 인한 문제가 생길 것이라고 설명하는 흐름이므로, 탄소의 분자 구조 형성 능력을 언급하는 (C) ‘탄소는 복잡한 분자 구조를 형성하는 놀라운 능력으로 인해 오랫동안 인정받아 왔다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
When most people were ⓐfascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there?” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I (A)delight in the life ⓑthat I see.” Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but ⓒwhat it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.
Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. ⓓHaving moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, (B)perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do ⓔare dive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a (C)clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle was ⓕthrilling to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the (D)nervousness of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists ⓖto use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately ⓗled her to become a (E)pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 네 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
(4) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓒ that이 이끄는 앞의 명사절(that ~ life)과 상관접속사 ‘not only A but (also) B(A뿐만 아니라 B도)’에 의한 병렬구조를 이루는 명사절을 이끌어야 하며, 뒤에 완전한 절(it ~ protected)이 이어지므로, what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다. 참고로, 의문대명사 또는 관계대명사 what 뒤에는 불완전한 절이 와야 한다.
ⓔ 주어 all you have to do에 대한 동사 자리에 원형부정사 dive를 보어로 취하는 be동사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 관계사가 생략된 불완전한 절(you have to do)의 수식을 받는 all은 ‘모든 것, 전부’라는 뜻으로서 단수 취급하므로, 수일치를 위해 복수동사 are를 단수동사 is로 고친다.
ⓕ 2형식 동사 was의 보어로 분사 형태의 형용사가 올 수 있으나, 주어 Earle이 ’짜릿하게 만든‘ 주체가 아니라 ’짜릿하게 된‘ 대상이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 형태의 형용사 thrilling을 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 형태의 형용사 thrilled로 고친다.
ⓗ 완전한 절(Her innate sense ~ academic journey)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로, 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상의 주어이자 원인이 되는 앞 절의 내용(그녀의 타고난 모험심과 호기심이 그녀의 학문적 여정을 이끈 것)이 ‘이끈’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 her와 to become 이하의 to부정사구가 이어져 ‘lead+목적어+to부정사(~가 …하도록 이끌다)’의 능동태 구문을 이루어야 하므로, led를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 leading으로 고친다.
오답
ⓐ 2형식 동사 were의 보어로 형용사나 분사가 올 자리이며, 주어인 most people이 ’매료되는’ 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 형태의 형용사 fascinated는 알맞다.
ⓓ 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰인 분사구문을 이끄는 분사가 올 수 있으며, 주절의 동사 began이 나타내는 과거 시점보다 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로, Having 뒤에 ‘move to ~(~로 이주하다)’의 자동사 move가 과거분사(p.p.)형태로 쓰여 완료형 분사구문(Having+p.p. ~)을 이룬 Having moved는 알맞다.

Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists ⓐ[living / to live] in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge (A)남녀가 수중에서 함께 산다는 발상에 대응할 수 없었어요,” she said. The following year, ⓑ[choosing / having been chosen] to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes.
Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, receiving attention similar to ⓒ[those / that] of the astronauts’ historic moon landing.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: living / choosing / those
to live / having been chosen / that
to live / choosing / that
living / having been chosen / that
to live / having been chosen / those
solution:
ⓐ 동사 allowed와 목적어 scientists에 이어져 ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로 to live가 알맞다.
ⓑ 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰인 분사구문을 이루는 자리이며, 주절의 동사 spent가 나타내는 과거 시점보다 더 먼저 일어난 일을 나타내며 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 she가 ‘선정된’ 대상이므로, 수동형 완료 분사구문(having+been+p.p.~)을 활용한 having been chosen이 알맞다.
ⓒ 앞에 나온 명사의 반복을 피하기 위해 쓰인 지시대명사로, 흐름상 단수명사 attention을 대신하므로 단수형인 that이 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.

• 동격의 전치사 of를 사용할 것
• 동명사의 의미상 주어로 목적격을 사용할 것

solution:

• <조건>에 따라 동격의 전치사 of를 사용해 추상명사구 the idea의 구체적인 내용에 해당하는 동명사구를 연결하고, 동명사의 의미상 주어로 목적격을 사용한다. 즉, the idea 뒤에 동격의 전치사 of를 쓰고, 동명사의 의미상 주어를 목적격 형태인 men and women으로 쓴 뒤, live together를 동명사구 living together로 변형하고 부사 underwater를 쓴다.

Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, ⓐincreasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes have been found to ⓑexceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that has ⓒdissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming.
Nevertheless, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet ⓓsaving function depends on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and aid in the planet’s decarbonization. Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, ⓔencouraging industrial fishing practices, restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution entering the sea. By (A)______, we can unlock its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ encouraging(장려하는 것) → rethinking(재고하는 것)

Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, ⓔencouraging industrial fishing practices, restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution entering the sea. By (A)______, we can unlock its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.

choices: Blue Carbon: A New Frontier in Marine Science

body:
In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. ⓐHaving used the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures ⓑthat flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them ⓒwas some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor ⓓto symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and ⓔnoted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day ⓕwhich human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ Having used → Using (완전한 절(she dove ~ for two hours) 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰인 분사구문을 이루는 분사(구)가 올 수 있으며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the JIM suit가 있으므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사(구)가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주절의 과거 시점보다 앞선 시점이 아닌 같은 시점에서 일어나는 상황이므로 Having p.p. 형태의 Having used를 Using으로 고친다.)
ⓒ was → were (부사구 Among them이 강조를 위해 문두에 쓰이면서 부사구 도치에 의해 흐름상 과거시제의 be동사가 주어 앞에 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 주어 some species가 복수명사구이므로 수일치를 위해 단수동사 was를 복수동사 were로 고친다.)
ⓕ which → on which 또는 when[that] 또는 which 삭제 (완전한 절(human beings ~ underwater)을 이끌어 선행사인 시간 명사구 the day를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 which를 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 쓴 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태의 on which로 고치거나 관계부사 when으로 고친다. 또한 선행사가 time, day, year와 같은 일반적 시간을 나타내는 명사일 때 관계부사 when 대신 관계부사 대용의 that을 쓰거나 생략할 수 있으므로, that으로 고치거나 which를 삭제하는 것도 가능하다.)
*원래 지문에는 when이 쓰였음
오답
ⓔ 주어 She에 대한 첫 번째 과거동사 associated와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 있으며, 뒤에 목적어로 인용 부호(“ ”)와 함께 쓰인 명사절(“These ~ ocean.”)이 있으므로, 능동태 과거동사 noted는 알맞다.

For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, ⓐdriving by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks ⓑremains. They are not all gone. However, there is hope of ⓒpreserved endangered marine species. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes ⓓwhich we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the importance of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.”
With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and ⓔpreserving the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.

Sylvia Earle has made valuable ______ to marine science while continually striving to raise awareness of the ______ of the ______ and the need to protect it.
solution: 제시문 Sylvia Earle은 해양의 중요성과 그것을 보호해야 할 필요성에 대한 인식을 높이고자 지속적으로 애쓰면서 해양 과학에 귀중한 기여를 해 왔다.

body:
Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge just couldn’t cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater,” she said. The following year, having been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes.
Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts’ historic moon landing.

윗글에서 유추할 수 있는 Sylvia Earle의 심경 변화로 알맞은 것은?
choices: frustrated → proud
confident → perplexed
disappointed → apathetic
indifferent → pleased
satisfied → anxious
solution:
남녀가 함께 수중에서 생활하는 것을 받아들일 수 없었던 책임자들 때문에 Earle은 처음에 텍타이트 프로젝트에 참여하지 못했으나, 이듬해 전부 여성으로 구성된 텍타이트 II 프로젝트의 리더로 선정되었으며, 지구 표면으로 돌아온 후 우주 비행사의 역사적인 달 착륙과 비슷한 주목을 받았다고 했으므로, 처음 프로젝트에 참여하지 못했을 때에는 실망과 좌절감을 느꼈고, 이후 프로젝트에 참여하여 팀을 성공적으로 이끌면서 기쁘고 자랑스러운 마음이 들었을 것이라고 유추할 수 있다. 따라서 글에서 유추할 수 있는 Sylvia Earle의 심경 변화로 ① ‘좌절한 → 자랑스러운[뿌듯해하는]’이 알맞다.
오답
② 자신감 있는 → 당황한
③ 실망한 → 무관심한
④ 무관심한 → 기쁜
⑤ 만족한 → 불안한

body:
Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds (A)[virtually / firsthand], fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support.
Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as (B)[triggers for / refuges from] pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for (C)[maintaining / worsening] ocean health.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: virtually / triggers for / maintaining
virtually / refuges from / maintaining
virtually / refuges from / worsening
firsthand / triggers for / worsening
firsthand / refuges from / maintaining
solution:
(A) 앞서 Earle이 글로벌 디지털 플랫폼을 시작하는 데 중요한 역할을 했다고 언급했으므로, 이 플랫폼을 통해 사용자들이 가상으로 수중 세계를 탐험하며 해양 생태계에 대한 이해를 높일 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 virtually((컴퓨터를 이용하여) 가상으로)가 알맞다.
firsthand 직접 체험으로
(B) 해양 보호 구역인 ‘Hope Spots’가 하는 역할로서 언급되어야 하므로, 오염, 남획 및 기타 위협으로부터 해양 생태계를 보호하는 역할을 한다는 흐름이 되는 refuges from(~로부터의 피난처)가 알맞다.
triggers for ~의 촉발 요인
(C) 미션 블루는 바다를 탐험하고 보호하기 위한 행동을 촉구하는 비영리단체로서 2030년까지 해양의 30%를 보호한다는 목표를 갖고 있다고 했으므로, 이러한 목표가 국제자연보전연맹(IUCN)이 해양 건강을 유지하기 위해 권장하는 목표에 부합하는 것이라는 흐름이 되는 maintaining(유지하는 것)이 알맞다.
worsening 악화시키는 것

B: Hello, Ms. Han. Can I take a rest for a while? I don’t feel good.
W: Uhm, you have a fever and a runny nose. It seems that your immune system is working hard to protect your body.
B: Immune system? What is that exactly?
W: ______ the body system that helps fight against germs causing diseases.
B: But what does the runny nose have to do with the immune system?
W: When you’re sick, your body produces more liquid inside your nose to wash the germs away.
B: I see. Then, what’s the deal with the fever? Why does my body get all hot?
W: Your body heats up because viruses or bacteria cannot survive above the normal body temperature.
B: Is there anything I can do to boost my immune system?
W: Absolutely! Eat a healthy diet, get regular exercise, manage your stress level, and get enough sleep.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞지 않은 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: It means
It refers to
It results from
It is caused by
It is defined as
solution:
소년이 면역 체계가 정확히 무엇인지 물었고, 이에 대한 대답으로 ‘병을 일으키는 균과 싸우는 것을 돕는 신체 시스템’이라는 정의를 언급하고 있으므로, 어떤 용어나 개념의 정의를 제시할 때 사용하는 표현이 빈칸에 와야 한다. 따라서 인과관계를 설명할 때 쓰이는 표현인 ③ ‘It results from ~(그것은 ~에 기인해)’과 ④ ’It is caused by ~(그것은 ~에 의해 야기돼)‘는 빈칸에 알맞지 않다.
오답
① 그것은 ~을 의미해
② 그것은 ~을 나타내
⑤ 그것은 ~로 정의돼

It appears (A)[that / what] viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated (B)[to kill / to have killed] 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, (C)[affecting / affected] almost every aspect of human life worldwide.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: that / to kill / affecting
what / to kill / affected
that / to have killed / affected
what / to kill / affecting
that / to have killed / affecting
solution:
(A) 가주어 It에 대한 진주어 자리에서 완전한 절(viruses exist ~ humanity)을 이끌고 있으므로, ‘It appears that+완전한 절(~한 것처럼 보이다)’ 형태의 가주어-진주어 구문을 이루는 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.
(B) ‘~한 것으로 추정되다’라는 뜻의 ‘be estimated+to부정사(구)’에서 추정되는 시점이 현재이므로 현재시제 is estimated가 쓰였으나 사람들이 사망한 것은 과거의 일이며, to부정사(구)의 내용이 본동사의 시제보다 이전 상황이면 완료부정사(to have p.p.)를 사용하므로, to have killed가 알맞다.
(C) 앞의 완전한 절(the recent ~ lives)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이끄는 분사가 올 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 the recent COVID-19 pandemic이 ‘영향을 미치는’ 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구(almost every aspect of human life)가 이어져 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 affecting이 알맞다.

body:
ⓐWhat is less commonly known is that viruses play crucial roles in supporting much of life on Earth. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses that sustain us and the planet, instead of just ⓑthose that harm us. Therefore, scientists have ⓒmuch more to learn about viruses than they currently know. (A)그들이 정말로 알고 있는 것은 바이러스가 박테리아와 곤충 개체군의 주요 조절자의 역할을 한다는 것이다.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, they steal the reproductive functions of other organisms ⓓto multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses go on to infect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses ⓔcontrolling the excessive growth of certain bacteria.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ controlling → (to) control (‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식 구문에서 준사역동사 help의 목적격보어로 to부정사나 동사원형이 쓰이므로, controlling을 to control이나 control로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 control이 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 불완전한 절 ‘is less commonly known’과 문장의 본동사 is, 보어절인 that절(that viruses play ~ on Earth)이 이어지므로, 문장의 주어 자리에서 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 불완전한 절을 이끌어 명사절을 이루는 관계대명사 What은 알맞다.
ⓑ 흐름상 복수명사구 the viruses를 대신해 쓰인 복수형 지시대명사 those는 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 비교급(more)을 강조하기 위해 쓰인 much는 알맞다.
ⓓ 앞의 완전한 절(they steal ~ other organisms)에 ‘증식하기 위해’라는 의미로 이어져야 하므로, ‘크게 증가하다’라는 의미의 자동사 multiply를 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to multiply로 쓴 것은 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 관계대명사 what을 사용할 것
• 강조의 do를 사용할 것
• 명사절 접속사 that을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• 뒤에 주어진 어구를 제외하고 12단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
act, know, the primary regulators, viruses
→ ______ of bacterial and insect populations.
answer: What they do know is that viruses act as the primary regulators
solution:
• <조건>에 따라 관계대명사 what을 사용하여, ‘~한 것은 바로 …이다’라는 뜻으로 보어를 강조하는 ‘What절+be동사 ~’ 형태로 쓴다.
• <조건>에 따라 강조의 do를 사용해 주어 they에 수일치한 do와 동사원형 know를 쓴다.
• What절 주어는 보통 단수 취급하므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is를 쓰고, 이어지는 보어절에 <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사를 사용해 ‘that+완전한 절’ 형태의 명사절을 쓴다.
• ‘~의 역할을 하다’를 뜻하는 ‘act as ~’를 사용한다.

ⓐOutbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter human bodies that have no prior ⓑimmunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has ⓒdestroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in a ⓓdecrease in interactions between human and wild animals, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may ⓔincrease in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses did not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans to survive.
Insect species populations are also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses that infect those insects also increase, reducing their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects to flourish. Considering the chain of food in nature, it would not be difficult to assume that viruses fulfill important functions in ______. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: producing oxygen
regulating other species
causing genetic mutations
supporting the growth of all species
helping different organisms fairly compete for limited resources
solution:
특정 유형의 곤충이 과도하게 증가하면 해당 곤충을 감염시키는 바이러스도 증가하여 그 곤충의 수가 감소하며, 이는 다른 종류의 곤충이 번성할 여지를 만들어준다고 설명했으므로, 자연의 먹이 사슬을 고려할 때 바이러스가 다른 종을 조절하는 중요한 기능을 수행한다는 것을 가정할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② '다른 종들을 조절하는 것'이 알맞다.
오답
① 산소를 생성하는 것
③ 유전적 돌연변이를 일으키는 것
④ 모든 종의 성장을 지원하는 것
⑤ 서로 다른 생물들이 제한된 자원을 두고 공정하게 경쟁하도록 돕는 것

solution:
플랑크톤의 주요 먹이는 바이러스 감염으로 죽은 박테리아에서 방출된 영양소라고 했으므로, ② '플랑크톤은 바이러스 감염에 의해 파괴된 박테리아에서 나온 영양분을 먹이로 삼는다.'는 글의 내용과 일치한다.
오답

body:
Another less recognized role of viruses is their contribution to the evolution of life on Earth. When a virus infects a reproductive cell of its host, such as an egg or sperm, the viral DNA may be passed down to the host’s offspring. The insertion of new DNA into genomes is a significant mechanism of evolution. Without viruses, in other words, the evolutionary potential for all life on the planet would be (A)[impacted / unaffected].
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution is their role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ that helps the fetus grow securely inside its mother’s body. It (B)[facilitates / inhibits] the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while protecting the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, making them (C)[vulnerable / invulnerable] to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to carry their young inside their bodies safely from one location to another. Viruses that infected our remote ancestors more than 130 million years ago have been reported to have served a key function in the development of this vital organ.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: impacted / facilitates / vulnerable
impacted / inhibits / vulnerable
impacted / facilitates / invulnerable
unaffected / facilitates / invulnerable
unaffected / inhibits / vulnerable
solution:
(A) 바이러스가 숙주의 생식 세포를 감염시키면 바이러스의 DNA가 숙주의 자손에게 전달될 수 있으며, 새로운 DNA가 게놈에 삽입되는 것은 진화의 중요한 메커니즘이라고 했으므로, 바이러스가 없다면 지구상의 모든 생명체의 진화 잠재력이 영향을 받게 될 것이라는 흐름이 되는 impacted(영향을 받는)가 알맞다.
unaffected 영향을 받지 않은
(B) 태반은 태아가 엄마의 몸 안에서 안전하게 성장할 수 있도록 돕는 기관이라고 했으므로, 그것이 산소, 영양분, 노폐물의 교환을 용이하게 한다는 흐름이 되는 facilitates(~을 용이하게 하다)가 알맞다.
inhibits ~을 억제[방해]하다
(C) 진화 초기에는 암컷이 새끼를 한 곳에 두어야만 했다는 이유가 앞에 제시되었으며, 뒤에는 태반의 출현 이후 암컷이 새끼를 몸 안에 넣어 한 장소에서 다른 장소로 안전하게 옮길 수 있게 되었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 포식자의 공격에 취약했다는 흐름이 되는 vulnerable(공격받기 쉬운)이 알맞다.
invulnerable (공격 등에) 끄떡없는, 영향을 받지 않는

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick.
(A) The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
(B) The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
(C) Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
(D) But they were wrong. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 1600년대 유럽에서 흑사병이 발병했을 때 의사들이 환자를 치료하기 위해 기묘한 복장을 입었다고 언급한 주어진 글에 이어, 그 복장의 구성에 대해 구체적으로 묘사한 (B), 의상에서 가장 특이한 부분이었던 마스크와 의사들이 그것을 착용한 이유로 흑사병이 나쁜 공기로 인해 발생한다고 생각했다고 언급한 (A), But(하지만)을 사용해 앞서 언급된 의사들의 생각이 틀렸다는 대조적인 내용을 연결 후, 실제로 흑사병의 원인이 박테리아였음을 밝힌 (D), 앞서 언급한 과거 상황을 then(그 때)으로 가리켜 그 이후 상황이 크게 바뀌었고, 현대 의학으로 인해 박테리아와 바이러스를 신속하게 탐지하고 대응할 수 있게 되었으며, 보호 장비가 우리를 바이러스에서 보호해준다고 설명한 (C)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

(A)1억 3천만 년 이상 전에 우리의 먼 조상을 감염시켰던 바이러스가 이 중요한 기관의 발달에 핵심적인 역할을 한 것으로 보고되었다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓒ Without viruses가 If절의 역할을 대신하며, 흐름상 문장이 과거 사실이 아닌 현재 사실의 반대를 가정해야 하므로, ‘Without+명사(구), 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …(~가 없다면, …할 것이다)’ 형태의 가정법 과거를 사용해 would 뒤의 have been impacted를 be impacted로 고친다. 참고로, ‘Without+명사(구), 주어+조동사 과거형+have+p.p. …’ 형태의 가정법 과거완료는 ‘~가 없었다면, …했을 것이다’라는 뜻으로 과거 사실의 반대를 가정할 때 쓰인다.
ⓔ 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사를 남겨 둔 ‘접속사+분사(구) ~’ 형태의 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 it(=a placenta)이 ‘보호하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the fetus가 있으므로, protected를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 protecting으로 고친다.
ⓕ 현재분사 형태의 making과 목적어 them에 이어져 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …하게[…한 상태로] 만들다)’의 5형식을 이루어야 하며, 보어 자리에 부사는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사 vulnerably를 형용사 vulnerable로 고친다.
오답
ⓑ 주어 the viral DNA가 ‘타동사+부사’ 구조의 구동사 ’pass ~ down(~을 물려주다)’의 대상이며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사 to가 이어져 있으므로, 수동태인 be passed down은 알맞다.

body:
Another less recognized role of viruses ⓐis their contribution to the evolution of life on Earth. When a virus infects a reproductive cell of its host, such as an egg or sperm, the viral DNA may ⓑbe passed down to the host’s offspring. The insertion of new DNA into genomes is a significant mechanism of evolution. Without viruses, in other words, the evolutionary potential for all life on the planet would ⓒhave been impacted.
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution is their role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ that ⓓhelps the fetus grow securely inside its mother’s body. It facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while ⓔprotected the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, making them ⓕvulnerably to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to carry their young inside their bodies safely from one location to another. (A)1억 3천만 년 이상 전에 우리의 먼 조상을 감염시켰던 바이러스가 이 중요한 기관의 발달에 핵심적인 역할을 한 것으로 보고되었다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 적절한 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• 현재완료 수동태와 완료부정사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• (1)은 5단어, (2)는 9단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
serve, infect, report, remote, a key function, ancestor
→ Viruses (1)______ more than 130 million years ago (2)______ in the development of this vital organ.
answer:
(1) that[which] infected our remote ancestors
(2) have been reported to have served a key function
solution:
(1) <조건>에 따라 적절한 관계대명사를 사용해 주어 Viruses를 수식하는 관계사절을 쓰되, 선행사 Viruses가 과거(1억 3천만 년 이상 전)에 ‘감염시켰던’ 주체이므로, 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which를 쓰고 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 연결한다.
*원래 지문에는 that이 쓰였음
(2) 주어 Viruses가 ‘보고된’ 대상이고, 현재까지 보고된 상태임을 나타내야 하므로, <조건>에 따라 현재완료 수동태(have[has] been p.p.)를 사용한다. 주어가 ‘핵심적인 역할을 했던’ 것이 보고된 상태인 현재시점보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로, ‘be reported+to부정사(~한 것으로 보고되다, ~라고 한다)’의 to부정사 자리에 <조건>에 따라 완료부정사(to have p.p.)인 to have served를 쓴다.

body:
We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. The more we learn about viruses, however, the better equipped we will be to use certain viruses for beneficial purposes and to develop defenses against viruses that could lead to the next pandemic. More than that, learning more about viral diversity will help us reach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.

choices: the need to identify unknown types of virus
the dangers posed by the diversity of viruses
the importance of continued research on viruses
the role of viruses in shaping Earth’s ecosystems
the benefits of using viruses for medical purposes

body:
As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing them in the battle against diseases are arising. Of notable interest are the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment. Genes can be compared to instruction guides that govern how our bodies function. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, which can lead to health problems. Gene therapy steps in to fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering corrected genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, enabling them to function properly. In this process, specially modified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, it can potentially help the body fight off certain diseases.
Using viruses to treat cancer, another use of viruses, is based on the notion of utilizing their natural ability to infect and kill cells. If successful, viruses can be manipulated to specifically target and destroy cancer cells while leaving healthy cells unharmed. The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment is still in the early stages. However, many researchers are involved in hundreds of projects with the goal of discovering cures for diseases that were once thought to be incurable.

body:
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter human bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.

destruction / eliminates

body:
M: Hey, Kate! You seem a bit down.
W: Ugh, I made a big mistake during my presentation. I can’t stop thinking about it.
M: Oh, that’s tough. But hey, how about going outside and soaking up some sunlight?
W: Hmm, I don’t think that’ll change my mood.
M: Trust me! Sunlight stimulates the production of vitamin D, (A)[which / what] plays a crucial role in serotonin production. This natural boost in serotonin levels can have significant effects on your mood.
W: I’m not sure I understand. Are you saying (B)[what / that] sunlight can actually improve my mood?
M: Exactly! Look at this article I read. It says sunlight triggers the release of serotonin, which (C)[calls / is called] the “feel-good” hormone.
W: Alright, I’ll give it a try.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: which / that / calls
what / what / is called
which / that / is called
what / what / calls
which / what / is called
solution:
(A) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(plays ~ production)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 vitamin D를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(sunlight ~ mood)을 이끌어 saying의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 serotonin을 부연 설명하는 관계사절의 동사 자리이며, serotonin이 "기분 좋은" 호르몬이라고 ‘불리는’ 대상이므로 수동태 is called가 적절하다.

body:
Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny?

A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why did Jenny have to skip breakfast in the morning?
How did Jenny behave as she became hungrier during her science class?
Why does a delicious meal make us feel happy and relaxed?
What does the slogan “You’re not you when you’re hungry” mean?
What words were combined to create the official English word “hangry”?
solution:
맛있는 식사를 한 후에, 우리는 배가 부르고, 행복하며, 편안한 기분을 느낀다고만 언급되었을 뿐, 맛있는 식사가 왜 우리의 기분에 영향을 미치는지는 언급된 바가 없으므로 ③ ‘맛있는 음식이 우리를 행복하고 편안하게 느끼게 만드는 이유는 무엇인가?’는 답할 수 없다.
오답
① 왜 Jenny는 아침에 아침 식사를 걸러야만 했는가? (→아침에 학교 가는 버스를 타려고 서둘러야 했기 때문이다.)
② Jenny는 과학 수업 중에 점점 더 배가 고파지면서 어떻게 행동했는가? (→Jenny는 연필을 책상에 두드리고 시계를 화난 듯 바라보았으며, 친구들에게 짜증을 내며 쏘아붙였다.)
④ “배고플 땐 너답지 않아.”라는 슬로건은 무엇을 의미하는가? (→배고픔이 사람의 기분과 수행 능력을 심각하게 변화시킬 수 있다는 것을 의미한다.)
⑤ 어떤 단어들이 결합되어 공식 영어 단어인 “hangry”가 만들어졌는가? (→hungry와 angry가 결합되어 만들어졌다.)

body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either ⓐskip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and ⓑanalyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating ⓒhad poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were ⓓshowing a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they ⓔwere asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest (A)______.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ showing → shown (주어 the participants가 색 이름이 ‘보여진’ 대상이므로 앞의 be동사 were과 함께 수동태를 이루도록 showing을 과거분사 shown으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘~하기를 요청받다’를 뜻하는 ‘be asked+to부정사’의 구조로, 앞의 to와 함께 to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 skip은 적절하다.
ⓑ 주어 Their performance and behavior가 기록되고 분석되는 대상이므로 등위접속사 and 앞에 있는 be동사 were와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 analyzed는 적절하다.
ⓒ that절의 주어 participants를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절(who skipped eating) 뒤에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, 실험이 과거에 발생했으므로 과거형 동사 had는 적절하다.
ⓔ 주어 they(=the participants)가 말하도록 ‘요청 받은’ 대상이므로 수동태 were asked는 적절하다.

body:
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you’re just hangry.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Individual variations in genes, personality, and experiences lead to different responses to hunger.
An animal's behavior can be influenced by whether it has access to enough food.
When deprived of food, fruit flies become more aggressive, while schooling fish show stronger group unity.
Recognizing negative emotions allows people to manage them more successfully.
To check if you skipped a meal can help you realize that your sudden anger is simply due to being hangry.

body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. (A)그 결과는 식사를 거른 참가자들이 미리 식사를 했던 참가자들보다 더 나쁜 수행 능력을 가졌다는 사실을 보여 주었다. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• who를 두 번 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 16단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
performance, the results, poor, skip, show, eating, have, beforehand, those
→ ______
answer: The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand.
solution:
• 주어 The results, 동사 showed 뒤에 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• that절의 주어 participants를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계대명사 who를 쓰고 ‘식사를 걸렀다’를 뜻하도록 동사 skipped와 목적어 eating을 쓴다.
• 관계사절 뒤에 주어 participants에 이어지는 동사 had를 쓰고, ‘더 나쁜’을 뜻하도록 poor를 비교급 poorer로 변형하여 동사 had의 목적어로 poorer performance를 쓴다.
• 비교 대상을 이끌며 ’~보다’를 뜻하는 than 쓰고, those를 쓴 뒤, those를 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계대명사 who를 쓰고 동사 ate와 ‘미리’를 뜻하는 부사 beforehand를 차례대로 쓴다.

body:
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(D)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) “Lonely hunger” refers to a phenomenon where physical hunger causes a person to feel socially isolated. (T/F)
(B) Brain imaging shows that different brain areas are activated by loneliness and physical hunger. (T/F)
(C) Emotional eating can temporarily ease negative emotions, but it can pose long-term health risks. (T/F)
(D) While a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment causes social hunger. (T/F)

body:
Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which ⓐseem to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered ⓑthat there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, ⓒcreating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate ⓓto give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact ⓔwhich we are all different and share a plate of understanding.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the unique substances found in foods like cucumbers and their characteristics
ways to overcome the tendency to avoid foods with unpleasant tastes and smells
individual variations in food taste and smell preferences caused by genetics
how environmental factors and personal habits shape our food preferences
chemical compounds that help protect plants from animals and insects

These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making ⓔare greatly altered. body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks ⓐinvolve selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had (A)______ than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, ⓑwhich the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.

Hunger and the Brain
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. ㉠신경학자들은 코르티솔의 높은 수치는 뇌 속의 세로토닌 수치가 감소시킨다는 것을 밝혀냈다. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that ⓒhelps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of (B)______ is disturbed, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by ⓓusing brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making ⓔare greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: worse outcomes / digestive processes
better memory / emotional control
greater accuracy / long-term memory
poorer performance / mood regulation
higher physical energy / glucose absorption
solution:
(A) 뒤에 이어지는 예시인 스트룹(Stroop) 과제에서 식사를 거른 참가자들이 실수를 더 많이 했다고 언급되고 있으며, 마지막 문장에서 심리학 연구들은 공복 상태가 더 낮은 주의 지속 시간과 자기 통제력에 일조한다는 점을 뒷받침한다고 언급하고 있으므로, 식사를 거른 참가자들이 '더 나쁜 결과들(worse outcomes)' 또는 ‘더 낮은 수행능력(poorer performance)’을 가졌다는 흐름이 자연스럽다.
*본문에는 poorer performance가 쓰였음
(B) 앞 문장에서 신경 전달 물질인 세로토닌이 감정의 균형 및 전반적인 안정감을 유지하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다고 했으므로, 세로토닌 수치가 불균형해지면 방해 받게 되는 정상적인 기능으로 ‘감정 조절(emotional control, mood regulation)’이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.
*본문에는 mood regulation이 쓰였음

① 나쁜 결과들 소화 과정들
② 더 좋은 기억력 감정적 조절
③ 더 높은 정확성 장기 기억력
⑤ 더 높은 신체적 에너지 포도당 흡수

body:
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you’re just hangry.

by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl ⓐnamed Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs ⓑto receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments ⓒusing multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting ⓓwhich teachers and students are present together.
Which one do you think ⓔis better? We decided to explore this topic by considering the perspectives of our readers. The following represents two sides of the debate.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ which → where 또는 in which (완전한 절(teachers ~ together)을 이끌어 a classroom setting을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 관계부사 또는 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태로 써야 한다. 따라서 which를 관계부사 where로 고치거나, 전치사 in을 함께 쓴 in which로 고친다.)
*본문에는 in which가 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 문장의 동사 receives가 있으므로, 명사구 a young girl을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a young girl이 Margie라고 ‘이름 지어진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 named는 적절하다.
ⓑ 동사 long은 to부정사를 목적어로 취해 ‘~하기를 간절히 바라다’라는 뜻으로 쓰이므로 longs의 목적어 자리의 to receive는 적절하다.
ⓒ 명사구 electronically supported learning environments를 수식하는 분사 자리로, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어 multimedia and Internet platforms가 이어지므로, 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 using은 적절하다.
ⓔ think, suppose, believe 등이 주절의 동사일 때 의문사가 있는 의문문이 뒤에 이어지면 의문사가 맨 앞으로 이동하므로, ‘do you think+which is better’에서 which가 앞으로 이동하고 남은 is better가 think 바로 뒤에 이어져야 한다. 따라서 think 뒤에 이어지는 is는 알맞다.

LETTERS TO THE EDITOR
Innovative Approaches for All Learners
Dear Editor,
Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. ⓐ우리는 기술적 혁신과 무한한 연결성을 누리는 시대에서 살아가고 있으므로, 교육에서도 이용 가능한 것을 활용해야 합니다. In the following, I will explore the reasons why online education is a better choice.
First, online education (A)[breaks down / builds up] the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living (B)[far away / nearby]. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
Second, online education caters to personalized learning opportunities that meet the various needs of each learner. One of the criticisms of traditional education is that it takes a one-size-fits-all approach that (C)[manages / fails] to address the various needs of students. In contrast, online learning can offer a customized learning path for each learner. To achieve this, a computer learning program first assesses each learner’s current level and weaknesses. Based on the assessment, each learner is offered personalized online lessons and more detailed explanations when necessary. This kind of personalized feedback process can be highly interactive and motivate learners to reach higher levels of achievement.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: breaks down / nearby / fails
builds up / far away / manages
breaks down / far away / fails
builds up / nearby / fails
breaks down / far away / manages
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 학습자들이 언제 어디서나 학습 프로그램에 접속할 수 있다고 했으므로 온라인 교육은 시간과 공간의 장벽을 없앤다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 breaks down(~을 무너뜨리다)이 적절하다.
build up ~을 강화하다, ~을 더 높이다
(B) 앞에서 학습자들이 언제 어디서나 학습 프로그램에 접속할 수 있으며, 뒤에서 전 세계의 학습자들이 원하는 시간에 언제든지 뛰어난 강의를 즐길 수 있다고 했으므로 Sal Khan이 멀리 살고 있는 사촌을 위해 강의 영상을 만들었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 far away(멀리)가 적절하다.
nearby 가까이에
(C) 뒤에서 대조를 나타내는 In contrast(이에 반해)와 함께 온라인 학습은 각 학습자에게 맞춤형 학습 경로를 제공할 수 있다고 했으므로, 그와 반대로 전통적 교육은 학생들의 다양한 요구를 다루지 못한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 fails(~하지 못하다)가 적절하다.
manage ~을 해내다

First, online education (A)[breaks down / builds up] the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living (B)[far away / nearby]. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
Second, online education caters to personalized learning opportunities that meet the various needs of each learner. One of the criticisms of traditional education is that it takes a one-size-fits-all approach that (C)[manages / fails] to address the various needs of students. In contrast, online learning can offer a customized learning path for each learner. To achieve this, a computer learning program first assesses each learner’s current level and weaknesses. Based on the assessment, each learner is offered personalized online lessons and more detailed explanations when necessary. This kind of personalized feedback process can be highly interactive and motivate learners to reach higher levels of achievement.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 분사구문으로 시작할 것
• ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용할 것
• 관계대명사 what을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
an era, take advantage of, boundless connectivity, available, should, technical innovations, enjoy, is, live
→ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ and ______ ______, we ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ as well.
answer: Living in an era in which we enjoy technical innovations and boundless connectivity, we should take advantage of what is available in education as well.
solution:
• 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 we가 ‘살아가는’ 주체이므로, 자동사인 live를 사용하여 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Living을 쓰고, 전치사 in과 ‘시대’를 뜻하는 an era를 이어 쓴다.
• <조건>에 맞게 ‘전치사+관계대명사’를 사용하여 선행사 an era(시대)를 수식하는 관계사절을 영작해야 한다. an era는 전치사 in과 함께 쓰이므로, 관계대명사 which 앞에 전치사 in을 쓴다. 관계사절의 주어 we 뒤에 동사 enjoy를 쓰고, 목적어인 technical innovations와 boundless connectivity는 제시된 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결한다.
• 주절의 주어 we 뒤에 조동사 should와 ‘~을 활용하다’를 뜻하는 take advantage of를 이어 쓴다. ‘~하는 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what을 사용하고, what이 이끄는 명사절의 동사로 단수동사 is를 쓰고, 이어서 ‘이용 가능한’을 뜻하는 형용사 available과 이를 수식하는 in education을 쓴다.

온라인 교육이 전통적인 교육보다 우수하다고 주장하며, 그 이유로 온라인 교육이 시간과 공간의 제약을 없애 학습자가 언제 어디서나 학습 프로그램에 접근할 수 있다는 점과 학습자의 수준과 약점을 평가하여 각자의 다양한 필요에 맞는 맞춤형 학습 과정과 수업을 제공할 수 있다고 설명하는 글이므로 이 글의 요지로 ⑤ ‘디지털 학습은 더 큰 유연성과 개별화된 수업을 가능하게 하기 때문에 전통적인 학교 교육보다 장점을 가진다.’가 적절하다.
오답
① 자동화된 평가 프로그램은 결국 교실에서 인간 선생님의 역할을 대신할 것이다.
② 전통적인 학교의 교육자들은 현재의 트렌드를 따라가기 위해 자신들의 수업 자료를 업데이트할 필요가 있다.
③ 무료 온라인 강의는 외딴 지역에 사는 학생들의 교육 격차를 메우기 위해 확대되어야 한다.
④ 온라인 학습은 학생들의 개별적인 능력과 관계없이 모든 학생에게 동등한 교육 결과를 제공할 수 있다.

Dear Editor,
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter ⓐthat advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable that online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks that education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, ⓑthat traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven more successful in providing an educational environment ⓒwhich students can concentrate and learn better.
(A) Traditional education also fosters the development of students’ social and interpersonal skills. Beyond classroom instruction, students interact during their lunch breaks and extracurricular activities.
(B) While ⓓspend time together and being engaged in various types of interaction, students are exposed to valuable opportunities to learn how to communicate with each other.
(C) According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. It seems that it is much easier for students to pay attention and understand the content ⓔteaching in a traditional classroom because they are learning together.
Consequently, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 전통적 교육이 학생들이 집중하고 더 잘 학습할 수 있는 교육 환경을 제공한다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 전통적 교실과 온라인 수업에서의 학생들의 집중도와 이해도에 관한 연구에 따르면, 전통적 교실의 학생들이 더 나은 성과를 보였다는 결과를 제시하는 (C), 전통적 교육의 첫 번째 장점을 제시한 (C) 뒤에 also(또한)로 전통적 교육의 또 다른 장점인 학생들의 사회적 기술과 대인관계 기술의 발달을 제시한 (A), 이어 교실 수업 외에도 점심시간과 특별 활동 중에 학생들이 상호작용을 한다고 설명하고, 이러한 상호작용이 결과적으로 협력과 갈등 해결, 리더십 같은 필수적인 사회성의 습득으로 이어진다고 설명하는 (B)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

Consequently, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지 못한 것은?
choices: ⓐ: that → how
ⓑ: that → which
ⓒ: which → where
ⓓ: spend → spending
ⓔ: teaching → taught
solution:
ⓐ that → what (‘~든지[~할지라도]’라는 의미로 양보의 부사절을 이루는 ‘no matter+의문사’의 표현이 되어야 하므로 의문사가 아닌 that은 알맞지 않다. 뒤에 with의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사구 advanced technology를 수식하는 의문형용사가 와야 하므로, 의문부사 how가 아니라 의문형용사 what으로 고쳐야 한다.)
오답
ⓑ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 전치사 on의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(traditional ~ on)을 이끌어, 명사구 the teacher-student relationship을 선행사로 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 계속적 용법에서 쓸 수 없는 관계대명사 that을 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which로 고친 것은 적절하다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(students ~ better)을 이끌어 장소를 의미하는 선행사 an educational environment를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 which를 관계부사 where로 고친 것은 적절하다.
ⓓ 접속사 While이 이끄는 절에 다른 동사가 없으며, 등위접속사 and에 의해 분사 being engaged와 함께 병렬 구조를 이뤄야 하므로, 접속사가 남아 있는 분사구문의 형태로 분사가 위치해야 한다. 따라서 의미상 주어 students가 ‘쓰는’ 주체이므로, spend를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 spending로 고친 것은 적절하다.
ⓔ 명사구 the content를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, the content가 ‘가르쳐진’ 대상이므로 현재분사 teaching을 과거분사 taught로 고친 것은 적절하다.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: guarantee the same learning pace and standardized content
assess student progress through traditional written exams

solution:
앞 문장에서 전통적 교육의 단점으로 모든 학생에게 적용되는 천편일률적인 접근법을 언급한 뒤 빈칸 문장에서 In contrast(이에 반해)라는 대조의 연결어가 사용되었으므로, 빈칸에는 전통적 교육의 천편일률적인 접근법과 대조되는 학습 방식이 언급되어야 한다. 또한 첫 문장에서 온라인 교육은 각 학습자의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 개인화된 학습 기회를 맞춤 제공한다고 언급되었을 뿐만 아니라, 빈칸 뒤에서는 각 학습자의 평가 수준에 맞는 개인화된 온라인 수업을 받는다는 내용이 이어지므로, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘각 학습자에게 맞춤형 학습 경로를 제공하다’가 적절하다.
오답
① 동일한 학습 속도와 표준화된 내용을 보장하다
② 전통적인 필기시험을 통해 학생의 학습 진도를 평가하다
③ 인공지능으로 교사의 역할을 대체하다
④ 학생들이 또래들과 협력하도록 장려하다

body:
First, online education breaks down the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living far away. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
Second, online education caters to personalized learning opportunities that meet the various needs of each learner. ⓐ전통적 교육의 비판 중 하나는 그것이 학생들의 다양한 요구를 다루지 못하는 천편일률적인 접근법을 취한다는 점입니다. In contrast, online learning can offer a customized learning path for each learner. To achieve this, a computer learning program first assesses each learner’s current level and weaknesses. Based on the assessment, each learner is offered personalized online lessons and more detailed explanations when necessary. This kind of personalized feedback process can be highly interactive and motivate learners to reach higher levels of achievement.
Finally, online education uses advanced technology such as multimedia materials or virtual simulations to provide more engaging and impactful learning experiences. For example, students can learn history more effectively by using virtual reality programs, (A)[which / that] can show them realistic details of famous historical sites or allow them to travel back in time.
Advances in technology can make education so much better. (B)[Learn / Learning] anywhere and at any time and receiving personalized lessons can make learning more effective and rewarding. (C)[What / It] is evident that the future of education lies in online education.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 주격 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 23단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
take, the criticisms, fail, approach, it, the various needs, address, one-size-fits-all
→ ______
answer: One of the criticisms of traditional education is that it takes a one-size-fits-all approach that[which] fails to address the various needs of students.
solution:
• ‘One of+(the+)복수명사(~들 중 하나)’를 사용한 One of the criticisms에 of traditional education을 붙여 쓰고, 주어의 핵 One이 단수명사이므로 수일치하도록 단수동사 is를 쓴다.
• 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작해야 하므로 <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사 that을 쓰고 traditional education을 가리키는 대명사 it, ‘~을 취하다’를 뜻하는 동사 takes, 목적어 a one-size-fits-all approach를 차례대로 쓴다.
• a one-size-fits-all approach를 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which를 쓰고 ‘~하지 못하다’를 뜻하는 ‘fail+to부정사’를 선행사 a one-size-fits-all approach에 수일치하여 fails to address로 쓰고 목적어 the various needs of students를 이어 쓴다.
*본문에는 관계대명사 that이 쓰였음

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: which / Learning / What
which / Learning / It
that / Learn / What
that / Learning / It
which / Learn / It
solution:
(A) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ time)을 이끌어, 선행사 virtual reality programs를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
(B) 뒤에 조동사 can이 이어지므로, 주어 역할을 하는 준동사 자리이며 등위접속사 and 뒤의 동명사 receiving과 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로 동명사 Learning이 적절하다.
(C) 흐름상 명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 완전한 절(the future ~ education)이 진주어 역할을 하고 있으므로, 이에 상응하는 가주어 It이 적절하다.

윗글을 다음과 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것)
By removing constraints of ______ and ______, providing ______ learning opportunities tailored to individual needs, and utilizing ______ ______ like virtual reality, online education makes learning more ______ and ______.
answer: time, space, personalized, advanced technology, effective, rewarding
solution: 요약문 시간과 공간의 제약을 없애고, 개인의 필요에 맞춘 맞춤형 학습 기회를 제공하며, 가상현실과 같은 첨단 기술을 활용함으로써, 온라인 교육은 학습을 더욱 효과적이고 보람 있게 만든다.

body:
Traditional education also fosters the development of students’ social and interpersonal skills. Beyond classroom instruction, students interact during their lunch breaks and extracurricular activities. While spending time together and being engaged in various types of interaction, students are exposed to valuable opportunities to learn how to communicate with each other. (A)______, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.
Finally, traditional education offers hands-on and practical learning opportunities. Subjects such as lab sciences and vocational training rely heavily on experiments and direct guidance from instructors. (B)______, in a biology class, students learn how to handle a microscope, and observing the shape of a cell through a microscope for the first time will present them with a truly engaging experience. Online platforms may provide simulations and virtual tools, but they cannot fully substitute the hands-on experiences offered by traditional classrooms.
In short, effective learning requires meaningful relationships between teachers and students, as well as among peers. This interpersonal connection represents the main advantage of traditional education. Guided by strong relationships, students can concentrate better, acquire interpersonal skills, and enjoy hands-on learning experiences. Traditional education makes all of this possible.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: As a result / That is
In addition / Nevertheless
Consequently / For instance
However / In other words
On the other hand / For example
solution:
(A) 앞에서 학생들이 함께 시간을 보내며 다양한 상호작용에 참여하는 동안 서로 소통하는 법을 배우는 귀중한 기회에 노출된다고 했고, 뒤에서 학생들은 협동, 갈등 해결, 리더십과 같은 필수적인 사회적 기술을 습득하게 된다고 했다. 소통 기회에 노출됨에 따른 결과로 사회적 기술 습득이 되는 것이므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 Consequently(결과적으로) 또는 As a result(그 결과)가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에서 실험 과학이나 직업 훈련과 같은 과목은 실험과 교사의 직접적인 지도에 크게 의존한다고 했고 뒤에서 구체적으로 생물학 수업에서 학생들은 현미경 다루는 법을 배운다고 했다. 일반적인 진술 뒤에 구체적인 사례를 제시하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 For instance(예를 들어) 또는 For example(예를 들어)이 적절하다.

body:
It is certainly not easy ⓐ[to judge / judging] which form of education is better. (A) Online education has advantages such as accessibility, personalized instruction, and innovative teaching materials based on advanced technology. (B) Traditional education, on the other hand, provides a more dynamic learning environment, based on the relationships students and teachers build together. (C)
At present, ⓑ[that / what] seems to be the most effective approach to this debate is to take advantage of each method by combining them. (D) For example, teachers in a traditional education environment can introduce personalized online programs ⓒ[using / used] AI technology or make use of VR as part of their classroom activities. (E) Selecting the best resources and methods for learners will lead us to the most successful and fulfilling educational outcomes.

Combining methods this way can benefit students by making up for what seems to lack in each method.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이런 식으로 방법들을 결합하는 것은 각 방법에서 부족해 보이는 점을 보완함으로써 학생들에게 유용할 수 있다.’라는 뜻으로, ‘Combining methods this way(이러한 방식으로 방법들을 결합하는 것)’가 사용되었으므로 이 문장 앞에는 this way가 가리킬 수 있는, 두 교육 방식을 어떻게 결합할 수 있는지에 대한 구체적인 내용이 언급되어야 한다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 ‘For example(예를 들어)’로 시작하여, 전통적인 교육 환경에서 교사가 AI 기술을 활용한 개인 맞춤형 온라인 프로그램을 도입하거나 VR을 교실 활동의 일부로 활용하는 구체적인 결합 방식을 제시하는 문장 뒤인 (E)에 위치해야 한다.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: to judge / what / using
judging / that / used
to judge / what / used
to judge / that / using
judging / what / using
solution:
ⓐ 가주어 It에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로, 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사 to judge가 적절하다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(seems ~ debate)을 이끌어 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계대명사 what이 적절하다.
ⓒ 명사구 personalized online programs를 수식하는 분사 자리로, personalized online programs가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어 AI technology가 이어지므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 using이 적절하다.
